drought.details: While general efforts in rapeseed-mustard breeding aim for drought-tolerant cultivars (RESULT_9, RESULT_30) and some varieties like NRCYS-05-02 are noted as moisture stress tolerant (RESULT_7, RESULT_12), specific drought tolerance for JMC-3 (or JM-3) is not detailed in the provided search results. Research on the genetics of drought stress tolerance in *Brassica spp.* is ongoing (RESULT_3).

heat.details: Heat stress is recognized as a major factor affecting rapeseed-mustard growth and productivity in India (RESULT_14, RESULT_19, RESULT_20). While some mustard genotypes (e.g., DRMRIJ16-3, RGN-403, RH-1556) have shown tolerance to high temperature stress with delayed sowing (RESULT_18), and NRCDR 2 (Indian mustard) is tolerant to high temperature at sowing (RESULT_24), specific heat tolerance for JMC-3 is not described. The reproductive stage is particularly susceptible to temperature stress in Indian mustard (RESULT_17).

salinity.details: Breeding efforts in *Brassica spp.* are directed towards understanding the genetics of salt stress tolerance (RESULT_3). Specific varieties like Pusa mustard-24 are noted as salt tolerant (RESULT_29), and NRCDR 2 (Indian mustard) is tolerant to salinity at sowing (RESULT_24). However, no specific information regarding JMC-3's salinity tolerance is provided.

flood.details: Economically important Brassicaceae crops, including *Brassica napus* (canola) and *Brassica oleracea* (broccoli, cabbage), are generally susceptible to flooding stress (RESULT_36, RESULT_41). No specific information on JMC-3's flood tolerance is available.

disease_resistance.summary: While JMC-3 (JM-3) is mentioned alongside varieties like JM-1 and JM-2 (RESULT_26, RESULT_28, RESULT_29, RESULT_39), and JM-1 and JM-2 are bred for disease tolerance (RESULT_22), specific disease resistance for JMC-3 itself is not explicitly detailed. Sclerotinia rot is a significant disease in rapeseed-mustard (RESULT_22).

pest_resistance.summary: The impact of increasing insect stress on crop production is acknowledged (RESULT_10), but specific pest resistance for JMC-3 or other mustard varieties is not provided in the search results.

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield data for JMC-3 is not provided in the search results.
agronomic_details.stability: Information on JMC-3's yield stability across different environments is not available.
agronomic_details.adaptation: JMC-3 (JM-3) is listed as an Indian mustard variety (RESULT_29, RESULT_39). Indian mustard is a major rabi oilseed crop in India (RESULT_40, RESULT_47). The original data indicates it is recommended for Jammu. Selection efforts for superior Indian mustard plants, including JM-3, have been practiced at various centers (RESULT_26).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in the search results.
agronomic_details.field_trials: JM-3 was involved in selection programs for superior plants/bulk at different centers, and crosses involving JM-3 (e.g., JM-3 x RH9615) have been part of breeding efforts in Indian mustard (RESULT_26).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for JMC-3. Research on Quantitative Trait Loci (QTLs) for heat stress tolerance has been conducted in *Brassica rapa L.* (yellow sarson), with identified tolerant lines (RESULT_13, RESULT_37). The genetics of salt and drought stress tolerance are also being explored in *Brassica spp.*, often using *Arabidopsis thaliana* as a model (RESULT_3).
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTLs related to heat stress tolerance have been identified in *Brassica rapa*, and tolerant groups showed cooler canopy temperatures (RESULT_13). No specific QTLs for JMC-3 were found.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not specified for JMC-3. General research indicates that molecular responses to stresses like flooding are being studied in Brassicaceae, but specific mechanisms for JMC-3 are not detailed (RESULT_36, RESULT_43).

commercial_info.seed_corporations: JMC-3 (listed as JM 3) is included in a list of Indian mustard varieties, alongside JM 1, JM 2, Jagannath, and Pusa Mustard 27, under Orissa, suggesting its potential availability through official seed channels (RESULT_29).
commercial_info.availability_status: Implied to be available for cultivation, given its inclusion in variety lists and breeding programs (RESULT_26, RESULT_29).

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rabi 2019-20, Palli Siksha Bhavana, Visva-Bharati (Sriniketan, Birbhum, West Bengal): transplanting gave the best growth, productivity and profitability among sowing methods; 90:45:45 kg N:P2O5:K2O per ha was the best nutrient treatment. No yield values were given in the digest. (2) Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University, rabi 2015-16 and 2016-17, split plot with 3 replications: Kesari Gold gave the highest seed yield (1746 and 2153 kg/ha in years 1 and 2), oil content 39.13%, 1000-seed weight 7.08 g; the comparison included other mustard hybrids. (3) Crop-spacing trial comparing Kesari 5111, Kesari 5222 and Kesari Gold across four spacings: Kesari Gold is named among hybrids with high seed yield. The digest notes that it is treated as V3 in this trial, and the trial details (spacing values, yields) were not provided.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned agronomic trial and marketing pages but nothing on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for Kesari Gold. Sowing-date text on a trial page is general background, not a tolerance finding. -- https://chemjournal.researchfloor.org/performance-of-indian-mustard-cv-kesari-gold-under-different-sowing-method-and-nutrient-management/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest reaction data for Kesari Gold. A seaweed biostimulant product named "Kesari Gold" (mescot.in) claims pest and disease defence, but it is a fertiliser product, not this variety, so it is discarded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364388719_Performance_of_Indian_Mustard_cv_Kesari_Gold_under_different_Sowing_Method_and_Nutrient_Management

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Rabi 2019-20 field trial at Palli Siksha Bhavana, Visva-Bharati (Sriniketan, Birbhum, West Bengal): transplanting gave the best growth, productivity and profitability among sowing methods, and 90:45:45 kg N:P2O5:K2O ha-1 was the best nutrient treatment -- https://chemjournal.researchfloor.org/performance-of-indian-mustard-cv-kesari-gold-under-different-sowing-method-and-nutrient-management/
Dev Bhoomi Uttarakhand University, rabi 2015-16 and 2016-17 (split plot, 3 replications): Kesari Gold gave the highest seed yield (1746 and 2153 kg/ha in years 1 and 2), oil content 39.13%, 1000-seed weight 7.08 g; the mustard-hybrid comparison included other hybrids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382360429_Comparative_Analysis_of_Different_Mustard_Hybrids_Analyzing_Growth_and_Yield_Perspectives
Crop-spacing trial comparing Kesari 5111, Kesari 5222 and Kesari Gold (treated as V3) across four spacings; Kesari Gold is named among hybrids with high seed yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361052260_SEED_PRODUCTION_TECHNOLOGY_OF_RAPESEED_MUSTARD
Dealer/marketing page for "Kesari Gold hybrid mustard": early maturity 110-115 days, height 170-190 cm, yield 8-10 q/acre, oil 40-41%. Not a trial or official record; relation to Bayer's variety unconfirmed -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Mustard/Kesari_Gold

GENETICS AND QTL
Official record (Rajya Sabha answer, 2022): Kesari Gold (31J3403) is a hybrid using the Ogu cytoplasmic male sterility (CMS) system -- https://rsdebate.nic.in/bitstream/123456789/735470/1/PQ_258_16122022_U1122_p122_p123.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa 3022 (BG 3022), chickpea

Name note: The evidence below refers to Pusa 3022 (BG 3022), the CSC release name. The Seednet name "PUSA-30" is listed under yellow sarson (mustard), so it cannot be the same crop. My search for PUSA-30 returned an error, so I have no Seednet evidence under that name. Four searches were run in total. The results contained no breeder name, breeder contact, or seed-dealer listing specific to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant to Fusarium wilt, per the DPD central-release table for Pusa 3022 (2015, IARI, NWPZ, irrigated) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Described as having ascochyta blight and wilt tolerance, with a 100-seed weight of 37 g -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Described as having moderate resistance to wilt and root rot, with yield potential of 20-25 q/ha for bold-seeded types in the group it belongs to -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to Pusa 3022 were found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to wilt and root rot (see Stress Tolerance line above) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- Moderately resistant to Fusarium wilt (see DPD line above) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- No pest-resistance data specific to Pusa 3022 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Identified by the AICRP for the NWPZ, with a mean yield superiority of 56.18% over ruling checks, 10.4% over the best check JGK 1, average grain yield of 1782 kg/ha, and yield potential of 3056 kg/ha; mean maturity 150 days; 100-seed weight 36 g -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf
- Mean maturity of 150-152 days and irrigated management, per the DPD table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Yield potential up to 3 t/ha and 1.8 t/ha average grain yield (10.4% above best check) -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- AICRP 2021-22 report row for Pusa 3022 (BG 3022), with 2015 release, IARI, large-seeded kabuli, 150 days, NWPZ, irrigated -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Field trial, Zn fertilization: Pusa 547 (desi) out-yielded Pusa 3022 (kabuli) by 19.1% in grain yield -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43538-026-00920-w
- Breeder seed indent figures (51.6 and 20.0 q) appear in an IARI table with no year label -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Developed through desi x kabuli introgression -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Also described as desi x kabuli introgression, extra-large seeded kabuli -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- AICRP table gives a pedigree string of the form "(BG 1083) x (BG 1048 x SBD 377)"; the text is garbled in the extract, so treat it as unverified -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The input parentage "Not specified" is therefore partly resolved by this unverified string.
- No QTL or marker study specific to Pusa 3022 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed at IARI, Pusa, New Delhi (institution and station) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. Chellapilla Bharadwaj, Pusa Chickpea 20211 and Pusa JG 16 sources are different varieties and are discarded.
- A quiz page describes Pusa-3022 as a wilt-resistant kabuli chickpea developed by IARI; low-reliability source -- https://questions.collegedunia.com/exams/questions/match-list-i-with-list-ii-list-i-variety-a-pusa-30-6a75b01685c0aaf2e35b6e90

CONTACT DETAILS
- Official email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL for IARI or a Pusa 3022 breeder: No evidence found. The retrieved pages do not include any contact information. IARI is named only as "IARI, Pusa, New Delhi" (see Breeder line above).

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2026). Zinc fertilization effects on nodulation, enzyme activity, biofortification, and productivity in desi and Kabuli chickpea. Springer journal article -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s43538-026-00920-w (DOI 10.1007/s43538-026-00920-w)
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Symbiotic nitrogen fixation for sustainable chickpea yield and prospects for genome editing in changing climatic situations. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1621191/full (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1621191). Pusa 3022 is a check genotype here.
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Developing microbial seed coating for enhancing seed vigour and prolonging storability in chickpea. Seed Science and Technology (ScienceDirect) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0254629924004174 (pii S0254629924004174). Pusa 3022 is one of two varieties tested.
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2023). Annual report 2021-22. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- IARI (2014). IARI News, Vol. 30 No. 4, Oct-Dec 2014 (identification announcement). IARI -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/IARI-News/Newsletter_October-December-2014.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper specific to Pusa 3022 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing specific to Pusa 3022 was found. The one seed listing retrieved is for "Pusa Manav" (a different variety), so it is discarded.
- Breeder seed indent figures for Pusa 3022 are listed (see Agronomy and Trials line above) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Seednet listing: No evidence found (PUSA-30 search failed).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified for NWPZ: Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and Delhi, per the DPD table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- IARI's own note lists Punjab, Haryana, western Rajasthan, western UP and Delhi (Uttarakhand not listed) -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
- Release year conflicts across sources: 2015 (DPD), 2016 (IARI best-practice note), 2017 (Krishi Jagran). The DPD table lists 2015 for the notification -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Krishi Jagran source dates release to 2017 -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Bahar (HD 2987), wheat

Name check: The variety_name is "Pusa Bahar" and the seednet_variety_name is "PUSA BAHAR". The release-minute name appears as "Pusa Bahar (HD 2987)" in the Bihar notified-variety list, so the evidence below refers to "Pusa Bahar (HD 2987)" under both names. The Seednet crop field says "Indian Rapeseed and Mustard (Yellow Sarson)", but every source found describes HD 2987 as a wheat variety, so the Seednet crop entry looks wrong. "Pusa Bahar" is also a marigold name in one source, so results for that name need care.

RELEASE AND NOTIFICATION
- Notified in the Bihar list as Pusa Bahar (HD 2987), notification date 25/03/2011, S.O. 632(E). This is one year after the 2010 release date in the input record. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- ICAR's 2011-12 crop improvement report lists HD 2987 (Pusa Bahar) among wheat releases for timely sown rainfed and restricted-irrigation conditions in the peninsular zone. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pusa Bahar is listed for timely sown, restricted-irrigation conditions in Central India. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- HD 2987 was used as a check in a drought-tolerance study of recombinant inbred lines grown under rainfed and irrigated conditions. This shows it was tested for drought, but it does not show its own tolerance level. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Prakash-Nautiyal
- Heat, salinity, flood, and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No variety-specific rust, smut, or other disease resistance data for HD 2987 was found. The AICRP FLD report notes no disease or insect incidence in its demonstration plots, but this applies to all FLD plots, not to HD 2987 alone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343381935_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2019-20_Social_Sciences

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A ResearchGate AICRP FLD table lists HD 2987 at Indore with a value of 49.00, but the column meaning is unclear, so it cannot be read as a yield. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343381935_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2019-20_Social_Sciences
- An AICRP-related social-sciences progress report (2016-17) lists HD 2987 among 11 improved or newly released varieties and reports yield gains for them. The report gives no figure for HD 2987 alone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321482036_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2016-17_Social_Sciences
- Sowing window: The Central India guidance gives 20 October to 10 November for timely sown, restricted-irrigation conditions. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- Maturity, plant height, and yield potential for HD 2987: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No parentage, pedigree, marker, or QTL data for HD 2987 was found. The marker-assisted rust studies found concern HD2967 and HD3209, not HD 2987. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9103291/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi. -- https://www.magazines.cornous.com/downloadpdf/192
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found.
- Station: No evidence found that HD 2987 was bred at a regional station.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact: No breeder contact found. The IARI institute introduction page is the only official institute page located. -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/introduction.php?div_id=28
- Official email, phone, and postal address for the wheat division: No evidence found in the search results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Nautiyal, P. C. (year not stated in source). Agronomic and physiological characterization of RILs for drought tolerance in wheat (Triticum aestivum L.). Conference paper; authors and journal not confirmed in the source. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Prakash-Nautiyal
- AICRP on Wheat and Barley Progress Report 2016-17 (Social Sciences). Report; the authors are not listed in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321482036_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2016-17_Social_Sciences
- AICRP on Wheat and Barley Progress Report 2019-20 (Social Sciences). Report; the authors are not listed in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343381935_All_India_Coordinated_Research_Project_AICRP_on_Wheat_and_Barley_Progress_Report_2019-20_Social_Sciences
- Full KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed variety paper for HD 2987: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Pusa Beej portal lists wheat seed from the Seed Production Unit at Pusa Institute, New Delhi, with pickup within ten days of booking. Listing of HD 2987 on this page was not confirmed. -- https://pusabeej.iari.res.in/varieties.php?crop_name=V2V5enlQSkV0anFPaTF6T3JkVTc5dz09
- Seednet, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listings for HD 2987: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Peninsular zone, timely sown rainfed and restricted irrigation. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/crop-improvement-AR-2011-12.pdf
- Central India timely sown restricted-irrigation recommendation. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/improved-wheat-cultivation-practices-in-central-india/
- A separate IARI page lists HD 2987 for Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Goa, and plains of Tamil Nadu. -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/cereals/wheat/
- The recommended_states field in the input is "Not specified", so these sources fill that gap.

Limits: I used four searches, one per topic plus a seed-availability search, and no fetch was possible, so the snippets were not checked against full documents. The parentage, lead breeder, and contact fields remain unresolved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search note: four web_search queries were run. Nothing matched the release-minutes name "Pusa Bold-", the variety code "WRR2", or the 2022 release date. No Seednet page was returned for "PUSA BOLD". The evidence below refers to the long-standing Pusa Bold mustard variety, not to a confirmed 2022 DU release, so the input record conflicts with the sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pusa Bold is listed among Indian mustard varieties suggested for rainfed drought-prone conditions, alongside RH-819, RH-781, GM1 and Pusa Bahar -- https://www.gcirc.org/fileadmin/documents/Bulletins/B25/B25_06Rapeseed.pdf
- Pusa Bold is named among the Indian mustard varieties in a rainfed Aravali list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258384157_Advances_in_Agronomic_Management_of_Indian_Mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czernj_Cosson_An_Overview
- Pusa Bold and Pusa Agrani are recommended for late-sown crops because they mature quickly when planted late -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6254
- No evidence found for salinity, flood, submergence or heat tolerance specific to Pusa Bold.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Pusa Bold in the retrieved sources. The searches returned only general variety lists.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pusa Bold is described as irrigated, with average yield of about 18 q/ha and maturity of 110-140 days, and suitable for northern states and high altitude -- https://www.krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/165-mustard.html
- Pusa Bold is grouped with varieties targeted at various agro-climatic zones, yielding above 40% oil content -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6254
- Pusa Bold was among the leading rapeseed-mustard varieties in seed production during 2002-2007 -- https://www.gcirc.org/fileadmin/documents/Bulletins/B25/B25_06Rapeseed.pdf
- No multi-location AICRP trial result specific to Pusa Bold was found; the official DAC oilseeds table retrieved did not show a Pusa Bold row -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx

GENETICS AND QTL
- A marker-study table lists Pusa Bold as IARI New Delhi, pedigree Varuna x BIC 1780, released 1984 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable (this conflicts with the 2022 release date in the input)
- The same source lists JM-1 (ZARS Morena, 1999) with Pusa Bold as a parent (Pusa Bold x L 6) -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- No QTL or marker study specific to Pusa Bold was found beyond this pedigree reference.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The pedigree source attributes Pusa Bold to IARI, New Delhi, not to the Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants, University of Delhi as stated in the input -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- No breeder name for Pusa Bold was found in the retrieved sources.
- The Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants (University of Delhi) is named in coverage of DMH-11 GM mustard, led by Deepak Pental. This is a different transgenic line, not Pusa Bold -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DMH-11_Mustard

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder or institute email, phone or address for Pusa Bold was found in the searches.
- Institute-level contact page for the Centre for Genetic Manipulation of Crop Plants (University of Delhi): not retrieved; no contact details found.
- Suggested check: the IARI division of genetics, or the Seednet/CSC notification record, for the official contact.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2023 or later review cited as ARCC source). Title and author list not in search result. Agricultural Science Digest (ARCC) article on mustard variety performance. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6254
- Authors not retrieved (year not in snippet). Marker study with Pusa Bold pedigree table. PLOS ONE. DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0272914 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- Yadava et al. (2014). Cited within a ResearchGate page on Pusa Mustard 30; full title not retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260917853_Mustard_Variety_Pusa_Mustard_30
- Thesis (KrishiKosh) and AICRP report entries: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listing: Pusa Bold mustard seed offered at about Rs 140/kg in Sri Ganganagar. Not an official seed source -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mustard-seeds-pusa-bold-26278511397.html
- Seednet, NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Input list (Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh) is not confirmed by any retrieved source. The krishisewa page only mentions northern states and high altitude -- https://www.krishisewa.com/crop-varietes/165-mustard.html
- The official DAC oilseeds table lists recommended states for other varieties, but no Pusa Bold row was found -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx

Discrepancies to resolve before filing: (1) release year 2022 versus the 1984 IARI pedigree record; (2) institution DU CGMCP versus IARI; (3) "Pusa Bold-" and WRR2 do not appear in any source; (4) one ResearchGate source describes Pusa Bold as low erucic, which conflicts with the variety's usual description and should be checked against the CSC notification.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the State of Jammu & Kashmir (plains), Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi and Western Uttarpradesh. It is also suitable for multiple cropping system. Early maturity - 107 days. Oil Yield - 578 Kg/ha.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: This variety is tolerant to lodging and shattering. Responsive to higher dosen of N (125% of recommended fertility)., Seed rate: 3-3.5 Kg/ha
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Leaf characters: - Simple or compound: Simple, - Shape of the pinae: Round and broad, - Colour: Green, - Pubscent/glabrous: Pubescent, Stem colour: Green becomes whitish at maturity, Flower colour: Yellow, Siliqua: Mediumk (4.30 cm with 13-17 seeds) ; seed : medium bold, round, brown in colour and 4.50 g./1000 seed wt.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 165 cm (154-175), b) Distinguishing morphological Characters: Medium plant height with average 5.0 primary branches and 14 secodary branches per plant, narrow and hairy green leaves. Very long main shoot (80 cm) with average 42, siliquae on it with high siliquae density.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Tolerant to salinity up to 12 dS/m, tolerant to high temperatures at seedling as well as at maturity. Escapes insect pests and diseases due to early maturity.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: NPJ-112 was found comparatively better or at par with the checks in relation to the above diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Aphid is the most serious insect-pest of all Brassica spp. It escates aphid infestation due to early maturity. NPJ-112 was found better or at par with checks in aphid infestation.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Mustard 25 (NPJ-112), Indian mustard (Brassica juncea)

Scope note: The search tool hit its limit after four queries, so a fifth check of the Oilseeds DAC table and the Global Agriculture page was blocked. Several headings are thin. Searches were run under "Pusa Mustard 25" and "PUSA MUSTARD-29".

NAME RECONCILIATION
- variety_name "Pusa Mustard 25" (NPJ-112) is matched by the DAC, Global Agriculture, ResearchGate and PMFME sources below.
- seednet_variety_name "PUSA MUSTARD-29" does not match this variety. Global Agriculture describes Pusa Mustard 29 as LET-36, a low erucic acid (single zero) variety with about 21.69 q/ha yield and 37.2% oil, suited to Delhi, Haryana, Jammu, Punjab and northern Rajasthan. That is a different variety. The Seednet record for "PUSA MUSTARD-29" should be checked before any data is merged. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-29-let-36/

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Shekhawat (2012) lists Pusa Mustard 25 (NPJ 112) among varieties described as tolerant in an agronomic review, but the snippet does not state which stress. Also listed in the same review's white rust resistance group. Treat as unverified. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2012/408284
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to this variety was found. Evidence found for stress tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The Shekhawat (2012) review's white rust resistance list includes Pusa Mustard 25 in the snippet. Confirm the rust designation with the original source. -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2012/408284
- No alternaria, downy mildew, aphid or other pest data found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturing variety, developed through a modified bulk method from a cross KRT 5 x NP 200, with a toria pollen parent. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25
- Global Agriculture (IARI listing) describes it as highly suitable for Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, plains of J&K and HP, and western UP, and suitable for multiple cropping between September and mid-December. This text is also on the Pusa Mustard 28 page, so attribution is uncertain. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-25-npj-112/
- Yield, maturity days and oil content: not confirmed for this variety in retrieved text. The DAC table likely holds them but its snippet was truncated. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx
- Field trial results: No evidence found for Pusa Mustard 25 specifically. The Krishi Jagran item concerns Pusa mustard and lentil varieties at Gogamukh, Assam, and does not name Pusa Mustard 25 in the retrieved text. -- https://krishijagran.com/news/pusa-mustard-and-lentil-varieties-show-good-yield-in-a-field-experiments-at-icar-iari-assam/

GENETICS AND QTL
- An SSR-marker diversity study of Indian mustard varieties places Pusa Mustard 25 in a cluster with admixture from another subpopulation, so it may be a poor choice for recombination breeding within that set. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0272914
- QTL or marker-assisted studies specific to this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Lead breeder: Devendra Yadava, listed at Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI). Co-author Sujata Vasudev, also IARI. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25
- Developing institution: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi (Global Agriculture, DAC listing). Station and division not confirmed. Institution field "Not explicitly stated" in the input is therefore resolved as IARI, though this is inferred from the IARI listing.
- Release year: not confirmed. The Global Agriculture page carries a "July 20, 2023" header, but the same header appears on other varieties, so it is not reliable for Pusa Mustard 25. Parentage: partly given as KRT 5 x NP 200 (see Agronomy). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-25-npj-112/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Named contacts: Devendra Yadava (IARI, breeder). No email, phone or postal address for him was found.
- Institute-level contact: No official IARI email, phone, postal address or contact page URL was found in retrieved results. Recommended: IARI main site, New Delhi, via https://www.iari.res.in (not retrieved; verify manually).
- Seednet portal: not reached; no contact data from it.

PUBLICATIONS
- Yadava, D.K.; Vasudev, S.; et al. (2010). Early maturing variety Pusa Mustard-25. Czech Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding 70(3):307-308. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750581_Early_maturing_variety_Pusa_Mustard-25 (DOI not retrieved)
- Shekhawat, N.S. et al. (2012). Advances in Agronomic Management of Indian Mustard (Brassica juncea (L.) Czernj. Cosson): An Overview. International Journal of Agronomy. DOI: 10.1155/2012/408284 -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1155/2012/408284 (author list partial; "Shekhawat" from the citation string)
- Molecular characterization and genetic diversity analysis in Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L.) varieties using SSR markers (2022, PLOS ONE). DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0272914 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0272914 (year and authors not confirmed from snippet)
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports and other peer-reviewed trials: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private listing: Sakshi Farms "Pusa 25 Black Mustard" seed on Flipkart. Unverified private seller. -- https://www.flipkart.com/sakshi-farms-pusa-25-black-mustard-seeds-for-seed-sowing-farming-agriculture-kheti-variety/p/itmdff0bbcba08ea

RECOMMENDED STATES

- Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, plains of J&K, western UP, per the Global Agriculture page (see Agronomy caveat). -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-25-npj-112/

drought.details: No evidence found in the searched sources for drought tolerance or its mechanisms in Pusa Mustard 26.

heat.details: Terminal heat tolerance is reported for Pusa Mustard 26 (NPJ-113) by a seed-company listing and by the IARI variety description, which credits PM-26 with terminal high-temperature tolerance. Both are descriptive claims without quantitative heat-stress data in the digest. A late-sowing study (rabi 2017-18 and 2018-19) included PM-26 but reports impaired biochemical stress mechanisms in Indian mustard generally, and PM-26 was not singled out. Level is rated medium because the tolerance claim is reported by two sources but is not supported by controlled stress data.

salinity.details: A third-party guide lists PM-26 as tolerant to salinity and high temperature at sowing. The digest states this is not confirmed by a primary source, so no level is assigned on the basis of that claim alone.

flood.details: No evidence found in the searched sources for flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence found for white rust, Alternaria, Sclerotinia or other disease resistance in Pusa Mustard 26.

pest_resistance.summary: No resistance rating found. An aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) yield-loss study used PM 26 (short duration) as one of the test cultivars, but the snippet reports no resistance rating for it. No other pest resistance evidence found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Official reference value: 16.00 q/ha under normal conditions (variety data). Multi-location trials over 4 years at 14 locations gave 16.04 q/ha, against 13.45 q/ha (national check) and 12.27 q/ha (zonal check), with higher oil content (secondary copy of the release summary). Conflict: the IARI variety page gives an average seed yield of 14.7 q/ha for PM-26 (NPJ-113). The two IARI-linked values (14.7 q/ha on the variety page and 16.04 q/ha in the release summary) are both recorded here and not reconciled. A third-party guide gives 1481-1895 kg/ha, which is not verified by a primary source.
agronomic_details.stability: The stability analysis reports PM-26 had above-average stability for seed yield per plant. Other cross-environment evidence is limited to the multi-location trials and the Tungabhadra and Assam trials summarised under field_trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adaptation ecology is recorded as multiple cropping systems. The release summary indicates 126 days to maturity under late-November sowing. The Tungabhadra command area trial was on paddy fallow land. The release recommendation covers the plains of Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Delhi and western Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Conflicting values. 126 days (Bhawani Seeds listing; IARI-linked page; release summary under late-November sowing). 107 days (IARI variety page, which conflicts with the 126-day figure on the other IARI-linked page). 131.22 days (days to maturity column in the stability analysis table). The digest does not resolve these values.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Morphological characteristics and agronomic features are not specified in the variety data or the digest. The digest records 37.6% oil content (Bhawani Seeds listing) and higher oil content in the multi-location trials.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location yield trials, 4 years, 14 locations: 16.04 q/ha vs 13.45 (national check) and 12.27 q/ha (zonal check), with higher oil content and 126 days to maturity under late-November sowing (secondary copy of release summary, Scribd). (2) IARI variety page: average seed yield 14.7 q/ha, 107 days to maturity (conflicts with 126 days elsewhere). (3) Assam field trial at Dhirpai Chapori, sown late December 2022: 26-28% higher grain yield and about 10% higher straw yield than the local check. This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed paper. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME CHECK: variety_name "Pusa Mustard 26" (code NPJ-113) is the name used in all evidence below. seednet_variety_name "PUSA MUSTARD-29" is not this variety. The sources that use "Pusa Mustard 29" describe LET-36, a low-erucic-acid variety released in 2013, so none of that evidence is attributed here. No Seednet portal page was found for either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Terminal heat tolerance is reported for Pusa Mustard 26 (NPJ-113) in a seed-company listing, which also gives 126 days to maturity and 37.6% oil -- https://www.bhawaniseeds.in/Mustard.html
- The IARI variety description also credits PM-26 with terminal high-temperature tolerance and a 126-day maturity -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/oil-seeds/mustard/
- A third-party guide lists PM-26 as tolerant to salinity and high temperature at sowing, but this is not confirmed by a primary source -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/cultivation-of-mustard-in-india
- A late-sowing study (rabi 2017-18 and 2018-19) included PM-26 and reports that late sowing impaired biochemical stress mechanisms in Indian mustard generally; PM-26 was not singled out -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9111527/
- Drought and flood/submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- An aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) yield-loss study used PM 26 (short duration) as one of the test cultivars, but the snippet reports no resistance rating for it -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0261219422001661
- White rust, Alternaria, Sclerotinia or other disease resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Multi-location yield trials over 4 years at 14 locations gave 16.04 q/ha, against 13.45 and 12.27 q/ha for national and zonal checks, with higher oil content and 126 days to maturity under late-November sowing -- https://www.scribd.com/document/561186540/NPJ-113 (secondary copy of the release summary)
- IARI's variety page gives an average seed yield of 14.7 q/ha and 107 days to maturity for PM-26 (NPJ-113), which conflicts with the 126-day figure on the other IARI-linked page and with the other sources. Record both values and flag the conflict -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/oil-seeds/mustard/
- Assam field trial at Dhirpai Chapori (sown late December 2022) reported PM-26 with 26-28% higher grain yield and about 10% higher straw yield than the local check. This is a news report, not a peer-reviewed paper -- https://krishijagran.com/news/pusa-mustard-and-lentil-varieties-show-good-yield-in-a-field-experiments-at-icar-iari-assam/
- IARI research farm, rabi 2020-21: PM-26 under integrated management gave 2,206 kg/ha seed yield and 877 kg/ha oil yield -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/view/98
- Tungabhadra command area (paddy fallow) trial: PM-26 gave 810 kg/ha seed yield, below PM-25 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-6-2020/M.%20A.%20Basavanneppa%20and%20B.%20Arun%20Kumar.pdf
- Stability analysis: PM-26 had above-average stability for seed yield per plant; the table lists its days to maturity as 131.22 -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue6/PartB/9-5-130-962.pdf
- A third-party guide lists PM-26 at 1481-1895 kg/ha -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/cultivation-of-mustard-in-india

GENETICS AND QTL
- SSR marker fingerprinting of 27 Indian mustard varieties, including PM-26, with pedigree table entry "VEJ Open x Pusa Agrani", IARI, 2010 -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article/file?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0272914&type=printable
- QTL or trait-mapping studies for PM-26: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi, released through the national (CVRC) process for Zone II -- https://www.scribd.com/document/561186540/NPJ-113 and https://www.bhawaniseeds.in/Mustard.html

- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. The sources identify the institute only.

- No breeder or scientist email, phone or personal contact was found for this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Pili Sarson-1 (mustard, yellow sarson)

Name note: "variety_name" (CSC minutes) and "seednet_variety_name" are both "Pant Pili Sarson-1". No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so every finding below refers to the name as written in the GBPUAT and AICRP documents. Seednet variety code A0403122 was not verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The AICRP objectives page only states a general aim of breeding for disease and insect resistance, with no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No variety-specific evidence found. The same AICRP document lists the variety in its breeding table but gives no resistance scores for it. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The AICRP table row for Pant Pili Sarson-1 gives the figures 15-19, 100-110 and 44, with a note that it is high yielding and suited to October sowing under irrigated conditions in the Uttarakhand plains. Column headers are not visible in the extracted text, so the figures are likely yield (q/ha), days to maturity and oil percentage, but this is unconfirmed. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The AICRP 2020 report lists Pant Pili Sarson-1 (GBPUAT, Pantnagar, 2010) in its variety table with small numeric entries (0.01, 0.01, 20.00, 0.19, 52). Column meanings are not stated. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The AICRP 2021 Project Coordinator's report lists Pant Pili Sarson-1 among varieties in the trial and seed-production tables, but the text does not give its yield values. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Partial pedigree only. The AICRP table gives the cross as PT-9719 × TS-50 for Pant Pili Sarson-1. No QTL or marker study was found. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand. Listed as a yellow sarson variety in the GBPUAT release list. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The AICRP table gives the notification as SO.211(E), dated 29.01.10, under the Pantnagar entry. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No lead breeder or scientist name was found for this variety. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder email or breeder phone found. Institute-level contacts found:
- Breeder Seed Production Centre, GBPUAT (Dr. A.S. Jeena, Joint Director): +91-7817005207; PO Pantnagar, Distt. U.S. Nagar, Uttarakhand-263145 -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html
- Pantnagar Centre of Plant Genetic Resources (Dr. J.P. Jaiswal, Nodal Officer): +91-9411159751; PO Pantnagar, Distt. U.S. Nagar, Uttarakhand-263145 -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html
- No official GBPUAT email or variety-specific contact page was found. The directorate page is the closest official institute contact page.

PUBLICATIONS -- No variety-specific paper, thesis or conference paper found.
- Project Coordinator's Report (2020-21), AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard. Authors not stated (2021). Report. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
- AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard, Uttarakhand (GBPUAT) variety performance summary, 1992-2018. Authors not stated (2018). Report. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
- AICRP Annual Report 2020 (DRMR). Authors not stated (2020). Report. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
- Not relevant to this variety: the Indianfarmer yellow sarson PDF and the GBPUAT combining-ability paper (Kumar, Pant and Pant, 2016) concern yellow sarson or Indian mustard in general.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No certified seed source found. Retail listings on Flipkart, Amazon, eBay and Meesho sell "pili sarson" grain as food, not seed of this variety. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listing was found. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in Pant Rai-20. The one trait tied to this variety is high-temperature tolerance at maturity. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf (AICRP table row for Pant Rai-20, spans 15-7 and 15-8; the URL is the gbpuat.res.in host as returned)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Results on Alternaria blight, white rust and aphid resistance concern other genotypes or programmes and were not attributed to Pant Rai-20. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf (search returned no variety-specific disease rating)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The AICRP rapeseed-mustard table lists Pant Rai-20 as a high-yielding, medium-maturity, bold-seeded line suited to irrigated and rainfed, timely-sown conditions, with a maturity of about 122-128 days and about 40% oil. The column headings are not fully legible in the extracted text, so the yield figure (25-30 in the same row) should be checked against the original table before use. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
No variety-specific multi-location trial data found. The Pantnagar sowing-date and planting-geometry study used an unnamed Indian mustard variety and does not name Pant Rai-20. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/paperdetail.php?paper=1272

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: the AICRP table records Pant Rai-20 as a pure-line selection from Kranti. The seednet record says "Not specified", so this is a discrepancy to resolve, not a confirmed pedigree. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf
No QTL or marker study on Pant Rai-20 found. The yellow sarson QTL and SSR papers returned concern other Brassica rapa lines. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0209982

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Breeder name: not found. No Pant Rai-20 breeder or developing scientist is named in any result, so none is attributed here. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf (lists the variety among GBPUAT Genetics & Plant Breeding releases)
Institution: G. B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar, which lists Pant Rai 20 among its mustard releases. The GBPUAT Pantnagar AICRP centre sits in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf ; http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf
Station: Pantnagar, Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/paperdetail.php?paper=1272

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No official email, phone or postal address for the GBPUAT Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding or the Pantnagar AICRP centre appeared in the results. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/DES/research_centre (Directorate of Research page; returned no contact fields)
Institute site URLs found: https://www.gbpuat.ac.in and https://www.gbpuat.res.in (contact pages not retrieved)

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry, thesis or conference paper that names Pant Rai-20. Papers by GBPUAT authors on mustard (for example, Usha Pant's SSR and heat-stress work) do not name this variety, so they were not attributed. -- https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=hH8lAM0AAAAJ&hl=en (author profile only; not attributed)

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Results were retail sellers of rai (black mustard spice) and unrelated Indian oilseed stock; none refer to Pant Rai-20 seed. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or seednet seed-sale record was retrieved. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/rai-seeds-15337203155.html (a spice seller, discarded as irrelevant)

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttarakhand is the seednet recommended state. The GBPUAT and AICRP results confirm only that the release comes from a Uttarakhand university and that the Pantnagar centre targets plains of Uttarakhand. Neither source names Pant Rai-20 with a recommended state. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf

NAME AND SPECIES NOTES
variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Pant Rai-20". GBPUAT and AICRP write it "Pant Rai 20" or "Pant Rai-20". The release notification is given as SO.2680(E) with date 01.10.15 in the AICRP table, which differs from the year_of_release field (2015-06-25). The species is also unresolved. The seednet crop is yellow sarson (Brassica rapa), but the GBPUAT list places Pant Rai-20 under mustard (Rai), and the AICRP table is for rapeseed-mustard. Verify the species against the CSC minutes before relying on the record.

heat.details: Marketed as highly adaptable and able to withstand heat and moisture stress (company product page). A distributor page reports tolerance to high temperature and moisture stress. A review of Indian pearl millet breeding names Proagro 9444, together with 86M64, as targeting high-temperature environments, with good seed set and grain yield of about 4-5 t/ha. Level is medium because the support is company/distributor claims plus one review statement, with no independent trial measuring heat tolerance mechanisms.

disease_resistance.summary: Downy mildew: resistance claimed for the base hybrid Proagro 9444 by a distributor page. No field-trial or independent disease reaction data found in the digest. Rust and smut: Not found in searched sources for the base hybrid (the digest's rust and smut tolerance statement concerns the separate Gold variant and was excluded).

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no pest reaction data from field trials for this variety. The termite tolerance statement refers to the separate Gaucho variant and was excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: Review of Indian pearl millet breeding reports grain yield of the order of 4-5 t/ha for Proagro 9444 and 86M64 under high-temperature targeting. Company page describes high grain and fodder yield without quantities. Munger (rainfed Eastern India, kharif 2013 and 2014) recorded 32.09 q/ha for Proagro 9444.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Performance was reported across several sites (Eastern India rainfed, Eastern UP plains, and a Jodhpur-area sowing-date study), but no stability analysis across environments was reported.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif season (CSC record). Distributor page lists kharif and summer cultivation. Performance reported in rainfed Eastern India, Eastern UP plains under summer irrigation, and a Rajasthan-area sowing-date study. Company page and 2006 article describe wide adaptability to adverse conditions.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 80-85 days (kharif, company and distributor pages); 85-90 days (summer, distributor page).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: High tillering capacity per plant (Proagro breeding head statement, 2006 article). Other morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: 1) Sowing-date study (Bhuva and Detroja, Jagadhar/Jodhpur-area journal): Proagro 9444 recorded the highest grain yield, statistically comparable with GHB 538, and the highest calendar days, heat units and heat use efficiency among all varieties tested. 2) Rainfed Eastern India, KVK Munger (kharif 2013 and 2014): Proagro 9444 yielded 32.09 q/ha, comparable to the top-yielding hybrid Proagro 9450 (33.87 q/ha, a different variety reported only for context). 3) Summer irrigation study, Eastern UP plains: Proagro 9444 with irrigation scheduled at 100 mm CPE gave the best benefit-cost ratio and net return. No disease or pest trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Marketed as withstanding heat and moisture stress, per the company's pearl millet product page (Bayer/Proagro, base 9444 entry) -- Highly adaptable and can withstand heat and moisture stress. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet
- A distributor page for the hybrid reports tolerance to high temperature and moisture stress -- Tolerant to high temperature & moisture stress -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9444
- The Proagro breeding head said the hybrid is widely adaptable to adverse conditions with high tillering (company statement, 2006 article) -- Proagro 9444 is widely adaptable to adverse conditions with high tillering capacity per plant. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/proagro-millet-gets-popular-in-rajasthan-106060201124_1.html
- A review of Indian pearl millet breeding names 9444 among hybrids with good seed set and high grain yield under high-temperature targeting -- 86M64 and Proagro 9444, which specifically target this environment for hybrid development, have been found having good seed set and high grain yield of the order of 4–5 t ha^−1. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40003-013-0089-z
- Drought, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for these specific stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew resistance is claimed for the base hybrid -- Resistant to Downy mildew -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9444
- Caution: the "Proagro 9444 Gold" variant is listed separately with downy mildew, rust and smut tolerance -- Matures in 75 days, good grain and fodder yield, excellent stay green, tolerant to downy mildew, rust aand smut. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet (this applies to Gold, not confirmed for base 9444)
- Caution: the "Gaucho" variant is listed with termite tolerance -- Good tolerance against termite. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet (variant only)
- Pest and disease reaction data from field trials: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and use, per company page: Full maturity 80-85 days. High grain and fodder yield. -- https://www.cropscience.bayer.in/Products-H/Brands/Seeds-and-Traits/Seed-ProAgro-Millet
- Distributor page gives maturity of 80-85 days in kharif and 85-90 days in summer -- in 80-85 days in Kharif and Summer season 85-90 days. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9444
- Sowing-date study (Jagadhar/Jodhpur-area journal, Bhuva and Detroja): Pearl millet variety 'Proagro 9444' recorded the highest grain yield which was statistically comparable with 'GHB 538' and took the highest calendar days, heat units and heat use efficiency as compared to all other varieties. -- https://journal.agrimetassociation.org/index.php/jam/article/download/577/479/522
- Rainfed Eastern India trial (KVK Munger, kharif 2013 and 2014): Significantly higher grain yield (33.87 q ha-1) was in hybrid 'Proagro 9450' which was comparable to 'Proagro 9444' (32.09 q ha-1) -- https://www.academia.edu/41689356/Evaluation_of_Pearl_millet_varieties_under_rainfed_region_of_Eastern_India
- Summer irrigation study, Eastern UP plains: The best benefit-cost ratio and net return were obtained when hybrid Proagro 9444 was planted with irrigation set at 100 mm CPE. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328600256_Productivity_and_Water_use_Efficiency_of_Summer_Pearlmillet_Pennisetum_glaucum_L_Hybrids_as_Influenced_by_Irrigation_Scheduling_in_Eastern_Uttar_Pradesh_Plains

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The search returned no QTL, marker or parentage studies naming this hybrid. The only nearby hits were general pearl millet heterotic-pool papers that do not name

seednet_fields.Parentage: Bio-902 x ZEM-1 Bio-902 was developed at IARI, New Delhi (NRCPB) in 1993 for zone IV and is a leading variety of the country after Pusa Bold and Varuna. ZEM-1 is an exotic yellow seeded genotype which possesses low erucic acid content. It is late in maturity and poor performer for seed and oil yields in Indian subcontinent.
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: Its plant is tall and compact type having profuse branching with high siliquae density and bold dark brown seeds resembles with Bio-902.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release & cultivation in the States of Uttar Pradesh, Uttrakhand, Madhya Pradesh and eastern Rajasthan  for timely sown irrigated conditions.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Tolerant to lodging and shattering. Responsive to higher doses on N (150% of recommended fertility). Recommended fertility level – 80 kg N, 40 kg P2O5, 40 kg K2O. Suitable for timely (October) sown irrigated conditions in zone III in the double cropping system.  Seed rate : 3 – 4 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm) - 200 cm.	BOLD SEEDED with low erucic acid content (<2.0%). ii.	Very long main shoot (87cm) and other branches with high siliquae density. iii.	Compact plant type with profuse branching having five primary and 14 secondary branches. iv.	Light green leaves without hairiness. v.	Dark brown seed coat colour. vi.	Light yellow flowers. vii.	Small siliqua with undulated texture.   Tall, compact plant type II.	Leaf characters i.	Simple / Compound - Simple, - Shape of leaf pinae - Round and broad, - Colour -  Light green,- Pubescent/Glabrous - Pubescent, - Stem colour -  Light green, -  Flower colour -  Light yellow, - Siliqua - Small,- Seed - Bold, dark brown in colour,
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
•	Tolerates salinity upto 12 dS/m and has lesser reduction in germination (%) and seedling dry weight. It recorded 10.3, 7.4 and 15.8 percent  reduction in germination percent at Kanpur, Hisar and S.K. Nagar, respectively, which was much lesser than salinity tolerant check CS 54. It was, therefore, rated as tolerant to salinity (<20%). At S.K. Nagar it has merely 15.7 % reduction in seedling dry weight. 
•	Variety was rated as moderately tolerant to terminal heat stress based on reduction in total dry weight at Hisar and Kanpur; 1000 seed weight and harvest index at Kanpur which is comparable to the tolerant check BPR 541-4 with respect to all the four parameters studied.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Mustard 34 (variety_name) / Pusa Mustard-32 (seednet_variety_name), mustard, ICAR-IARI

NAME NOTE: No search result mentioned "Pusa Mustard 34", "Pusa Mustard-34" or the code "LES 60". Every variety-specific finding below refers to Pusa Mustard-32 (Seednet name, also written PM-32 or Pusa Mustard 32). Pusa Mustard 34 is not confirmed as the same variety, so treat the two names as unreconciled.

STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to Pusa Mustard-32)
- Described as tolerant of low water stress and suited to areas with limited water supply -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/new-mustard-variety-pusa-mustard-32-promises-high-yield
- A table lists the variety with environmental tolerance (low water stress) and good adaptability -- https://www.indianfarmer.net/uploads/vikas%20article%20-mustard.pdf
- No heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found for this variety.
- Pusa Mustard 34: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to Pusa Mustard-32)
- A Hindi retailer listing says the variety is tolerant of white rust, so infection is unlikely -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/pusa-32-mustard-seeds-2854874813288.html
- A farmer-advice article calls the variety resistant to several common crop diseases, without naming them -- https://www.krishidunia.com/en/how-to-cultivate-pusa-sarson-32-after-rice-harvest-870
- No aphid, pest or formal AICRP disease-scoring data found for this variety.
- Pusa Mustard 34: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to Pusa Mustard-32)
- Average seed yield is reported at 27.1 q/ha, with up to 33.5 q/ha under optimal conditions -- https://www.cmv360.com/tractors/news/new-mustard-variety-pusa-mustard-32-promises-high-yield
- Maturity is reported as 132-145 days; plant height about 73 cm; sowing window last week of September to 15 October -- https://www.krishidunia.com/en/how-to-cultivate-pusa-sarson-32-after-rice-harvest-870
- A retailer listing gives 142 days maturity, 4.61 g per 1000 seeds, and 38.0% oil -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-Mustard-variety-Agricuture/dp/B0BBCQQBNG
- The IARI page gives 40.56% oil and describes the seed as yellow -- https://ztmbpd.iari.res.in/technologies/varietieshybrids/oil-seeds/mustard/
- Conflict: oil content is given as 38% in some sources and 40.56% on the IARI page.
- No replicated multi-location AICRP yield data for this variety found.
- Pusa Mustard 34: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No pedigree, parentage, marker or QTL evidence found for Pusa Mustard-32 or Pusa Mustard 34. The Seednet "parentage: Not specified" entry is unresolved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pusa Mustard 32 (seednet name: Pusa Mustard-32; variety code LES 54), Indian mustard / Indian rapeseed and mustard (yellow sarson)

Search limit note: the search tool hit its usage cap during my final pass, so only four queries ran, and I could only read the snippets that were printed, not the full pages. Several headings below are therefore thin or empty. Treat these as leads to verify on the original pages, not confirmed facts.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched for drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance; the returned pages did not describe these traits for Pusa Mustard 32. The results were about Pusa Mustard 30 and Pusa Aditya, which are different varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched for disease and pest resistance; the returned pages did not describe these traits for Pusa Mustard 32. Pusa Aditya (a Brassica carinata variety, a different variety) appeared in results and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The only page naming this variety was the AICRP-RM site, which lists it as a candidate but gives no yield or trial data in the snippet. Maturity and yield are not confirmed. -- https://aicrprm.icar.gov.in/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genetic-parentage source was returned. The record's parentage field ("Not specified") is unchanged.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi, per the AICRP-RM page, which says the variety (Pusa Mustard 32, LES-54) was developed by ICAR-IARI, New Delhi and identified for release at the 27th Annual Group Meeting of Rapeseed-Mustard research workers held 3-4 August 2020. -- https://aicrprm.icar.gov.in/ . No individual breeder name was found in the returned results.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone or postal address for this variety was returned. The AICRP-RM homepage is the only official source reached, and it is not a contact page: https://aicrprm.icar.gov.in/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, thesis or KrishiKosh entry naming this variety was returned in the results I could read.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- A retail listing names "Green World Pusa Mustard 32 variety seeds" (2 kg packs) on Amazon.in. This is a private seller listing, not an NSC, SAU or KVK source, and I did not check its seed-lot or certification status. -- https://www.amazon.in/Green-World-Mustard-variety-Agricuture/dp/B0BBCQQBNG . No NSC, state seed corporation, SAU or KVK listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No independent evidence found. The recommended-states list in the input record (Rajasthan northern and western parts, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, western Uttar Pradesh, plains of Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh) is unverified against any source here. The seednet_variety_name ("Pusa Mustard-32") did not appear in any result; all matches used "Pusa Mustard 32" or "LES-54".

RELEASE NOTE -- The input gives a release date of 9 November 2020. The AICRP-RM snippet supports identification for release in August 2020, but I found no notification or gazette entry confirming the 9 November 2020 date.

NAME CHECK -- Evidence refers to "Pusa Mustard 32" and "LES-54" (variety_name and variety_code). No page used "Pusa Mustard-32" (seednet_variety_name).

To finish this record, the stress, disease, trials, QTL, publications and contact headings need a rerun of searches, including a seednet.gov.in query for the notification entry, a KrishiKosh query, and an IARI Division of Genetics contact-page query.

drought.details: No search result mentions drought tolerance for Pusa Mustard 37 (NPJ-253). The results only give general information on drought losses in Indian mustard (17 to 94 percent yield reduction) and on climate resilient rapeseed-mustard varieties. The original data do not claim drought tolerance.

heat.details: Based on the original (CSC) data, the variety has high temperature tolerance at the seedling and grain filling stages. The search results do not independently verify this for NPJ-253. Related IARI varieties are documented as heat tolerant: Pusa Mustard 25 (NPJ 112) has high temperature tolerance at the juvenile stage, and Pusa Mustard 28 (NPJ 124) is listed among late sown/high temperature tolerant varieties.

salinity.details: Based on the original data, the variety tolerates salinity up to 12 dS/m, with a smaller reduction in germination, seedling dry weight and imbibition rate. The search results contain no independent confirmation for NPJ-253. The climate resilient varieties review covers salinity tolerance in rapeseed-mustard generally.

Seed rate is 3-4 kg/ha, seed is brown, oil content is 40.0-42.8 percent and 1000 seed weight is 4.8 g.

drought.details: RB-50 is identified as drought tolerant and resistant to drought stress. It is listed among varieties specifically suited for rainfed conditions. It has been described as one of the most drought tolerant mustard genotypes.

heat.details: RB-50 is tolerant to terminal heat stress, which is a significant issue for Indian mustard at its terminal stage in India.

salinity.details: RB-50 is listed as a salinity tolerant variety of Indian mustard.

flood.details: RB-50 is listed as a variety suitable for ACZ-III-B Flood Prone Eastern Plains (Alwar, Rajasthan), implying some level of flood tolerance, grouped under general 'submergence tolerant varieties'.

disease_resistance.summary: RB-50 is resistant to lodging, all rusts, white rust, and yellow mosaic virus. It is also mentioned as a highly resistant mustard genotype for biotic stresses.

pest_resistance.summary: RB-50 is tolerant to aphids and jassids.

drought.basis: Eight distinct cited documents (justagriculture 2022, Wiley 2012, HAU, ResearchGate reviews, Seednet, DFI, ICAR advisory) plus snippets from the water-stress and molecular-marker papers name RB-50 as drought tolerant.
drought.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

heat.basis: Four distinct cited documents (justagriculture 2022, ResearchGate 'Hundred years' review, HAU PDF, ResearchGate climate-resilient review) state RB-50 is terminal heat tolerant. The Scribd copy is not counted as a separate document.
heat.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

salinity.basis: Four distinct documents (Wiley 2012, ResearchGate 'Hundred years' review, ResearchGate agronomic management overview, ResearchGate climate-resilient review) list RB-50 as salinity tolerant.
salinity.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

flood.basis: Only one ResearchGate climate-resilient review cited; it lists RB-50 for a flood-prone zone and implies tolerance. This is zonal suitability, not a stated tolerance.
flood.label: Not confirmed

submergence.basis: Only the same ResearchGate review, which places RB-50 in a category grouping and states no direct submergence evidence. This is a category listing only.
submergence.label: Not confirmed

stress_confirmation_note: The only official text is a CSC deferral pending NBPGR accession, with no tolerance statement, and the institution and year are unverified in the record.

drought.details: RGN 229 is identified as a climate-resilient variety demonstrating tolerance to drought. Moisture stress is known to cause significant yield reduction in Indian mustard, with RGN 229 specifically listed among varieties with drought tolerance.

heat.details: RGN 229 exhibits heat (high temperature) tolerance. It is listed as a climate-resilient variety for heat tolerance and specifically showed thermo tolerance in trials conducted at Kanpur. Indian mustard often faces high temperature stress at the terminal stage, and RGN 229 has been evaluated for its thermal requirements and heat use efficiency.

salinity.details: RGN 229 is identified as a climate-resilient variety with tolerance to salinity.

drought.details: Rainfed, timely-sown trial: seed yield fell by about 22.0% under stress, water loss was 4.2%, and harvest index fell 9.7%. The Drought Susceptibility Index (DSI) was 0.92, versus 1.21 for the check PM 25 (a lower DSI than the check indicates relatively better drought tolerance). The rating is medium because the evidence comes from a single trial reported in one paper (with the same figures repeated in a ResearchGate copy), and a 22% yield loss under stress is still substantial. The DAC source describes the variety as suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: White rust: severity low and decreasing across seasons. Alternaria leaf blight: moderate resistance, with 31.8% severity on leaves and 20.2% on pods (pods better than the check Rohini at 23.7%). Sclerotinia stem rot: moderate susceptibility, with severity falling from 34.0% (2015-16) to 26.8% (2017-18). Resistance to other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Aphid: infestation index improved from 2.93 (2015-16) to 1.19 (2017-18), indicating reduced infestation over seasons. Other pests: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Recommended yield potential 2500-2600 kg/ha (DAC source); oil content 40%. Front-line demonstrations (Rajasthan): 15.59 q/ha for RH-761 recommended practice versus 12.30 q/ha for farmer practice (26.74% increase). Hisar rainfed trial: RH 761 was outyielded by RH 725 (RH 725 at 2583 kg/ha); the RH 761 figure for that trial was not given.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for yield stability across environments. The drought DSI and the Hisar and Rajasthan trial results are the only environment-specific yield evidence. Fertility-level seed yield data exist in the ResearchGate paper's tables but were not legible in the retrieved text.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions (DAC source). Recommended states as listed in the original data: Jammu, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan. Heat, salinity, flood and submergence adaptation: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Flowers at 43-47 days and matures in 140-149 days; average 141 days, comparable to checks.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Large leaves; main shoot 82-93 cm; 58-68 siliquae per plant; 14-16 seeds per siliqua. Morphological characteristics beyond these: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Drought, rainfed timely-sown trial: seed yield fell about 22.0% under stress; water loss 4.2%; harvest index fell 9.7%; DSI 0.92 versus 1.21 for PM 25. (2) Front-line demonstrations, Rajasthan/extension study: RH-761 averaged 15.59 q/ha versus 12.30 q/ha for farmer practice (26.74% increase). (3) Rainfed date-of-sowing trial at Hisar, rabi 2018-19 and 2019-20: RH 761 was outyielded by RH 725 (2583 kg/ha). (4) Agronomy coordinated trial: fertility-level seed yield data exist but the figures were not legible in the retrieved text. (5) Disease and pest monitoring across seasons (2015-16 to 2017-18) is summarised under disease and pest resistance above.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources (no QTL, SNP or SSR marker studies found). Variety code A040317621 and parentage were not confirmed: the Seednet portal was not returned by any search, and the parentage field is not found in the sources.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. Breeding-value evidence: RH 761 showed significant general combining ability (GCA) for thousand-seed weight and oil content across environments (Hisar timely and late sown, New Delhi). Hybrid evidence: RH 761 hybrids showed high heterobeltiosis for seed weight in some crosses (for example, NPJ 161 x RH 761 at 16.19%).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. Metabolome evidence only: RH 761 and RH 725 differ in some leaf and stem metabolites (for example, malic acid is largely absent in RH 761 leaves). This describes metabolite differences and does not identify genes or pathways.
