search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RH 761 / RH-761 EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The release-minutes name "RH 761" and the Seednet name "RH-761" both appear in the sources, and the evidence below refers to the same variety under either spelling. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so nothing here confirms the Seednet record, variety code A040317621, or the parentage field.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought (rainfed, timely-sown trial): seed yield fell by about 22.0% under stress, water loss was 4.2%, harvest index fell 9.7%, and the Drought Susceptibility Index was 0.92, versus 1.21 for PM 25 -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production
Drought (same paper, ResearchGate copy): same DSI and yield-reduction figures reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned nothing on these for RH 761.

DISEASE AND PEST
White rust: severity is low and decreasing across seasons -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production
Alternaria leaf blight: moderate resistance, 31.8% severity on leaves and 20.2% on pods (pods better than the check Rohini at 23.7%) -- same URL
Sclerotinia stem rot: moderate susceptibility; severity fell from 34.0% (2015-16) to 26.8% (2017-18) -- same URL
Aphid: infestation index improved from 2.93 (2015-16) to 1.19 (2017-18) -- same URL
Other pests and resistance to other diseases: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Recommended yield potential 2500-2600 kg/ha, oil content 40%, release year 2019, suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx (retrieved through a Google Translate wrapper: https://translate.google.com/translate?u=https%3A%2F%2Foilseeds.dac.gov.in%2FRapeseed.aspx&hl=hi&sl=en&tl=hi&client=srp&prev=search)
Maturity: flowers at 43-47 days and matures in 140-149 days; average 141 days, comparable to checks -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production
Plant type: large leaves, main shoot 82-93 cm, 58-68 siliquae per plant, 14-16 seeds per siliqua -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Front-line demonstrations (Rajasthan/extension study): RH-761 recommended-practice demonstrations averaged 15.59 q/ha against 12.30 q/ha for farmer practice, a 26.74% increase -- https://indianecologicalsociety.com/wp-content/themes/ecology/volume_pdfs/1681611840.pdf
Rainfed date-of-sowing trial at Hisar, rabi 2018-19 and 2019-20: RH 761 was outyielded by RH 725 (RH 725 seed yield 2583 kg/ha) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5947
Agronomy coordinated trial: fertility-level seed yield data for RH 761 exist in the ResearchGate paper's tables, but the figures were not legible in the retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production

GENETICS AND QTL
Breeding value: RH 761 showed significant general combining ability for thousand-seed weight and oil content across environments (Hisar timely and late sown, New Delhi) -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405844024165863
Hybrid performance: RH 761 hybrids gave high heterobeltiosis for seed weight in some crosses (for example, NPJ 161 x RH 761 at 16.19%) -- same URL
Metabolome: RH 761 and RH 725 differ in some leaf and stem metabolites (for example, malic acid is largely absent in RH 761 leaves) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-69865-8
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Lead breeders (per the 2025 RH 761 paper): Ram Avtar, Dalip Kumar, Rakesh Punia, Neeraj Malik, Nisha Kumari, Anita Kumari, Rajbir Singh Khedwal and Mahavir Bishnoi, Oilseeds Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar -- https://www.agriculturaljournals.com/archives/2025.v7.i1.C.257/mustard-variety-rh-761-enhancing-biotic-and-abiotic-stress-resistance-for-superior-yield-and-stable-production and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388388594_Mustard_variety-RH_761_Enhancing_biotic_and_abiotic_stress_resistance_for_superior_yield_and_stable_production
Developing institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar; its achievements page lists RH 761 as a national-level release -- https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-32
Sole-breeder attribution: the sources name the oilseeds team as developers; a single named lead breeder was not confirmed.
Parentage: No evidence found.

stress_confirmation_note: The drought-induced PEG snippet reports that RH 761 showed greater root elongation reduction than RH 725, which sits uneasily with the claimed medium drought tolerance and should be reviewed.

drought.details: Two independent studies classed RH-749 as drought-sensitive. A greenhouse PGPR study ranked it the most drought-sensitive of four genotypes, behind RH-30, while RH-725 and RH-761 were more tolerant. A metabolomic study classed it as drought-sensitive relative to RH-725, with lower relative water content, chlorophyll and membrane stability under drought. Irrigation and anti-transpirant field trials (Bawal, 2017-18 and 2018-19) are not drought stress evidence and are not used to upgrade this rating.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance evidence was found for RH 0749. Only general Brassica juncea heat studies exist, which do not directly apply to this variety.

salinity.details: A single study reports that 100 mM NaCl applied for 20 days reduced chlorophyll content, net photosynthesis and stomatal conductance in RH-749 (listed as RH0-749). This documents a stress response but provides no comparative tolerance rating, so no tolerance level can be assigned.

flood.details: No evidence found for waterlogging or flood tolerance in RH 0749.

disease_resistance.summary: The Tribune report states the variety is resistant to major diseases but names no specific pathogens and gives no test data. The AICRP progeny trial used RH 0749 as a check for disease tolerance but reports no RH 0749 resistance scores. No specific disease resistance is confirmed for RH 0749 from the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data were found. An avoidable-loss study on RH 0749 and other Brassica crops reports an insect-related loss of about 11.79% for RH 0749, which indicates susceptibility to insect damage rather than resistance. A pollinator foraging study used RH-0749 as a test variety but reports no pest resistance data.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported average yield of about 20-21 q/ha (approximately 2000-2100 kg/ha) with oil content of 39-40%.
agronomic_details.stability: No evidence found on stability across environments. The variety was identified at the All-India Rapeseed-Mustard group meet at Mathura, as reported by the Tribune, but no multi-environment stability data were provided.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Identified for timely-sown irrigated conditions in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan (Zone 3, per the original variety data). The 2019-20 AICRP summary mentions RH 749 in Jammu and Kashmir under irrigated conditions, but the text is cut off and no result is available.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Long siliquae with bold seeds, as described by the Tribune report. No other morphological data were found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Irrigation and anti-transpirant trials (Bawal, 2017-18 and 2018-19) found RH-749 outperformed RH-725 on yield attributes and seed yield per plant. Used as a check in AICRP progeny row trials alongside RH 725 for seed yield and disease tolerance, with no result values reported for RH 0749. A 2019-20 AICRP summary mentions a Jammu and Kashmir irrigated trial without usable results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No evidence found specific to RH 0749. An AICRP report mentions SSR markers for 154 genotypes, but RH 0749 is not named.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found for QTLs associated with RH 0749.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No evidence found for specific genes or pathways in RH 0749. The drought and salinity studies describe physiological responses (relative water content, chlorophyll, membrane stability, photosynthesis, stomatal conductance) but do not identify genes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RH 0749 (Indian mustard, Brassica juncea; CCS HAU)

BREEDER/INSTITUTION: Developed by CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar; the Tribune reports the variety was identified at the All-India Rapeseed-Mustard group meet at Mathura -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/hau-s-mustard-variety-suitable-for-other-states-too-283071
BREEDER/INSTITUTION: HAU's achievements page lists RH 0749 as a national-level release -- https://hau.ac.in/page/achievements-32
RELEASE YEAR: The input gives 2018-01-20, but the sources found do not state a release date, so this is unverified -- No evidence found
RECOMMENDED STATES: Identified for timely-sown irrigated conditions in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/hau-s-mustard-variety-suitable-for-other-states-too-283071
YIELD: Reported average yield of about 20-21 q/ha and oil content of 39-40%; the source describes long siliquae with bold seeds and 125-135 day maturity -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/hau-s-mustard-variety-suitable-for-other-states-too-283071
YIELD/TRIALS: Used as a check in AICRP progeny row trials alongside RH 725 for seed yield and disease tolerance -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
YIELD/TRIALS: 2019-20 AICRP summary mentions RH 749 in Jammu and Kashmir under irrigated conditions, but the text is cut off so no result is available -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
YIELD/TRIALS: Irrigation and anti-transpirant field trial (2017-18, 2018-19, Bawal) found RH-749 outperformed RH-725 on yield attributes and seed yield per plant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368848480_Irrigation_levels_and_anti-transpirants_impact_on_performance_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea
DROUGHT: Greenhouse PGPR study ranked RH-749 as the most drought-sensitive of four genotypes, behind RH-30, while RH-725 and RH-761 were more tolerant -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00344-025-11887-1
DROUGHT: Metabolomic study classed RH-749 as drought-sensitive relative to RH-725, with lower relative water content, chlorophyll and membrane stability under drought -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12195340/
SALINITY: 100 mM NaCl for 20 days reduced chlorophyll content, net photosynthesis and stomatal conductance in RH-749 (listed as RH0-749) -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/85495
HEAT: No variety-specific heat tolerance evidence found for RH 0749 (only general B. juncea heat studies) -- No evidence found
FLOOD/SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found
DISEASE RESISTANCE: Tribune states the variety is resistant to major diseases, but names no specific pathogens or test data -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/hau-s-mustard-variety-suitable-for-other-states-too-283071
DISEASE RESISTANCE: AICRP trial evaluated progeny against RH 0749 as a check for disease tolerance, with no RH 0749 resistance scores reported -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
PEST RESISTANCE: Entomology study on pollinator foraging used RH-0749 as the test variety; no pest resistance data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353337529_Effect_of_pollination_modes_on_yield_components_in_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L
PEST RESISTANCE: Avoidable-loss study on RH 0749 and other Brassica crops reports an insect-related loss figure of about 11.79% for RH 0749 -- https://journals.ansfoundation.org/index.php/jans/article/download/3701/2326/10260
QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found specific to RH 0749 (an AICRP report mentions SSR markers for 154 genotypes, but RH 0749 is not named) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporations or KVK distribution of RH 0749
NOTE: Most sources are older, and the Tribune report is about 10 years old; check current notification status with CCS HAU or the Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research.

agronomic_details.yield: Rainfed trials averaged about 26 q/ha, reported as roughly 14% above RH 725. In a timely-sown trial, RH 1424 gave 26.13 q/ha versus 23.13 q/ha for RH 725, statistically at par. A seller listing gives 24-26 q/ha. Nitrogen at 100 kg/ha gave the highest seed yield in the timely-sown trial.

(3) Cultivar comparison of RH 1706, RH 1424, RH 725, RH 749 and Giriraj under sowing and INM treatments, rabi 2023-24 and 2024-25 (academia.edu source; results not summarised in the digest). (4) AICRP 2019-20 report lists RH 1424 among entries in the varietal trial programme (no yield data given in the digest). (5) Seller listing: 24-26 q/ha, 40.5% oil.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RH 1424 (mustard) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "RH 1424". The sources below refer to RH 1424 under that name. I found no Seednet portal page; the Seednet entry itself is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Sources describe RH 1424 as suited to timely sowing under rainfed conditions, not as a drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerant line -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- A seed-seller listing claims RH 1424 is tolerant to frost (pala); this is a commercial claim, not trial data -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- Sowing-date trial: delayed sowing reduced growth and yield in RH 1424, and canopy temperature rose with delay -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOB/article/view/166710
- No peer-reviewed or official stress-tolerance screening data found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to RH 1424 (searched within the variety and crop query; no hits).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed trials averaged about 26 q/ha, reported as roughly 14% above RH 725 -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- Maturity is about 139 days; seed oil content about 40.5% -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- Seller listing gives 24-26 q/ha, flowering at 45-55 days, 17-18 seeds per pod, bold seed, 40.5% oil -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- Timely-sown RH 1424 gave 26.13 q/ha, statistically at par with RH 725 (23.13 q/ha); N at 100 kg/ha gave the highest seed yield in that trial -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOB/article/view/166710
- Cultivar comparison (RH 1706, RH 1424, RH 725, RH 749, Giriraj) under sowing and INM treatments, rabi 2023-24 and 2024-25 -- https://www.academia.edu/172118309/Effect_of_Different_Cultivars_and_INM_on_Physiological_Growth_Indices_of_Indian_Mustard_Brassica_juncea_L
- AICRP 2019-20 report lists RH 1424 among entries in the varietal/trial programme -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage RH-202 x RH-401B comes from the input record only; no search source confirmed it.
- No QTL, marker or genetic-mapping study for RH 1424 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university-has-developed-two-improved-varieties-of-mustard
- Announced on 17 August 2022 by the university's oilseed team; the input's release date of 26 Oct 2022 is not confirmed by any source -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/hr/updates-detaills/two-new-improved-mustard-varieties-have-been-introduced-by-ccs-hau-hisar/1173
- Identified for cultivation at the AICRP (Mustard) meeting at RARI, Durgapur (Rajasthan) -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university-has-developed-two-improved-varieties-of-mustard
- Scientists named as developers of the RH 1424/RH 1706 pair (mustard team): Dr. Ram Avtar, Dr. Neeraj, Dr. Manjeet and Dr. Ashok Kumar (lead team); with Dr. Rakesh Poonia, Dr. Nisha Kumari, Dr. Vinod Goyal, Dr. Mahavir and Dr. Rajbir Singh -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/haryana-agricultural-university-developed-another-new-mustard-variety-rh1975 and https://www.farmingcosmos.com/hau-develops-new-mustard-variety-rh-1975-for-higher-yield-oil-content/
- Officials quoted at release: Vice Chancellor Prof. B.R. Kamboj; Director of Research Dr. Jeetram Sharma -- https://www.amarujala.com/haryana/hisar/haryana-agriculture-university-develops-rh-1424-and-rh-1706-varieties-of-mustard
- Station: Hisar (oilseed section); a specific station name was not found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contacts: no email, phone or address found for Dr. Ram Avtar, Dr. Neeraj, Dr. Manjeet, Dr. Ashok Kumar or others.
- Institute contacts: no official CCS HAU email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL found in the searches.
- Seed-dealer listing (not an institute contact): phone +91 8224917065, email mykisanagro@gmail.com -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- Action: check the CCS HAU Hisar oilseeds/mustard research division site and the AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard directorate page for official contacts.

PUBLICATIONS
- Keerthi, P., Neelam, Ram Avatar & Bhaskar, P. (year not shown in source). Optimizing yield and physiological performance of Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L.) varieties through sowing dates and nitrogen management. Journal of Oilseeds Research(?) (journal name truncated in source) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOB/article/view/166710
- Authors not confirmed (2026). Effect of Different Cultivars and INM on Physiological Growth Indices of Indian Mustard (Brassica juncea L.). Journal of Advances in Biology & Biotechnology -- DOI 10.9734/JABB/2026/V29I94313 (https://doi.org/10.9734/JABB/2026/V29I94313); the source shows RH 1424 as one of five cultivars.
- AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard Annual Report 2019-20 (Varietal Improvement, Crop Production) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, ICAR annual report entry specific to RH 1424 beyond the above, or QTL paper found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- IFFDC lists certified and TL seed of RH-1424 among mustard varieties available -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed
- NSC (Bharatpur) listing of RH-1424 T/L seed, 1 kg pouch -- https://www.mystore.in/en/product/nsc-farm-sona-mustard-rh-725-t-l (product suggestion list)
- Private dealer listing at about ₹450 per 1 kg pack -- https://www.mkdseeds.com/RH%201424%20Mustard%20seeds
- No SAU/KVK or Seednet availability record found; state seed corporation stock not verified.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Haryana, Punjab, Delhi, North Rajasthan and Jammu, identified at the AICRP Mustard meeting -- https://www.drishtiias.com/state-pcs-current-affairs/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university-has-developed-two-improved-varieties-of-mustard
- The input lists "Jammu, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and northern Rajasthan"; this matches the sources.

Not yet verified: release notification number, Seednet listing, official HAU release notice.

Seednet portal pages themselves were not returned, so the seednet crop label "Indian rapeseed and mustard (yellow sarson)" is not confirmed by a search hit. The PAU page's "canola-quality Indian mustard" description conflicts with the crop label "yellow sarson" in the Seednet record, since yellow sarson is normally Brassica rapa; the evidence points to Brassica juncea.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RGN-303 (mustard)

Scope note: Four searches were run. A fifth call to pull the full text of the Bikaner station PDF hit the tool's usage limit, so the findings below come from search snippets only. Several headings have little or no evidence. Name note: the CSC name is RGN-303 and the Seednet name is RNG-303. Every search used RGN-303, and no result mentioned RNG-303, so all evidence below refers to RGN-303.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found in the captured snippets. The snippets did not describe drought, heat, salinity, or other stress reactions for RGN-303.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found specific to RGN-303. A ResearchGate paper on Alternaria blight management in rapeseed-mustard mentions evaluating genotypes, but the snippet does not name RGN-303, so I am not attributing it to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/257076397_Management_of_alternaria_blight_of_rapeseed-mustard

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Agriculture Research Station, Bikaner "at a glance" profile lists "RGN-303 (2014)" under mustard. Its snippet also mentions a fertilizer recommendation for the variety (half-dose fertilizer with vermicompost for mustard), but the snippet does not give the yield or maturity figures. -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Bikaner Agriculture Research Station profile lists RGN-303 among mustard varieties, and the station also lists an AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard project. No breeder name was found in the captured snippets. The record's institution is "Agriculture Research Station, S. K. Rajasthan Agricultural University." -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. No email, phone, or postal address for the Bikaner station was captured in the snippets. The station profile PDF is the only institute source located, and it should be opened directly to retrieve the station's address and contact information.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or thesis specific to RGN-303 was identified. Not verified: the ResearchGate Alternaria paper above, which is not confirmed to involve RGN-303.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No seller, NSC, state corporation, or KVK listing was found. The Bikaner station profile mentions breeder seed production for mustard, but the snippet does not say RGN-303 seed is currently available. -- https://raubikaner.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/ARS-at-a-glance-17.08.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No state recommendation list was captured from the search results. The record lists Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Jammu and Kashmir, and Uttar Pradesh, but I could not verify these against a source.

Discrepancies to resolve:
- The release year is 2015 in the CSC record, but the Bikaner profile lists RGN-303 as 2014.
- The Seednet name RNG-303 has not been verified on any page.

Suggested next steps: open the Bikaner ARS PDF in full, check seednet.gov.in for RNG-303, and search KrishiKosh and the AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard annual reports for RGN-303 trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to Sushree. A 2022 climate-resilient varieties newsletter lists Sushree among climate-resilient varieties, but the snippet gives no stress-specific data -- https://justagriculture.in/files/newsletter/2022/december/16.%20Climate%20Resilient%20Varieties%20and%20Genetic%20Stocks%20in.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches for disease or pest reaction of Sushree returned no page naming this variety with a resistance or susceptibility rating.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
On-farm participatory trial, rabi 2014-15, Bauligarh village, Angul district, mid-central table land zone of Odisha: Sushree gave 12.64 q/ha seed yield, about 45% above the local check Rai shoriso; plant height 153.78 cm; 173.19 siliquae/plant; 1000-seed weight 4.29 g; harvest index 22.98%; additional net return Rs 11,006.61/ha, benefit-cost ratio 1.80 -- https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
Same study, abstract summary page -- https://www.academia.edu/99448667/On_farm_assessment_of_toria_Brassica_campestris_L_variety_Sushree_under_mid_central_table_land_zone_of_Odisha
OUAT AICRP Rapeseed-Mustard centre (Ranital) reports Sushree as a released toria variety and the only one of its three released toria varieties still in the seed chain -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Sushree listed among varieties in a DRMR breeding table as a parent in fresh crosses (Tapeswari x Sushree) -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Sushree mentioned in a DRMR AICRP summary with a low seed quantity note; no yield or agronomy data in the snippet -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Sushree is described as a mutant of TS-29 (designation ORT(m)-7-2) -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
No QTL or marker study naming Sushree was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Odisha University of Agriculture & Technology (OUAT), via its AICRP on Rapeseed-Mustard, Ranital -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No page named a breeder for Sushree.
Release date conflict: the OUAT page says Sushree was released in 2012, while the CSC record gives 2014-10-20. Both are recorded here; the evidence does not resolve the difference -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.
Institute-level contact: No email, phone, or postal address for OUAT or its Ranital AICRP centre was found in the results. The only institute reference is the OUAT AICRP page -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Name tested: the evidence refers to "Sushree" for both variety_name and seednet_variety_name, since no separate Seednet name was found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not identified in the results (2015). On farm assessment of toria (Brassica campestris L.) variety Sushree under mid central table land zone of Odisha. International Journal of Applied Research -- https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
Authors not identified (year not stated in result). On farm assessment of toria (Brassica campestris L.) variety Sushree under mid central table land zone of Odisha. Academia.edu record of the same study -- https://www.academia.edu/99448667/On_farm_assessment_of_toria_Brassica_campestris_L_variety_Sushree_under_mid_central_table_land_zone_of_Odisha
Authors not identified (2020). Indian Society of Oilseeds Research executive council report 2018-2020, mentioning Sushree in the toria seed-chain context. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344426080_THE_INDIAN_SOCIETY_OF_OILSEEDS_RESEARCH_EXECUTIVE_COUNCIL_FOR_2018-2020
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), or AICRP annual report specifically on Sushree was found in the results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Sushree is in the seed chain per the OUAT AICRP page -- https://ouat.ac.in/aicrps/34-aicrp-on-rapeseed-mustard-ranital/
Seed-chain analysis lists Sushree among predominant toria varieties, contributing roughly 9.3%-40.6% in the cited seed-chain data (the range is across the listed varieties) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344668328_Analysis_of_seed_chain_and_its_implication_in_rapeseed-mustard_Brassica_spp_production_in_India
A private seed company product list includes SUSHREE among toria varieties. This is a commercial listing, not an NSC, state corporation, or SAU record -- https://www.indiaseeds.com/products.html
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or OUAT seed-sales listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Evidence is limited to Odisha's mid-central table land zone, from the on-farm trial above -- https://www.allresearchjournal.com/archives/2015/vol1issue9/PartB/1-8-120-423.pdf
No official notification or recommended-state list from the CSC or Seednet was found for this variety.

basic_info.institution: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV), (West Bengal) and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to TBM-143 in the searched sources. No mechanisms or tolerance rating were reported.

heat.details: A Zenodo study on salicylic acid and Indian mustard under terminal heat-stress conditions names TBM-143 as a studied genotype. The retrieved text reports only treatment effects on seed yield (seed yield was highest with 400 ppm salicylic acid under timely sowing), not TBM-143's heat tolerance level. No heat tolerance rating or mechanism was found.

salinity.details: The coastal trials at Kakdwip (a saline-zone station, BCKV Regional Research Station, Coastal Saline Zone) included TBM 143, but no salinity tolerance rating was reported. Yield performance in the coastal zone is recorded under agronomic_performance, not as a salinity tolerance result.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to TBM-143 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance evidence found for TBM-143 (searches for Alternaria blight, white rust, Sclerotinia and other diseases returned no record). Disease reaction field in the variety record: Not Specified.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistance to Plutella xylostella (diamondback moth): a reference cited in a ResearchGate paper on TBM-204 reports TBM 143 as superior in growth, yield components and seed yield, and as resistant to P. xylostella. This is secondhand. The retrieved text does not give the full Banerjee et al. (2023) citation, and the finding is not verified against a primary source. It is the only pest-related evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: BCKV crop variety listing: seed yield of 14.0 q/ha (equivalent to 1,400 kg/ha). Coastal trial (Kakdwip, 2015-16): 1.80 t/ha, under a caveat that the 'TM 143' alias is unconfirmed. Coastal study (Kakdwip, 2018-2020): 1.29 t/ha. The variety record field 'average_yield' is given only as 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Only single-site coastal results (Kakdwip) and one multi-location BARC-BCKV trial, judged promising without reported stability statistics, were retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Coastal West Bengal (Kakdwip, Coastal Saline Zone) late-sown after paddy (early December sowing) in the 2015-16 trial, and the 2018-2020 coastal study. The digest recommends 150% RDF fertilizer for the coastal belt. Broader agro-climatic adaptation for West Bengal is not otherwise specified.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 152 cm; appressed two-chambered siliqua; yellow seed coat; bold seed; oil content 41.3% (BCKV crop variety listing). Coastal trial also reports highest test weight and seeds per siliqua for 'TM 143' (alias unconfirmed).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) BCKV crop variety listing: duration 104 days, plant height 152 cm, seed yield 14.0 q/ha, oil content 41.3%. (2) Coastal West Bengal, Kakdwip (BCKV Regional Research Station), 2015-16, late-sown after paddy: 'TM 143' gave the highest seed yield (1.80 t/ha) among eight cultivars, statistically at par with TM 204, and the highest test weight and seeds per siliqua. The page does not confirm that 'TM 143' is identical to TBM-143. (3) Kakdwip coastal study, 2018-2020: TBM 143 and Kranti were the top yielders at 1.29 and 1.28 t/ha respectively. (4) BARC-BCKV multi-location yield trial of Trombay Mustard in West Bengal: TM-204 and TM-143 judged promising; a release proposal was sent to the SVRC. (5) Terminal heat-stress study (salicylic acid, three sowing dates): TBM-143 included as a genotype; no tolerance rating reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under terminal heat-stress conditions, a Zenodo study on salicylic acid and Indian mustard names TBM-143 as a studied genotype, but the retrieved text reports only treatment effects on seed yield, not TBM-143's tolerance level. -- https://zenodo.org/records/18681400 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.18681400)
- TBM 143 was reported as superior in growth, yield components and seed yield, and as resistant to the insect pest P. xylostella, in a reference cited in a ResearchGate paper on TBM-204. The retrieved text does not give the full Banerjee et al. (2023) citation, so this is secondhand. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No evidence found for drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to TBM-143. The coastal trials at Kakdwip (a saline-zone station) included TBM 143, but no salinity tolerance rating was reported. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602

DISEASE AND PEST
- The P. xylostella (diamondback moth) resistance finding above is the only pest-related evidence found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- No evidence found for disease resistance (e.g., Alternaria blight, white rust, Sclerotinia) specific to TBM-143. Searches returned no such record.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- BCKV's crop variety listing gives TBM 143 a duration of 104 days, plant height of 152 cm, appressed two-chambered siliqua, yellow seed coat, bold seed, seed yield of 14.0 q/ha and oil content of 41.3%. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Coastal West Bengal (Kakdwip, BCKV Regional Research Station, Coastal Saline Zone), 2015-16 trial: TM 143 gave the highest seed yield (1.80 t/ha) among eight cultivars, statistically at par with TM 204, under a late-sown (early December) schedule after paddy. The text also states TM 143 gave the highest test weight and seeds per siliqua. "TM 143" is a BARC gamma-mutant designation; the page does not state it is identical to TBM-143, so this is a likely alias to be confirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332653138_Selection_of_Rapeseed-mustard_Varieties_in_Coastal_Region_of_West_Bengal_A_Way_Forward_to_Rice-fallow_Intensification
- A 2018-2020 coastal study (Kakdwip) found TBM 143 and Kranti as the top yielders, at 1.29 and 1.28 t/ha respectively. The study recommends 150% RDF fertilizer for the coastal belt. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- BARC-BCKV multi-location yield trial of Trombay Mustard in West Bengal: TM-204 and TM-143 were judged promising, and a proposal was sent to the SVRC for release. -- https://bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/barc-bckv-programme-en
- Terminal heat stress: TBM-143 was used with salicylic acid treatments under three sowing dates; the paper reports seed yield was highest with 400 ppm under timely sowing. -- https://zenodo.org/records/18681400

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker, parentage or mutagenesis-lineage record specifically for TBM-143 was retrieved. The parentage field in the record is "Not specified", and the search did not resolve it. The BARC bulletin on Trombay crop varieties describes mutation and recombination breeding in general terms only. -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institutions for TBM-143, per the BCKV listing: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV) with a BARC project, and the Department of Seed Science and Technology. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- BARC's Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division (NA&BTD) runs the Trombay crop-variety programme; mustard is one of its 12 crops. The bulletin does not name TBM-143 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name for TBM-143 was found. Names appearing in TBM-204 literature (e.g., Dutta, A.; Rai, A.N.) belong to a different variety's paper and are not attributed here. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only (no breeder contact found): Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252. Phone and email not found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Institute-level only: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Trombay, Mumbai 400085, Maharashtra (postal code written with spaces in the source, "4 00 08 5"). Phone and email not found in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344217293_Trombay_Bidhan_Mustard-204_TBM-204_A_high_yielding_yellow_seed_coat_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_variety_notified_for_West_Bengal
- BARC Director named in press coverage: Vivek Bhasin (institute head, not a breeder for this variety). -- https://www.deccanherald.com/india/maharashtra/barc-dedicates-8-new-trombay-crop-varieties-to-farmers-3308421
- No official email, phone, or contact page for the BCKV or BARC division was retrieved. -- (no URL)

PUBLICATIONS
- Dutta, A., Jambulkar, S.J., Rai, A.N., Bhujbal, S., Banerjee, H., Das, R., Dewanjee, S., Sarkar, S., Pramanik, M., and Mandal, S. (2019). Varietal and Fertilization Effects on Growth and Yield of Mustard under Coastal Environment. JISCAR (ICAR e-Journals) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JISCAR/article/view/137602
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not confirmed). Selection of Rapeseed-mustard Varieties in Coastal Region of West Bengal: A Way Forward to Rice-fallow Intensification. Journal not confirmed; BCKV Kakdwip trial 2015-16 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332653138_Selection_of_Rapeseed-mustard_Varieties_in_Coastal_Region_of_West_Bengal_A_Way_Forward

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches for "TSH 387 cotton variety" (seednet name TS-38, SVPR-7) returned no page about this cotton variety. Results were unrelated US patents, a Texas trial table, and craft or game items.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The variety-name search returned no pest or disease data for TSH 387. The only Srivilliputtur cotton pest note retrieved concerned cotton hybrid SVPR 1 (moderately resistant to jassid), which is a different variety and is discarded. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No trial, yield, or maturity record for TSH 387 was retrieved. The Srivilliputtur station table retrieved lists other releases (SVPR 1 hybrid, 1991 SVPR 1 entry). Those rows are not TSH 387 and are discarded. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree, or marker study for TSH 387 was retrieved. The parentage field is "Not specified" in the record and remains unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for TSH 387. The search confirmed only that Cotton Research Station, Srivilliputtur (TNAU) is the releasing centre for other cotton varieties, such as SVPR 4 and SVPR 6 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/. No breeder name was linked to TSH 387.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The retrieved text from the station's variety-release page contains no email, phone, or postal address. The station page is the only institute-level URL retrieved: https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-srivilliputhur/varieties-released/

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming TSH 387 was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. For the seednet name TS-38 under the crop heading "Indian Rapeseed and Mustard (Yellow Sarson)", the search returned a news item about a toria rapeseed variety TS-38 from Assam Agricultural University. This is a different crop and institution, so it is discarded -- https://ajmaliasacademy.in/ts-38-climate-resilient-rapeseed-variety/. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for TSH 387 or cotton TS-38 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The states listed in the record (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu) could not be confirmed from any retrieved page.

Notes on what was discarded:
- Seednet name TS-38: the only hit is a rapeseed variety from Assam, so it is not this cotton variety.
- Variety name TSH 387: the hits are unrelated (a Texas trial table, a crochet pattern, US patents).
- SVPR 4 papers (Ramalingam et al., MASU journal, 1999; ResearchGate record) and SVPR 6 (Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding): these name other Srivilliputtur cotton varieties, so they are not evidence for TSH 387.
- Kaderbad Ravindranath and Rajagopalan Krishnamurthy (Wikipedia): these breeders are not linked to TSH 387 in the retrieved text.

Absolute yield (kg/ha) for Tapeshwari: Not found in searched sources. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Tapeshwari (variety_name) / Tapeshwari. (seednet_variety_name), toria, TK 06-1

Name note: all four searches used "Tapeshwari." Sources spell it "Tapeshwari", "Tapeswari", "Tapeshvari" and "Tapeswari (LC)", and the seednet name with the trailing period did not match any source. Every finding below refers to this same variety unless a line says otherwise. Note the release date conflict: CSC minutes give 2014-02-14, the AICRP table lists 2014, and the CSAUA&T page gives a 2018 notification (S.O. 6318E).

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tapeswari (LC) is one of several toria genotypes listed as promising on the AAII ≤1.5 criterion in a moisture-stress trial, but the source does not state the tolerance mechanism for this variety specifically. GSH 1717, GSH 1699, GSH 6 (QC), Tapeswari (LC), BSH-1, Kranti (NC), RGN 73(LR), GSL 1 (ZC) were found promising since these recorded AAII ≤1.5. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
Heat: toria germplasm was screened for thermo-tolerance at early and terminal stages, but no Tapeshwari-specific heat result was found. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found for Tapeshwari. The salinity study on B. rapa var. toria (BRSRT) is a different genotype. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322264501_Effect_of_salinity_on_Brassica_rapa_var_toria_BRSRT_under_selenium_defence_A_trial_to_assess_the_protective_role_of_selenium

DISEASE AND PEST
White rust (WR): In a multi-location screen of Brassica entries, the B. rapa toria and yellow sarson entries largely escaped WR infection. This is a group-level finding; Tapeshwari is not named individually. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
Other diseases and pests (Alternaria, insects, lodging): No evidence found for Tapeshwari.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and sowing: Tapeshwari is described as suited to early sowing (15-20 Sept) with extra-early maturity of 88-90 days, medium brown grain, and suitability for irrigated conditions in all ecological zones. -- https://csauk.ac.in/some-university-developed-varieties/
Yield vs check: At Kanpur, toria strains yielded up to 17.18% above the check Tapeshwari (56 strains tested at Kanpur, Chatha, Ludhiana and Dholi). -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/PC-REPORT-2020-DRMR.pdf
Yield vs check (2025 round): The yield superiority in toria station trial was up to 22.07 over the check (Tapeshwari) at Pantnagar. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2025/AICRP-Proceeding-2025.pdf
Absolute yield (kg/ha) for Tapeshwari: No evidence found. The Kanpur PYT table lists a 1350 kg/ha benchmark next to Tapeshwari, but the layout does not show which entry the figure belongs to. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Seed production: 258.64 q breeder seed was produced against an indent of 76.02 q, but less Tapeshwari seed was produced than indented. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
Agronomy-specific trials for Tapeshwari (sowing date, N, spacing): No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: Tapeshwari is used as a parent in crosses including Tapeswari x Sushree, Parbati x Tapeswari and Bhawani x Tapeswari. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
Population improvement: Tapeshwari is listed among toria parents used in population improvement and in RIL/composite programmes. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf
QTL, marker or genomic studies: No evidence found for Tapeshwari.
Parentage as released: Not specified (no source gives the original cross).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture and Technology (CSAUA&T), Kanpur, UP. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
Notification: Tapeshwari (T.K. 06-1) was notified (S.O. 6318E) by the central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards at its meeting on 26 December 2018 in New Delhi. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
Breeder names: The CSAUA&T Oil Seeds Section page lists "Mahak Singh, Ranjeet, R.K. Dixit and S.B.L. Srivastav" next to the Tapeshwari entry. The layout does not label them explicitly as breeders, so treat this as unconfirmed. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
Station: Kanpur (CSAUA&T campus), per the AICRP trial centre list. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/PC-REPORT-2020-DRMR.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder contact: No evidence found.
Institute contact: No email, phone or postal address for CSAUA&T was found in the results. The only institute URL found is https://www.csauk.ac.in (Wikipedia gives the same website and Kanpur as location). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chandra_Shekhar_Azad_University_of_Agriculture_and_Technology
Project Coordinator (DRMR, AICRP-RM) contact: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard (2020). Project Coordinator's Report 2019-20, Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR). Authors not stated. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Basundhara (CSC name) / VASUNDHARA (Seednet name), rice, AAU Jorhat**

**Search note:** Four web searches were run, one per topic. None returned a Seednet page, so no Seednet record for VASUNDHARA was found. The Seednet entry is listed under yellow sarson (rapeseed/mustard), which is a different crop. Every rice finding below refers to "Basundhara" as a rice variety. Findings about Basundhara Seeds (Kolkata), a seed company with a similar name, were discarded.

**Conflicts in the record:**
- Release year: the user input says 2014-10-20. Retrieved sources say 1996 (Basundhara, IET 9711/IET 11161, release 1996, 130 days, transplanted sali in multiple cropping areas) and 1999 (the AAU compilation, which pairs Satyaranjan and Basundhara under one release year).
- Parentage: the user input says RH 839 x RH 30. The AAU compilation gives IET 9711 X IET 11161 (Basundhara). The user's parentage was not confirmed by any retrieved source.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- The "Hundred years of rice research in Assam" table describes Basundhara as photoperiod insensitive, multiple resistant, fine grained, suitable for sali in areas where sali is followed by rabi crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- The same source lists Basundhara among varieties that perform well under low land situations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- Flood and submergence tolerance: the AAU compilation has a flood-tolerance block that may refer to Basundhara, but the snippet does not clearly attach it to this variety, so it is not counted as evidence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Drought tolerance: No evidence found for Basundhara. The AAU stress-tolerant page covers other varieties only -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Pest and disease: multiple resistant is the only general statement retrieved, with no named pathogens or resistance genes -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- A Basundhara-specific disease-management table in the same source recommends it for double-cropped areas, but it does not name a specific disease -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- The Assam kharif package of practices (AAU and Department of Agriculture, Assam, 2015) lists Basundhara in a duration/yield table. The column headers are not legible in the retrieved text, so the figures cannot be assigned with confidence -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
- Season and land: the AAU compilation places Basundhara in the sali group for double-cropped areas, where sali rice is followed by rabi crops -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Yield: No Basundhara-specific yield figure was confirmed. The yield values in the retrieved compilation sit in blocks for other varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: IET 9711 X IET 11161 (Basundhara) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University (conflicts with the user's RH 839 x RH 30)
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found for Basundhara. Searches for Basundhara QTL and marker studies returned only Basmati and Joha work, which was discarded.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Institution: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar, Jorhat, which is the AAU rice station that compiled the variety list -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Named scientists: The compilation is authored by Dr. Safiqul Hussain, Ms. Pompi Dutta and Chetia, S. K. (2023) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University. No source states that any of them bred Basundhara, so this is not attributed as a breeder finding.
- Lead breeder for Basundhara: No evidence found.

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- AAU (institute-level): Assam Agricultural University, Jorhat, PIN 785013, Assam; phone 0376-2340001; email webadmin@aau.ac.in -- https://www.rkbassam.aau.ac.in/contact-us and https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/stress-tolerant-rice-varieties
- Rice research station contact (RCSKB): 5th Floor, Nayantara Building, Six Mile, Guwahati-22, Assam; email rkbassam2021@gmail.com -- https://www.rkbassam.aau.ac.in/contact-us
- Titabar station address: AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar-785630, Jorhat, Assam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Named breeder contact: No evidence found.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Hussain, S.; Dutta, P.; Chetia, S. K. (2023). Rice varieties developed by Assam Agricultural University. AAU-Assam Rice Research Institute, Titabar; SM Press, Jorhat; ISBN 978-81-962645-1-2 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Hundred years of rice research in Assam. Journal/report not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393846178_Hundred_years_of_rice_research_in_Assam
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Basundhara was found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No evidence found. The only "Basundhara Seeds" listing is a Kolkata wholesale seller of unspecified rice seed, not linked to this variety -- https://m.indiamart.com/basundhara-seeds
- AAU seed sources, NSC, state seed corporation, and KVK listings for Basundhara were not retrieved. Seed-source details on the AAU stress page apply to other varieties.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Assam: Basundhara appears in the Assam kharif (sali) package of practices. The "recommended states" field in the user record is blank -- https://diragri.assam.gov.in/sites/default/files/swf_utility_folder/departments/diragri_medhassu_in_oid_4/portlet/level_2/11(A).2.pdf
- Basundhara also appears in the AAU list of sali rice varieties for multiple-cropping areas, but no other state recommendation was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378393499_Rice_Varieties_Developed_by_Assam_Agricultural_University

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VAMSADHARA / VASUNDHARA

Name check: "VAMSADHARA" (CSC minutes name) and "VASUNDHARA" (Seednet name) refer to different entries in the evidence. Under each heading I state which name the evidence refers to.

RECORD CONFLICTS (read first)
- The variety_code RGL 11414 and the name VAMSADHARA appear together in a rice notification list, not in a mustard or yellow sarson context. The record lists crop as rice but seednet_crop_name as yellow sarson, and the institution as CCS HAU Oilseeds Section. The "RH" prefix in the parentage matches Hisar mustard naming, but I found no source linking RGL 11414 to CCS HAU. Treat the institution and parentage fields as unverified.
- No source I found ties VASUNDHARA to yellow sarson. The only VASUNDHARA variety entry in the PPV&FRA compendium is a maize hybrid, Vasundhara (DH-101). Vasundhara Agro is a commercial spice and grain trader with no link to breeding.

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
- VAMSADHARA (rice): No evidence found for stress or disease traits. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No evidence found. The only stress information located was general rapeseed-mustard recommendations by stress type, which do not name this variety. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/75542

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- VAMSADHARA (rice): No evidence found for yield, maturity or trial results.
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No evidence found. A 2019-20 AICRP report mentions yellow sarson strain trials at Kanpur and Dholi, with yield superiority up to 16.66% over the check Pitambari, but it does not name Vasundhara. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/2.pdf
- An HAU yellow sarson entry, YSH 0401 (2009), appears in an AICRP-related table. It is a different variety from Vasundhara. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2020/5a.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- VAMSADHARA: No evidence found for markers or QTL.
- VASUNDHARA: No evidence found. Related context only (not about this variety): a fine-mapping study of a seed coat colour QTL in Brassica rapa var. Yellow Sarson. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6361427/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- VAMSADHARA (rice): The 2011 notification list records it as RGL 11414, notified under S.O. 283(E) dated 07.02.2011, for AP. No breeder or institution is named. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No breeder name found. The CCS HAU Oilseeds Section is confirmed only as a university; no yellow sarson release by that section was found under this name. -- https://hau.ac.in/
- Note: the ICAR Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (Bharatpur) says it has released one yellow sarson variety, NRCYS 05-02, which is not Vasundhara. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/rm_varieties.php

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar (no breeder contact found; no email or phone found for the Oilseeds Section): website https://hau.ac.in/ ; HAU is located at Hisar, Haryana. -- https://hau.ac.in/
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (formerly DRMR), postal address: Sewar, Bharatpur 321303 (Rajasthan), India. No email or phone was in the retrieved text. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/rm_varieties.php
- Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- VAMSADHARA: No evidence found.
- VASUNDHARA: No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was retrieved. KrishiKosh was not searched directly; this search covered only the general web.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- VAMSADHARA: No evidence found for seed sellers. The notified status is for AP, so check AP seed channels (not searched).
- VASUNDHARA (yellow sarson): No evidence found for variety seed. HAU's RDS Seed Farm sales page lists Kharif crops (guar, moong, dhaincha) and Rabi crops (raya, barley, gram, wheat, oats), with no yellow sarson. Sales counters are at Gate No. 3 (Balsamand Road) and ATIC at Gate No. 4 (Rajgarh Road). -- https://hau.ac.in/page/seed-sale-information
- Commercial listing, grain only, not verified seed of this variety: National Seeds Corporation Limited, Hisar (C/o CSF Farm, Sirsa Road) appears in an IndiaMART yellow mustard seed listing. -- https://dir.indiamart.com/hisar/yellow-mustard-seed.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- VAMSADHARA: Andhra Pradesh (AP), per the 2011 notification list. This contradicts the record field "Not specified." -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-rice-varieties-in-india-during-2011-to-2021/
- VASUNDHARA: No evidence found.

drought.details: Resistant to drought stress.

heat.details: Tolerant to terminal heat stress. Used as a National Check in studies evaluating heat tolerance in Indian mustard, suggesting inherent heat tolerance.

salinity.details: Information on salinity tolerance for YSH 0401 is not specified in the provided search results.

flood.details: General information about rapeseed/mustard not tolerating waterlogging was found, but specific tolerance for YSH 0401 is not specified.

drought.details: While specific drought tolerance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not detailed, the crop 'tinda' (round gourd) generally exhibits some drought tolerance. Another tinda variety, Hisar Tinda (HT 10), is resistant to drought stress. Abiotic stress, including drought, is a significant challenge in Indian agriculture.

heat.details: Round gourd (tinda) is known as a warm season crop. There is a general demand for stress tolerance against heat in cucurbit crops. However, specific heat tolerance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not mentioned.

salinity.details: General round gourd (tinda) is indicated to be salt-tolerant, growing well in well-drained soils with a pH of 5.5-7.0. Another variety, Hisar Tinda (HT 10), is explicitly tolerant to salt. Specific salinity tolerance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not available.

flood.details: Water stress includes flooding or waterlogging situations. No specific flood tolerance details are provided for Punjab Tinda-1 or the general tinda crop in the context of field resilience.

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for Punjab Tinda-1 is not specified. However, for other tinda varieties, Hisar Tinda (HT 10) is reported to be resistant to all rusts. General strategies for managing viral diseases in round gourd include mulching, and there is a recognized need to grow resistant varieties in cucurbits.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance is mentioned for Punjab Tinda-1. Melon fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) is a major pest of cucurbitaceous vegetables.

agronomic_details.yield: Punjab Tinda-1 is described as an early bearing new variety. While a specific quantitative yield for Punjab Tinda-1 is not provided, the recommended seed rate for this variety is 1.2 kg, compared to 1.5 kg for Tinda 48. Mulching can increase early and total fruit yield in round gourd.
agronomic_details.stability: No specific information on yield stability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The variety is recommended for cultivation in Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Jharkhand. Indian round gourd landraces are found in Western Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, and Punjab. The origin of round melon is likely western India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: While specific morphological characteristics for Punjab Tinda-1 are not detailed, it is noted as an 'early bearing' variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), the institution that developed this variety, is actively involved in teaching, research, and extension education, including organizing Kisan Melas, indicating ongoing research and field evaluation of varieties.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GPUF 3 -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "GPUF 3". The evidence found uses "GPUF 3" and, in one place, "GPUF-3". I did not reach a Seednet portal page, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found on a formal drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence rating for GPUF 3. One study on PEG-induced seedling growth of dry and hydroprimed GPUF-3 seed was located, but its page title is about foxtail millet supplementation in diabetics, so the link between that page and the seedling study is unverified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287753024_Effect_of_foxtail_millet_setaria_italica_supplementation_on_serum_glucose_serum_lipids_and_glycosylated_hemoglobin_in_type_2_diabetics

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found on disease or pest resistance for GPUF 3.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Station trials averaged 29.89 q/ha, multilocation trials 26.33 q/ha, and farm trials 15.16 q/ha, with a mean of 23.79 q/ha across all trials, about 19.12% above check SiA 3156. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
All-India Coordinated trials yielded 2753 kg/ha across locations, ranking 11th. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
Farm trials in Zone 5 and Zone 6 were run during Kharif 2020. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
Maturity is 85-90 days. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Molecular-profile-of-proposed-variety-GPUF-3-and-check-variety-SiA-3156_fig1_387227757
Fodder quality (crude fibre, protein, fat) was reported as higher than the check SiA 3156. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica

GENETICS AND QTL
GPUF 3 was developed by pure-line selection from germplasm IC 479864, so the parentage field "Not specified" can be filled with this origin. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Molecular-profile-of-proposed-variety-GPUF-3-and-check-variety-SiA-3156_fig1_387227757
A molecular profile of GPUF 3 versus SiA 3156 is shown in the paper, but no QTL or marker results were extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing unit: Project Coordinating Unit, ICAR-AICRP on Small Millets, University of Agricultural Sciences (UAS), GKVK, Bengaluru. Target zones are 5 and 6 of Karnataka. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Molecular-profile-of-proposed-variety-GPUF-3-and-check-variety-SiA-3156_fig1_387227757
Lead author listed in citing literature: T. E. Nagaraja, with C. Nandini, S. Bhat, K. B. Palanna, P. C. Ganiger, and T. S. Sukanya et al. -- https://link.springer.com/rwe/10.1007/978-3-031-91605-2_1-1
No breeder profile page was found. The fourth search for breeder and institution details returned no results.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder email, phone, or personal contact was found in any result. The fourth search returned nothing, so no institute-level contact page URL was found either. Recommended next step: check the UAS GKVK, Bengaluru website and the ICAR-AICRP Small Millets site for a contact page.

PUBLICATIONS
Nagaraja, T. E., Nandini, C., Bhat, S., Palanna, K. B., Ganiger, P. C., Sukanya, T. S., et al. (2022). GPUF 3: A new high yielding foxtail millet variety (Setaria italica). Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding, 13, 810-819. -- https://doi.org/10.37992/2022.1303.103
GPUF 3: A new high yielding foxtail millet variety (Sateria italica). Full-text record dated Dec 2025 on ResearchGate. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
Study on PEG effects on seedling growth of dry and hydroprimed GPUF-3 seed. Authors and year not verified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287753024_Effect_of_foxtail_millet_setaria_italica_supplementation_on_serum_glucose_serum_lipids_and_glycosylated_hemoglobin_in_type_2_diabetics
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report, or QTL paper was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, UAS seed sales, or dealer listing was located in the search results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka, specifically zone 5 and zone 6 dry areas. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica

drought.details: No measured drought score for SiA 3085 was found. Indirect evidence only: (1) a general foxtail millet statement describes short-duration, drought-tolerant types, but this is not variety-specific; (2) AMMI analysis showed narrow adaptation to Anantapur, a scarce-rainfall rainfed site, which suggests drought-prone suitability but is not a measured drought tolerance result. The CSC record lists the variety as suitable for rainfed and irrigated kharif and summer seasons and for early sowing conditions, but does not state drought tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to blast and downy mildew. A second source lists it as high yielding and resistant to blast and downy mildew, 75-82 days, 20-30 q/ha, for 'All states'. No quantitative disease scores were reported. Digest sources give 20-30 q/ha (2000-3000 kg/ha) for the 75-82 day class and yield potential up to 2500 kg/ha for short-duration types SiA 3085/3088/3156. EVIDENCE DIGEST: SiA 3085 (Italian/foxtail millet)

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "SiA 3085", so all evidence below refers to that name. Seednet variety code A0205027 and Seednet crop name "ITALIAN MILLET (THENAI/NAVANE/FOX TAIL MILLET/KANG" were not confirmed by any search result. Searches run: 4 (variety, breeder, research, seed availability). The seed-availability search returned mostly unrelated results.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a pure line from RARS Nandyal, 2011, from SiA 2644; described as resistant to blast and downy mildew in the 80-85 day, 20-30 q/ha class -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/foxtail_millet.pdf
- Listed as high yielding and resistant to blast and downy mildew, 75-82 days, 20-30 q/ha, "All states" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Described as short-duration and drought tolerant (general foxtail millet statement, not variety-specific) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- AMMI analysis showed narrow adaptation to Anantapur (scarce-rainfall rainfed site), suggesting drought-prone suitability but not a measured drought score -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-5950

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SiA 3156 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical; crop is foxtail/Italian millet, Setaria italica). Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). No seednet.gov.in page was returned.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to blast and downy mildew, listed in an on-farm trial table alongside its yield range -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf
- Relatively drought-tolerant at seedling stage under PEG stress; seedling length falls by about 50% at roughly -6 bars PEG (drought screening of foxtail millet cultivars) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372105159_Evaluation_of_drought_resistance_and_index_screening_of_foxtail_millet_cultivars
- Seedling-stage drought tolerance is described as genotypic variation and SiA-3156 is cited as a tolerant reference line -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336418136_Foxtail_Millet_Setaria_italica_L_Potential_of_Smaller_Millet_for_Future_Breeding
- Heat: no direct heat-tolerance finding. A sowing-date study used it as a check to expose the crop to a temperature range, but did not report a heat-tolerance result -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331401436_Response_of_Growth_Yield_and_Quality_Parameters_of_Foxtail_Millet_Genotypes_to_Different_Planting_Density
- Flood, submergence, salinity: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant to blast and downy mildew (see Stress Tolerance source) -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed Andhra Pradesh trials reported higher grain yield with SiA 3156 among several varieties -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2
- Maturity 85-90 days and yield 2000-2500 kg/ha in a varietal table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- Rabi-season yield of about 1290 kg/ha in Andhra Pradesh (Ramyasri et al., as cited in review) -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2
- Plant height 93.7 cm, taller than SiA 3088 (79.9 cm); tiller count 2.4-4.6 versus GPUF 3 -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336418136_Foxtail_Millet_Setaria_italica_L_Potential_of_Smaller_Millet_for_Future_Breeding
- Karnataka station and farm trials (2017-2020) against GPUF 3: SiA 3156 mean grain yield 25.73 q/ha, versus 29.89 q/ha for GPUF 3 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica
- Andhra Pradesh on-farm comparison with SiA 3223: SiA 3156 yielded about 2032-2070 kg/ha, below SiA 3223 -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf
- Nutrition: protein about 13.09 g% in an AICRP-SM comparison -- https://icar-iirr.org/CRP/index.php/small-millets

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The parentage "Selection from SiA 2871" comes from the input record only; no search result confirmed it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The MILLETS cultivar list places a "Developed at RARS (ANGRAU), Nandyal" line near the SiA 3156 entry, but the text is jumbled and the line may belong to an adjacent variety. Not confirmed for SiA 3156 -- https://www.millets.res.in/ztmc/Millet_Cultivars_Commercialisation.pdf
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for SiA 3156: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Jayalakshmi, M. et al. (year not shown in retrieved text). On-farm Testing of Foxtail Millet Variety SiA-3223 (Renadu) in Semi-arid Regions of Andhra Pradesh. Blended-field journal (researchtrend) -- https://www.researchtrend.net/bfij/pdf/On-farm-Testing-of-Foxtail-Millet-Variety-SiA-3223-(Renadu)-in-Semi-arid-Regions-of-Andhra-Pradesh-M-Jayalakshmi-28.pdf (SiA 3156 is the comparator here, not the focus)
- Nagaraja et al. (year not shown; GPUF 3 paper). GPUF 3: A new high yielding foxtail millet variety (Setaria italica). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/387227757_GPUF_3_A_new_high_yielding_foxtail_millet_variety_Sateria_italica (SiA 3156 is the check)
- Authors not shown (2023 study). Drought resistance and index screening of foxtail millet cultivars. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372105159_Evaluation_of_drought_resistance_and_index_screening_of_foxtail_millet_cultivars
- Authors not shown. Foxtail Millet (Setaria italica L.): Potential of Smaller Millet for Future Breeding. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336418136_Foxtail_Millet_Setaria_italica_L_Potential_of_Smaller_Millet_for_Future_Breeding
- Authors not shown. Response of Growth, Yield and Quality Parameters of Foxtail Millet Genotypes to Different Planting Density. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331401436_Response_of_Growth_Yield_and_Quality_Parameters_of_Foxtail_Millet_Genotypes_to_Different_Planting_Density
- Authors not shown. A brief review on world of foxtail millet. Journal of Applied Biology (JAB) -- https://jabonline.in/abstract.php?article_id=1374&sts=2
- KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report on SiA 3156: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or private dealer listing for SiA 3156: No evidence found. Seednet portal listing was not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Vikaspedia lists SiA 3156 under Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu, and separately under Rajasthan and Uttarakhand -- https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/cereals-and-millets/foxtail-millet?lgn=en
- The input record says Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Bihar. Bihar was not found in any SiA 3156 source; Rajasthan and Uttarakhand were found instead.

Release year: the input says 2014. One varietal table gives 2014 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India. Another snippet from the on-farm paper gives 2012 for the same variety, so the year needs checking against the CSC minutes.

- Name: Bidhan Pat 13 (variety_name). Seednet name BIDHAN PAT-3 (D-110) is a separate entry. The Pat-3 line below refers to Bidhan Pat-3, not Bidhan Pat 13.
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): flood-prone adaptation and tolerance to waterlogging/submergence. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546 (Bidhan Pat-3 Jute varieties tolerant to water logging / submergence is listed among tolerant varieties; the same deck notes Pat-3 is suitable for flood-prone areas.)

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13) disease or pest resistance. Searches returned only the BCKV variety table, which gives no resistance data.
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): the slide deck lists it among varieties tolerant to waterlogging and submergence, not to a named disease or pest. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Bidhan Pat 13: fibre yield 32.2 q/ha recorded in the BCKV variety table. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): fibre yield 25-27 q/ha, photo-sensitive. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): matures about 110 days after sowing, with sowing possible from 1 March to 1 July. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Bidhan Pat-3 seed-crop trial (seednet-name evidence only): seed yield was maximised under rainfed conditions in the red and laterite zone with sowing in late June to mid-July plus topping. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319469619_Jute_seed_production_as_influenced_by_dates_of_sowing_and_topping_in_red_and_laterite_zone_of_West_Bengal
- No evidence found for multi-location trial results of Bidhan Pat 13.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage D-154 and D-18 was supplied in the task input only. No search result confirmed it for Bidhan Pat 13.
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): pedigree is a variety-by-mutant cross. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290909716_Jute_Biology_Diversity_Cultivation_Pest_Control_Fiber_Production_and_Genetics
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies of Bidhan Pat 13.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13): applicant is BCKV, and the release was through SVRC under the AINP on Jute and Allied Fibres. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- No breeder name was found for Bidhan Pat 13. Developing institution: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya (BCKV), Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): registered as a public variety under PPV&FR, with the applicant given as ICAR-CRIJAF with BCKV. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/index.php/en/bckv-ipr-crop-varieties2-en
- Name discrepancy: the Pat-3 (D-110) evidence refers to a white jute (C. capsularis) variety registered in 2012, not to Bidhan Pat 13, which is a tossa-type variety released in 2022.
- Breeder names in the search results (for example Sanjoy Shil, JRC 9057) refer to another variety and were discarded.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute address: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf
- Institute website: www.bckv.edu.in. -- https://wbjeeb.in/assets/ALPG/SU/BCKV.pdf
- No breeder email or phone was found for Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13).
- The only BCKV email found (pkdhara9@yahoo.in, admission in-charge) is an admissions contact, not a research contact, so it is excluded.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh entry naming Bidhan Pat 13 or BCCO-13.
- Authors not stated in the result (year not stated). Jute seed production as influenced by dates of sowing and topping in red and laterite zone of West Bengal (Bidhan Pat-3 seednet-name evidence only). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319469619_Jute_seed_production_as_influenced_by_dates_of_sowing_and_topping_in_red_and_laterite_zone_of_West_Bengal
- Authors not stated in the result (year not stated). Descriptors for jute (Corchorus olitorius L.) (lists Bidhan Pat-3 among capsularis varieties characterised; not specific to Bidhan Pat 13). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/305624674_Descriptors_for_jute_Corchorus_olitorius_L

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Bidhan Pat 13 (BCCO 13) seed from NSC, the West Bengal state seed agency, KVKs, BCKV seed sales or private dealers. The seed-production centres listed by BCKV cover paddy, mustard and pulses, not jute. -- https://bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/SSR-University_bckv.pdf
- Bidhan Pat-3 (seednet-name evidence only): no seed-source listing was found.
- The search returned only RuneScape game items and Bangladeshi jute seed reviews, which are unrelated.

RECOMMENDED STATES
