drought.details: The 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper reports tolerance to moisture stress for JLS-66 and states it was released for rainfed situations in Madhya Pradesh. The digest gives no graded scale, so 'medium' reflects a qualitative tolerance statement only, with no quantitative stress data. Rainfed adaptation is supported by the same paper.

heat.details: The 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper reports tolerance to high temperature stress for JLS-66. The digest gives no graded scale or quantitative heat data, so the level reflects a qualitative statement only.

salinity.details: No evidence found for JLS-66 specifically. The PMC review lists the variety only in an irrigated/rainfed variety table with no stress data.

flood.details: No evidence found for JLS-66 specifically. The PMC review lists the variety only in an irrigated/rainfed variety table with no stress data.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance to major diseases is stated in the 2020 paper (no named diseases). The DOD table lists resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and wilt, with bud fly marked 'Mod.' (moderate). The AICRP page lists moderate resistance to powdery mildew and moderate susceptibility to Alternaria blight. This conflicts with the DOD row for Alternaria blight and is unresolved. Rust: No evidence found for JLS-66.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistance to bud fly, described as the most damaging pest, is stated in the 2020 paper. The DOD table lists bud fly as moderate ('Mod.'). The AICRP page lists moderate resistance to bud fly. Capsule borer: No evidence found for JLS-66.

agronomic_details.yield: Seed yield about 1200 kg/ha and 42.85% drying oil (2020 paper). The search snippet figures of 849 kg/ha and 35.67% oil are not clearly attributed to JLS-66 and were excluded.
agronomic_details.stability: All India coordinated trials (zone III): seed yield 10.8 to 20.97% above comparison varieties, and oil yield 16.03 to 37.80% above them. Multi-environment stability beyond these trial summaries is not reported in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed situations in Madhya Pradesh (2020 paper). Suitability for intercropping with pulses (AICRP page). Zone III (Bundelkhand in UP, Rajasthan and MP) was the trial zone; this is not confirmed as the notified recommendation. The PMC review lists the variety among irrigated-condition varieties with no yield data.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.field_trials: All India coordinated trials, zone III (including Bundelkhand in UP, Rajasthan and MP): seed yield 10.8 to 20.97% above comparison varieties JLS-67, NL-97, JLS-9 and T-397; oil yield 16.03 to 37.80% above them. A castor-paper snippet reports rainfed Alfisol trial data for linseed varieties, but JLS-66 is not reported in those figures. No separate irrigated trial yield data found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JLS-66 (linseed)

Name note: The CSC release name is JLS-66 and the Seednet name is also JLS-66, with variety code SLS 66. Seednet's crop field says "LENTIL (MASUR)", but every linseed source found names JLS-66 as a linseed variety. I found no Seednet page for JLS-66 under any crop, so all findings below refer to the linseed variety. Release year conflicts across sources: the input says 2011-06-28, the AICRP page says 2018, and a DOD row says 2010 for "Jawahar Linseed-66 (SLS-66)" released at Hoshangabad.

STRESS TOLERANCE
-- The 2020 Journal of Oilseeds Research paper reports tolerance to moisture stress and high temperature stress for JLS-66 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Rainfed adaptation is stated for the variety in the same paper, which says it was released for rainfed situations in Madhya Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Suitability for intercropping with pulses is listed on the AICRP linseed page -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
-- Flood, submergence, salinity and heat-specific tolerance: No evidence found for JLS-66 specifically (the PMC review lists it only in an irrigated/rainfed variety table, with no stress data) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
-- Paper states resistance to major diseases and to bud fly, the most damaging pest -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- DOD table: resistant to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt and bud fly (marked "Mod.", i.e. moderate) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- AICRP page: moderately resistant to powdery mildew and bud fly, moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight. This conflicts with the DOD row for Alternaria blight -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
-- Rust and capsule borer: No evidence found for JLS-66

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
-- Maturity of about 114 days, seed yield about 1200 kg/ha, and 42.85% drying oil -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- A second set of figures in the search snippet (104 days, 849 kg/ha, 35.67% oil) is not clearly attributed to JLS-66 in the snippet, so I have not used it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378072674_Jawahar_Linseed_Sagar-66_JLS-66_Development_and_dissemination_of_newly_developed_linseed_variety_for_nutritional_security_of_India_SAGAR-66_JLS-66_DEVELOPMENT_OF_NEW_LINSEED_VARIETY_FOR_NUTRITIONAL_SE
-- All India coordinated trials (zone III, including Bundelkhand in UP, Rajasthan and MP): seed yield 10.8 to 20.97% above comparison varieties, and oil yield 16.03 to 37.80% above them. Comparators are JLS-67, NL-97, JLS-9 and T-397 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Rainfed Madhya Pradesh trial trend: the castor-paper snippet reports rainfed Alfisol performance data for linseed varieties, but JLS-66 is not reported in trial figures there -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
-- Irrigated-condition performance: the PMC review lists JLS66 among irrigated-condition varieties, but gives no yield data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

GENETICS AND QTL
-- No evidence found for QTL, marker, parentage or pedigree studies naming JLS-66. The PMC/MDPI review lists JLS66 only in variety tables -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461
-- Parentage: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
-- Developers named in the paper: Devendra K. Payasi and M. P. Dubey, AICRP on Linseed, Regional Agricultural Research Station, JNKVV, Sagar 470002, Madhya Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Developing institution: Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, via the AICRP linseed centre at Sagar -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376
-- Released centre listed as Sagar on the DOD table, and as Hoshangabad for the 2010 row -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- The ICAR-IIOR linseed breeder page and the Nagpur AICRP page are about other linseed programmes and are not linked to JLS-66, so I did not use them

CONTACT DETAILS
-- Devendra K. Payasi (AICRP Linseed, RARS Sagar): email dpayasi@gmail.com, as printed in an affiliation of a related review -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
-- M. P. Dubey (AICRP Linseed, RARS Sagar): no direct contact found for this person. A JNKVV telephone directory lists a Dr. M. P. Dubey, phone 9425620205, as Nodal Officer at Khurai, which is a different role. I have not attributed it to this breeder -- https://www.jnkvv.org/public/file/1756984461.TelephoneDirectory.pdf
-- Directorate of Farms, JNKVV (breeder seed production): Dr. V. K. Yadav, Director, mobile 8770867088, email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
-- JNKVV postal address: Krishinagar, Adhartal, Jabalpur 482004 (M.P.), India -- https://www.jnkvv.org/contact-us
-- Institute contact page (Vice Chancellor and office directory): https://www.jnkvv.org/contact-us
-- Postal address for RARS Sagar: Regional Agricultural Research Station, JNKVV, Sagar 470002, Madhya Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376

PUBLICATIONS
-- Payasi, D. K. and Dubey, M. P. (2020). Jawahar Linseed Sagar-66 (JLS-66): Development and dissemination of newly developed linseed variety for nutritional security of India. Journal of Oilseeds Research 37(1) -- https://doi.org/10.56739/jor.v37i1.136376
-- Chauhan, S. and co-authors (2023). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. Genes 14(7) -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461 (JLS66 appears only in variety tables; full author list not retrieved, so I have not listed it as a study of JLS-66)
-- Conference papers, AICRP annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, and field-trial reports specific to JLS-66: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
-- In the 2020-21 breeder seed indent for linseed, JLS 66 is named as contributing about 7.5% of the indent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols (this is a castor paper that quotes seed-chain data for linseed; treat as indicative)
-- JNKVV Directorate of Farms handles breeder seed production under the national seed programme -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
-- Seednet listing, NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU sales, or private dealers: No evidence found for JLS-66 in the search results

RECOMMENDED STATES
-- Madhya Pradesh, rainfed state release -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
-- Madhya Pradesh, rainfed areas (2010 row, Hoshangabad) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, KNK and Odisha are listed against the JLS-66 row of a DOD table. This conflicts with the MP-only entries and needs checking against the gazette notification -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
-- Zone III (Bundelkhand, UP, Rajasthan, MP) appears as the trial zone, not confirmed as the notified recommendation -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136376

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Searches used: 4 of 4 allowed. The third search (research/publications) returned mostly off-topic hits, and the fourth (seed availability) returned only foreign retail listings, so several headings are thin. Both name fields are "LL 1613", so the evidence applies to the same name under both the CSC and Seednet headings. I did not query the Seednet portal directly, so no Seednet listing is confirmed.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE
No LL 1613-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found in the search results. -- No evidence found
Seed-size context: the ICAR-IIPR report lists LL 1613 as a small-seeded AVT-2 genotype alongside LL 1373, but the captured text is truncated before any stress data. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Unattributed disease note: the PAU 2022 annual report says a lentil variety is resistant to red leaf spot and moderately resistant to zonate leaf spot diseases. The captured text does not name the variety, so this may not refer to LL 1613. -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
The DPD release table lists LL 1613 under lentil release data with no disease entry in the captured row. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
LL 1613, released 2023, PAU Ludhiana, NWPZ (HR, PN, UP, UK, DL, RJ), irrigated condition; yield 16-17 and days 114-145 as shown in the table (the column order is ambiguous in the extraction, so verify before use). -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Trial data: the ICAR-IIPR Rabi 2021-22 report lists LL 1613 among entries with numeric values (1653, 1792, 1467, 1617, 14.27, 23.72), but the captured text does not label these columns, so their meaning is unverified. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Agronomy: the same report mentions AVT-2 small-seeded genotypes LL 1373 and LL 1613 under sowing-date work, but the sowing-date results are cut off. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No LL 1613 QTL, marker or parentage-validation study found. The parentage "LL 1112 x PL 02-6" is from the input record only, not from any search result. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: PAU, Ludhiana per the DPD table. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
Release: LL 1613 is an open pollinated variety of lentil recommended for sale in Haryana, Punjab, Northern Rajasthan, Plains of Uttarakhand, Delhi, Western Uttar Pradesh and part of Jammu and Kashmir. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/lentil-variety-ll-1613/
Lead breeder name(s): not found in any result. -- No evidence found
Institute station: PAU Ludhiana is the developing institution; the specific breeding station is not stated in the results. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
Breeder: none found. -- No evidence found
Institute-level: the PAU website is listed as www.pau.edu, Ludhiana, Punjab, with no email, phone or postal address in the results. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab_Agricultural_University
Verification needed: the official PAU email, phone and postal address, and the Department of Plant Breeding contact page, must be taken from the PAU site directly.

PUBLICATIONS
PAU Registrar (2022). Annual Report 2022, Punjab Agricultural University. Annual report -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
ICAR-IIPR (2023). Project Coordinator Report, MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22. Institutional report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
Kailash Chandra et al. (2016). Lentil Breeding for Improving Productivity Using Classical and Molecular Approaches. Review (no LL 1613 content in captured text) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329609948_Lentil_Breeding_for_Improving_Productivity_Using_Classical_and_Molecular_Approaches
No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on LL 1613 was found. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, PAU seed-sales or Indian private-dealer listing for LL 1613 was found. The seed-related results were foreign retail sites, which I have excluded. -- No evidence found
Breeder seed context: ICAR-IIPR reports total lentil breeder seed production of 857.36 q against an indent of 547.44 q for 45 indented varieties in Rabi 2021-22, without naming LL 1613. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified recommendation: Haryana, Punjab, Northern Rajasthan, Plains of Uttarakhand, Delhi, Western Uttar Pradesh and part of Jammu and Kashmir. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/lentil-variety-ll-1613/
Zone: the PAU report places LL 1613 in the Northwest Plains Zone (Punjab, Haryana, western Uttar Pradesh, north Rajasthan and Jammu & Kashmir). -- https://pau.edu/content/registrar/ar/ar_2022.pdf
Release date and type: 25 September 2023 notification, open-pollinated, released by the Central Seed Committee process. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/lentil-variety-ll-1613/

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: L 4727 (lentil, A0309083)

DROUGHT: No direct drought-tolerance evidence found for L 4727. A Bundelkhand trial describes it as a low-water-requirement variety, but that is a regional agronomic note, not a stress-tolerance test. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5491

HEAT: No evidence found. (The heat-tolerant entry in the DPD table is Kota Masoor-1, a different variety.) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

SALINITY: No evidence found.

FLOOD: No evidence found.

SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found.

DISEASE RESISTANCE: Moderately resistant to wilt per the DPD central-release listing for L 4727 (2018, IARI). -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf ; https://www.dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
DISEASE RESISTANCE (corroboration): Its moderate resistance to wilt is also noted in a Legume Research paper. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5491
DISEASE RESISTANCE (rust/pests): No evidence found for rust, Ascochyta or pod-borer resistance in L 4727.

PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found.

QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found for L 4727 specifically.

PARENTAGE: The AICRP annexure lists L 4727 as Sehore 74-3 x (the cross is truncated in the source). -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

YIELD AND TRIALS: The IARI best-practice note gives an average yield of 11.5 to 14.5 q / ha and exhibited yield superiority of 23.7 percent over the best check IPL 316. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
YIELD RANGE (central release listing): 11-15 q/ha, with 92-128 days to maturity. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
MATURITY/AGRONOMY: Developed by ICAR-IARI, New Delhi in 2018 and matures in 92-128 days. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5491
FLD DEMONSTRATIONS: L 4727 had 2,500 FLDs conducted in MP in 2018. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
SEED TRAITS: Early maturity and bold seed size are noted as its distinguishing features. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf

BREEDER/INSTITUTION: ICAR-IARI, New Delhi; notified and released in 2018. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf ; https://www.dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY: Breeder seed indent for L4727 is listed in the IARI note (values 7.0, 8.0, 10.0 and a total of 22.07 qtl, year not clearly stated). This is demand data, not a supply or NSC/State Seed Corporation listing. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC/SSC/KVK): No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Central Zone, covering Madhya Pradesh, parts of Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and Chhattisgarh, for timely planting under rainfed conditions in rabi. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Latest-News/Best_Practices_lentil_and_chickpea_Varieties.pdf
RECOMMENDED STATES (input check): The input lists Maharashtra as a recommended state. The IARI note does not include Maharashtra, while the DPD listing is for CZ/NWPZ (CG, ...). Verify Maharashtra against the official notification. -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Lentil-14 (CSC name) / PANT LENTIL-4 (Seednet name), lentil (Lens culinaris), PL-320

Search status: four web_search calls were made. A fifth lookup hit the tool-call limit, so the gaps below could not be filled. The evidence is thin. Nothing found so far confirms the variety's own release notification, yield, or trial data.

Name mapping: The evidence does not confirm that Seednet's "PANT LENTIL-4" is the same entry as CSC "Pant Lentil-14". The only "PL4" reference I found is a ScienceDirect study that lists PL4 as a GBPUAT lentil variety, which may be an older line. Treat the two names as unreconciled until checked on seednet.gov.in.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Pant Lentil-14 or PANT LENTIL-4. The DPD listing gives tolerance notes for other Pant lentil varieties only (for example, Pant Lentil-9 is listed as resistant to rust) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found specific to this variety. Related context only: the DPD listing includes rust resistance and wilt tolerance for some Pant lentil lines -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for this variety's maturity, yield, or trial results. The DPD table has maturity and yield columns for other entries, but I did not see a row for Pant Lentil-14 in the captured text -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage (UPL 175 x (Pant L 184 x P 288)) was supplied in the brief and was not independently verified. A MULLaRP report lists lentil crosses attempted in 2021-22 at GBPUAT Pantnagar (10 crosses) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, under the ICAR-AICRP on Pulses. The GBPUAT Directorate of Research page lists "Pant Lentil 14" among its varieties -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6. The AICRP centre at Pantnagar was established in 1966 in the Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/43%20pantnagar.pdf. Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level only, as no breeder contact was found:
- Dr. S.K. Verma, Director Research, GBPUA&T, Pantnagar – 263145, Uttarakhand, India -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6
- Email: directorresearch@gbpuat.ac.in -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/directorates/directorate_experiment/index.html?id=6
- Phone: No evidence found.
- Breeder name, breeder email, and breeder phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report entry, or thesis specific to Pant Lentil-14 was found. Related item only: a study of Indian lentil varieties that includes PL4 and other GBPUAT lines, for physical, nutritional and cooking traits. Authors and year were not captured in the search output. -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. This search was not run, as the tool-call limit was reached before it.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Per the brief (CSC minutes, not independently verified): Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, North-West & Central Rajasthan, Western Uttar Pradesh. No independent source found.

Recommended next steps: (1) Check the CSC release notification and the Seednet entry for the official name, notification year, and the PANT LENTIL-4 mapping. (2) Search KrishiKosh and the GBPUAT lentil breeding programme for the breeder's name and contact. (3) Look for the AICRP-MULLaRP annual report entries for the variety's multi-location trials. (4) Check seed sources with GBPUAT Seed Production, the Uttar Pradesh and Punjab state seed corporations, and the NSC.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: Pant L 6 (CSC name) is listed as resistant to rust in a single-trait entry (DPD table), and Pant L-6 is described as rust-resistant/tolerant in a state-wise guide. Disease tolerance/resistance: Pant Lentil 5 (Seednet name) is named among tolerant/resistant varieties recommended for disease management, with no pathogen-specific data. Mapping of these entries to PL 02 is unconfirmed. Pod borer, wilt and ascochyta resistance were reported for other Pantnagar lines (Pant Lentil 9, Pant Lentil 12), not for PL 5 or PL 6, and are excluded here.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest data were found for PL 02, PL 5 or PL 6. Pod borer resistance was reported only for Pant Lentil 9 and Pant Lentil 12, so it is not attributed to this variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Original CSC record: 1500.00 to 2000.00 Kg/Ha. DPD table (Pant L 6, CSC name): 16-18 q/ha (approximately 1600-1800 kg/ha). The two ranges are consistent in part but are reported from different sources and the name mapping is unconfirmed. No multi-location yield data were found.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or across-environment yield stability data were found for PL 02 or PL 6.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: timely sown condition of Uttar Pradesh. Digest evidence: recommended for Uttarakhand (DPD table and state-wise guide). Digest reports Pant L 6 as small seeded, while ICAR-IIPR (Rabi 2021-22) lists Pant Lentil 5 among large-seeded lentils for central India. The seed-size and region statements conflict across sources and are not reconciled by the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Lentil 6 / PANT LENTIL-5 (PL 02), lentil (masoor)

Name note: The CSC name is "Pant Lentil 6" and the Seednet name is "PANT LENTIL-5". The evidence below refers to whichever name each source uses, and I label it. No source I found links "PL 02" to either name explicitly, so the identity of the variety is unconfirmed. Parentage "L4126 X LG 171" was not found in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pant L 6 (2009, GBPUA&T Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, small seeded) is listed as resistant to rust; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for it were found -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf and https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Lentil 5 is named among tolerant/resistant varieties recommended for disease management (ref. to "Pant Lentil 5" as tolerant/resistant to disease) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF
- Pant L-6 is listed as rust-resistant/tolerant in a state-wise guide -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
- No stress-tolerance evidence specific to PL 02 or to the Seednet name was found beyond the above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant L 6 (CSC name): resistant to rust (single-trait entry) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Lentil 5 (Seednet name): listed as tolerant/resistant for disease reduction; no pathogen-specific data -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF
- Pod borer, wilt and ascochyta resistance were reported for other Pantnagar lines (Pant Lentil 9, Pant Lentil 12), not for PL 5 or PL 6 -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No pest data for PL 02 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant L 6 (CSC name): yield 16-18 q/ha, 125-145 days, small seeded, Uttarakhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Pant Lentil 5 (Seednet name): listed among large-seeded lentils for central India (ICAR-IIPR report, Rabi 2021-22) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- A 2023 IJES fertilizer trial used "Pant Masoor-5" at Dehradun, Uttarakhand (seed rate 40 kg/ha); this is the Seednet name's trial, reported under a variant spelling -- https://www.iaras.org/iaras/filedownloads/ijes/2023/008-0009(2023).pdf
- No multi-location yield data for PL 02 or PL 6 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Biparental progenies were developed from PL 6 x PL 8 and PL 6 x L 4147 crosses, with gene-action work, at Norman E. Borlaug Crop Research Centre, GBPUA&T -- https://isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/3421/3146
- No QTL or marker study for PL 02 or PL 6 was found.
- Note: the Pant L 406 mutant study (Laskar et al., 2018) concerns a different variety and is not evidence for PL 6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328006648_Morphological_characterization_of_gamma_rays_induced_multipodding_mutant_mp_in_lentil_cultivar_Pant_L_406

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (inferred from the sponsoring state and the DPD listing): G.B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology (GBPUA&T), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name for PL 6 or PL 5: No evidence found. Searches returned no breeder names for either variant.
- Station: Norman E. Borlaug Crop Research Centre, GBPUA&T (cited for the PL 6 crosses only) -- https://isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/3421/3146

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, role, email, phone: No evidence found.
- Institute email, phone, postal address, or contact-page URL for GBPUA&T Pantnagar: No evidence found in the results.
- Not an institute contact: a seed company site (https://www.pantnagarseeds.com/our-strength) and a state seed corporation page (https://www.indiamart.com/uttarakhand-seeds/aboutus.html) appeared, but neither gave contact details for this variety. Do not treat either as the breeding institute.

PUBLICATIONS
- Laskar, R.A. et al. (2018). Morphological characterization of gamma rays induced multipodding mutant (mp) in lentil cultivar Pant L 406. International Journal of Radiation Biology -- DOI 10.1080/09553002.2018.1511927 (different cultivar; background only)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Generation of biparental progenies and dissection of gene action in lentil (PL 6 x PL 8; PL 6 x L 4147). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/3421/3146
- Authors not shown (2026). Screening of Selected Indian Varieties of Lentils (Lens culinaris) for Physical, Nutritional and Cooking Characteristics (includes PL 5 and PL 6 from GBPUA&T). ScienceDirect -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807
- Dikshit, H.K., Mishra, G.P., Aski, M.S., Singh, A., Tripathi, K., Bansal, R. (year not shown). Lentil Breeding. Springer chapter -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-981-16-9257-4_24 (general review; no PL 5 or PL 6 data)
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report entry or KrishiKosh thesis specific to PL 02, PL 5 or PL 6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pant L 6 / PL 5 / PL 6 specific seed sources: No evidence found.
- Uttarakhand Seeds and Tarai Development Corporation (UKS&TDC), originally the Tarai Development Corporation set up in 1969 and linked to GBPUA&T seed production -- https://www.indiamart.com/uttarakhand-seeds/aboutus.html
- A 2023 contingency plan lists seed supply through TDC/NSC/VPKAS for Dehradun -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/Uttarkhand/UKD7-Dehradun-10.07.14.pdf
- NSC, KVK, SAU seed-sales listings for PL 5 or PL 6 were not found in the searches (the fourth search was not run).

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand: PL-5 and PL-6 are listed among recommended lentil varieties -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF and https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
- Pant L 6 (CSC name): recommended area Uttarakhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- YEAR OF RELEASE: Pant L 6 is listed as 2009 in the DPD table (CSC name). Release year for PANT LENTIL-5 (Seednet name): not found. The record's "NaT" value should be replaced with 2009 only if the CSC name is confirmed as the same variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pant Lentil 7 (variety_name) / PANT LENTIL-5 (seednet_variety_name), lentil (Lens culinaris), code PL 024

Name note: the Seednet name "PANT LENTIL-5" matches a different variety in the sources. The variety "Pant Lentil 5" appears as a 2001 GBPUAT release, so the Seednet entry may not refer to PL 024. Searches returned no Seednet page for either name. Findings below are labelled by the name they refer to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pant Lentil 7 (Pant L 7) is listed as rust resistant in a national lentil variety table, with large seed, 125-145 days and 16-18 q/ha, released 2009 by GBPUA&T Pantnagar -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- The same table lists "Pant Masoor 7" (2010, GBPUA&T, large seed, rust resistant, 114-145 days, 16-18 q/ha, NWPZ) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf (this may be the same variety under another name; unverified)
- Pant L-7 is named as rust resistant or tolerant in a lentil crop-management list -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/check-out-state-wise-suggested-varieties-of-lentil/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for PL 7 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pant L-7 is named among rust-resistant lentil varieties (rust and wilt context) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/lentilpptx-detail-cultivation-practices-of-lentil/267717293
- No wilt, ascochyta, Orobanche or pod-borer ratings specific to PL 7 were found.
- PANT LENTIL-5 (not PL 7): a 2001 GBPUAT release recorded as rust resistant, bold seeded, 15-18 q/ha, 135 days -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pant Lentil 7 (PL 024) appears in a review table with GBPUAT as source, release 2010, and adoption listed for Punjab, Haryana and UP, with about 15 q/ha yield. This conflicts with the Uttarakhand recommendation in the record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- The table gives a 2009 release year for Pant L 7 in one source and 2010 in another. No notification number or gazette date was found, so the NaT release year remains unresolved.
- A 2023 Dehradun fertilizer trial used "Pant Masoor-5" (not PL 7), sown at 40 kg/ha -- https://bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0006201
- No multi-location trial results for PL 7 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage L4126 x LG 171 or for any PL 7 marker, QTL or mapping study. The general lentil consensus DArT map is not specific to this variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5774769/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution (inferred): Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture & Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, per the variety tables above. No breeder name was found for PL 7 -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Lentil breeding context at ICAR-IIPR, Kanpur (Division of Crop Improvement): Jitendra Kumar is named as corresponding author on a lentil breeding review. This is not evidence that he bred PL 7 -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-76-4-015
- Dr. S. K. Verma (Professor, GBPUAT) is thanked for supplying lentil varieties, including PL 7, to a study. This does not identify him as breeder -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807

CONTACT DETAILS
- Jitendra Kumar, Principal Scientist, ICAR-IIPR (lentil breeding context, not confirmed for PL 7): jitendra.kumar@icar.gov.in; alternate jitendra73@gmail.com -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-76-4-015
- Dr. S. K. Verma, Professor, GBPUAT: no email or phone found.
- ICAR-Indian Institute of Pulses Research, Crop Improvement Division, Kanpur, Uttar Pradesh 208 024 (institute address, no phone or email found) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/ ; see also https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9896981/ (not a contact source)
- GBPUAT, Pantnagar: no official contact page was found in the results.
- Phone and email for the PL 7 breeder: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not given in the retrieved snippet (2019). Scenario of Lentil in India -A Review. ResearchGate (PDF) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- Authors not given in the retrieved snippet (2024 or later). Screening of Selected Indian Varieties of Lentils (Lens culinaris) for Physical, Nutritional and Cooking Characteristics. ScienceDirect -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S2949824426000807 (this study procured PL 7 from GBPUAT)
- Kumar, J. et al. (authors not confirmed in snippet). Breeding strategies to improve lentil for diverse agro-ecological environments. Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding, 76(4) -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-76-4-015 (general lentil breeding, not PL 7-specific)
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report entry or peer-reviewed PL 7 field study was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Uttarakhand Seeds & Tarai Development Corporation (TDC), Haldi, Pant Nagar, US Nagar, Uttarakhand -- https://www.pantnagarseeds.com/ (no lentil or PL 7 stock listing found)
- Breeder seed production data for lentil nationally (2021-22 Rabi) is recorded, without variety-level detail -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- Seednet listing for PANT LENTIL-5 or Pant Lentil 7: No evidence found.
- NSC, KVK, SAU seed sale or private dealer listings for PL 7: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttarakhand, per the national table entry for Pant L 7 -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Punjab, Haryana and UP, per the GBPUAT review table entry for Pant Lentil 7 (PL 024) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- Uttarakhand lentil recommendations list PL-5 and PL-6 (not PL 7) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF

drought.details: No search result provides drought tolerance data for Pant Lentil 11. The search results describe 'Pant Lentil-5' (GBPUAT, 2001, Uttarakhand) as resistant to rust and bold seeded, but do not report its drought response, and that information does not transfer to Pant Lentil 11. General lentil guidance in the results notes that the crop is drought-resistant but susceptible to waterlogging and frost, and recommends tolerant varieties, without naming Pant Lentil 11.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance evidence for Pant Lentil 11 was found. General crop notes state that lentil requires cold temperatures during vegetative growth and warm temperatures at maturity. No heat tolerance data is attributed to Pant Lentil 11.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance data for Pant Lentil 11 was found in the search results. The only salinity reference found concerns chickpea varieties (NAU Navsari) and is not applicable to lentil or to this variety.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for Pant Lentil 11 was found. General lentil guidance notes that the crop is sensitive to waterlogging, which is a crop-level trait and not a variety-specific result.

drought.details: None of the search results mention Pant Lentil 16 (PL-366). The release data lists stress reaction as NONE. General crop-level evidence only: lentil is described as moderately tolerant to drought, with differences between cultivars, and tolerance to moisture stress is a key trait in rainfed production (CABI). Other released varieties such as Kota Masoor 2 are listed as tolerant to drought and high temperature, but this cannot be attributed to PL-366.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data for PL-366. Heat tolerance is reported only for other varieties (for example Kota Masoor 2 and L 4727) in the central lentil varieties list.

salinity.details: No PL-366 data. CABI states lentil is generally very sensitive to salinity, and a review reports salt exposure can reduce plant growth or yield by 20% to 100%. Salinity tolerance for this variety is not documented.

flood.details: No PL-366 data. Lentil in general is intolerant of waterlogging and water stagnation (CABI, agriguru, CUTM notes).

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified for PL-366 in the release data or search results. Other Pant varieties (Pant Lentil 5, Pant L-6, Pant L-7) are listed as rust or wilt tolerant or resistant in other documents, which should not be extrapolated to PL-366.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified for PL-366. Pant Lentil 9 is listed as resistant to root knot nematode, which is a different variety.

agronomic_details.yield: Not specified in the release table, and no yield data were found in the search results.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-location stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for the northern hill regions (Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, hills of West Bengal) per the release data. Lentil generally needs cool temperatures during vegetative growth and warm temperatures at maturity.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SEMI ERECT ,STEM COLOUR IS DARK GREEN ;FLOWER IS BLUE IN COLOUR ;BOLD SEED SIZE ,GREY MOTTLED;
agronomic_details.field_trials: No trial results for PL-366 were found. Its AICRP origin implies multi-location testing, but this is not documented in the results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No markers, QTL or SNP information was found for PL-366.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None found. The parentage is L4126 x LG 171 (from the release data), with no associated mapping data in the results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: None specific to the variety. The general lentil literature covers omics approaches to salt tolerance and heat shock proteins. The lentil genome is diploid, 2n=14, about 4 Gbp.

drought.details: Lentils, including Pusa 6, are considered relatively tolerant to drought and can be grown with lesser soil moisture. They continue to flower even under some stress, such as drought. Pusa 6 is identified as a lentil variety suitable for dryland farming conditions.

heat.details: Pusa 6 is a lentil variety, an annual winter season crop that requires cool and warm weather. The optimum temperature range for lentil growth is 18–30 °C. It needs moderate temperatures for optimal growth.

salinity.details: Pusa 6, as a lentil variety, is described as a salt-tolerant crop that can grow well even in salt-affected soils and is tolerant to salt conditions.

flood.details: Lentil, including Pusa 6, cannot tolerate waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: Pusa 6 is resistant to wilt disease, specifically Fusarium wilt.

pest_resistance.summary: Pest is not generally considered a major problem for lentil. While leaf-eating caterpillars can occur, no specific resistance or susceptibility to pests for Pusa 6 is detailed.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: The variety has government release-list citations (DPD) confirming rust resistance and moderate pod borer resistance, plus yield data of 12-13 q/ha. However, there is no peer-reviewed research and no abiotic stress evidence (drought, heat, salinity, flood). It is also a temperate Kashmir valley variety with a 204-day maturity, not recommended for Gujarat, so its suitability there is doubtful. The score sits at the 60 tier (citation present, weak stress evidence) and the biotic traits do not justify the 75 tier.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: SKUAST-K release; rust resistant; moderately resistant to pod borer; 12-13 q/ha; Kashmir valley
dashboard_data.seasons: Not explicitly stated; presumably rabi/autumn sowing in the Kashmir valley (inferred from the 204-day duration)

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: Shalimar Masoor-3 (SKUA-L-96) is a lentil variety released in 2019 by SKUAST-K for the Kashmir valley, with a yield of 12-13 q/ha and 204 days to maturity. It is resistant to rust and moderately resistant to pod borer, with no evidence of abiotic stress tolerance. Evidence comes only from government release lists, with no peer-reviewed or molecular data.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Kashmir valley lentil released in 2019 by SKUAST-K as SKUA-L-96. It yields 12-13 q/ha and matures in about 204 days. Parentage and plant traits are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: Biotic resistance is documented for rust (resistant) and pod borer (moderately resistant). No evidence exists for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance, since those snippet entries belong to other varieties. Suitability for Gujarat is unproven.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Masoor-3 (lentil)

Name note: The release-minute name and the Seednet name are both "Shalimar Masoor-3". Every finding below refers to that name. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists in this digest. Several sources list the variety under other names: SKUA-L-96 in the DPD tables, and KLS 221 as a possible parent or selection in the ICAR-IIPR report.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as tolerant to frost and winter chilling, Kashmir valley bold-seeded type, released 2019 by SKUAST-K Srinagar (DPD state list; the same row also appears as SKUA-L-96) -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Same frost and winter-chill tolerance entry, with the year given as 2018 in a second DPD table -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Same frost and winter-chill tolerance entry in the ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DPD entry reading "resistant to rust, moderately resistant to pod borer" sits in the same table cell as the Shalimar Masoor-2 entry (it repeats under the -2 heading). It is not attributable to Shalimar Masoor-3 -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- The ICAR-IIPR report lists the -3 entry as bold seeded with no disease claim. Its row for the -2 variety carries the "moderately resistant to wilt and rust" claim -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Shalimar Masoor-3.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield listed as 11-12 q/ha in one DPD table and 12-13 q/ha in another; maturity listed as 204 days -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- Yield listed as 11.5-12.5 q/ha, maturity 204 days, in the ICAR-IIPR report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No multi-location trial results or agronomic packages specific to Shalimar Masoor-3 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage field in the ICAR-IIPR report reads "KLS 221 (Sel..." and is truncated; this is unverified and conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage in the record -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No QTL or marker studies specific to Shalimar Masoor-3 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: SKUAST-K, Srinagar Centre (released 2019); the ICAR-IIPR report lists the same centre -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
- No breeder or scientist name was found for Shalimar Masoor-3. The search returned a Shalimar Masoor-related Jammu paper (Singh et al. 2022), but it concerns other derivatives, so it is not attributed here -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9499259/
- Discarded: the SKUAST-K wheat article about the Shalimar wheat-3 (SW-3) variety names a breeder, but that is a different crop and variety -- https://brighterkashmir.com/shalimar-wheat-3-launched-in-gurez

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or postal address for this variety.
- Institute-level only: SKUAST-K, Srinagar Centre (the release institution). No official contact page URL was returned by the search.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry or thesis that names Shalimar Masoor-3 as its subject. Items that name other Shalimar lentils (Masoor-1, Masoor-2, Jammu Lentil 71/144) were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The ICAR-IIPR MULLaRP Rabi 2021-22 report records breeder seed indents across 45 lentil varieties, but the line does not give a figure for Shalimar Masoor-3 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SKUAST seed sales or private dealers offering this variety. Results returned generic masoor dal sellers, which were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Jammu and Kashmir, Kashmir valley (state release, SKUAST-K). The DPD and ICAR-IIPR sources list the Kashmir valley region for this variety -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

- The central DPD lentil list gives VL Masoor 133 (VL 133), released 2011 by ICAR-VPKAS Almora, as tolerant to wilt, root rot and rust. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found for this variety. -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf (the state-released table with the VL Masoor 133 row is in http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf)
- Evidence refers to: VL Masoor 133 (variety_name). No evidence found for the seednet name VL MASOOR-103 in this heading.

DISEASE AND PEST

- No pest-resistance evidence was found for VL Masoor 133. -- (no URL)
- The Frontiers 2022 disease-resistance review's source tables do not list VL Masoor 133 (they cite VL Masoor 4 and VL507), so they were not used. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.1001682/full
- VL MASOOR-103 (seednet name): the only VL 103 evidence found (a 2000 VPKAS release described as rust tolerant) is a different variety and was discarded. Evidence for VL MASOOR-103 under this heading: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Name matched: VL Masoor 514 (VL 514). The SEEDNET name "VL MASOOR-4" was not searched and nothing found links it to this variety.
- Resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to rust in Uttarakhand hills (ICAR tribal/hill AR 2011-12) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/tribal-hill-region-AR-2011-12_3.pdf
- Moderately resistant to wilt and rust (DPD central/state lentil list) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to wilt and root rot, and tolerant to pod borer (compositional review table) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW
- Moderately resistant to wilt and rust, listed as bold seeded (DPD state list) -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf (http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2011 by ICAR-VPKAS, Almora; yield 8-10 q/ha; maturity 155-160 days; bold seeded; Uttarakhand hills -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- Protein content about 21.04%; 11.19% yield advantage over checks VL Masoor 507 and PL 05 in Uttarakhand hills under organic conditions -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/tribal-hill-region-AR-2011-12_3.pdf
- Listed among varieties used in an Indian pulse seed-system/technology demonstration paper -- https://www.isss-india.org/img/Bulletin31.pdf
- No evidence found for multi-location AICRP yield trial data specific to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genetic-diversity studies on VL Masoor 514.
- Parentage as supplied in the input (pure line selection from hill collection VHC 6553, Sera village, Berinag, Pithoragarh) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: ICAR-VPKAS (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan), Almora, Uttarakhand -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for a named lead breeder or scientist.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for breeder email, phone or postal address, and no institute contact page was returned by the searches.
- Institute name only: ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (UK) -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
- The Seednet-style contact details and the official VPKAS address need to be checked directly on vpkas.icar.gov.in.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not identified (2020s compositional study of five lentil varieties including VL Masoor 514). Journal: PMC article on dehulling, germination and cooking effects on lentil nutrients, anti-nutrients and antioxidants -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5336446/
- Authors not identified. Compositional review of lentil seed listing VL Masoor 514 with stress notes. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698673_COMPREHENSIVE_STUDY_OF_LENTIL_LENS_CULINARIS_MEDIK_SEED_AND_THEIR_NUTRITIONAL_PROFILE-A_REVIEW
- Authors not identified. Current scenario of lentil production in Madhya Pradesh, listing VL-514 among varieties in breeder seed production. Bioinfo Publication -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report with trial data, or DOI found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder seed production listed for VL-514 in Madhya Pradesh (not a sales listing) -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193
- ICAR-IIPR rabi 2021-22 PC report shows breeder seed indent of 1007 q for VL 514 in an indent table (cross-check needed) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-Report-MULLaRP_Rabi_2021-22.pdf
- The VPKAS seed portal page returned only shows VL Masoor 514 as a related product on the VL Masoor 148 page, so it is not evidence of stock -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VLMasoor148_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%80.%E0%A4%8F%E0%A4%B2.%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%B0148
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listings for VL Masoor 514. Indiamart results were generic masoor seed and not this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VL Masoor 129 (lentil)

Name note: the evidence below uses the spelling "VL Masoor 129" (dpd.gov.in). I did not see the Seednet listing "VL Masoor-129" in any result, so the Seednet-side evidence is absent, not confirmed.

Search budget note: four web_search calls were made. A fifth call was blocked by the tool limit, so the breeder, contact, and publication searches were not fully run. Gaps are marked below.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the state-release table entry for VL Masoor 129 notes resistance against wilt and root rot. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: VL Masoor 129 is listed as resistant against wilt and root rot. No pod borer or other pest evidence specific to this variety found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the table row for VL Masoor 129 contains the values "7-11" and "145-150" with no column headers in the snippet. These are most likely yield (q/ha) and days to maturity, but this is inferred and needs checking against the source. No multi-location trial data found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "VL 101 x VL 1" comes only from the input record; no independent source was retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: the release row names VPKAS, Almora as the developing institution (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora). No individual breeder name was found in the results. Breeder search was not completed.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The breeder-contact search was not completed, so no official email, phone or address has been verified. The institute name VPKAS, Almora is the only institute-level identifier available.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for VL Masoor 129. The PMC article (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5336446/) studies VL Masoor 125, 133, 142, 507 and 514, not 129. No AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI was located.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned the release table but no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf: listed as a state-released variety for Uttarakhand. A second source (dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF) lists Uttarakhand varieties, but the snippet I saw was truncated before the VL Masoor 129 entry.

RELEASE YEAR CONFLICT -- The input record says year of release is "NaT" (missing). dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf gives 2009. Treat 2009 as a source-supported value to verify, not as confirmed CSC minutes.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- VL Masoor 150 (variety_name) is listed as moderately resistant to wilt under field conditions in the DPD table of central and state released lentil varieties; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- VL Masoor 150: moderate resistance to wilt in field conditions (DPD released-varieties table, 2023 entry, ICAR-VPKAS Almora). No rust, root rot, Ascochyta or pod borer data found for this variety -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf

drought.details: Ratan exhibits remarkable tolerance to drought and is described as a drought-tolerant and drought-resistant genotype. It shows seed size consistency under water deficit, a useful adaptation mechanism. While its root growth can be drastically affected and relative water content (RWC) reduced under stress, its overall tolerance is consistently reported.

heat.details: Ratan is considered among heat stress-tolerant crops. Studies have investigated the influence of heat stress on its genome.

salinity.details: Ratan demonstrates enhanced tolerance to salt and is superior in salinity tolerance compared to other legume crops. It is included in screenings of grasspea genotypes for salinity response, indicating its known tolerance to salt stress.

flood.details: Ratan is noted for its tolerance to water logging conditions, which is essential for future production in flood-prone environments.

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified in search results.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified in search results.

agronomic_details.yield: Ratan (Bio L-212) has a reported yield of 15.0 (likely q/ha). It has outperformed chickpea (cv JG-74), lentil (cv JLS-3), and linseed (cv R), and is considered superior in yield compared to other legume crops.
agronomic_details.stability: Ratan is tolerant to various stress conditions, implying good stability across challenging environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Thrives well in all types of soils except high acidic. It is adapted to moisture stress and heat, and is recommended for the North Eastern Plains Zone (NEPZ) covering East Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 3.5 FEET PROSTRATE ; SIZE OF LEAF : BROAD LEAF ; LEAF WIDTH : 22.6MM ; LEAF LENGTH : 103.6MM ; INTERNODAL LENGTH : 59.0MM ; LEAF AREA : 10.24CM SQUARE ; 100 SEED WT. : 9.29 GM. SEED COLOUR : BOLD REDDISH GREY ; PROTEIN CONTENT : 25-30% ; FLOWER COLOUR : BLUE. It is known for its bold seeds and blue flowers. The variety has a low ODAP (β-N-oxalyl-L-α,β-diaminopropionic acid) content, generally reported as less than 0.1%. Seed size consistency is observed in response to water deficit.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Ratan has been cultivated by farmers in Bihar, with trials conducted over 26.33 acres involving 46 farmers. Seeds for experiments were obtained from Regional Research Station, Karnal, and Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur (Chhattisgarh).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Differential gene expression analysis revealed downregulation of abiotic stress tolerance and redox metabolism-responsive genes in Ratan. Several genes related to chromatin remodeling are differentially expressed in Ratan. β-ODAP biosynthetic genes are also investigated in this cultivar.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs were identified for Ratan directly in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological responses of Ratan to PEG-6000 induced drought stress have been measured. Ratan's genetic mechanisms involve chromatin remodeling and regulation of abiotic stress tolerance and redox metabolism genes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Lime VRM-1 (VRM-1, Agriculture Research Station, Vellore; release recorded as 2015-04-07)

RELEASE/BREEDER: No evidence found confirming the 2015 release date or the Vellore station as breeder. -- No source located
VARIETY IDENTITY: TNAU lists "VRM 1" among acid lime varieties, but another TNAU page calls it a "local variety" and elsewhere pairs it with "Tahithi lime," so its origin and identity need verification. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_fruits_acidlime.html
DROUGHT: No evidence found for VRM-1. A drought-tolerance claim exists only for a different, farmer-developed grafted acid lime selection, not VRM-1. -- https://nif.org.in/innovation/new_acid_lime_variety/292
HEAT: No evidence found.
SALINITY: No evidence found.
FLOOD/SUBMERGENCE: No evidence found. TNAU's general acid lime guidance says water stagnation should be avoided, which applies to the crop generally, not VRM-1 specifically. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_fruits_acidlime.html
DISEASE RESISTANCE: No evidence found for VRM-1. Canker tolerance is reported for other acid lime varieties (Pramalini, Sai Sarbati), not VRM-1. -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/acid-lime/
PEST RESISTANCE: No evidence found for VRM-1. Leaf miner and citrus butterfly tolerance is reported only for PKM 1. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_TNAU_varieties_fc_acidlime.html
QTL/MARKERS: No evidence found for VRM-1. -- No source located
YIELD: No VRM-1-specific yield found. The general acid lime yield guideline is about 25 t/ha/year. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf
TRIALS: TNAU Sankarankovil's 2017–2020 scheme included VRM 1 among four acid lime varieties in an evaluation of acid lime genotypes for year-round production; no results were reported. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/crs-sankarankovil/ongoing-schemes/
PROPAGATION: TNAU recommends layering for VRM 1 (listed as Tahithi lime). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf
SEED AVAILABILITY (NSC/State Seed Corporations/KVKs): No evidence found. -- No source located
RECOMMENDED STATES: Not confirmed by a release notification. TNAU's crop guide lists VRM 1 among acid lime varieties and names Vellore among the growing districts, which indicates Tamil Nadu use only. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/HORTICULTURE.pdf ; https://mapmycrop.com/acid-lime-crop-guide/

Mid-March sowing is recommended in the improved technology deck and in a pre-kharif extension table.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: ARPITA (JBC-5), jute**

**Name note:** The CSC/release-minutes name is ARPITA (code JBC-5), a white jute (*Corchorus capsularis*) variety. The Seednet name "Arpita" is listed under LINSEED (ALSI). The only Arpita-named Seednet-linked evidence I found is a linseed cultivar from Odisha, so it does not describe this jute variety. I did not access seednet.gov.in directly. Evidence below refers to the jute variety (JBC-5 / Arpita) unless stated otherwise.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The release listing describes it as having resistance to premature flowering. JBC 5 (Arpita) 2010 W.B. S.O. 2137 (E) 31.08.2010 28-30 Suitable for mid-March, pod non- shattering type, resistance to premature flowering, better fibre quality, resistance to major pest and diseases -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to JBC-5 was found in the searches. No evidence found for those traits.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The variety is described as resistant to major pests and diseases, but the named pathogens and pests are not specified. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Same claim from a second source (CRIJAF-derived improved technology deck). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- No pest- or disease-specific resistance data (for example, stem rot or Ophiomyia) for JBC-5 was found. No evidence found for named pathogen resistance.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. It is recommended for sowing in mid-March, and the reported yield is 28–30 q/ha. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/improved-technologies-for-jute-cultivation-in-india/144826546
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The ICAR 2010–11 report gives a potential of 2.8–3.0 t/ha in rainfed and transplanted-aman systems, and notes non-shattering pods. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Sowing-date recommendation for JBC-5 (mid-March) also appears in a pre-kharif extension table. -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/pre_kharif.pdf
- No multi-location trial data specific to JBC-5 were found. No evidence found for trial-level yields beyond the above.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- No evidence found. Parentage is not specified in the input, and no pedigree, marker or QTL study for JBC-5 was found. A 2024 hybridization study on tossa jute (*C. olitorius*) mentions JBO 1 but not JBC-5 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC11896985/

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Evidence refers to JBC-5 (Arpita), jute. The variety is listed in the CRIJAF variety table as a white jute variety. -- https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/SideLinks/Research/Varieties.php
- The developing institution is ICAR-CRIJAF, Barrackpore. No named breeder or scientist was found for JBC-5. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- Institution's own description of CRIJAF's role: Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibers (CRIJAF) established in 1953, is a research institute on jute & allied fibre crops under the Indian Council of Agricultural Research of Government of India. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/advances-in-agronomy-of-jute-corchorus-sp/205801621

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Institute: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Jute and Allied Fibres (CRIJAF). Address as found: Barrackpore, North 24 Parganas, West Bengal, India. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- Official website: https://crijaf.icar.gov.in/ (institute contact page URL, not fetched)
- Director named on the Wikipedia page: Dr. Gouranga Kar. This may be out of date and was not verified against the institute site. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Research_Institute_for_Jute_and_Allied_Fibers
- No breeder name, official email or phone number was found in the searches. The institute contact page should be checked directly for these.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- Indian Council of Agricultural Research (2011). DARE/ICAR Annual Report 2010–11, Crop Improvement. ICAR annual report, which reports JBC 5 (Arpita) yield and recommended states -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Authors not captured in search results (year not captured). Scientific Cultivation of Field Crops, Vol. 1. Book chapter listing JBC-5 (Arpita) for state recommendations -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh) or AICRP report specific to JBC-5 (jute) was found.
- Off-crop item, listed only because of the name match: Naik, B.S., Mishra, D., Lenka, D. and Sahoo, K.C. (2017). Arpita: a new linseed cultivar for Odisha. Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding 8(1): 84–88. DOI 10.5958/0975-928X.2017.00012.6 -- https://doi.org/10.5958/0975-928X.2017.00012.6 (linseed, not jute)

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No evidence found for JBC-5 (Arpita) at NSC, a state seed corporation, KVK or SAU in the searches. The West Bengal State Seed Corporation availability page lists other jute varieties (JRO-524, Irra, S-19, JRO-204, JBH-2004) but not Arpita. -- https://www.wbsscl.com/availability-of-seeds/
- Seednet portal listing for jute JBC-5 was not accessed. The Seednet "Arpita" entry under linseed refers to a different crop.

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- West Bengal, as notified in 2010 under S.O. 2137(E) dated 31.08.2010. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/ainpjaf/achievements/details-of-varieties/
- Assam is recommended in the ICAR 2010–11 report. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-05/crop-improvement-AR-2010-11_0.pdf
- Additional state lists that include JBC-5 (Arpita) for Bihar, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Meghalaya, Tripura and Nagaland. These are from compiled cultivation guides, not the notification. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376269572_Scientific_Cultivation_of_JUTE
- Release year: the state notification is dated 2010, so year_of_release "NaT" in the input can be replaced with 2010 (state notification). Release origin and institution are not stated in the notification excerpt.

drought.details: The HPKV crop improvement document lists 'Tolerant to water stress conditions' near the KL 215 (Bhagsu) entry, but the snippet does not clearly tie this trait to Bhagsu rather than a neighbouring entry. The Seednet list gives 'drought tolerant' for other varieties. General textbook statements that linseed is fairly drought resistant are crop-level, not variety-specific. The HPKV Research Council agenda mentions a drought mapping population derived from DH 40 (tolerant) and a susceptible parent, with Bhagsu among eight varieties studied, but no Bhagsu drought rating is given.

heat.details: No Bhagsu-specific heat tolerance data. A symposium abstract mentions heat-tolerant genotypes, but Bhagsu is not identified as one of them.

salinity.details: No Bhagsu-specific salinity data. Salt tolerance screening with NaCl is mentioned in a symposium abstract, but Bhagsu's result is not given.

flood.details: No evidence found. Textbook sources note that oilseed crops, including linseed, do not tolerate waterlogging.

disease_resistance.summary: Bhagsu is described as resistant to rust (a Scribd summary lists 'resistant to rust (KL-215)', suited to utera sowing). The PMC release table also describes it as resistant to rust and powdery mildew, though the snippet wording is ambiguous. A symposium abstract lists Bhagsu among genotypes that were highly resistant (disease score 0) in a screening, but the disease is not named in the snippet.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data found in the results.

agronomic_details.yield: The Scribd summary lists 4-5 q/ha, with 37.0 (likely oil content %). The HPKV document's 400-500 q/ha figure appears to belong to a forage crop entry, not Bhagsu.
agronomic_details.stability: In AMMI analysis, Bhagsu and Surbhi were the most unstable genotypes, although both had above-average oil content. A G x E study also reported a 11.69 percent difference for Bhagsu at Dhaula Kuan.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Bred and recommended for Himachal Pradesh, in hill conditions, with dual-purpose and utera use noted in one source.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 178-209 days per the Seednet list (180-185 days per the Scribd summary)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium height, blue flowers, small brown seeds. Pedigree RL-50-3 x Surbhi, developed by the pedigree method at Palampur.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Included in multi-environment G x E trials and in an eight-line genetic analysis of seed, fibre and dual-purpose traits.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No Bhagsu-specific markers, QTL or SNP data found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None reported for Bhagsu. HPKV is developing a drought mapping population from DH 40 (tolerant) and a susceptible parent, and Bhagsu is used in other studies only as one of eight diverse lines.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not reported for this variety.

commercial_info.availability_status: limited. The HPKV Annual Report 2020-21 lists 12.00 (units as in the report) of Bhagsu (KL 215) seed, compared with 60.00 for Himani and 23.00 for Baner.

disease_resistance.summary: A release table attributes resistance to rust and moderate resistance to wilt, powdery mildew and alternaria blight to Birsa Tisi-2 (BAU 14-09). Attribution is uncertain because the same block sits next to a tomato entry. A general BAU statement says released varieties resist major diseases and pests, but this has no variety-level scoring and is not measured in the sources. Resistance ratings for Birsa Tisi-1 (high rust and alternaria resistance) are a separate release and are excluded from this variety's profile.

pest_resistance.summary: Only a general BAU statement that released varieties resist major pests was found, with no variety-level scoring. Bud fly resistance is recorded for Birsa Tisi-1 only and is excluded from this variety's profile. No pest-specific resistance evidence for Birsa Tisi-2 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Krishi Jagran reports a potential yield of 19.7 q/ha and 10.46% superiority over the national check T-397. The BAU release table gives conflicting values of 19-20 q/ha potential and 13-14 q/ha average. Average yield in CSC record: Not Available.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described as suited to the drought-prone, dryland (rainfed) ecosystem of Jharkhand. A Punjab recommendation appears beside a Birsa Tisi-2 block but is unverified and excluded.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Open-pollinated (IAUA listing). Flowers blue and bold capsules (BAU release table). Oil content reported as 36.75% (Krishi Jagran) and 42-43% (BAU release table), which conflict.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Krishi Jagran: 19.7 q/ha potential yield, 36.75% oil, 128-130 days maturity, 10.46% superior to national check T-397. (2) BAU release table: 19-20 q/ha potential, 13-14 q/ha average, 42-43% oil, 128-129 days; values conflict with item 1. (3) BAU release set (not specific to Tisi-2): 15-20% yield advantage over traditional varieties. (4) Rabi 2024-25 trial of 30 linseed genotypes including BIRSA-TISI-2 (LC) at the Ranchi-6 research farm, BAU: genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits; secondary branches, capsules per plant and seeds per capsule were the main direct contributors to yield; days to maturity had a negative direct effect. (5) Seed rate guidance of 25-30 kg/ha for linseed comes from an organic trial in which T-397 was the farmer-field variety, not Tisi-2.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: QTL/marker studies: No evidence found. A 30-genotype trial reported that genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits, which indicates genetic control of those traits. This is a trait-level inference, not a mapped QTL.
