search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as suited to the drought-prone, dryland ecosystem of Jharkhand, with resistance to major diseases and pests (general claim, not measured in the sources) -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Listed as an open-pollinated variety suited to rainfed conditions of Jharkhand -- https://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistance to rust, moderate resistance to wilt, powdery mildew and alternaria blight are attributed to Birsa Tisi-2 (BAU 14-09) in a release table, but the same block sits next to a tomato entry, so attribution is uncertain -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
General statement that the released BAU varieties resist major diseases and pests (no variety-level scoring) -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Do not confuse with Birsa Tisi-1 (a separate, earlier BAU linseed release): high rust and alternaria resistance, moderate wilt and bud fly resistance -- http://www.iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_637852580202036105.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Potential yield 19.7 q/ha, 36.75% oil, 128-30 days maturity, 10.46% superior to national check T-397 -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Conflicting values in the BAU release table: 19-20 q/ha potential, 13-14 q/ha average, 42-43% oil, 128-129 days, flowers blue, bold capsules -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Varieties were described as offering 15-20% yield advantage over traditional varieties (BAU release set, not specific to Tisi-2) -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Seed rate guidance of 25-30 kg/ha for linseed, with T-397 cited as the farmer-field variety in organic trials (not Tisi-2) -- https://icar.gov.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Organic-linseed-Tisi-Farming.pdf
Field trial of 30 linseed genotypes including BIRSA-TISI-2 (LC), rabi 2024-25, Ranchi-6 research farm, BAU -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Genotypic correlations exceeded phenotypic correlations for yield traits in the 30-genotype trial, indicating genetic control -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
Secondary branches, capsules per plant and seeds per capsule were the main direct contributors to yield; days to maturity had a negative direct effect -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
QTL/marker studies: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Birsa Tisi-2 was developed by BAU principal/chief scientist Sohan Ram -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Developing institution: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand; code BAU 14-09 -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf
Release was approved at an SVRC meeting on 24 March (year not stated in the page) with Director of Research A. Wadood -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Release year conflict: the record says 26 Oct 2022 (CSC), while the news reports describe an SVRC release that appears to be from around 2021 -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/16-all-new-high-yielding-varieties-of-crops-developed-by-this-agri-research-institution/
Institution profile: Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, established 1981; the Wikipedia infobox lists a Vice-Chancellor that conflicts with the 2021 news (Onkar Nath Singh) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS
Lead breeder: Dr Sohan Ram, BAU principal/chief scientist. No email or phone found -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Director of Research: Dr A. Wadood. No email or phone found -- https://lagatar24.com/ranchi-bau-scientists-develop-four-different-varieties-of-high-yielding-crops/
Institute postal address (Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding affiliation): Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi - 834 006, India -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
Institute website: www.bauranchi.org -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Official BAU email and phone: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
Kumar K., Alka K., Yadav N.P., Barnwal M.K., Chakraborty M., Mishra S. (year not stated; trial 2024-25). Correlation and path analysis in linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) for seed yield and yield attributing traits. Journal not identified -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/209%20CORRELATION-AND-PATH-ANALYSIS-IN-LINSEED-(Linum-usitatissimum-L.)-FOR-SEED-YIELD-AND-YIELD-ATTRIBUTING-TRAITS.pdf
Ram S.D., Singh R.S. (2002). Response of linseed (Linum usitatissimum) varieties to seeding and nutrient management under rainfed conditions. Journal of Research, Birsa Agricultural University 14(2): 193-195. Not specific to Birsa Tisi-2 -- https://medplants.blogspot.com/2012/04/linum-usitatissimum-flax-seed.html
KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports, and DOI-level records for Birsa Tisi-2: No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
BAU states that its crop breeders, seed directorate, zonal stations, KVKs and seed villages will cooperate on seed production for farmer access -- https://www.bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/
Seed sales by NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealers for Birsa Tisi-2: No evidence found
Seednet name "Birsa Tisi-3" (LINSEED (ALSI)): No evidence found under this name; all results refer to Birsa Tisi-2

RECOMMENDED STATES
Jharkhand (SVRC release for the drought-prone dryland ecosystem) -- https://krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/jharkhand-agri-research-institutes-release-16-high-yielding-crop-varieties-for-farmers/
Recommended for Punjab appears beside a Birsa Tisi-2 block but is most likely from an adjacent entry; treat as unverified -- http://iauaindia.org/publications/PUB_638236779124884630.pdf

drought.details: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) is characterized by tolerance to drought, low soil fertility, and low moisture. Breeding efforts specifically target drought stress tolerance in related Brassica species including Indian mustard and Gobhi sarson. The annexin gene is associated with general stress tolerance, including drought, in relevant Brassica species. Specific tolerance levels for PGSH 1699 are not available in the provided results.

heat.details: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) exhibits tolerance to high temperature, including terminal heat stress, with some varieties showing seed yield reduction of ≤30%. It is also tolerant to high temperatures at sowing time. Breeding programs aim to develop varieties tolerant to heat stress. Specific tolerance levels for PGSH 1699 are not available in the provided results.

salinity.details: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) is tolerant to salinity. Breeding efforts are focused on developing salt-tolerant varieties. Transgenic methodologies are being explored to investigate the impact of salt-tolerant genes, and the annexin gene is implicated in salt tolerance in relevant Brassica species. Specific tolerance levels for PGSH 1699 are not available in the provided results.

flood.details: No specific evidence of flood tolerance for Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) is found in the provided results, although floods are mentioned in general climate resilience contexts for other crops like rice.

disease_resistance.summary: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) is moderately resistant to white rust. Water stress at flowering can favor disease development.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance information for Gobhi sarson is available in the provided results, beyond a general mention of developing varieties tolerant to pests.

agronomic_details.yield: Specific average yield for 'PGSH 1699' is not available in the provided results. However, higher seed yields for Gobhi sarson have been recorded, for instance, at Palampur. A yield of 875 kg/ha with significant net returns (Rs. 15805/ha) has been observed for Gobhi sarson. Bed planting is recommended as an agronomic practice that can increase Gobhi sarson yield by 10-15% and save 20-25% irrigation water. Higher yields have also been noted under Zero Budget Natural Farming (ZBNF) practices.
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Gobhi sarson (Brassica napus) is adapted as a Rabi crop and is suitable for transplanting on raised beds. It demonstrates adaptability to various intercropping systems including Maize-Gobhi sarson, blackgram-Gobhi sarson, rice-Gobhi sarson, soybean-Gobhi sarson, toria+Gobhi sarson, and berseem+Gobhi sarson. It is considered an emerging oilseed crop in India with limited cultivation area. Field trials for Gobhi sarson have been conducted at locations such as Chatha-Jammu, Ludhiana, and Palampur. Specific adaptation details for PGSH 1699 are not available.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified in detail. Information includes mentions of seed germination and plant survival percentages during trials.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials have been conducted at Chatha-Jammu, Ludhiana, and Palampur for general Gobhi sarson performance and stress tolerance, particularly terminal heat stress. Trials also explored its performance under Zero Budget Natural Farming.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for PGSH 1699.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specified for PGSH 1699. QTLs for flood tolerance were mentioned for rice, not gobhi sarson.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: While specific genetic markers or QTLs for 'PGSH 1699' are not detailed in the provided search results, general genetic advancements in 'Gobhi sarson' (Brassica napus) include the development of 'double low' varieties (e.g., Hyola 401, GSC 5, TERI-Uttam), which implies genetic modifications for low erucic acid and low glucosinolates. Additionally, 'GSL-2' is noted as the first atrazine herbicide-resistant variety of Gobhi sarson, demonstrating successful genetic engineering for herbicide resistance. Research using transgenic methodologies for salt-tolerant genes and the role of the annexin gene in drought and salt tolerance are also mentioned in the broader context of Brassica species.

commercial_info.availability_status: Specific commercial availability details (seed corporations, KVK, private dealers, or status) for 'PGSH 1699' are not available in the provided search results. Gobhi sarson as a crop is cultivated in the recommended states.
commercial_info.private_dealers: Not specified for PGSH 1699.

seednet_fields.Parentage: Giza-7 x KLS-1, Giza-7 is an exotic dual purpose, brown seeded Egyptian plant with blue flowers and erect growth habit. KLS-1 is a Kangra local selection adapted to local conditions having brown, small seed and blue flower.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: All the traditional linseed growing areas in Mid and Low hills of H.P. under Utera system of cultivation under assured moisture conditions during rabi season.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: (A)	It is resistant to lodging. (B)	Method of sowing: Broadcasting in standing paddy in dough stage under assured moisture conditions. (C)	Seed rate: 75 kg/ha. (D)	Responsive to fertilizer upto 60 kg N/ha. (E)	Suitable for sowing under Utera system of cultivation.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect growth habit, disc shaped blue flower, pointed tip capsule and brown seeded.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
The variety has shown highly resistant reaction to rust and powdery mildew and resistant to wilt wheras national check was highly susceptible.
Highly resistant to rust under natural and artificial conditions. Resistant to Wilt under natural and artificial conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 60 kg N/ha. Method of application: Apply half dose of nitrogen after emergence of crop and rest half dose of nitrogen before flowering.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed as resistant to rust, powdery mildew and wilt -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Listed as moderately resistant to powdery mildew and moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight, under the name "JL 41 (Jawahar Alsi-41)" -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
No evidence found on drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to rust, powdery mildew and wilt (DAC notified-varieties table) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Moderately resistant to powdery mildew, moderately susceptible to Alternaria blight (AICRP release table, "JL 41") -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
Named among linseed lines in an IIOR 2022 report where whitefly, leafhopper and aphid populations peaked in late December 2021. The sentence is garbled, so the link between this variety and those pest counts is uncertain -- https://www.scribd.com/document/738239893/56-Annual-Report-IIOR-AR-2022

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release table: irrigated, Madhya Pradesh, State level, year 2011, listed range 1500-1600 with a value of 40, suitable for intercropping with sugarcane (units not stated in the snippet; the "40" may be a days or yield field) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
DAC table: year 2011, released at Hoshangabad, yield potential 40.00 and oil content 1600 (I) as listed; the columns look misaligned, so units are unverified -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
No evidence found for multi-location trial results or maturity days.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Parentage "(RL 102-7X0-7) X J-23" was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released at Hoshangabad (DAC table); the developing institution is not confirmed as JNKVV or any named station -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
No evidence found naming the lead breeder(s). The breeder search did not complete (see note below).

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, address or institute contact page for this variety was returned.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Results were general linseed reviews and reports, not papers on this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Seed-dealer, NSC, SAU or KVK sale listings for this variety or for "Jawahar Linseed-9" were not returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh: listed among recommended linseed varieties for the state, with the note that the variety suits areas of Madhya Pradesh with limited irrigated facility -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Madhya Pradesh is also given as the release state with "Irrigated" and "State" categories in the AICRP release table -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

NAME NOTES
Variety name "Jawahar Linseed-41" was matched in DAC (also as "PKDL-41") and AICRP ("JL 41 / Jawahar Alsi-41"). Seednet name "JAWAHAR LINSEED-9" produced no evidence for this variety; the ICAR-CRIDA document mentions "JLS-9" and "J-23", which I discarded as different varieties. The ICAR 2024-25 report and the Jawahar Linseed Sagar (JLS 121) entry were also discarded.

NOTE: The search tool returned a usage-limit error partway through, so the breeder/contact search and the seed-availability search did not run successfully, and the publications search returned only general linseed material. Those headings should be re-run before the record is final.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: JNKVV, Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Powarkheda, Hoshangabad- 461110 (MP).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Zone 1 of the country comprising of J&K, HP, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Hariyana.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1.	Lodging/shattering: Non lodging & non shattering. 2.	Fertilizer: Responsive to optimum doses of fertilizer (80:40:20:20:5::N:P:K:S:Zn, kg/ha). 3.	Suitability: Suitability for timely sown irrigated condition (25 October to 20 November). 4.	Medium duration. 5.	Seed rate: 30 kg/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Growth habit: semi erect. 2.	Petal aestivation: Valvate. 3.	Flower size: Medium. 4.	Flower color: Violet. 5.	Flower shape: Star. 6.	Stamen color: Colourless. 7.	Anther color:  Cream. 8.	Stigma color: Colorless. 9.	Capsul size: Medium. 10.	Seed color: Dark brown.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress:
1.	Being medium late maturing variety it escapes from both biotic and abiotic stresses ie. Major diseases, pest and drought.
2.	Fertilization and seed setting process occurs before raising the atmospheric temperature and moisture stress condition. Grain filling and dough stage is over before the
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
1.	Rust: Highly Resistant.
2.	Powdery mildew: Moderately Resistant.
3.	Wilt: Moderately Resistant.
4.	Alternaria blight: Moderately Susceptible.
(Both under natural and controlled conditions).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests:
Budfly: Moderately resistant (6.08%)
(Both under natural field conditions).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Name used: JLS-73 (variety code SLS-73). Seednet name JLS-79 has no evidence linking it to this entry; see the note under RECOMMENDED STATES.
- Directorate of Oilseeds Development characters table lists SLS-73 (JLS-73) as resistant to rust, powdery mildew and bud fly -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- A ResearchGate table of abiotic-stress-tolerant varieties lists JLS-73 (SLS-73) as "moderately resistant" to an unclear disease (text truncated in snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351224957_Abiotic_Stress_Tolerant_Crop_Varieties_Livestock_Breeds_and_Fish_Species
- Plant-disease reference lists SLS-73 (JLS-73) among rust-resistant linseed varieties, citing "Anonymous, 2022" -- https://www.plantsdiseases.com/p/diseases-of-linseed.html
- Drought, heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found for JLS-73 specifically. The review found lists JLS73 in rainfed-condition tables without tolerance data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screening (2023–24 isolates) grades JLS-73 as susceptible, with wilt incidence of 30.1–50% -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
- Rust, powdery mildew and bud fly resistance: see STRESS TOLERANCE (DOD source).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Sowing-date trial comparing PKV-NL-260, PKV-NL-97 and JLS-73 in split-plot design; PKV-NL-260 sown in the 44th meteorological week outperformed PKV-NL-97 and JLS-73 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi study in drought-prone area: JLS-73 among three cultivars, with 73.33% root colonisation at site three -- https://ijfans.org/uploads/paper/44d1a9b8e41cd079600968587e2df7a6.pdf
- Yield figure in the DOD table: 38.82 (units not stated; the oil-content column "1090 (R)" appears misaligned) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Excluded: Punjab "LS-73" trials and Nagaland "JLS-95" trials are different genotypes.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. No QTL, marker-assisted or pedigree study for JLS-73 was returned. The Fusarium SSR study characterises the pathogen, not the variety's genetics.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Release centre: Sagar, year 2011 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Institution conflict: a ResearchGate table gives LNKVV Jabalpur for JLS-73 (SLS-73), 2011, with the same states -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351224957_Abiotic_Stress_Tolerant_Crop_Varieties_Livestock_Breeds_and_Fish_Species
- Institution listed as "Not specified" in the input record. Release date in the input (2010-12-23) differs from the 2011 year in the sources.
- Named breeder: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. An ICAR IIOR linseed page lists breeder and centre contacts, but it does not name JLS-73, so it is excluded under the strict relevance rule -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed

PUBLICATIONS
- Mane, P. A. (2022). Arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal association with different cultivars of linseed in drought prone area. IJFANS, 11(12) -- https://ijfans.org/uploads/paper/44d1a9b8e41cd079600968587e2df7a6.pdf
- Authors not captured (2023/2024). Characterization of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini based on ITS and SSR markers and identification of resistance of Indian linseed. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Growth, Yield, Nutrient Uptake and Quality of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Varieties as Affected by Varying Sowing Dates. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- AICRP on Linseed, Varieties Released list (JLS 73, rainfed, 2011) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed: A Comprehensive Review. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

SEED AVAILABILITY
- JLS 73 is among varieties whose breeder-seed indent and production share was tracked for 2007-08 to 2018-19, with a share of 4.8–7.6% -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/b37b/81289b537bdd60a2fba6aac040168c05a884.pdf
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales and private dealers: No evidence found for JLS-73. The only shop result (NY Spice Shop) is for generic flax seed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Input record: Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bundelkhand UP, north-east and central Maharashtra, north-east Gujarat.
- DOD notified-variety table: Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- AICRP list: Bundelkhand part of UP, Rajasthan and MP, rainfed, 2011 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- JLS-79 (Seednet name): the DOD table lists JLS-79 as a separate entry for MP. A castor paper states JLS 79 was released in 2016, so it refers to a different variety. No evidence links JLS-79 to JLS-73 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
- No Seednet portal page was returned, so no evidence under the Seednet name for JLS-79 was found for this entry.

disease_resistance.summary: Alternaria blight: highly resistant (AICRP table). Powdery mildew: resistant (AICRP table); resistant (DOD table). Rust: resistant (DOD table only; the AICRP table does not mention rust). Wilt: resistant (DOD table); the AICRP table does not rate wilt, so the DOD rating is unconfirmed by a second source. The DOD and AICRP tables conflict on wilt and bud fly ratings.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly (Dasyneura lini): moderately resistant (AICRP table) and resistant (DOD table). The two sources conflict. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JLS-79 (linseed, variety code A0404091)

Names searched: "JLS-79" (CSC release name and Seednet name, which are identical). Variant spellings found in the evidence: "JLS 79" (AICRP table) and "Jawahar Linseed Sagar-79" (MDPI review). Four searches were run in total. Most results were about other linseed varieties or unrelated flax products, and those were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for JLS-79 was found. The only stress material was general linseed reviews that do not name JLS-79. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2023.1165580/full (general; does not name JLS-79)

DISEASE AND PEST
- AICRP table: JLS-79 is listed as irrigated, released 2016, for Madhya Pradesh, with a "highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to bud fly" rating. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- DOD (Directorate of Oilseeds Development) table: JLS-79 is listed as resistant to rust, powdery mildew, wilt and bud fly. This conflicts with the AICRP table on bud fly and wilt ratings, and the AICRP table does not mention rust. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Field study of insect pests on JLS-79 at JNKVV College of Agriculture, Rewa, Madhya Pradesh (rabi 2020-21). Insect pests were identified on the crop in Rewa district. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342881084_Insect_herbivores_and_their_natural_enemies_in_linseed_and_their_population_dynamics
- Companion study of bud fly (Dasyneura lini) population dynamics, same JNKVV Rewa trial, names JLS-79. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential is listed as 36.85 in the DOD table and 38.82 in the AICRP table. Neither table states units. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The AICRP table also gives an unlabelled oil figure of 45.10 and an iodine value of 165.49 for this variety. The label is unclear. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- DOD describes the variety as early to medium duration. No maturity days were found. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- The AICRP table describes the variety as suitable for intercropping with pulses. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No multi-location trial results specific to JLS-79 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Searches returned no QTL, marker or pedigree study for JLS-79. The parentage field in the input is "Not specified", and no source supplied one.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The institution is JNKVV (Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya), Jabalpur, per the input record. The DOD table gives the released centre as Sagar. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- The JNKVV Rewa and Powarkheda colleges of agriculture appear in the pest studies, which used JLS-79 in trials. No named breeder was found in any source. The Rewa and Powarkheda colleges are JNKVV units and do not identify the breeder. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Directorate of Farms, JNKVV, Jabalpur (institute-level, breeder seed production; not a breeder contact): mobile 8770867088; email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com. -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms
- Postal address of the institute or division: No evidence found in the results.
- Breeder email or phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Gautam Kunal and others (2019). Insect herbivores and their natural enemies in linseed and their population dynamics. ResearchGate preprint (year as listed in the metadata; the paper text refers to the 2020-21 rabi trial). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/342881084_Insect_herbivores_and_their_natural_enemies_in_linseed_and_their_population_dynamics
- Authors not shown in the snippet (n.d.). Studies on the qualitative composition of insect pests and population dynamics of bud fly (Dasyneura lini Barnes) on linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.). PlantArchives journal, year and volume not shown in the snippet. -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/103-%20Studies%20on%20the%20Qualitative%20Composition%20of%20Insect%20Pests%20and%20Population%20Dynamics%20of%20Bud%20Fly%20(Dasyneura%20lini%20Barnes)%20on%20Linseed%20(Linum%20usitatissimum%20L.).pdf
- Authors not shown (n.d.). Performance of elite castor hybrids and varieties under rainfed Alfisols. ResearchGate. This is a castor paper that also reports JLS 79 seed indent data. Authors and year not shown in the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report with JLS-79 trial data, or DOI-bearing journal paper specific to JLS-79 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder seed indent: JLS 79 is one of the linseed varieties released in the last 10 years that were indented for breeder seed. It accounted for about 6.3% of the linseed crop indent in the cited period. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353769937_Performance_of_elite_castor_Ricinus_communis_L_hybrids_and_varieties_under_rainfed_Alfisols (this paper cites a Seednet readyreckoner page: https://seednet.gov.in/readyrecknor/Seed_III_VI.aspx)
- Seednet portal listing for JLS-79 (LINSEED (ALSI), code A0404091): No evidence found. The Seednet page was not returned by any search.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealer listings: No evidence found.
- JNKVV seed contact: see CONTACT DETAILS.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Madhya Pradesh: The DOD state-wise table lists JLS-79 among varieties notified for Madhya Pradesh from 2008 to 2019. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
- Madhya Pradesh: The AICRP table lists JLS 79 as released in 2016 for Madhya Pradesh, state level. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Conflict: A separate DOD entry for JLS-79 lists recommended states as Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, KNK and Odisha. This may belong to a different row on the same page. Treat it as unverified until checked against the DOD source. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The CSC name "Kota Alsi-6" and the Seednet name "Kota Alsi" were both searched. The evidence found uses "Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165)" (AICRP), "Kota Alsi-6" (Dholi seed directory), and "KOTA ALSI 6 (RL 13165)" (PMC review). No Seednet page was retrieved, so no evidence is attributed to the Seednet name directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Irrigated-condition classification with no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Listed among irrigated-condition varieties in a national linseed genetic-resources table. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to Kota Alsi-6 found in the four searches.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rated moderately resistant to powdery mildew and moderately resistant to Alternaria blight. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Bud fly resistance is not stated for this entry; bud fly tolerance is attributed to the rainfed sister line Kota Barani Alsi 6 (RL 15584) on the same page, so it should not be assumed for Kota Alsi-6. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturity. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Table row shows 1277 and 35.04 with no column labels; these are most likely mean seed yield (kg/ha) and oil content (%), but the page does not confirm this. Presented at Central 85th CVRC meeting. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No multi-location trial report specific to Kota Alsi-6 was found. The Kota-region sustainability-index study names other genotypes (PA-1, PA-2, KB-3, KB-4), not this variety. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019.v8.i4.8857/studies-on-sustainability-index-for-selecting-stable-genotypes-of-linseed-ltemgtlinum-usitatissimumltemgt-l-in-south-eastern-plain-zone-of-rajasthan

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree recorded as RLC 25127 x RL 26016. The input record says "Not specified", so this is a discrepancy to resolve against CSC minutes. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- No QTL, marker or genomic study naming this variety was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder or lead scientist name: No evidence found. Searches returned no named breeder.
- Developing institution: Agriculture University, Kota, which lists Kota Alsi 6 among linseed varieties released or identified in its assessment period, with the scientists credited with developing the technologies. -- https://www.aukota.org/notifications/21_SSR-Agriculture-University-Kota.pdf
- Notification: 2020, No. 3482 E, 7 October 2020 (the input release date is 9 November 2020; this discrepancy should be checked). -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- Station: Agriculture University, Kota, Rajasthan (linseed research station not named in the evidence). -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_University,_Kota

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute website: aukota.org. No official email, phone or postal address for the institute or linseed division was found in the retrieved pages. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_University,_Kota
- Named officials (for reference only; the Wikipedia page lists two different vice-chancellors, Dinesh Chandra Joshi appointed 2019 and Dr. Vimla Dunkwal, so verify on aukota.org): not linked to this variety. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_University,_Kota
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. PMC review, which lists Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165) with notification details -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- AICRP-Linseed. Varieties Released (national list entry for Kota Alsi 6 (RL 13165)). AICRP Linseed website -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No peer-reviewed paper, thesis (KrishiKosh), AICRP annual report chapter or conference paper that names Kota Alsi-6 was found. Two Kota papers were excluded because they name other varieties, not this one.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Directorate of Seed, Dholi (Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University) listed Kota Alsi-6 among rabi seed availability for 2026-27, with quantity ranges shown (06-12, units not stated on page). -- https://rpcau.ac.in/directorate-of-seed-dholi/
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales listings beyond Dholi: No evidence found. Flipkart, IndiaMART and Amazon listings are generic alsi/flaxseed products, not this variety, and were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Irrigated; Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal and Assam. Matches the input list. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

disease_resistance.summary: Alternaria blight: moderately resistant (MR) per the AICRP release table. Powdery mildew: resistant per the AICRP release entry. Alternaria blight reactions in coordinated IVT-Rainfed trials (2010-11) at several locations were a mix of MR, MS, S and R scores; the digest does not attribute these scores to KB-3 individually at each location. Wilt (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini): reaction not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: described as resistant in the AICRP release entry and as tolerant in the release listing. No quantitative bud fly scores were found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: Sustainability-index study in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha (approximately 1257 kg/ha). The AICRP release table lists figures of 1370 and 38.73 against this variety, but column headings were not captured, so their meaning (likely yield in kg/ha and oil percentage) is unconfirmed. The CSC average_yield field gives units only (Kg/Ha) with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: Sustainability index of 89.79% in the south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan study, where the variety was suggested as a breeding parent. No additional multi-location yield data for KB-3 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed conditions; south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan (sustainability-index study). Recommended state: Rajasthan. Broader agro-climatic adaptation details were not found in the retrieved sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified (days not given in the digest; the AICRP listing describes the variety as early-maturing)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed described as light brown and medium-sized in the AICRP release entry. Other morphological characteristics: Not specified in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Coordinated IVT-Rainfed trials, 2010-11: Alternaria blight reaction recorded at several locations with a mix of MR, MS, S and R scores. (2) Seed rate and fertility level optimisation under rainfed conditions, 2012-13: a seed yield table is present in the source, but values were not legible in the snippet, so no yield figures can be reported. (3) Sustainability-index study, south-eastern plain zone of Rajasthan: KB-3 yielded about 12.57 q/ha with a sustainability index of 89.79%, and was suggested as a breeding parent. (4) AICRP release table: figures of 1370 and 38.73 listed against the variety, meaning unconfirmed. No additional multi-location trial results were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for KB-3 specifically. KB-3 appears only as a reference variety in an SSR-marker profiling study of Indian and exotic germplasm; this is not a variety-specific genetic study. Parentage: not specified in the variety record. An ISOR table row reads 'Kota Barani 2015 Triveni x RL-1011 Kota', but it cannot be confirmed as belonging to KB-3.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Listed under moderate resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly on the DOD notified-variety table, with a yield potential of 37.95 (unit not shown in the snippet) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
In a 2022-23 Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini screen, LSL-93 was graded 4 (susceptible, 30.1-50% wilt incidence), which conflicts with the DOD "moderately resistant to wilt" entry -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to LSL-93. The PMC review lists LSL93 among rainfed-condition varieties, but gives no tolerance data -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew, wilt, rust and bud fly (DOD notified table, Maharashtra) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx
Wilt susceptibility in the Fusarium screen (grade 4) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
Bud fly screening (Dasyneura lini) lists "LSL 93 (ZC)" in the group rated moderately resistant (>10-25% damage). The snippet is partial and the source is a 2025 journal PDF, so treat it as indicative -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Nagaland irrigated foothill trial, seven varieties including LSL-93: LSL-93 had the lowest seed yield (671.33 kg/ha), fewest capsules per plant (29.13) and lowest oil yield, but the highest test weight (9.08 g) and earliest 50% flowering (65 days) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6060 and https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6042
Nagaland University, Medziphema trial: the authors' conclusions on LSL-93 are not in the snippets (listed under the same trial; no separate finding) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6042
Fertilizer-level trial with LSL-93, RLC-148 and NL-260 under NPK levels 0-30:30:30 kg/ha; LSL-93 was the reference variety and differed from the others in growth and yield, with NL-260 at par except for oil content. Location and year not captured -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=2&ArticleId=10545
Latur College of Agriculture, Rabi 2023-24, nano-urea and phosphorus foliar trial on LSL-93: seed yield across treatments ranged from 890.31 to 1401.22 kg/ha, protein 18.6-28.54% -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue11S/PartE/S-8-11-54-195.pdf
Germplasm evaluation (2,576 accessions, two seasons, ICAR-NBPGR and Akola): LSL93 used as the best check for earliness, with 132.19 days to physiological maturity -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL or marker-trait associations specific to LSL-93. The Nature 2024 germplasm study and the Fusarium SSR study use LSL93 only as a check or differential entry, not as a genetic study of the variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8 ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
No parentage found. The task form lists "Not specified", and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Released centre listed as Latur on the DOD notified table (2019), with the notification recorded as 2019 S.O. 3220(E), 5 September 2019 in the PMC review. Developing institution given in the task record: VNMKV, Oilseeds Research Station (Latur) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx ; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist(s) for LSL-93. The ICAR-IIOR linseed page lists breeder posts and centre vacancies, but does not name LSL-93 or its developers -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
ICAR Nagaland scientist Dr Harendra Verma recommended LSL-93 for seed purposes in an extension report. He is not identified as a breeder of this variety -- https://www.morungexpress.com/icar-nagaland-centre-conducts-workshop-on-promoting-oilseeds

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for an email, phone, postal address or institute contact page specific to LSL-93 or the VNMKV Oilseeds Research Station, Latur.
Not attributed to this variety: the PDKV AICRP linseed breeder entry (Nagpur, phone 0712-2541245) at http://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm is a different AICRP centre and is not evidence for LSL-93.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not captured (2025). Screening of Linseed Germplasm against Bud Fly (Dasyneura lini). Journal of Plant Protection/UPJOZ manuscript (PDF) -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf
Authors not captured (year not captured). Molecular Advances to Combat Different Biotic and Abiotic Stresses in Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.): A Comprehensive Review. PMC review -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
Authors not captured (year not captured). Characterization of Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini based on ITS and SSR Markers and identification of resistance of Indian Linseed to Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. lini. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12095111/
Authors not captured (2024). Effect of foliar application of nano-urea on growth, yield ... (linseed, Latur, Rabi 2023-24). Biochemistry journal (Biochem Journal, vol. 8, issue 11S) -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue11S/PartE/S-8-11-54-195.pdf
Authors not captured (2022). Response of different linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) varieties to fertilizer levels. The Pharma Innovation Journal, 11(2) -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2022&vol=11&issue=2&ArticleId=10545
Authors not captured (year not captured). Performance of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Varieties in Foothills of Nagaland under Irrigated Condition. Indian Journal of Agricultural Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/indian-journal-of-agricultural-research/A-6060
Authors not captured (year not captured). Yield Attributes and Economics of Linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.) Cultivars under Irrigated Uphill Condition of Indian Himalayan Region in Nagaland. Agricultural Science Digest -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-6042
Authors not captured (2024). Leveraging genetic resource diversity and identification of trait-enriched superior genotypes for accelerated improvement in linseed (Linum usitatissimum L.). Scientific Reports -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-71044-8
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or ICAR report naming LSL-93 was found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, a KVK, an SAU or a dealer for LSL-93. The results were retail flax/linseed packets from overseas shops (UK and US) and cover-crop sellers, which are unrelated to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Maharashtra -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Linseed.aspx (DOD notified table, released at Latur)

Search note: four web searches were run (variety/release, breeder/institution/contact, research papers, seed availability). The variety name and Seednet name are identical ("LSL-93"), so no name-variant split was needed.

drought.details: No specific drought tolerance level for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified in the provided results. Linseed generally experiences drought as a major abiotic stress, and research aims to develop drought-resilient varieties through multi-environment phenotyping and molecular studies. Pratap Alsi-2, a different variety, is noted as tolerant to drought. (Results 2, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 31, 32, 37, 38, 40, 43)

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified. Elevated temperature (heat stress) is reported to impact Linum usitatissimum production. (Result 19)

salinity.details: No specific salinity tolerance level for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified, though 'Pratap Alsi-1 (RLU-6)' was part of studies involving treatment with neutral salt and alkaline conditions. Salinity is a known detrimental constraint for flax (linseed) production, and research focuses on identifying salinity-tolerant genotypes for breeding. (Results 3, 10, 21, 22, 24, 25, 29, 34)

flood.details: No specific information on flood tolerance for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was identified. Pratap Alsi-2, a different variety, is noted as tolerant to both submergence and drought. (Result 43)

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease resistance information for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was found. General linseed research involves screening for biotic stress like Alternaria blight and linseed bud fly. (Results 6, 10)

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance information for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) was found. General linseed research involves screening for biotic stress like linseed bud fly. (Results 6, 10)

agronomic_details.yield: Not specified for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) in the provided results. For reference, a general linseed variety was reported with 950-1000 kg/ha, and 'Pratap Alsi-2' with 1960 kg/ha. (Results 6, 14)

agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Rajasthan. It is listed as a linseed variety suitable for the region. (Results 14, 26, 28, 39)
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not available in provided table. Not specified for Pratap Asalia-1 (Pratap Alsi-1) in the provided results. 'Pratap Alsi-2' was reported to mature in 129 days. (Result 14)

drought.details: Fairly resistant to drought and tolerant to moisture stress, also indicated as drought tolerant. It can tolerate both submergence and drought situations.

heat.details: Tolerant to heat stress and shows better stress tolerance indices. It is also mentioned as heat tolerant.

salinity.details: Can withstand slight alkalinity and salinity. It is recommended as a salt-tolerant improved variety and is considered a good option for sodic soils. It was part of studies involving neutral salt and alkaline treatment for linseed genotypes.

flood.details: Tolerant to flood situations and suitable for flood-prone Eastern Plain Zone IIIB.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to rust, powdery mildew, wilt, and Alternaria blight. Tolerant to phyllody, leaf curl, and Jammu and Kashmir virus.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant/tolerant to bud fly.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary between 1957 kg/ha (for irrigated conditions, 'I') and 1960 kg/ha. It is also described as a high yielding variety for irrigated conditions, capable of producing 2000-2200 kg/ha (20-22 q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly mentioned, but recommended for varied agro-climatic zones and tolerant to multiple stresses, indicating adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Rajasthan, specifically suitable for the climatic conditions of South-Eastern Rajasthan, including the Humid South Eastern Plain Zone V and Flood Prone Eastern Plain zone IIIB. Linseed thrives in cool seasons and moderate to cool temperatures. It grows well on medium soil and is tolerant to a soil pH range of 5.0-7.0.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: White seeded.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tested and released from Kota, Rajasthan. Yield data suggests performance under irrigated conditions.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to linseed bud fly (Dasyneura lini) in a Bihar AU Sabour field screen of 150 germplasm lines, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24, with bud fly infestation in the >10-25% range. agronomic_details.yield: CSC record average_yield: 511 kg/ha. This value is not confirmed by any retrieved page. Yield values for RLC-138 from trial pages were not found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record adaptation_ecology: Chhattisgarh and Odisha, where moisture is available in the field of medium to late duration rice varieties; utera (under moisture stress), rabi season, and rice-based relay cropping ecosystem. The rice-fallow listing (see field_trials) supports suitability for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India. CSC agronomic_features also report 2.20 B:C ratio against national check T-397 (1.68), zonal check Shekhar (2.08) and JLS-9 (1.73) for Zone-IV; non-lodging and non-shattering; responsive to recommended fertilizer doses; broadcasting at milking to drooping stage of paddy. These CSC features are not confirmed by retrieved pages.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Plant height and branching for RLC-138 were not found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nutrient-level (RDF) study with five linseed varieties (RLC-92, RLC-133, RLC-138, RLC-143, RLC-148): the snippet reports RLC-138 among the best-performing entries for yield and cost, but table values are fragmentary and unit-labelled unclearly, so no quantitative result is reported. (2) Rice-fallow cultivation: RLC-138 listed among linseed cultivars judged promising for rice-fallow cultivation in eastern India, alongside RLC-143 and BAU 06-03; no yield data given. (3) Bud fly screen at Bihar AU Sabour (150 germplasm lines, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24): RLC-138 moderately resistant, with bud fly infestation in the >10-25% range. (4) Bold-seeded genetic variability study (Markandey et al., 2022): RLC-138 used as one of five checks among 40 bold-seeded genotypes, rabi 2021-22; no RLC-138 result reported. The cluster-mean maturity table in that paper is not variety-specific and was discarded. (5) Association analysis study (2024): RLC-138 listed as a check from AICRP Linseed IGKV, rabi 2022-23; no RLC-138 result reported. (6) Characterisation of 23 IGKV released varieties (Acharya et al., 2023), rabi 2022-23: RLC-138 among varieties characterised; no result reported.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Name matched: RLC-138 (CSC and Seednet names are identical; no Seednet page was retrieved)

DISEASE AND PEST
Name matched: RLC-138
Bud fly moderate resistance finding above -- https://mbi-prh.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2025/JANUARY/10_Jan_2025/2024_UPJOZ_4401/Ms_UPJOZ_4401.pdf

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: AICAR on Linseed, Department of Genetics & plant Breeding, IGKV, Raipur, CG-492012 India.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for Rainfed condition of Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chhattisgarh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: i)	Lodging/shattering: Non lodging & non shattering. ii)	Fertilizer: Responsive to recommended doses of fertilizer. iii)	Suitability: Suitable for timely sown (mid of October to mid of November) showed 55.4% superiority over national check T-397at 100% RDF in rainfed condition. iv)	Spacing: 25-30cm Row-Row.

Capsule size: Medium. 13.	Seed colour: Brown  14.	No. Of Capsules/plant:56 15.	No. Of seeds/capsules:8.33 16.	1000seed weight: 6.9gm 17.	Oil content(%):32.1 18.	Oil yield (Kg/ha): 395.7

drought.details: The variety is suitable for timely sown conditions (mid-October to mid-November) and showed superiority in rainfed conditions, suggesting a degree of tolerance to moisture stress. Linseed in general is known to experience moisture stress.

heat.details: No specific information regarding heat tolerance for RLC-161 was found in the provided data.

salinity.details: No specific information regarding salinity tolerance for RLC-161 was found. However, general molecular advances in linseed research indicate that specific miRNAs (miR398a and miR530) are linked to salt stress tolerance in flax.

flood.details: No information regarding flood tolerance for RLC-161 was found in the provided data.

disease_resistance.summary: Not Specified

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified

agronomic_details.yield: The variety showed 55.4% superiority over the national check T-397 at 100% Recommended Dose of Fertilizer (RDF) in rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety is suitable for timely sown conditions (mid-October to mid-November) and has demonstrated superior performance under rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for timely sown conditions (mid-October to mid-November) in rainfed environments. It is responsive to recommended doses of fertilizer.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: RLC-161 is a non-lodging and non-shattering variety. Recommended spacing is 25-30 cm row-to-row.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials indicated a 55.4% superiority in yield over the national check T-397 when grown under 100% RDF in rainfed conditions during timely sowing periods.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: General linseed research has identified two miRNAs, miR398a and miR530, linked to salt stress tolerance in flax. However, no specific genetic markers or QTLs for RLC-161 were identified in the provided information.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTL information for RLC-161 was provided.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: In the broader context of linseed, miR398a and miR530 have been reported to be linked to salt stress tolerance.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RLC 164 (linseed / ALSI)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RLC 164". The AICRP page writes it as "RLC-164", and I treated that as the same variety. No search returned a Seednet portal page, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found. Four searches were run, one per topic plus one extra for seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The AICRP release table classes RLC-164 as rainfed, not irrigated or utera -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to RLC 164. A general statement that linseed is drought tolerant was found, but it is not about this variety, so I discarded it -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4912539/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Under artificial conditions it is moderately resistant to Alternaria blight and moderately susceptible to powdery mildew. Under natural conditions it is moderately resistant to Alternaria blight and to bud fly -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Same table text also contains "highly resistant to Alternaria blight, resistant to powdery mildew, moderately resistant to bud fly". The snippet does not clearly tie this to the RLC-164 row, so it is unverified -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Bud fly resistance is noted in the same source. No separate bud fly trial data for RLC 164 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The AICRP row gives RLC-164's release details (CVRC 2020) alongside two unlabelled numbers, 1161 and 32.6. The column headers are not visible in the snippet, so I cannot assign them to yield, maturity or oil content -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No evidence found for field-trial or multi-location yield results for RLC 164. The Chhattisgarh sowing-date trial tested RLC-92, not RLC 164, so I discarded it -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025.v8.i9.M.3881
- The IGKV 2023 genetic analysis study names RLC-92, RLC-133 and RLC-143 only, so I discarded it -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/?year=2023&vol=12&issue=6&ArticleId=21111

GENETICS AND QTL
- RLC 164 is listed among national linseed genetic resources in a seed-type table. This is a germplasm listing, not a genetic study -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- RLC-164 appears in a DUS descriptor context, with stigma-position and related trait groupings in the linseed variety characterisation -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- No QTL or marker study specific to RLC 164 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is attributed to Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur. This comes from the input record. The AICRP release row retrieved does not show the institution name in the visible text -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The IGKV Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Raipur is the institute-level unit that works on linseed. No lead breeder name for RLC 164 was found -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- The Chhattisgarh linen-fibre paper lists RLC 164 among seven recent IGKV-linked varieties released after 2012, but it does not name a breeder -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder name, official email, phone or contact-page URL for RLC 164 was found.
- Institute-level address only: Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya, Raipur-492 012 (Chhattisgarh), India -- https://www.indianjournals.com/article/ejpb-8-2-001
- Same address form appears on another IGKV College of Agriculture paper, which names no breeder for RLC 164 -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137093
- Individual authors' names on other IGKV papers were not attributed to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (2023). Title not retrieved. The Pharma Innovation Journal 12(8): 2203-2206. Mentions RLC-164 in a DUS descriptor context for IGKV-released linseed varieties -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- No DOI or full bibliographic record was retrieved for this item. Its author list must be confirmed from the journal before citing.
- No ICAR/AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or peer-reviewed field paper specific to RLC 164 was found. Other linseed papers and a KrishiKosh budfly thesis were retrieved but do not name RLC 164, so I discarded them.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RLC 164.
- The results were non-Indian linseed sellers and a Scribd Rabi 2025-26 tentative seed availability document. The visible text of that document did not name RLC 164, so I discarded it -- https://www.scribd.com/document/902605334/Rabi-2025-26-Seed-Availability-Tentative

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP release row gives the recommended zone as Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chhattisgarh, with release by CVRC in 2020 (85th CVRC, dated 09-11-2020) -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- The input record says "Jammu & Kashmir", while the source says "Jammu".

Institute-level evidence: IGKV reports that it has released 16 linseed varieties, with RLC 161, RLC 164 and RLC 167 among the seven most recent (released after 2012). -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue3/PartK/8-4-8-452.pdf ; https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- IGKV's linseed work sits in the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Raipur, which hosts an AICRP on Linseed research farm. -- https://www.chemistryjournals.net/archives/2022/vol4issue2/PartA/4-2-50-637.pdf

- Telephone directory 2021 (older listing): Office 0771-2443419, Fax 91-771-2442302, website www.igau.edu.in, email vcigkv@gmail.com, pa2vc.igkv@gmail.com. These may be superseded. -- https://igkv.ac.in/images/tp2021.pdf
- Journal of Agricultural Issues editorial office: jai@igkv.ac.in, Telefax 0771-2972070, website https://igkv.ac.in/ . -- https://igkv.ac.in/__files/JAI/1/Journal_pub_1__uctfbwn0aq54uzg3dmwcx50h_202204051610516PM046.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Pharma Innovation Journal 2023, 12(8): 2203-2206. Study of IGKV Raipur linseed genotypes in Rabi 2022-23, in which RLC-167 appears among the genotypes and in colour and seed-trait groupings. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue8/PartZ/12-7-733-170.pdf
- Indian Journal-style list (Biochem journal, IJABR 2024; 8(3): 968-970). Mentions RLC 167 only in a list of IGKV releases; not a trial on this variety. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2024/vol8issue3/PartK/8-4-8-452.pdf
- International Journal of Fiber and Innovative Hybrid Materials (inence), charkha paper. Lists RLC 167 among IGKV releases only. Authors not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://journal.inence.org/index.php/ijfiahm/article/download/211/140/301
- Note: The Pharma Journal 2023 (12(6)) and IJCMAS 2022 papers name other IGKV genotypes but not RLC 167, so I excluded them. No peer-reviewed trial or thesis on RLC 167 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seednet and seed-dealer sources were not returned by the search. The results included a National Seed Project at IGKV Raipur (Badshahbhoge), but no page links it to RLC 167, so it is not listed as a source. -- https://cgcert.com/wp/wp-content/uploads/2023/05/List-of-Individual-Producer.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICRP-Linseed table lists RLC-167 as irrigated, released by CVRC 2020 (85th CVRC), for Jammu, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab and Chhattisgarh. The source says "Jammu", not "Jammu & Kashmir" as recorded in the input. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

- variety_name ("RLC 167") and seednet_variety_name ("RLC 167") are identical. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so all evidence above refers to the AICRP/IGKV name "RLC-167" or "RLC 167" and has not been checked against Seednet.

drought.details: A Patna Press article (BAU Best AICRP-Linseed award, 2024-25) describes Sabour Tisei-4 as drought-tolerant and suited to climate-change adaptation. The article uses the spelling 'Sabour Tisei-4' and gives no BRLS code, although the digest treats it as this variety. This is a press claim, not peer-reviewed data, and no quantitative drought trial data, physiological mechanism, or yield-under-stress result was found for Tisi-4.

heat.details: The same Patna Press article describes Sabour Tisei-4 as heat-tolerant. This is an unverified press claim, not peer-reviewed data. No quantitative heat trial data, sowing-date response, or physiological mechanism specific to Tisi-4 was found.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance is credited to Sabour Tisi-4 in any source in the digest. The Patna Press article attributes Alternaria blight and powdery mildew tolerance to Sabour Tisei-3, not Tisi-4. No evidence was found for resistance to any disease in BRLS 121 / Tisi-4.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: Kumari et al. (2024) screened 150 linseed genotypes at BAU Sabour farm (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24). BRLS 121 appears in a 28-entry list of germplasm, but the snippet does not state its reaction (resistant or susceptible). Status is unresolved. No other pest resistance evidence was found.

agronomic_details.yield: The original variety data lists an average yield of 13 quintal/ha. The digest does not independently confirm this value. It states that the BAU yield values in the sources refer to other entries. No Tisi-4-specific yield data was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Uttar Pradesh (excluding Bundelkhand), Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam, and Nagaland, as stated in the original variety data and the release press coverage. No agro-climatic validation data was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP linseed trials, rabi 2019-20: BRLS 121 and BRLS 110-4 were promoted from IVT irrigated to AVT 1st year irrigated. This is the only trial-advancement result for BRLS 121 in the digest, and no yield, oil content, or maturity values are given. (2) Kumari et al. (2024) bud fly screening at BAU Sabour farm, rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24: 150 linseed genotypes were screened, and BRLS 121 is among a 28-entry germplasm list, but its reaction is not stated. No Tisi-4-specific maturity, grain yield, oil content, or sowing-date trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SABOUR TISI-4 (BRLS 121) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: The release-minutes name and the Seednet name are both given as "Sabour Tisi-4 (BRLS 121)". I did not reach the Seednet portal, so all evidence below is from the release-notification press coverage and BAU documents. Under "Sabour Tisei-4", the Patna Press article uses a spelling variant of the same name. Those mentions refer to this variety, but the article gives no BRLS code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Patna Press article (BAU Best AICRP-Linseed award, 2024-25) describes Sabour Tisei-4 as drought- and heat-tolerant and suited to climate-change adaptation. This is a press claim, not peer-reviewed data. -- https://patnapress.com/bau-sabour-best-linseed-centre-award-2024-25/
STRESS TOLERANCE -- Salinity, flood, submergence, and waterlogging tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST -- The same Patna Press article attributes Alternaria blight and powdery mildew tolerance to Sabour Tisei-3, not Tisi-4. No disease resistance is credited to Tisi-4 in any source. -- https://patnapress.com/bau-sabour-best-linseed-centre-award-2024-25/
DISEASE AND PEST -- Bud fly: Kumari et al. (2024) screened 150 linseed genotypes at BAU Sabour farm (rabi 2022-23 and 2023-24) for bud fly reaction. BRLS 121 appears in a 28-entry list of germplasm, but the snippet does not state its reaction (resistant or susceptible). Treat as unresolved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389249120_Article_noUPJOZ4401_Original_Research_Article_Kumari_et_al

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- BRLS 121 and BRLS 110-4 were promoted from IVT irrigated to AVT 1st year irrigated in AICRP trials (rabi 2019-20). -- https://bausabour.ac.in/album/File104_12_202311_41_57PIMG1.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity, grain yield, oil content, and sowing-date response for Tisi-4 specifically: No evidence found. The BAU yield values in the sources refer to other entries.

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage "(NL 260 x Shekhar) x PKDL 71" was not verified in any search result. Shekhar appears only as a zonal check in the Kumari et al. bud-fly trial. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389249120_Article_noUPJOZ4401_Original_Research_Article_Kumari_et_al
GENETICS AND QTL -- QTL, marker, or genomic-selection studies specific to BRLS 121: No evidence found. The Patna Press article mentions genomic selection in general terms for BAU varieties, not for this variety.

Chaudhary, and A. Lokeshwar Reddy, is named for the 2021-22 to 2023-24 project team that developed the BAU linseed varieties including Tisei-4. -- https://patnapress.com/bau-sabour-best-linseed-centre-award-2024-25/

drought.details: Identified as drought tolerant (e.g., in Annual Report 2022-23 and Journal of Oilseeds Research). Research has focused on improving drought resilience (flax) and studying drought stress at the seedling stage through PEG.

heat.details: While research on flax cultivars for high temperature stress is mentioned in the context of Sabour Tisi-3, a direct statement of its heat tolerance level is not provided. It is linked to climate change stress tolerant varieties.

salinity.details: Listed among genotypes developed after treatment with neutral salt and alkaline, and is associated with research on salt-tolerant microbial inoculants. It is described as a salt-tolerant variety.

flood.details: No information found regarding flood tolerance specifically.

disease_resistance.summary: Sabour Tisi-3 is described as multiple disease resistant. It is specifically resistant to powdery mildew, rust, and downy mildew. It shows moderate resistance to wilt and Alternaria blight. It is generally effective against many plant diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: Sabour Tisi-3 is moderately resistant to linseed bud fly. It is generally resistant/tolerant to biotic stress including pests.

agronomic_details.yield: High yielding, with reported seed yield of approximately 5.47 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for twelve states of India, including Uttar Pradesh (excluding Bundelkhand), Bihar, and Jharkhand. It is suitable for Utera conditions (relay cropping system) of zone-II&III, indicating good adaptability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to Utera conditions of Zone-II&III and widely adaptable across multiple states (Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttar Pradesh, and 9 other unnamed states).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed contains 24-36% oil and 71–75% linoleic acid.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tested in disease screening nurseries of AICRP-small millets. Involved in linseed experimental plots and farmer training programs.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific QTLs, SNPs, or SSR markers are detailed for Sabour Tisi-3 in the provided results. However, it is mentioned in the context of molecular advances to combat biotic and abiotic stresses, and marker-assisted breeding is a research focus at the developing institution.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Research mentions bisulphite sequencing in flax related to high temperature stress and a novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for irrigated condition of Zone-II of linseed growing area of India which includes states of Uttar Pradesh Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam and Nagaland.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: i.	Lodging/Shattering: Noon lodging and non Shattering. ii.	Fertilizer: Responsive to recommended doses of Fertilizers. iii.	Suitability: Suitable for timely sown (last week of October first week of November) RDF in irrigated condition. iv.	Spacing: 25-30 cm R-R
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Flower shape-Funnel, petel aestivation-Valvate, stamen-colorless, flower size-medium.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: TL 99 showed resistance to wilt & rust; whereas moderately susceptible to alternaria blight & powdery mildew under Unifom Disease Nursey Trial under natural condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Modertaely resisatnce to linseed bud fly in breeding trials.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Fertilizer with 40:20:20kg/ha, N,P&K receptively at the Basal application. *Phosphors should be applied through single phosphors. Foliar sprya of ura (2%) at pre flowering stage.

drought.details: TL 99 is identified as a drought tolerant linseed variety, showing moisture stress tolerance. It has been studied under rainfed moisture stress conditions to assess its drought tolerant morpho-physiological traits and is also noted for its tolerance to low moisture stress.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to heat stress, showing better stress tolerance indices. It is specifically mentioned to be tolerant to high temperature at the time of sowing and is generally resilient to environmental stresses including heat.

salinity.details: TL 99 shows good salinity tolerance, described as fairly tolerant to salinity. It is tolerant to salinity at the time of sowing and has been screened after treatment with neutral salt and alkaline conditions.

flood.details: Na

disease_resistance.summary: TL 99 exhibits tolerance to necrosis disease and is broadly described as resistant/tolerant to various diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety shows resistance/tolerance to pests, consistent with attributes of recently released BARC varieties.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield ranges from 1300-1400 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: While specific stability data is not provided, its recommendation across multiple states (Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Assam, Nagaland) suggests adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for timely sowing (last week of October to first week of November) with Recommended Dose of Fertilizers (RDF) under irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: TL 99 is non-lodging and non-shattering. It is responsive to recommended doses of fertilizers, with a recommended row-to-row spacing of 25-30 cm. It features a black seed coat and recorded high protein (27.72 g/100g) and total ash (4.55 g/100g) content.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been studied under rainfed moisture stress conditions. It is considered a promising edible quality linseed (LINOLA) and has been used in efforts to develop low ALA edible grade linseed oil.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular analysis for identification of molecular markers, specifically involving FAD3A and FAD3B genes, has been conducted for TL 99.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs are identified in the provided search results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: TL 99 possesses a unique fatty acid composition, notably having very low linolenic acid (2-5%) and being recognized as the first low ALA (<5%) variety in India. It also has Linoleic Acid at 58.9%. Molecular analysis with FAD3A and FAD3B genes is linked to developing its low ALA edible grade linseed oil.

drought.details: No drought trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. The only related evidence is species-level: little millet (Panicum sumatrense) as a species is reported to tolerate drought, salinity and waterlogging. This is not specific to DHLM-28-4 and cannot be attributed to the variety.

heat.details: No heat stress trial or evidence specific to DHLM-28-4 was found in the digest.

salinity.details: No salinity trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. Species-level reports indicate little millet tolerates salinity; this is not variety-specific.

flood.details: No flood trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found. Species-level reports indicate little millet tolerates waterlogging; this is not variety-specific.

disease_resistance.summary: No specific disease is named as resisted by DHLM-28-4 in any source. A ResearchGate-hosted promotional page describes the variety as having pest and disease resilience, without field data. A popular-science article claims natural resistance to pests and diseases without naming pathogens. The same ResearchGate source mentions strong resistance to an unnamed pest or disease, but the text is truncated and the target is unverified.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly (Atherigona species) is the only pest named. The ResearchGate source describes DHLM-28-4 as shoot-fly resistant and reports a shoot-fly tolerance figure of 19.42%, but the source does not clarify the scoring basis and is a promotional page without field data. An ICAR/AICRP proceedings report gives the peak shoot-fly timing in small millets (second half of August screening window); it does not provide resistance data for DHLM-28-4.

agronomic_details.yield: Input record gives 7.00 to 7.70 Kg/Ha. The ResearchGate-hosted source reports grain yield of 17.14 q/ha (about 1,714 kg/ha) and fodder yield of 6.5 t/ha. The input value and the reported grain yield differ by roughly two orders of magnitude and the input unit appears inconsistent with the source; this discrepancy is unresolved.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or multi-year stability analysis was found. Evaluation years are given as 2013-2014 by one source.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Andhra Pradesh per the input record and the global-agriculture.com source. No agro-climatic analysis beyond these state listings was found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: Grain yield exceeded national checks OLM-203 and JK-8 by 9.59% and 11.21% respectively in one passage of the ResearchGate-hosted source. The same source gives 11.95% over OLM-203 in another passage, so the check margins are internally inconsistent. Evaluation years are given as 2013-2014. Maturity of 85-90 days is reported by the nutrichemsci.com article, which conflicts with the 114-116 day input value. The release year reported by the ResearchGate-hosted source is 2021, which conflicts with the 2023 input release year. No multi-location trial data beyond these summary figures was found.
