DHLM-28-4 (LMV 513) -- little millet (Panicum sumatrense) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The CSC minutes name and the Seednet name are both "DHLM-28-4 (LMV 513)", so all evidence below refers to that name. No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so Seednet-specific fields (crop name, notification details) are unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Little millet as a species is reported to tolerate drought, salinity and waterlogging; this is species-level, not specific to DHLM-28-4 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12769566/
- A study reports the variety maintaining a shoot-fly tolerance figure of 19.42%; the source does not clarify the scoring basis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence trial data specific to DHLM-28-4 was found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The variety is described as shoot-fly resistant and as having pest and disease resilience, though the source is a promotional page without field data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- A popular-science article claims natural resistance to pests and diseases without naming pathogens or pests -- https://www.nutrichemsci.com/posts/lmv513-the-little-millet-revolutionizing-climateresilient-agriculture
- The same ResearchGate source mentions strong resistance to an unnamed pest/disease, but the text is truncated, so the target is unverified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- ICAR/AICRP reporting on shoot-fly peak timing in small millets (second half of August screening window) -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity of 85-90 days is reported -- https://www.nutrichemsci.com/posts/lmv513-the-little-millet-revolutionizing-climateresilient-agriculture
- Grain yield 17.14 q/ha and fodder yield 6.5 t/ha are reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Grain yield exceeded national checks OLM-203 and JK-8 by 9.59% and 11.21% respectively in one passage; the same source gives 11.95% over OLM-203 in another passage, so the check margins are inconsistent -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Evaluation years are given as 2013-2014 for the variety; release/notification is said to be 2021 by this source, which conflicts with the 2023 CSC release -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601239_Modified_crossing_SMUASB_method_for_artificial_hybridization_in_proso_millet_Panicum_miliaceum_L_and_Little_millet_Panicum_sumatrense
- Multi-location trial data beyond the summary figures above was not found -- No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No QTL, marker-assisted or mapping study specific to DHLM-28-4 was found -- No evidence found.
- Parentage/pedigree of DHLM-28-4 is not given in any source (the input record also says "Not specified") -- No evidence found.
- A chromosome-scale little millet genome paper provides species-level genomic resources and GWAS on micronutrient traits, not on this variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66716-6

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to GV-2, the same name in both variety_name and seednet_variety_name; crop: little millet)
- NAU Waghai technology sheet describes GV-2 as resistant to lodging and shattering, and lists its panicles as long, semi-compact and well branched with bold grains, with more grains per earhead and productive tillers -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- The same NAU sheet lists GV-2 as a medium-duration, early-maturing, high-yielding type that is multi-tillering and non-lodging -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf (note: the sheet's table rows are garbled, and its lodging wording differs between entries, e.g. "moderately resistant" vs "resistant")
- No GV-2-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. General little millet drought and waterlogging tolerance pages were discarded because they do not name GV-2.

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to GV-2)
- A table of improved little millet varieties lists GV-2 (2016, 115-125 days, 26-28 q/ha, Gujarat) as resistant to pests and diseases, with white and bold seeds -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
- A second listing of released little millet varieties also describes GV-2 as resistant to pests and diseases, though its text is garbled and the colour wording conflicts -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- No pathogen or pest species-level screening data for GV-2 were found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to GV-2)
- A little millet agronomy review uses GV-2 as the local check, reporting that the pure line WV-125 gave 2864 kg/ha, about 8.77 per cent above GV-2 at 2633 kg/ha -- https://renupublishers.com/images/article/ijbsv6n2i.pdf (GV-2 appears only as a comparator here)
- NAU advice for kharif GV-2 in South Gujarat heavy-rainfall zone (AES-I) recommends 40 kg N/ha and 20 kg P2O5/ha -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- GV-2 yield and duration figures conflict across sources: 1700 kg/ha with 32.6 per cent gain over GV-1 and 115-130 days (NAU sheet, GV-2 entry); 26-28 q/ha and 115-125 days (millets.res.in table); 1100 kg/ha and 120-125 days in a second NAU row -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- The NAU sheet also lists a separate older "Guj. Vari-2" (2006, 1700 kg/ha, medium duration). It is not the same entry as GV-2 and was not used for GV-2 traits -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (evidence refers to GV-2)
- A review of artificial hybridization in small millets records a GV-2 x WV 126 cross made with the SMUASB crossing method, reporting 50-60 per cent seed set at the AICRP-Small Millets centre, Hill Millet Research Station, NAU Waghai -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1112117/full
- No QTL, marker or genomic study naming GV-2 was found. Genome papers on little millet found do not name GV-2 and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence refers to GV-2)
- The NAU sheet gives GV-2 as a mutant derived from GV-1 and says it was developed at the Waghai station of Navsari Agricultural University -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- The release table credits the GV-2 release to Waghai, NAU, 2016 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/little_millet.pdf
- The input record names "Pearl Millet Research Station, Navsari Agri. University", but every GV-2 source points to Hill Millet Research Station (HMRS), NAU, Waghai (The Dangs). The input institution appears to be wrong for this crop -- https://nau.in/assets/uploads/7cd3e-hmrsw_1542905486_109technology-developed.pdf
- No named lead breeder for GV-2 was found in any retrieved source.

CONTACT DETAILS (evidence refers to GV-2)
- No evidence found. No breeder

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: GV-4 (Ambika), little millet**

Name check: the release-minutes name ("GV-4 (Ambika)") and the Seednet name ("GV-4 (Ambika)") are identical. The Seednet portal did not appear in any search result, so every finding below refers to the variety name as written in the sources ("Gujarat Vari-4", "GV-4: Ambika", "Guj. Navsari Vari-4 (Ambika)"). No Seednet entry was confirmed.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- No GV-4-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found. Species-level only: It can withstand both drought and waterlogging. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panicum_sumatrense
- Species-level: little millet is described as a hardy crop which can withstand drought better than most of other cereal crops and water logging to a certain extent. -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-6-2018/Savankumar%20N.%20Patel2,%20et%20al.pdf

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- No GV-4-specific disease or pest reaction was found. The compendium lists GV-4 only as Tolerant to shattering. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384431249_MILLET_CONCLAVE_COMPENDIUM_2023_-_FULL_BOOK
- Comparator only (GV-5, not GV-4): This genotype is resistant to diseases like leaf blast, neck blast and grain smut and also reported resistant reaction against shoot fly. -- https://journaljabb.com/index.php/JABB/article/view/3747

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Little millet variety Gujarat Vari 4 (GV 4: Ambika) is recommended for little millet growing regions of Gujarat. -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf (item 17.1.1.28, release proposal)
- This little millet variety produces average grain yield of 2933 kg/ha which is 13.78 % higher over local check GNV 3 -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf
- Maturity and plant type: the compendium describes GV-4 as Medium duration and non lodging type with Long panicle with more number of grains and yellowish grains. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384431249_MILLET_CONCLAVE_COMPENDIUM_2023_-_FULL_BOOK
- Release-year field in the input record is 2022-10-26; the search results did not independently confirm the notification date.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- No GV-4-specific QTL, marker or genetic-mapping study was found.
- Institute-linked genomics only: the little millet genome paper lists Navsari Agricultural University, Waghai, among its affiliations. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66716-6 (not GV-4-specific)
- Parentage (from input record): pure-line selection from local germplasm 'Vari-126' collected from local land races of The Dangs district. No independent source confirmed this.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Developing station: Hill Millet Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Waghai (The Dangs). It was established in the year 1954-55 with a mandate of developing early maturing, high yielding varieties of paddy and various small millet crops as well as their production technology. -- https://nau.in/unithome/Hill%20Millet%20Research%20Station%20Waghai
- Lead breeder for GV-4 not named in any retrieved source. Scientists associated with the station (not confirmed as GV-4 breeders): Dr. V. P. Usdadiya, Professor & Head, NAU, Navsari, who appears on the AGRESCO release proposal -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//17th_agresco_proceeding_20251226_772.pdf ; Savankumar N. Patel, Harshal E. Patil, Harshalkumar M. Modi and Th. Joydeep Singh (little millet variability study) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-6-2018/Savankumar%20N.%20Patel2,%20et%20al.pdf
- Station is ranked first position among all AICRP centres during the period 2017-18. -- https://nau.in/unithome/Hill%20Millet%20Research%20Station%20Waghai

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- Hill Millet Research Station, Navsari Agricultural University, Waghai, Dist. The Dangs -- 394 730 (postal address as printed) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384431249_MILLET_CONCLAVE_COMPENDIUM_2023_-_FULL_BOOK

International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-6-2018/Savankumar%20N.%20Patel2,%20et%20al.pdf (general variability study, not GV-4-specific)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Til-12 (variety_name) / JAWAHAR KUTKI-2 (seednet_variety_name)

Name mismatch: the evidence found is for Jawahar Til-12 (PKDS-12), a sesame variety. The Seednet name "JAWAHAR KUTKI-2" is listed under little millet, and no evidence for it turned up. The only Kutki-named release found is Jawahar Kutki-95 (JK-95 / DLM-95), a little millet variety notified in 2023. It is a different variety and is not treated as a match below.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Til-12 sesame)
Moderately resistant to Macrophomina stem/root rot is the only varietal stress-tolerance trait found; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or waterlogging data was found for this variety. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://mswt.in/nuts/sesame-seeds/
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST (Til-12 sesame)
Macrophomina resistance: moderate, per DOD listing and trade pages. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://pisumfoods.com/oilseeds/sesame
Insect management: AICRP guidance is for insecticide spraying at bud initiation (imidacloprid, quinalphos, dimethoate). This is not variety-specific. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Trade pages also claim capsule-borer tolerance, but this appears to be for TKG-308, not Til-12. -- https://mswt.in/nuts/sesame-seeds/
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Til-12 sesame)
Duration 82-85 days, white seed, 700-750 kg/ha yield potential, 48-52% oil content. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/ ; https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
Compact plant architecture and uniform capsule distribution are reported in a Central India varieties article. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-more-earn-more-improved-sesame-varieties-and-practices-for-mp-chhattisgarh-farmers/
Conflict: that article gives a 2006 release year, while DOD and AICRP give 2008.
Field-trial data from official multi-location trials: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (Til-12 sesame)
Parent use: PKDS-12 appears as a parent in a segregating-population study (Thilarani x PKDS-12) that reports heritability and genetic advance for yield-related traits. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Yengkhom-Devi-4/publication/364292115_VARIABILITY_AND_HERITABILITY_STUDIES_FOR_YIELD_AND_QUALITY_CONTRIBUTING_TRAITS_IN_SEGREGATING_GENERATIONS_OF_SESAME_Sesamum_indicum_L_Scientist_The_official_Journal_of_Scientist_R_Academy/links/6343b09c9cb4fe44f317bcc7/VARIABILITY-AND-HERITABILITY-STUDIES-FOR-YIELD-AND-QUALITY-CONTRIBUTING-TRAITS-IN-SEGREGATING-GENERATIONS-OF-SESAME-Sesamum-indicum-L-Scientist-The-official-Journal-of-Scientist-R-Academy.pdf
QTL/marker studies for PKDS-12: No evidence found.
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (Til-12 sesame)
Release centre: ZARS, JNKVV, Powarkheda (MP), released 2008 per DOD. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Developing institution: JNKVV, Jabalpur, which has developed several sesame varieties by conventional breeding. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seasame-breeding-crop-improvement-kharif/239907924
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. A JNKVV presenter (Dr. Pratibha Bisen, Plant Breeding and Genetics, College of Agriculture, Balaghat) is listed in a sesame breeding slide deck, but no link to PKDS-12 was found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seasame-breeding-crop-improvement-kharif/239907924
Parentage (Gariyaband local selection, from the input record): not verified by any search result.
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): No evidence found. Note that Jawahar Kutki-95 is linked to JNKVV-type naming, but this is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS
Directorate of Farms, JNKVV (Breeder Seed Production): mobile 8770867088; email seeds.jnkvv@gmail.com (a Gmail address, not an official domain). -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-directorate-details/directorate-of-farms

Official JNKVV website: https://www.jnkvv.org

PUBLICATIONS

Scientist, official journal of Scientist R Academy -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Yengkhom-Devi-4/publication/364292115_VARIABILITY_AND_HERITABILITY_STUDIES_FOR_YIELD_AND_QUALITY_CONTRIBUTING_TRAITS_IN_SEGREGATING_GENERATIONS_OF_SESAME_Sesamum_indicum_L_Scientist_The_official_Journal_of_Scientist_R_Academy/links/6343b09c9cb4fe44f317bcc7/VARIABILITY-AND-HERITABILITY-STUDIES-FOR-YIELD-AND-QUALITY-CONTRIBUTING-TRAITS-IN-SEGREGATING-GENERATIONS-OF-SESAME-Sesamum-indicum-L-Scientist-The-official-Journal-of-Scientist-R-Academy.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
Not searched. The 4-search budget was used on the variety, Seednet name, breeder and research queries. Trader listings exist, such as ampimex.in, which lists the variety among products, but this is not a seed-availability record. -- https://www.ampimex.in/product/sesame-seeds/
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed-sales records: not checked.
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): not checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh only, for summer sowing. This is the official listing. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Conflict: trade sites claim recommendations for West Bengal and several kharif states. These are uncorroborated and were not used. -- https://globaltradeplaza.com/product/sesame-seeds-5
Seednet (JAWAHAR KUTKI-2): The seednet listing for Kutki-2 was not found. The state listing for the little millet category exists only at category level.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalinga Suan 18 (CSC release name) / Kalinga Suan 18 (CLMV-2) (Seednet name), little millet

Scope note: Four searches were run. The first included "CLMV-2" but no result mentioned that code. No search targeted the Seednet portal directly, so the Seednet-name evidence is absent rather than checked. Almost all evidence below is for the closely related variety Kalinga Suan 217 (OLM 217), not Kalinga Suan 18. Where a finding concerns 217, it is labelled as such.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Kalinga Suan 18. Searched under both names. The only related data is for Kalinga Suan 217, which an ICAR table lists as tolerant to shootfly and moderately resistant to sheath blight (not KS18) -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
General little millet context, not specific to KS18: the crop is described as withstanding both drought and waterlogging -- https://www.smartfood.org/smart-food-little-millet/

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for Kalinga Suan 18. Kalinga Suan 217 is listed as resistant to rust and grain smut (not KS18) -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
AICRP on Small Millets reports that grain smut in little millet has chemical control measures, and that shoot fly management technology has been developed for little millet -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicrp_small.php

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Kalinga Suan 18 specifically: one news-style article reports that OUAT developed a little millet variety with enhanced productivity and quality, released by the central variety release committee, with no yield or trial data -- https://shyamalasubarna.com/kalinga-suan-18-a-little-millet-variety-developed-by-ouat/
Related to 217 (not KS18): a KVK Ganjam-II 2024 on-farm trial report gives an average yield of 10.2 q/ha and says it suits rainfed uplands. Its source is listed as OUAT Annual Report 2021 -- https://www.kvkganjam2.org/upload/progress-report/800182006_APR-2024-25,KVK,Ganjam-II.pdf
Related to 217 (not KS18): a KVK Koraput assessment found it out-yielded OLM 208 and the local Sana Suan -- http://kvkkoraput.org/upload/menu_13052025014125.pdf
Related to 217 (not KS18): a national table lists maturity 105-110 days, average yield 15-16 q/ha, and Odisha as its area of adaptation -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
Agronomy context: AICRP small millets trials have produced good agronomic practice packages (not KS18-specific) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363535506_Good_Agronomic_Practices_for_Higher_Yield_in_Small_Millets

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for Kalinga Suan 18. A 2025 little millet genome paper with GWAS on agronomic traits exists, but it does not mention this variety -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66716-6
General context: little millet is described as the least studied minor millet, with few molecular markers -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/499087.full.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Kalinga Suan 18: developed by Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), per https://shyamalasubarna.com/kalinga-suan-18-a-little-millet-variety-developed-by-ouat/
Breeder name: No evidence found. The breeder or lead scientist is not named in any result.
Institution context: the ICAR-AICRP on Small Millets centre at OUAT, Berhampur, is listed in the AICRP proceedings. A scientist's name is given there but truncated ("Dr. PM Mahapatr") -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf
Network context: the AICRP on Small Millets is coordinated from ICAR-IIMR, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf
Parentage: the input gives "Selection from Kandhamal Local." No result confirms this -- no evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- Breeder: No evidence found.
Institute-level (not confirmed as the KS18 contact):
- Name: Dr. PM Mahapatr[a] (truncated in source), ICAR-AICRP on Small Millets, OUAT, Berhampur, Odisha. Email, phone: No evidence found -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf
- Address: ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030, Telangana, India. Email, phone: No evidence found -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip21/Sorghum/reports21/AGM2022-AICRP_on_Sorghum_and_Small_millets-Proceedings.pdf
- Institute contact page URL: https://www.millets.res.in/aicrp_small.php (AICRP Small Millets page; no email or phone in the extract)

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for Kalinga Suan 18. No paper, thesis, or AICRP report was located that names this variety. The related items below concern other varieties or general topics and are NOT citations for KS18:
- Hariprasanna, K. (2023). High yielding varieties for enhancing the production of small millets in India. Indian Farming (ICAR, January 2023). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India (lists Kalinga Suan 217, not KS18)
- Little millet genome paper (2025), Nature Communications. -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-025-66716-6 (no mention of KS18)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Kalinga Suan 18: No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer sources.
Context: a national article notes seed availability of improved small millet varieties is a limitation, and that IIMR-backed seed hubs have been set up -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India
Not usable: retail listings found (for example, https://www.flipkart.com/nabarna-odisha-little-millet-suan-samai-natual-whole-grain-rich-protein-fiber-millet/p/itmbfd7b9d02a4bf) are grain products, not certified planting seed, and do not name KS18.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input lists Odisha, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. No search result confirmed this for Kalinga Suan 18. Related evidence for KS217 gives Odisha as its area of adaptation -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2023-05/Indian-farming-January-2023.pdf
Release year: the input gives 2022-10-26. The only search source says it was recently released by the central committee, with no date or notification number -- https://shyamalasubarna.com/kalinga-suan-18-a-little-millet-variety-developed-by-ouat/

Open gaps: no official CSC notification, no Seednet listing for CLMV-2, no yield or stress data, no breeder name, and no seed source for Kalinga Suan 18. These should be checked directly on seednet.gov.in, the CSC notification, and OUAT/AICRP Odisha pages.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Sweta (variety_name) / ARKA SHEETAL (seednet_variety_name), chilli hybrid, MSH-149

Search budget note: The four permitted searches are used up. My first batch returned full results, but I printed only the first 300 characters of each, and my attempt to re-read the full pages hit the tool-call limit. Findings below are limited to those snippets. Items marked "not captured" may exist on the pages I could not re-open.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Arka Sweta. -- none

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data appeared in the captured text. -- none

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Listed as an F1 hybrid from a cross of IHR 3903 (a CGMS line) with IHR 3315. Reported yields are 28-30 t/ha fresh and 4.5 t/ha dry. Fruits are smooth and light green, turning red at maturity. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
- Maturity, plant habit and multi-location trial results: not captured.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Conflict with the supplied record: the IIHR listing describes an F1 hybrid (IHR 3903 CGMS × IHR 3315), while the supplied parentage describes IIHR 3-1-1-1-5-1, a Lucknow collection developed by pure-line breeding. These cannot both be right for this variety. The supplied parentage is not supported by any evidence I found and should be checked against IIHR records. -- https://iihr.res.in/varieties
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The IIHR page for Arka Sweta lists it under "Varieties / Technologies released by ICAR - IIHR." -- https://www.iihr.res.in/chilli-arka-sweta-0
- Lead breeder or scientist names: not captured. The supplied record names no breeder either.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact found. The only institute reference found is the IIHR website. Official email, phone and postal address were not captured. -- https://iihr.res.in
- Seednet contact details: not searched separately.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for Arka Sweta. A ResearchGate paper on hybrid chillies in Salem covers TNAU CO1 and Arka Meghana, not this variety, so I discarded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354579998_Per_se_performance_of_hybrid_chillies_Capsicum_annuum_l_TNAU_

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for Arka Sweta. A Gramik listing for "Sheetal Research Long Melon Seeds" is a private product for a different crop, so I discarded it. -- https://shop.gramik.in/product/Sheetal-Research-Long-Melon-Seeds-yOtUj
- Seednet name conflict: "ARKA SHEETAL" under "LONG MELON" does not match the chilli record. No Seednet listing was found under either name.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found. The supplied record says "Not specified," and no state recommendation appeared in the captured text.

Release year: the supplied date is 2015-04-07. This was not verified against any source.

seednet_candidate_fields.Parentage: IIHR 3-1-1-1-5-1, a collection from Lucknow, developed as an improved variety by pure line breeding method.
seednet_candidate_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: Monoecious plant with medium long, lush green fruits covered with soft hairs, each weighing 90 to 100 gm at marketable stage.
seednet_candidate_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height  - 150-200 cm; Stem and foliage distinct features - Angular stem with dark green shallow lobed leaves; Distinct fruit characters - Medium long fruit (length 22 cm, girth 7.8 cm), light green skin colour, crisp texture, free from bitter principles; Distinct seed characters - Light tan coloured seeds; Seed to seed duration - 100-110 days; 1000 seed weight - 25 gm.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: M/s. Khoja Habib Mamad, Near Gramin Bank, Post. Nagalpur, Tehsil. Anjar, Dist. Kutchh, (Gujarat) PIN- 370110.
seednet_fields.Parentage: Preliminary selection was made from the local material ‘Kutchhi Rajka’ and phenotypically similar elite plants were selected over several cycles and bulked.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: South Zone comprising states of Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Resistant to lodging, medium to high fertilizer responsive, suitable to early sowing 15th October to 15th November. 1.	Seed rate: 15-18 kg for line sowing. 35-40 kg for broadcasting. 2.	30 cm between lines (mostly broadcasting). 3.	FYM: 20-25 t/ha. 4.	NPK: 25:50:50kg as basal dose. 2nd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number. 3rd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Perennial for 3 years, long root system, suitable in high temperature ranges from 48 to 50 Co, dry and salt affected area. Tall variety having number or tillers per plant. More number of leaves per plant with oblong shape and tender shoot so high digestible protein. Seeds are yellowish kindly shaped.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Drought resistant due to long root system so suitable in warm condition.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: H. armigera and Lucerne weevil had low incidence and all entries showed non significant variations.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 1.	NPK: 25:50:50kg as basal dose. 2nd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number. 3rd year, 0:50:50 kg. NPK in Number.

basic_info.institution: Alamdar Beej, M/s. Khoja Habib Mamad

drought.details: Drought resistant due to a long root system, making it suitable for warm conditions. Classified as moderately tolerant in genetic parameter studies for fodder yield and yield components.

heat.details: Suitable for warm conditions, inferred from its drought resistance mechanism (long root system).

salinity.details: Demonstrated high germination indices and seedling vigor under salt stress conditions, indicating strong tolerance at the germination stage.

flood.details: Not specified.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is not specified in quantitative terms.
agronomic_details.stability: Its classification as a 'check' variety (Alamdar-51) in studies for estimation of genetic parameters suggests it is a known and possibly stable performer.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for cultivation in Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana. Suitable for warm conditions. Best suited for early sowing between October 15th and November 15th.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Resistant to lodging and shows medium to high responsiveness to fertilizer application.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Alamdar-51 was utilized as a 'check' genotype in studies focusing on the estimation of genetic parameters for fodder yield and its components in lucerne, indicating its inclusion in performance evaluations.

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The increase in grain yield with increase in plant density at each fertilizers dose indicates that the hybrid shows better response to higher plant density.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: 1.Tall, semi erect and Broad leaf blade, presence of anthocyanin colour of tassel and silk, few tassel branches. 2. Semi erect leaf, Dark purple plants, tassel and husk, long tassel length.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi erect leaves, stay green plants, Long thick cobs with excellent tip filling, Uniform cobs.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Multiple disease resistance and shows resistance to Curvularia leaf spot (CLS), Rajasthan Downey Mildew (RDM) and Moderate resistance to Turcicum leaf blight (TLB), maydis leaf blight (MLB), Fusarium Stalk Rot (FSR), charcoal Rot, Sorghum Downey Mildew (SDM), Polysora Rust and common Rust.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Found to have moderate tolerance against Chilopartellus.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 1.	The following fertilizers dosage and scheduled may be adopted. FYM: 10 tons/ha 15-20 days before sowing PZ: 200kg N: 65 kg P2O5: 80 kg K2O.

drought.details: Specific drought tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. However, maize is generally highly sensitive to drought, especially from pre-flowering to maturity, with critical periods during tasseling and grain-filling stages. Foliar calcium spray has been shown to confer drought stress tolerance in maize by modulating plant growth, water relations, proline content, and hydrogen peroxide activity. Calcium also regulates water status, proline, and H2O2 levels in maize plants under drought stress.

heat.details: Specific heat tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. Rising temperatures due to greenhouse gas emissions cause heat stress in plants, including maize. Research indicates a calcium-dependent tolerant response of the cell wall in maize mesocotyl under heat stress.

salinity.details: Specific salinity tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. Increased soil salinity reduces the availability of water and nutrients in the root zone, leading to water stress, oxidative stress, and ion toxicity in plants. Plants differ in their tolerance to soil salinity. Calcium plays a role in increasing the tolerance of corn (Zea mays L.) to salinity. Organic amendments have also been shown to mitigate salinity induced toxic effects in maize.

flood.details: Specific flood tolerance for ADV 762 is not specified. Maize is highly sensitive to waterlogging. Flooding influences maize plants.

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for ADV 762 is not specified. However, diseases in maize are highly influenced by abiotic stress. Another Advanta maize product, PAC 741, is noted as tolerant to late wilt.

pest_resistance.summary: Specific pest resistance for ADV 762 is not specified. Pest issues in maize are highly influenced by abiotic stress.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: UPL Limited (formerly Advanta Limited) Hyerabad- 500034 TS.
seednet_fields.Parentage: 330093 x 330094 330093 and 330094 were select from Introduction T12004 (EC No. 745652) & T12012 (EC no. 745660) respectively.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rabi irrigated areas in – Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Maharashtra in Peninsular Zone. Peninsular Zone– Karnataka, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Tamil Nadu under rabi irrigated condition.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Erect leaves, Stay green plants, Long thick cobs with excellent tip filling and shelling %.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Multiple Diseases Resistant and shows Resistance to Sorghum Downey Mildew (SDM), Moderately Resistance to Turcicum Leaf Blight (TLB), Charcoal Rot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Found to have better tolerance to Chilo partellus and Sesamia inferens.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): The following fertilizer dosage and schedule may be adopted. FYM: 10 ton/ha 15-20 days before sowing. PZ: 200 kg N: 65 kg P2O5: 80 kg K20. Zinc (Zn): 25 kg of ZnSO4 if required.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: UPL Limited (formerly Advanta Limited) Hyerabad- 500034 TS.
seednet_fields.Parentage: 330104 x 330105 330104 and 330105 were select from Introduction T12011 (EC No. 745659) & T12014(EC no. 745662) respectively.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Irrigated and Rainfed areas in (NWPZ) – Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, (Plain) and Western Uttar Pradesh. North West Plain (NWPZ) – Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand, (Plain) and Western Uttar Pradesh under irrigated and rainfed conditions.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The hybrid shows better yield for the increase in fertilizer dose as well as increased plant density.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi erect leaves, Stay green plants, Long thick cobs with excellent tip filling and shelling %.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Multiple Diseases Resistant and shows Resistance to Maydis Leaf Blight (MLB), Turcicum Leaf Blight (TLB), Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight (BLSB), Charcoal Rot and Rajasthan Downey Mildew (RDM), Cuvrularia Leaf Spot (CLS), Common Rust (CR) and Polysora Rust (PR).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Found to have moderately tolerance against Chilo partellus.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): The following fertilizer dosage and schedule may be adopted. FYM: 10 ton/ha 15-20 days before sowing. PZ: 200 kg N: 65 kg P2O5: 80 kg K20. Zinc (Zn): 25 kg of ZnSO4 if required.

drought.details: Specific tolerance for ADV 752 is unknown. General maize is prone to drought stress, especially during tasseling and grain-filling stages. However, some maize varieties are recognized as drought tolerant. Foliar calcium spray can confer drought stress tolerance in maize by modulating plant growth, water relations, proline content, and hydrogen peroxide activity. Calcium also regulates water status, proline, and H2O2 levels in maize plants under drought stress. Drought tolerance in maize can also be observed in varieties tolerant to both submergence and drought.

heat.details: Specific tolerance for ADV 752 is unknown. General maize adaptability to warm temperatures is noted. Physiological, biochemical, and molecular mechanisms of heat stress tolerance in maize, including calcium-dependent responses, have been observed. Heat stress is a significant factor influenced by temperature increases.

salinity.details: Specific tolerance for ADV 752 is unknown. Increased soil salinity reduces water and nutrient availability, leading to water stress, oxidative stress, and ion toxicity in plants. Calcium has been shown to increase the tolerance of corn (Zea mays L.) to salinity. Organic amendments can also mitigate salinity-induced toxic effects in maize.

flood.details: Specific tolerance for ADV 752 is unknown. General maize is described as highly sensitive to waterlogging. Flooding stress can significantly influence maize plants.

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for ADV 752 is unknown. General maize production can be significantly affected by diseases, which are highly influenced by abiotic stress. Another Advanta maize variety, PAC 741, is known to be tolerant to late wilt.

pest_resistance.summary: Specific pest resistance for ADV 752 is unknown. Pests can cause significant havoc in maize production, often influenced by abiotic stress.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bhanu (variety_name) / BHANU (seednet_variety_name), sunflower, code A0207528

Name note: The only page that names this variety is a sunflower guide that lists "Bhanu" and gives a 2010 release year. The CSC record gives 2011-06-28. Both names refer to the same variety only if the guide and the CSC record describe the same entry, which I could not confirm. The Seednet crop name is MAIZE (MAKKA), and no evidence links BHANU to maize. Four searches were used, the maximum allowed, so seed availability was not searched.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. No search result names Bhanu with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/sunflower-cultivation-in-india (searched in release/trait query; the page lists only yield, oil and centre)

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No search result names Bhanu with disease or pest resistance. The DOD sunflower table (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sunflower.aspx) lists resistance traits for Phule Raviraj and RSFV-901 only, which are different varieties, so they are discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: "Bhanu" sunflower is listed with a 2010 year of release, a ZARS Solapur / MPKV Rahuri centre, seed yield of 1600–1800 kg/ha and oil content of 37–39%. This is a non-official blog table and conflicts with the CSC year of 2011 -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/sunflower-cultivation-in-india

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No search result on genetics, markers or QTL names Bhanu.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found for a named lead breeder or scientist for Bhanu. The only institution hint is the centre column of the blog table, which names ZARS Solapur and MPKV Rahuri -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/sunflower-cultivation-in-india. This is a centre listing, not a breeder attribution. Phule Bhaskar (ZARS Rahuri) and Marigold "Arka Bhanu" (IIHR) are different varieties and are discarded -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sunflower.aspx ; https://jssonline.org/marigold-flowers-new-variety-arka-bhanu-launched/

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address or contact page for Bhanu appeared in the results. The Seednet index page (https://seednet.gov.in/material/Agriculture_Variety.htm) lists maize varieties but does not name BHANU in the retrieved text.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The retrieved sunflower papers (ccsenet.org Journal of Agricultural Studies pages, https://ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/jas/article/download/0/0/50111/54222 ; https://ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/jas/article/download/0/0/50101/54217) and the IIOR compendium "Varieties and Hybrids of Sunflower" (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357478059_Varieties_and_Hybrids_of_Sunflower) do not name Bhanu in the retrieved text, so they are not listed. The Phule Bhaskar release paper (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332110521_Phule_bhaskar-_a_new_variety_of_sunflower_Helianthus_annuus_L_with_higher_seed_yield_and_oil_content_suitable_for_cultivation_in_kharif_season_under_rainfed_regions_of_Maharashtra) is about a different variety and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: Not searched. The four-query limit was used for the release, Seednet, breeder and research topics. The Seednet maize listing (https://seednet.gov.in/material/Agriculture_Variety.htm) names Maize (Makka) but no BHANU entry was found. Commercial maize seed pages (Amazon, Flipkart) are unrelated hybrids and are excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Not specified in the CSC record. The only related page names ZARS Solapur and MPKV Rahuri (Maharashtra institutions) as the centre -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/sunflower-cultivation-in-india. It does not state recommended states, so none is recorded.

drought.details: One study (GGE biplot analysis under drought and irrigated conditions) names BIO 9682, the Seednet name recorded for this variety, as one of the highest-yielding entries under drought at about 5.5 t/ha, against a low of 3.5 t/ha. It was identified with CMH 12-686 as one of the relatively more drought-tolerant genotypes. Its stress-index profile was favourable: it had a high RSI (above 1.1) and was among the entries with the lowest SSI (CMH 12-686, BIO 9682 and CMH 08-287). It was grouped with late-maturing entries showing low drought sensitivity (SSI and TOL). Evidence comes from a single study. Identity of BIO 9682 with BIO 9782 is inferred from the Seednet name mapping and is not independently confirmed. The CSC record lists a general stress reaction of 'Tolerant' without naming the stress, so it is not used as drought evidence. Mechanisms were not described.

agronomic_details.yield: In the AICRP National Initial Variety Trial (Late), Kharif 2020-21, the check Bio 9682 recorded a grain yield of 8.41 t/ha. The Seednet name is used here; identity with BIO 9782 is not confirmed in that source. The Nepal trial (identity with this variety not confirmed) reported a yield of 15.96 for the hybrid 'Bioseed 9782', but this is not counted as variety-level evidence. Units are not stated for that figure in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: From the GGE drought study (BIO 9682 name): low SSI and TOL, and high RSI (above 1.1), indicating stable yield across drought and irrigated conditions. The evidence is from one study and the identity link is unconfirmed.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The Nepal trial authors suggested the hybrid 'Bioseed 9782' for commercial growing in Chitwan and similar agro-climatic regions. Identity with this variety is not confirmed, so this is noted but not treated as confirmed adaptation. Recommended states from the release brief are listed under variety_profile; the digest contains no supporting evidence for them.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not found in searched sources. Cob traits from the Nepal trial (cob length 21.33 cm and cob diameter 17.67 cm, the highest in that trial) are reported under field_trials with identity caveats.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRP National Initial Variety Trial (Late), Kharif 2020-21: BIO 9682 was one of four commercial checks among 45 entries. As a check, it recorded a grain yield of 8.41 t/ha and an AD value of 55 days, and grain moisture at harvest of 18.1%. Five experimental hybrids beat this check by at least 5% in grain yield without a significant anthesis difference. These are different entries and are excluded from this variety's evidence. (2) Nepal trial (identity with the Indian entry not confirmed): the hybrid 'Bioseed 9782' gave the highest grain yield at 15.96, followed by Gangakaveri at 14.26 t/ha and Shresta at 12.12 t/ha. It also had the highest standard heterosis at 64.81% and the highest cob length (21.33 cm) and cob diameter (17.67 cm) in that trial. (3) GGE biplot drought study (BIO 9682 name): under drought, yield of about 5.5 t/ha, versus a low of 3.5 t/ha; see stress_tolerance.drought. Maturity, released-variety yield in India, and Indian state-trial data for BIO 9782 were not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BL 45 (Seednet name: BML-45), berseem (Trifolium alexandrinum)
Searches run: 4 (release/traits; breeder/institution; research papers; Seednet name check). No search returned a page naming BL 45 or BML-45 together with berseem or maize.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The trait search returned only BL 44 and BL 42 pages (e.g., agrospectrumindia.com, PAU/Tribune notices). Those name other varieties, so I discarded them.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for BL 45.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Trial pages returned were about berseem in general or other varieties (e.g., researchgate.net herbicide and NPK trials, pub.isa-india.in PGR trial). None names BL 45.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The only genetics material was general berseem breeding history (PMC11336856, studocu.com), which does not mention BL 45.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The input lists Punjab Agricultural University (PAU) as institution. PAU pages found (pau.edu notices) concern seed production of BL 10, BL 42, BL 43 and BL 44, not BL 45, so no breeder or station is attributed to BL 45.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The pau.edu notice refers only to the "Office of the Director (Seeds), PAU, Ludhiana" with no email, phone or address, and it concerns other varieties. No breeder contact was found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. Papers returned name other berseem varieties or none (e.g., researchgate.net weed-management and herbicide papers, forageresearch.in comparison of notified varieties, Journal of Pharmacognosy and Phytochemistry 2019 SP1:234-237). None names BL 45, so none is listed.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The PAU seed-production EOI (pau.edu) covers BL 10, BL 42, BL 43 and BL 44 only. The Seednet-name search for BML-45 returned only unrelated commercial maize products (agribegri.com, flipkart.com, amazon.in) and a Karimnagar Makka-1 hybrid paper (researchgate.net) that mentions an inbred "BML 7". These are name resemblances and were discarded. No berseem seed source for BL 45 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input list (J&K, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) is unverified; no search result supports it for BL 45.

NOTES FOR THE RECORD
- Release year 2022-06-17 from the input is unverified; no release or notification evidence was found.
- Parentage is "Not specified" in the input; no evidence was found either way.
- Name check: "BL 45" is a berseem name, but the Seednet entry "BML-45" is listed under MAIZE (MAKKA) with variety code BM 12. The crop mismatch and the name difference should be checked against Seednet and the CSC release minutes before this record is used.
- Off-target pages seen (BL 42, BL 43, BL 44, BL 10, Karimnagar Makka-1, Siri 4555, CP 858, DKC 9081, GO-BER-10 clover patent, and others) were excluded under the strict relevance rule.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: National Pulses Research Centre, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Vamban Colony-622303, Pudukkottai District Tami Nadu.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: South zone comprising states of Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka and Odisha.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Seed ratea: 20 kg/ha Spacing: 30 x 10 cm Fertilizer: 25:50:25 kg NPK/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: (i)Plant height-Semi erect and determinate plant type with lanceolate leaflet. (ii)Flower colour-Yellow. (iii)Days to 50% flowering-40 days (30-53 days). (iv)Pod charcter-Pubescent, matured pod is black in colour. (v)Pod length-4.2 cm (4.0-4.5 cm).
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The culture VBG 12-034 is resistant to Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus, Urdbean Leaf Crinkle Virus, Leaf Curl Virus diseases.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Modertaely resistant to pod borer complex Number of white flies per plant number of thrips per flowers and incidence of stem fly is very less when compared to the variety.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Apply fertilizers based on the soil testing or apply recommended dose of fertilizers of NPK @ 25:50:25 Kg/ha. Apply all the recommended dose of fertilizers as basal dose. Spray 2 per cent fertilizers

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: BPCH-6 (variety_name) / BPCH-6 (seednet_variety_name), maize (MAKKA), code A0207854, ANGRAU, release 2015-06-25

Name note: Both names are "BPCH-6" and no Seednet page surfaced in my four searches, so every finding below refers to the name "BPCH 6"/"BPCH-6" as written in the source. Two results describe BPCH-6 as a popcorn hybrid; one describes it as a landrace. Treat the crop type as unresolved until the CSC minutes or Seednet entry is checked directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- A drought screen of Indian maize landraces reported that BPCH-6 had high relative water content and was selected as a drought-tolerant landrace for further study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371013636_Breeding_Drought-Tolerant_Maize_Zea_mays_Using_Molecular_Breeding_Tools_Recent_Advancements_and_Future_Prospective
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to BPCH-6.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for BPCH-6 resistance to any disease or pest. The only AICRP-style benchmarking slides I found list resistance for other hybrids, not BPCH-6 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A field experiment at the Maize Research Centre, Agricultural Research Institute (ARI), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, tested plant densities and nitrogen levels on the newly published popcorn hybrid BPCH-6 over two rabi seasons, reporting growth, yield and economics -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Popular-popcorn-varieties-in-India_tbl1_305145700
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Andhra Pradesh/Telangana maize package of practices lists BPCH 6 as a recommended popcorn hybrid under speciality corn -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/MaizePackage.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity, yield (t/ha) and plant population for BPCH-6: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for BPCH-6 parentage, marker studies or QTL. The parentage field in the input is "Not specified", and no source filled that gap.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per the release record and the Rajendranagar paper: Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh. The Rajendranagar paper names the variety's origin as Professor Jayashankar Telangana State Agricultural University, previously ANGRAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Popular-popcorn-varieties-in-India_tbl1_305145700
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. No breeder name was attached to BPCH-6 in any source I retrieved.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The university's general description (headquarters at Lam, Guntur; established 1964 as Andhra Pradesh Agricultural University, renamed 1996) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acharya_N._G._Ranga_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS -- Institute-level contact (no breeder contact found): Acharya N G Ranga Agricultural University Administrative Office, Lam, Guntur, Andhra Pradesh, 522 034; email registrar@angrau.ac.in -- https://angrau.ac.in/
CONTACT DETAILS -- Breeder email, direct phone, and division or maize-station postal address: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (Year not captured). Field experiment on plant density and nitrogen effects on the popcorn hybrid BPCH-6, Maize Research Centre, ARI Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. ResearchGate figure record -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Popular-popcorn-varieties-in-India_tbl1_305145700
- Authors not captured (Year not captured). "Breeding Drought-Tolerant Maize (Zea mays) Using Molecular Breeding Tools: Recent Advancements and Future Prospective." Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371013636_Breeding_Drought-Tolerant_Maize_Zea_mays_Using_Molecular_Breeding_Tools_Recent_Advancements_and_Future_Prospective
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, or DOI specific to BPCH-6 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The Seednet portal was not reached in these searches, and the fourth search (seed availability) returned only non-Indian seed listings.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The input record states "All states (across the country)", which I could not verify. The only Indian listing found names BPCH 6 solely as a popcorn option in an Andhra Pradesh/Telangana package of practices -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/MaizePackage.pdf

Search note: The web_search budget ran out after four queries. My last call hit the limit, so I could not open the full pages. The findings below come only from the truncated result snippets I already captured, so several headings are incomplete. Treat this as a partial record.

The variety code in the input is L-173, but the AICRP page lists L 201, so the code needs checking against the official notification.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. Drought, heat, salinity, flood, and submergence tolerance were not captured. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found in the retrieved snippets. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The IIMR page carries agrotechnique material, but only for the single-cross hybrid HQPM-1 (seed production with a 4:1 female-to-male row ratio). It does not describe Bajaura Makka-1, so it should not be attributed to this variety. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The Bajaura Makka-1 snippet shows only its registration and code, with no parentage or QTL data. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The variety is recorded as registered under Registration No. 41 of 2015 (PPV&FRA, notification dated 22 January 2015) and listed as Bajaura Makka 1 (L173). The developing institution is not named in the snippet. The Bajaura station is the CSKHPKV Hill Agricultural Research and Extension Centre (HAREC), which is an AICRP maize centre, so the station link is supported. No breeder name was found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/ ; https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

No breeder name, email, or phone was found. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/bajaura-himachal-pradesh/

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. My searches returned no journal article, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI for this variety. A Karimnagar Makka-1 ResearchGate record appeared, but it is a different hybrid from a different state and is excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The AICRP and IIMR pages place the variety at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh, under CSKHPKV. Bio-22027 (name on Seednet): a different, earlier entry. The IIMR cultivar list shows a 01-10-2008 notification by Bioseed Research India Pvt. Ltd., rabi season, for Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh, with a yield value of 8.7 (unit not stated) -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
The AICMIP list of maize hybrids released from 2000 records Bio-22027 (2008) as medium maturity, for Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Uttar Pradesh, with a yield of 7.4 and yellow semi-dent grain -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
Note: the 2008 Bio-22027 and the 2024 BIO 207 (code BIO Seed 9577) do not appear to be the same entry, and no source links them. Treat them as separate until verified against the Seednet record.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for Bisco X 5129.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for Bisco X 5129 appeared in the results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A consumer farming blog describes Bisco X 5129 as grown under irrigated conditions in the kharif/spring and summer seasons, as a long-duration variety of about 95 days -- https://tractorjunction.com/blog/maize-cultivation-and-varieties-in-india
Another farming blog lists the same four states but places the crop in the Rabi season, which conflicts with the blog above -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Both blogs are secondary and unverified against CSC minutes or Seednet. Yield figures: No evidence found.
A 2016 Journal of Maize Research and Development paper evaluated 117 hybrids from 20 seed companies at three sites in Nepal, and its visible text names other Bisco hybrids (e.g., Bisco x 81) but no Bisco X 5129 data appeared in the excerpt -- https://www.nepjol.info/index.php/JMRD/article/download/16210/13147
A separate Nepal study found Bisco Gold 941 to be a top yielder; it is a different hybrid, not Bisco X 5129 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9674539/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No QTL or marker evidence found. The parentage BS 251 / (BSI 226 x BSI 252) comes only from the supplied variety record, not from an independent source. No search result confirmed it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per the record: Bisco Bio-Sciences Pvt. Ltd. A company listing page names Bisco Bio-Sciences Pvt Ltd in its about text and carries the heading Limagrain India Private Limited -- https://www.indiamart.com/bisco-bio-sciences/
Breeder or scientist names: No evidence found. No station or institute page for this hybrid was located.
Note: Seednet name and CSC name are both "Bisco X 5129", so no separate Seednet-name search was needed. Seednet itself was not reached in these results.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The only company-level source is the IndiaMART listing page, which gives no verified email, phone, or postal address for the company's breeding division -- https://www.indiamart.com/bisco-bio-sciences/
No official institute contact page was found. No email or phone numbers were verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- No publication specific to Bisco X 5129 was found. Related but non-target items:
Authors not captured in the search excerpt (2016). Journal of Maize Research and Development, vol. 2(1), pp. 1-12: multi-hybrid evaluation in Nepal, Bisco X 5129 not confirmed in the excerpt -- https://www.nepjol.info/index.php/JMRD/article/download/16210/13147
Authors not captured in the search excerpt (year not captured). Study comparing Bisco Gold 941 and other hybrids in Nepal; not Bisco X 5129 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9674539/
KrishiKosh and AICRP/ICAR reports: No evidence found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Bisco X 5129 from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or dealers. Related but non-target: a trade-data site lists Bisco maize seed export records under HS code 10051000, including a 2016 entry for a different Bisco variety -- https://www.seair.co.in/bisco-maize-seed-export-data/hs-code-10051000.aspx
A dealer listing offers a different Limagrain Bisco hybrid (Seedtec 97 Gold) in Guwahati -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/limagrain-bisco-seedtec-97-gold-hybrid-maize-seed-2853608476097.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CMH 08-282 (maize)

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "CMH 08-282". The evidence below refers to CMH 08-282 under both names. Some sources write it as "CMH-08-282" or "TNAU maize hybrid CO 6". No Seednet portal page was found in these searches, so no Seednet-specific record could be checked.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- A slide deck on maize improvement in India lists CMH 08-282 among hybrids tolerant to waterlogging, grouped with DMRH1419 and PMH3 -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/maize-improvement-in-india/119916953
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, or submergence tolerance specific to CMH 08-282.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- The TNAU 44th Research Council highlights (2011) describe CMH-08-282 as a single-cross hybrid with downy mildew resistance and yield of about 9 t/ha, nominated for testing in rainfed conditions in kharif 2010 -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/44th-RC-Research-Highlights-2011.pdf
- A Maize Journal article titled as a high-yielding, multiple-disease-resistant TNAU hybrid says the hybrid was selected for grain yield, disease resistance and grain quality -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
- No pest-specific evidence found for CMH 08-282.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- The Maize Journal article states that CMH 08-282 (TNAU maize hybrid CO 6) is a single cross of UMI 1200 x UMI 1230, matures in 110 days, and is suited to irrigated (June-July) and other seasons -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
- The TNAU 2011 highlights report a yield of about 9 t/ha and seed weight of 38-42 g per 100 seeds -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/44th-RC-Research-Highlights-2011.pdf
- The TNAU 2011 highlights give parentage as DU 2 x VB 20 in a table that appears to belong to the sister hybrid CMH-08-259. This conflicts with the UMI1200 x UMI1230 parentage in the record and needs checking -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/44th-RC-Research-Highlights-2011.pdf
- The 2020-21 National Initial Variety Trial (NIVT) under AICRP on Maize used CMH 08-282 as one of four commercial checks among 45 entries -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/408548476_Validating_superior_maize_hybrids_in_all_India_coordinated_trials_using_REMATTOOL-R_a_decision_support_approach

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No evidence found for QTL, marker, or genetic studies specific to CMH 08-282. The Maize 282 panel results found in searches are unrelated inbred panels.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- The TNAU research highlights (2011) place CMH-08-282 in the TNAU Research Council programme -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/44th-RC-Research-Highlights-2011.pdf
- The Maize Journal article attributes the hybrid to the TNAU maize programme at Coimbatore. Individual breeder names were not visible in the retrieved text -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
- No named lead breeder found for CMH 08-282.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder-level contact found.
- No official TNAU Department of Millets or Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics contact page, email, phone, or postal address was retrieved in these searches. The record's institution address is Coimbatore-3 but was not verified online.
- A 2016 AICRP Maize annual report lists a plant breeder email and phone, but the snippet does not link them to TNAU or CMH 08-282, so I have not attributed them -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf

PUBLICATIONS:
- Author(s) not visible in retrieved text (year and journal unverified). "A high yielding multiple disease resistant TNAU maize hybrid" (Maize Journal, Madras Agricultural Journal-type archive). -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
- Author(s) not visible (2011). TNAU 44th Research Council Meeting Research Highlights, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/research/wp-content/uploads/sites/60/2020/02/44th-RC-Research-Highlights-2011.pdf
- Author(s) not visible (2025/2026). "Validating superior maize hybrids in all India coordinated trials using REMATTOOL-R: a decision support approach", AICRP Maize NIVT 2020-21 analysis. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/408548476_Validating_superior_maize_hybrids_in_all_India_coordinated_trials_using_REMATTOOL-R_a_decision_support_approach
- No KrishiKosh thesis or DOI-based paper specific to CMH 08-282 found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- No evidence found for CMH 08-282 seed from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVKs, TNAU seed sales, or private dealers. An IFFDC seed page lists other maize hybrids (MH Super-074, CMH Super-18) but not CMH 08-282 -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Release year is listed as NaT in the record. The Maize Journal article says the hybrid was released as TNAU maize hybrid CO 6 during 2012 for commercial cultivation in Tamil Nadu -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
- The Maize Journal article describes cultivation suitability as irrigated (June-July) and other seasons. No official notified-state list was found, so the record's "Not specified" stands unless verified against the CSC notification or Seednet.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: COBH 2 (CSC name) / COH-2 (Seednet name)

Search note: I ran four searches, all on "COBH 2" and its brinjal context. I did not run a search on "COH-2" or the Seednet portal, so Seednet evidence is absent, not checked. The Seednet listing is filed under MAIZE (MAKKA), and nothing I found connects that record to brinjal.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately tolerant to shoot and fruit borer, per the HOR 211 teaching slides. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/hor-211-2-tomato-brinjal-chilli-pptx/269858871
- Same tolerance wording, repeated in a brinjal production-technology deck. -- https://slideshare.net/kousalyahorti/warm-ppt
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for COBH 2.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The "moderately tolerant" wording covers shoot and fruit borer only. The TNAU brinjal page gives shoot and fruit borer figures for the COBH line, but I could not confirm which hybrid they describe. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_brinjal_varieties_COBH.html
- No evidence found for bacterial wilt, little leaf, phomopsis or nematode resistance specific to COBH 2.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- F1 hybrid with a crop duration of 120-130 days and yield of 58-60 t/ha (TNAU COBH.2 entry). -- https://slideshare.net/hor-211 (see HOR 211 deck): https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/hor-211-2-tomato-brinjal-chilli-pptx/269858871
- Commercial checklist gives average yield of 60 t/ha, fruit 55-60 g, medium oblong dark violet. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/pdf/tech_bulletin/national/Checklist-of-Commercial-Varieties-of-Vegetables.pdf
- Earlier TNAU list gives average yield of 58 t/ha. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/achievements-in-crop-improvement-of-brinjal/104058156
- Grafted trial: COBH 2 scion on Solanum torvum rootstock, tested for spacing and fertigation levels at Coimbatore. Authors include V. Rajasree and S. Praneetha; year and journal not shown in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344087071_Performance_of_grafted_brinjal_Solanum_melongena_L_under_different_spacing_and_fertigation_levels
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results for COBH 2: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: TNAU and teaching sources give EP65 x Pusa Uttam, an F1 hybrid. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/hor-211-2-tomato-brinjal-chilli-pptx/269858871 ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/pdf/tech_bulletin/national/Checklist-of-Commercial-Varieties-of-Vegetables.pdf
- The parentage in the input record ("UMI 810 X UMI .90") does not match this. No source supports it. Flag for correction.
- QTL, marker or SSR studies on COBH 2: No evidence found. The PubMed and Nature hits concern other brinjal hybrids and landraces and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Horticultural College and Research Institute, Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU). -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-technologies-developed/
- Release year conflict: the TNAU HCRI list shows COBH 1 and COBH 2 released in 2001 and 2009. The TNAU bulletin-style deck gives COBH.2 (2002). The input record gives 2015-04-07. Verify against the CSC minutes.
- Named breeder or lead scientist: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or postal address for COBH 2 was found.
- Institute contact page URL: none retrieved from the TNAU HCRI pages I reached.
- The VFPCK phone numbers and Kochi address in one result belong to a seed-production body, not TNAU. Discarded.

PUBLICATIONS
- Praneetha S., Rajasree V. (year not shown). Performance of grafted brinjal (Solanum melongena L) under different spacing and fertigation levels. Horticultural College and Research Institute, TNAU, Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344087071_Performance_of_grafted_brinjal_Solanum_melongena_L_under_different_spacing_and_fertigation_levels
- Gill A.K., Sidhu M.K., Dhatt A.S., Chawla N. (2023). Heterotic combinations among advanced breeding lines of brinjal (Solanum melongena L.). Vegetable Science 50(2): 288-294. -- https://isvsvegsci.in/index.php/vegetable/article/download/389/321 (Not COBH 2; listed only as a non-match. Do not attribute to this variety.)
- No COBH 2-specific AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet listing: not checked (see search note). Filed as MAIZE, so it is inconsistent with brinjal.
- A TNAU Agritech input-price list includes a line "Brinjal (parents of COBGHOH-1) CoBH.2" at a price of 5000.00, with no unit and no clear link to COBH 2 as a public hybrid. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/input_source_tnau_seed.html
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed sales for COBH 2: No evidence found.
- Private dealer listings found (VNR, Mahyco, Seminis, Plant Orbit and others) do not name COBH 2. Discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The record says "Not specified". TNAU-linked sources point to Tamil Nadu. One source recommends irrigated conditions in July-December and January-June. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_brinjal_varieties_COBH.html
- Districts named in the HOR 211 deck: Coimbatore, Dharmapuri, Madurai, Dindigul, Theni, Cuddalore, Villupuram, Pudukkottai, Erode and Kanyakumari. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/hor-211-2-tomato-brinjal-chilli-pptx/269858871
- No other state recommendation found.

drought.details: The hybrid is described as suited to rain-fed areas and performed well under both rainfed and irrigated conditions in station, multi-location, AICRP, adaptive and on-farm trials (the paper uses the name 'COH 3'). Non-lodging habit is reported. The press report gives no drought test data, and no specific drought tolerance scores or mechanisms were found.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance scores or mechanisms in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance scores or mechanisms in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance. The press report gives no flood test data.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to necrosis, leaf spot and powdery mildew, reported in the release paper (uses the name 'COH 3') and in the TNAU press report. No quantitative disease scores were found.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for pest resistance in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 2214 kg/ha, about 20.5% above the check Sunbred 275. Kharif yield 2384 kg/ha and rabi yield 2043 kg/ha. Fertilizer study: 2194 kg/ha. The CSC record gives the average_yield field only as 'Kg/Ha' with no value.
agronomic_details.stability: The hybrid performed well under both rainfed and irrigated conditions across station, multi-location, AICRP, adaptive and on-farm trials. Non-lodging habit is reported. No quantitative stability statistics were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described as suited to rain-fed areas. The CSC record gives rainfed sowing in September-October and irrigated sowing in June-July and January-February in Tamil Nadu. The digest does not independently verify these windows.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: COH 3 (variety_name) / COH-3 (seednet_variety_name), sunflower

Search note: Four searches were run (variety, breeder, research, seed availability). Every search returned the same core source, a 2021 Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding paper on the hybrid. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search, so there is no Seednet evidence under either name. Where the evidence refers to the "COH 3" name rather than "COH-3", that is noted below. All findings below are about the sunflower hybrid.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Non-lodging habit, and the hybrid performed well under both rainfed and irrigated conditions in station, multi-location, AICRP, adaptive and on-farm trials (the paper uses "COH 3" and "CSFH 12205") -- https://www.academia.edu/49582284/Sunflower_COH_3_A_high_yielding_and_high_oil_content_sunflower_hybrid_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Described as suited to rain-fed areas; the press report gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence test data -- https://www.ofimagazine.com/news/tnau-launches-high-yielding-sunflower-variety
- No evidence found for specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance scores.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to necrosis, leaf spot and powdery mildew (the paper uses "COH 3") -- https://www.academia.edu/49582284/Sunflower_COH_3_A_high_yielding_and_high_oil_content_sunflower_hybrid_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Same moderate disease-resistance statement, reported from TNAU -- https://www.ofimagazine.com/news/tnau-launches-high-yielding-sunflower-variety
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average yield 2214 kg/ha, about 20.5% above the check Sunbred 275; 2384 kg/ha in kharif and 2043 kg/ha in rabi; duration 90-95 days -- https://www.academia.edu/49582284/Sunflower_COH_3_A_high_yielding_and_high_oil_content_sunflower_hybrid_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Oil content about 42%, against 38% for Sunbred 275 and 39% for CO 2 hybrid; oil yield 716 kg/ha -- https://www.academia.edu/49582284/Sunflower_COH_3_A_high_yielding_and_high_oil_content_sunflower_hybrid_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Fertilizer study: the COH 3 hybrid gave 2194 kg/ha, 39.8% oil and 875 kg/ha oil yield; 60:90:60 kg NPK/ha at 100% fertilizer was economical -- https://www.masujournal.org/109/ZpXQ5qwKHUUfHdYrLQtUKtQeAGQ5Sj.pdf
- Seed-stage status reported by TNAU in the press report -- https://www.ofimagazine.com/news/tnau-launches-high-yielding-sunflower-variety

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (UMI 101 x UMI 130) x (UMI 90 x UMI 28): No evidence found in the retrieved pages.
- Molecular marker, QTL or marker-assisted work specific to COH 3: No evidence found.
- The TNAU Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics staff page lists COH 3 (hybrid) among sunflower entries in a project list, not as a marker study -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/manivannancv

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Department of Oilseeds, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore-641003 (affiliation given on the fertilizer paper) -- https://www.masujournal.org/109/ZpXQ5qwKHUUfHdYrLQtUKtQeAGQ5Sj.pdf
- Release-level institutional statement: TNAU developed the hybrid -- https://www.ofimagazine.com/news/tnau-launches-high-yielding-sunflower-variety
- Lead breeder: the paper's first author is N. Manivannan, and he is listed as the lead author of the COH 3 release paper. No page states explicitly that he is the breeder of COH 3, so treat this as authorship, not a confirmed breeder designation -- https://www.mdpi.com/2311-7524/9/10/1079 (reference list) and https://www.academia.edu/49582284/Sunflower_COH_3_A_high_yielding_and_high_oil_content_sunflower_hybrid_for_Tamil_Nadu
- Other listed co-authors of the release paper: R. Chandirakala, S. Manonmani, P.L. Viswanathan, K. Ganesamurthy, M.Y. Dudhe, M. Sujatha, A. Vishnuvardhan Reddy, R. Sasikala, L. Rajendran (per the same reference list)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Individual breeder email, phone or address: No evidence found.
- Institute-level: Department of Oilseeds, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, TNAU, Coimbatore-641003, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.masujournal.org/109/ZpXQ5qwKHUUfHdYrLQtUKtQeAGQ5Sj.pdf (postal address only; no phone or email on the retrieved page)
- Institute contact or website page: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Manivannan, N.; Chandirakala, R.; Manonmani, S.; Viswanathan, P.L.; Ganesamurthy, K.; Dudhe, M.Y.; Sujatha, M.; Vishnuvardhan Reddy, A.; Sasikala, R.; Rajendran, L.; et al. (2021). Electronic Journal of Plant Breeding -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=DJ20220765377 ; https://www.academia.edu/49582284/Sunflower_COH_3_A_high_yielding_and_high_oil_content_sunflower_hybrid_for_Tamil_Nadu (volume and page numbers not found)
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Fertilizer-response study on COH 3 and other sunflower hybrids. Journal: Mahatma Phule ... (MASU journal, per URL) -- https://www.masujournal.org/109/ZpXQ5qwKHUUfHdYrLQtUKtQeAGQ5Sj.pdf (full title and authors not visible in the snippet)

- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or DOI specific to COH 3 was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- TNAU Seed Centre, Coimbatore, seed stock position as on 31.07.2021: Sunflower COH3, 80 (quantity unit not stated), held by Dept. of Oilseeds, TNAU. The page says stock is subject to availability at enquiry -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES

The same report's 2008-2011 overall mean table for CMH-08-282 lists COH(M) 5 as the check. No other trial results for COH(M) 5 were found.
