search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specifically for COH (M) 5. The only performance data are yield comparisons against it under irrigated and rainfed conditions (see AGRONOMY AND TRIALS). -- https://masujournal.org/view_archive_journal.php?id=1123

DISEASE AND PEST
Compendium entry for COH(M) 5 (TNAU, Coimbatore, 2007) lists resistance to MLB (maydis leaf blight). The table layout is scrambled, so this could be attached to a neighbouring entry; treat as unconfirmed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
No evidence found for resistance to other diseases or pests (e.g., downy mildew, stalk rot, fall armyworm) specifically for COH(M) 5.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Compendium gives COH(M) 5 a medium maturity and an average yield of 54 q/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
In the Co 6 trial report, COH(M) 5 served as the check hybrid. Its mean grain yield was 5739 kg/ha under irrigation and 4209 kg/ha under rainfed conditions, and the report notes the trials covered 100 adaptive, 16 multi-location, 138 on-farm, 9 station and 49 All India trials. This is comparison data for a different hybrid, not a trial of COH(M) 5 itself. -- https://masujournal.org/view_archive_journal.php?id=1123
Same report, full text: Department of Millets, TNAU, Coimbatore authors; the 2008-2011 overall mean table for CMH-08-282 lists COH(M) 5 as check. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
TNAU Coimbatore AICRP-Maize page lists COH(M) 5 among state-level single-cross releases for Tamil Nadu. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/coimbatore-tamil-nadu/
Note: no record for "CoH (M) 10" or "CMH 08-433" was found in any result. The closest match is COH(M) 5 by parentage (UMI 285 x UMI 61), which the compendium entry gives as the pedigree of COH(M) 5. The 2014 release date in the record does not match the 2007 date in the compendium.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage of COH(M) 5 per the Directorate of Maize Research compendium: UMI 285 x UMI 61 (TNAU, Coimbatore). This matches the record's parentage, but the source does not mention the variety name "CoH (M) 10" or variety code "CMH 08-433". -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on COH(M) 5.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Dr. G. Nallathambi, Professor (Maize Breeding), AICRP-Maize, Department of Millets, TNAU, Coimbatore. His CV page lists COH(M) 5 among the maize hybrids he has released. This is the lead breeder attribution; no page explicitly states "developed by" for COH(M) 5. -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/nallathambicv
Developing institution: TNAU, Coimbatore (Department of Millets, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics). -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/coimbatore-tamil-nadu/

CONTACT DETAILS
Dr. G. Nallathambi, Professor (Maize Breeding), AICRP-Maize, Department of Millets, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore-641003, Tamil Nadu, India. Office: +91 0422 2450507. Fax: +91 0422 6611415. Mobile: +91 9486913279. Email: nthambi2002@yahoo.co.in -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/nallathambicv
Institute address: Department of Millets, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore -641003. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/coimbatore-tamil-nadu/
Department of Millets (phone and email as listed in the TNAU seed stock notice): 0422-2450507; millets@tnau.ac.in -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
TNAU Seed Centre (listed in the 2019 seed availability notice): seed@tnau.ac.in; 0422-6611363 (the number is printed next to the millet row, so confirm before use). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/pdf/seedavailabilityon13.08.2019.pdf
Dr. Nallathambi's email and phone number appear on a personal lab web page; confirm before use. The official TNAU directory page for these contacts was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
Nallathambi, G.; Ganesan, K.N.; Tamilarasi, P.M.; Dass, S.; Thiyagarajan, K.; Veerabadhiran, P.; Paranidharan, V.; Sridharan, S. (year not shown in retrieved text). A High Yielding Multiple Disease Resistant TNAU Maize Hybrid Co 6 for Tamil Nadu. Journal of Maize Research/MASU journal -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-10-12-677-680.pdf
Note: this paper is about Co 6 (CMH-08-282). It is included only because COH(M) 5 is the check hybrid in it; it is not a paper on COH(M) 5.
No evidence found for a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report or KrishiKosh thesis specifically on CoH (M) 10, CMH 08-433 or COH(M) 5.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for COH(M) 5 in TNAU seed stock lists. The 2022 stock list shows TNAU maize hybrid CO 6 (Department of Millets), and the 2019 list shows COH(M) 6 at KVK, Kattupakkam, not COH(M) 5. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf
No evidence found on the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) or from NSC, a State Seed Corporation, or private dealers for COH(M) 5 or CoH (M) 10.
Contact for seed enquiries: Director (Seeds), Seed Centre, TNAU, Coimbatore-641003. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
Compendium entry for COH(M) 5: area of adaptation given as Tamil Nadu under irrigated and rainfed conditions, with the list truncated in the retrieved text. Another TNAU compendium entry gives Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Karnataka for a different hybrid, not COH(M) 5. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
The record's eight-state list (adding Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh) is not supported by any retrieved source. The TNAU Coimbatore AICRP page lists COH(M) 5 for Tamil Nadu release. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/coimbatore-tamil-nadu/

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: AICRP- Maize (ICAR), Department Of Millets, Centre for Plant Breeding & Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural university, Coimbatore-3.
seednet_fields.Parentage: It is a single cross hybrid of two inbreds (UMI 1201 x UMI1230).
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology:
Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Rajasthan. Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Punjab, Haryana, Delhi 
and Maharashtra in kharif season.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: CMH 08-292 is non-lodging and non shattering type. Highly efficient at moderate level of N (150: 50: 40 NPK Kg/ ha). It is grouped under medium maturity group (84-92 days), Seed rate is 20 Kg/ha.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: It possesses multiple disease resistance viz., Maydis leaf blight, Turcicum leaf blight, Rajasthan downy mildew, Downy mildew and moderately resistant to post flowering stalk rot, banded leaf and sheath blight
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Resistant to cyst nematode (Heterodera zeae) and moderately resistant to stem borer (Chilo partellus)

disease_resistance.summary: Specific disease resistance for CoH (M)8 is not specified in the provided information. Maize in India is prone to various biotic stresses like foliar diseases. drought.details: CP-333 exhibits strong drought tolerance and is suitable for rainfed conditions. It is also tolerant to variable weather conditions.

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance for CP-333 was found.

salinity.details: No specific information on salinity tolerance for CP-333 was found.

flood.details: No specific information on flood tolerance (water logging resistance) for CP-333 was found.

disease_resistance.summary: CP-333 is described as resistant to major and common diseases. Specifically, it shows resistance to Northern Corn Leaf Blight (NCLB), turcicum-leaf blight, bacterial leaf blight, and bacterial sheath blight.

pest_resistance.summary: CP-333 is tolerant to Fall Armyworm and generally described as resistant to common insect pests.

agronomic_details.yield: CP-333 is described as a high-yielding hybrid. Reported yields include 67.15 quintals/hectare (q/ha) in Himachal Pradesh (2020-21), 71.37 q/ha in Zone-II of Himachal Pradesh (2021-22), and 94.7 q/ha in Zone V of Assam under rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety demonstrates wide adaptation and is broadly adapted for cultivation in mid to high-yield environments. It is tolerant to variable weather conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CP-333 is suitable for rainfed conditions in Assam (Zone V) and for cultivation in Zone-II of Himachal Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Key morphological features include big and long ears with excellent color, and big, deep kernels. It is also noted for better germination and vibrant growth.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field trials in Himachal Pradesh recorded yields of 67.15 q/ha (2020-21) and 71.37 q/ha (2021-22, Zone-II). Trials in Assam showed a yield of 94.7 q/ha in Zone V under rainfed conditions.

drought.details: No drought evidence found for CP 858. Searched; no page names drought tolerance for this hybrid. The seller page gives a generic growing condition of 21 to 27 degrees C and 50 to 100 cm rainfall, which is not a drought tolerance measure.

heat.details: No heat stress evidence found for CP 858. Searched; no page names heat tolerance for this hybrid.

salinity.details: No salinity evidence found for CP 858. Searched; no page names salinity tolerance for this hybrid.

flood.details: No flood evidence found for CP 858. Searched; no page names flood tolerance for this hybrid.

disease_resistance.summary: Seller marketing copy claims strong disease tolerance for CP 858, but no named pathogen, resistance rating, or trial data is given. No specific disease resistance data found beyond this generic claim.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified' and no pest resistance data was found for CP 858.

agronomic_details.yield: Seller specification sheet gives a yield potential of about 23 to 30 quintals per acre. The catalogue describes the hybrid as higher yielding, with no trial data. The input record's average_yield field ('Kg/Ha') has no numeric value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The manufacturer's catalogue claims wide adaptation, but no multi-location or stability data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended states in the input record are Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand (Plains), Uttar Pradesh (Eastern and Western regions), Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal; these are not confirmed by any independent source. Seller page gives a generic growing condition of 21 to 27 degrees C and 50 to 100 cm rainfall, and states that some northern states grow it in rabi season.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 105 to 115 days to first harvest, per the seller specification sheet. No independent trial confirms this figure.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Hybrid with erect growth habit, medium-to-tall plants, deep kernels, and a big, long ear with big and deep grain (manufacturer catalogue description, no trial data).
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location, AICRP, or field-trial results found for CP 858. The only trial hits concerned other hybrids (CP 808 in Nepal) and were excluded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CP 858 (maize)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "CP 858". The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any search result, so all evidence below comes from commercial and company pages, not from Seednet or ICAR records.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Strong disease tolerance is claimed in seller marketing copy, with no named pathogen or trial data -- https://agribegri.com/products/cp-858-maize-seeds-makka-seeds.php
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence evidence found for CP 858 -- searched; no page names these traits for this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No specific disease or pest resistance data found for CP 858 beyond the generic "strong disease tolerance" claim above -- https://agribegri.com/products/cp-858-maize-seeds-makka-seeds.php

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Seller specification sheet: hybrid, erect growth habit, medium-to-tall plants, deep kernels, yield potential about 23 to 30 quintals per acre, first harvest 105 to 115 days -- https://agribegri.com/products/cp-858-maize-seeds-makka-seeds.php
- Maturity of 105 to 115 days is stated on the same seller page; no independent trial confirms it -- https://agribegri.com/products/cp-858-maize-seeds-makka-seeds.php
- Manufacturer's catalogue describes it as higher yielding with a big, long ear, big and deep grain, and wide adaptation (no trial data) -- https://www.cpseeds-india.com/
- Seller page gives a generic growing condition of 21 to 27 °C and 50 to 100 cm rainfall, with some northern states growing it in rabi -- https://www.shinebrandseeds.com/product/maize---cp-858---cp-seeds
- No multi-location, AICRP, or field-trial results for CP 858 found -- searched; the only trial hits concerned other hybrids (e.g., CP 808 in Nepal).

GENETICS AND QTL
- No parentage, pedigree, or QTL/marker evidence found for CP 858 -- searched; "Not specified" in the record is consistent with the search results.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing company: Charoen Pokphand Seeds (India) Pvt. Ltd. (listed as manufacturer on the product pages) -- https://www.cpseeds-india.com/
- No named lead breeder or scientist found for CP 858 -- searched; no breeder page or institute page returned for this variety.
- Catalogue lists it under a code "IRF858" alongside the name CP 858 (meaning of the code unverified) -- https://www.cpseeds-india.com/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No official company email, phone, or head-office postal address found for CP 858 -- searched.
- Trade-listing location only: Thippasandra, Bengaluru, Karnataka, for Charoen Pokphand Seeds (I) Pvt. Ltd. (exporter listing, not an official contact page) -- https://www.exportersindia.com/charoen-pokphand-seeds-india-pvt-ltd/c-p-858-hybrid-maize-seeds-5508801.htm
- Company website exists but no contact page was retrieved -- https://www.cpseeds-india.com/

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. Searches returned no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record naming CP 858. Hits that were discarded: a 2022 Nepal terai trial featuring CP 808 (different variety) -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9674539/ ; a 2026 AICRP decision-support paper with no CP 858 naming in the retrieved text -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2026.1885434/xml

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Shine Brand Seeds (online retailer): listed as out of stock; 4 kg pack at about ₹1600 (list ₹2300) -- https://www.shinebrandseeds.com/product/maize---cp-858---cp-seeds

- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or SAU seed-sales listing found for CP 858 -- searched.

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Searches run: 4 (the maximum allowed). Names: "Central Maize VL Sweet Corn 1" (CSC minutes name) and "Central maize VL Sweet Corn 1 (FSCH18)" (Seednet name). Every hit that names this variety is the ICAR-IIMR cultivar list or a Scribd copy of the 1969–2017 maize release table, and both use the same name and code. The Seednet portal itself did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. No search result states drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. -- No evidence (searches 1 and 3 returned only generic maize and sweet corn pages)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No result mentions disease or pest resistance for this variety. -- No evidence

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Release table lists plant as sturdy and medium in height, with large open tassel, green glumes, and yellow anthers; the snippet gives these as the plant description. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
Release table lists average yield of 10.8 for this variety (unit not shown in the snippet; likely t/ha but unconfirmed). -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
Release table lists the season as Kharif and the type as Sweet Corn. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf ; https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/
Release table shows maturity-related figure "90-95" beside this entry; the snippet does not label it, so treat it as unconfirmed. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
Multi-location trial data: AICRP Maize Kharif 2016 report lists sweet corn entries FSCH 55, FSCH 75 and FSCH 91 (VPKAS Almora) but the snippet does not show FSCH 18 or this variety. No evidence for this variety's trial results. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No pedigree or parentage information for this variety (the input record also says "Not specified"), and no QTL or marker study was found. -- No evidence

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution listed as VPKAS (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan), Almora, Uttarakhand, public sector, for this variety. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/ ; https://www.scribd.com/document/451634301/Maize-cultivars-1969-2017-pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. -- No evidence
Notification/release record: listed with notification date 22-11-2016 and notification number 3540 E. The input "year_of_release" field shows 12 Aug 2016; the record dates differ, so the notification date should be confirmed against the Gazette. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a named breeder, official email, phone, postal address or contact page. Institute-level pointer only: VPKAS Almora is the listed developer (no address or contact details appeared in results). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/cultivars-2/

PUBLICATIONS

drought.details: The provided search results contain general discussions on drought stress tolerance in maize, and mention DHM-117 as being drought tolerant (Result 9, 20, 35, 44), but specific information regarding HM-11's drought tolerance is not available.

heat.details: While the search results discuss the importance of heat stress tolerance in maize (Result 19, 20) and mention DHM-117 in the context of elevated temperature conditions (Result 11), specific information regarding HM-11's heat tolerance is not available.

salinity.details: Maize generally does not perform well in saline or alkaline soils (Result 27, 29). The results mention the cultivation of salt-tolerant crops like bitter gourd in affected saline lands (Result 26), but no specific information on HM-11's salinity tolerance is provided.

flood.details: The results indicate that maize does not come up well in waterlogged soils (Result 27) and advise avoiding waterlogging (Result 36). While DHM-117 is mentioned as having water logging tolerance (Result 37), specific information about flood tolerance for HM-11 is not available. Other varieties are mentioned for submergence tolerance (Result 32, 49), but not HM-11.

No plot-level, multi-location yield-trial results, or FLD data for DHM 119 were found in the searched sources.

Caveat: the source page URL refers to DHM 121 in its title, so the attribution to DHM 119 rests on the digest's reading of that page and should be verified against the full text.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
DHM 119 maize -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: all four searches used "DHM 119" and "BH 4062" (the CSC minute name). I did not run a separate search on the Seednet name "DHM-117." because the four-search limit was reached. Pages that discuss DHM 117 or DHM 121 were discarded as other varieties, so nothing below is attributed to DHM-117.

STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to DHM 119 / BH 4062)
Hybrid is described as nutrient responsive and resistant to lodging -- Listed as a 2011 medium-maturity hybrid with yellow flint grain, nutrient responsive, and resistance to lodging -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found for DHM 119 in these results. -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST (evidence refers to DHM 119 / BH 4062)
No evidence found. The only trait listed for DHM 119 is lodging resistance (see above). The disease resistance text in the same table applies to other rows, not to DHM 119. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to DHM 119 / BH 4062)
Maturity: Listed under medium duration (90-100 days) in the Andhra Pradesh package of practices -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/package%20of%20practices/MaizePackage.pdf
Yield: the release table gives an average yield of 7.0 (units not stated in the snippet) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
A benchmarking presentation lists DHM 119 with a value of 8.6 in an unlabelled yield-type column, unit unclear -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
Multi-location trial data: Listed in the Kharif 2016 AICRP annual report with a PPV&FRA-linked period from August 2016 to August 2031, ANGRAU Hyderabad -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
No DHM 119 yield-trial data (plot-level, multi-location, or FLD) was found. The Karimnagar rainfall-adaptation trial and the Mahabubnagar FLD papers concern DHM 117, DHM 115 and 30V92, so they were discarded. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL (evidence refers to DHM 119 / BH 4062)
Pedigree: BML 2 x BML 15 (single cross hybrid) -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hyderabad-telangana/

drought.details: DHM 117 exhibits drought stress tolerance, requires less water, and is recognized as a drought-tolerant maize variety. It has been included in marker-assisted selection programs for drought tolerance and demonstrated as such. Physiological responses like reduced stomatal conductance (gs) and transpiration rate (Tr) were observed under elevated temperature (eT) and combined stress (eT+) conditions.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to abiotic stresses, including heat. Its medium duration maturity (90-100 days) is advised to escape terminal heat stress.

salinity.details: General statements indicate that maize does not perform well in saline and alkaline soils, and these soil types should be avoided. No explicit salinity tolerance is stated for DHM 117.

flood.details: DHM 117 is noted for water logging tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: DHM 117 has been identified as a susceptible check for Post-Flowering Stalk Rot (PFSR) in maize research.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific information on pest resistance is provided.

agronomic_details.yield: DHM 117 is recognized as a high-yielding maize variety and a resilient performer. While specific average yield figures vary or are not explicitly quantified consistently across all sources, it is listed among top high-yielding varieties.
agronomic_details.stability: Described as a 'Resilient Performer', indicating good stability across different environmental conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for both Kharif and Rabi seasons, particularly suitable for areas where a single crop is grown. It is also noted as nutrient responsive.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DHM 117 exhibits tolerance to lodging. Its grain is typically yellow to orange-yellow and of flint type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been part of research and demonstrations on drought tolerance in locations like Kullu, Himachal Pradesh. It has also been studied under elevated temperature and water stress conditions, and its performance related to submergence tolerance has been evaluated in trials.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Quantitative Trait Loci (QTLs) for flowering time have been identified using SSR markers in maize under water stress, with DHM 117 being part of these studies. It has also been utilized in marker-assisted selection (MAS) for drought tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Studies have identified QTLs for flowering time under water stress involving DHM 117; however, specific QTL locations or detailed effects are not provided.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Physiological responses, such as reductions in stomatal conductance (gs) and transpiration rate (Tr), have been observed in DHM 117 under elevated temperature and combined stress conditions, indicating specific physiological mechanisms for stress reaction.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: As a public sector-released hybrid from ANGRAU, it is likely available through government agricultural channels and state seed corporations.
commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available. The variety is consistently recommended in recent ICAR Kharif and Rabi Agro-Advisories for farmers (as late as 2025 Kharif) and is listed among top high-yielding varieties, suggesting ongoing and widespread availability.
commercial_info.private_dealers: DHM 117 is also known as Dekalb Hybrid Maize, indicating commercial availability through private seed dealers associated with the Dekalb brand.

flood.label: Confirmed by 2+ sources

drought.details: DHM 121 is listed with Pusa Hybrid Makka 1, HM 4, Pusa Hybrid Makka 5 and Buland as a drought-tolerant maize variety in the ICAR/PIB/APN-GCR lists of stress-tolerant varieties. The snippets give no quantitative drought data, no yield penalty under stress, and no mechanism. The CRIDA Annual Report 2021 mentions DHM-121 in a CO2 response experiment, which is not a drought trial. The rating is therefore medium on the strength of list-based evidence only.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat tolerance data were found. The ICAR Rabi advisory lists DHM 121 among recommended hybrids and discusses escaping terminal heat stress through sowing time. This is an agronomic recommendation, not evidence of genetic heat tolerance.

salinity.details: The salinity-tolerant crops and varieties named in the snippets are mostly rice (Binadhan-8 and 10) and other crops. DHM 121 is not identified as salt tolerant.

flood.details: DHM 121 appears in the same stress-tolerant list as drought-tolerant varieties, but no flood or waterlogging tolerance is stated for it specifically. The ResearchGate release compendium snippet mentions waterlogging-tolerance breeding in general terms.

disease_resistance.summary: The ResearchGate compendium snippet says DHM-121, BIO-9544, HT5106 and NK6802 were found moderately resistant to a disease whose name is truncated in the snippet. The disease cannot be identified from the available text.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance information was found.

agronomic_details.yield: No quantitative yield was found in the snippets. The ISGPB paper reports that DHM 121 accounted for 9.7% of the maize breeder seed indent, which indicates substantial adoption.
agronomic_details.stability: The only evidence is its inclusion in the stress-tolerant lists and the heterosis abstracts. No multi-environment stability analysis was found. In a Himachal (CSKHPKV) trial, none of the tested entries, including DHM 121, recorded significantly higher yield than the check.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kharif season. The release region covers eastern, western and central India. It is also recommended in ICAR advisories for the Telangana rabi rice-fallow zero-till system as a medium-duration hybrid, and in the ICAR Kharif advisories 2021 and 2025 as a medium-maturity variety. Odisha's contingency crop plan lists it as well. The classification is single cross hybrid (SCH), released by PJTSAU, Telangana, in 2014.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: CRIDA experiments tested DHM-121 under elevated CO2, where it showed a response. The Himachal trial showed no significant superiority over the check. AICRP on Maize released it in 2013 (compendium) and the release is dated 2014 here.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SNP or SSR information specific to DHM 121 was found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found. The CRIDA report mentions marker-assisted selection for drought tolerance in maize in general, not for DHM 121.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found. The 13th Asian Maize Conference abstracts mention DHM 121 in relation to grain yield per plant and heterosis, which indicates a single cross hybrid with substantial heterotic effects. No genes or pathways are reported.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not specifically identified. The ISGPB paper's breeder seed indent share indicates public-sector seed chain production.
commercial_info.availability_status: readily available (inferred from continued inclusion in ICAR advisories through 2025 and its breeder seed indent share)
commercial_info.private_dealers: Not found. The Rajasthan value chain report lists DHM 121 (BH 41009) among hybrids available in the state.

disease_resistance.summary: The AICRP Kharif 2016 report lists DMRH 1305 against MLB (maydis leaf blight), CLS (curvularia leaf spot) and RDM (rajasthan downy mildew), but the snippet does not show whether these entries denote resistance or susceptibility. A ResearchGate article on newly released single-cross hybrids mentions moderate resistance to charcoal rot under artificial inoculation, but the snippet does not clearly link this to DMRH 1305. The HAU document mentions moderate resistance to leaf blight in an adjacent entry that may not refer to this hybrid. No confirmed resistance profile can be stated.

agronomic_details.adaptation: A normal field corn single-cross hybrid developed by ICAR-IIMR for the Northern hill ecology. The eGyanKosh table lists it for Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand (hill region) and several north-eastern states (Meghalaya, Sikkim, Assam, Tripura, Nagaland). An ICAR advisory recommends it for areas below 1850 m altitude. The HAU document describes it as having normal and light orange coloured grain and early maturity. The sugarcane ready reckoner snippet lists it with year 2018 and notes suitability for irrigated rainy-season conditions, though the numeric values (93, 60) are unclear.

agronomic_details.field_trials: Evaluated under AICRP maize trials, including Kharif 2016 disease screening. It is registered with PPV&FRA (Registration REG/2019/183, received 31-12-2019).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GK 3155 (maize)

Search note: I ran four web_search queries (variety, breeder/institute, research trials, seed availability). Seednet was not reached and no search returned a Seednet page, so the portal name "GK 3155" has no verified record. The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical, so both headings refer to the same name. The search evidence below is for the name "GK 3155" in general, and I could not confirm that it matches the Ganga Kaveri entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for GK 3155.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for GK 3155.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A multi-location genotype-by-environment study lists GK 3155 among hybrids judged stable across environments, with stability reported alongside grain yield, though the study's specific yield figures were not captured -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11776175/
The same study ranks GK3155 among hybrids with superior stability and performance in its joint probability analysis -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11776175/
No yield, maturity or days-to-maturity values were found for GK 3155 in these results.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage or marker/QTL study for GK 3155 was returned. The input parentage is "Not specified."

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Conflict to resolve: the ICAR AICRP on Maize cultivar list records GK 3155 with the developer/owner JKAgrigenetics Limited, Hyderabad, Telangana, listed as Private. This does not match the input institution, Ganga Kaveri Seeds Private Limited -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/
No lead breeder or scientist name was found for GK 3155 in any source.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found. The only institutional entry found is JKAgrigenetics Limited, Hyderabad, Telangana, from the AICRP list, which gives no email, phone or street address -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/cultivars/
No contact details for Ganga Kaveri Seeds Private Limited were found.

PUBLICATIONS
Multi-location GEI and stability study of maize hybrids, including GK 3155 (full author list, title and journal not captured in the search output) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11776175/
The AICRP maize cultivar list is a listing, not a publication, and is included under BREEDER AND INSTITUTION for the release record.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Searches did not return NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listings for GK 3155. A Seednet check is still needed.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Not verified by search. The only source is the input record: Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, and Rabi season in West Bengal. The release year 2018 (input value 2018-01-20) is also unverified.

Recommended next steps: confirm the release notification and the owner name against the CSC minutes and Seednet, since the AICRP list says JKAgrigenetics while the input says Ganga Kaveri Seeds. Obtain the full citation for the PMC11776175 study.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PHB-3 (CSC name) / HB-3 (Seednet name), crop "millet" (CSC) vs "MAIZE (MAKKA)" (Seednet)

Note on names: the evidence below refers to "PHB-3" (and "PHB 3") as a pearl millet (bajra) hybrid. I found no evidence for "HB-3" as a maize hybrid, and no search returned a Seednet record for it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to PHB-3. A general review of pearl millet drought adaptation exists but does not name PHB-3 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3475983/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for PHB-3 resistance to disease or pests. -- (searched; no PHB-3 record returned)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In a 2013-14 rainfed trial at the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Tirupati, PHB-3 and PHB-306 were sown on three dates; PHB-3 gave higher ear-head length, girth, weight, and 1000-grain weight than PHB-306, and the second-fortnight-June sowing gave the best yield attributes -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-sowing-date-on-yield-and-yield-components-of-bajra-in-rainfed-alfisols-of-andhra-pradesh/
- ANGRAU Annual Report 2018-19 uses PHB 3 as the best check, with 3.88 t/ha grain yield, against hybrid ABH 15 at 4.07 t/ha (5.0% higher) -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/Annual%20Report%20%20-%202018-2019%20(1).pdf
- Yield under the 2013-14 Tirupati trial was not captured in the retrieved text -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-sowing-date-on-yield-and-yield-components-of-bajra-in-rainfed-alfisols-of-andhra-pradesh/

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for PHB-3 parentage, cytoplasm, or QTL/marker studies.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The trial evidence places PHB-3 at the Regional Agricultural Research Station, Tirupati (dryland farm), under ANGRAU, Andhra Pradesh -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-sowing-date-on-yield-and-yield-components-of-bajra-in-rainfed-alfisols-of-andhra-pradesh/
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.
- Developing institution: not confirmed. Tirupati is a testing site in the evidence, not a confirmed developer. The CSC release record's "Regional Agricultural Research Station" is consistent with it but unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for breeder names, emails, phone numbers, or postal addresses. No institute contact page for RARS Tirupati or ANGRAU was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (n.d.). Influence Of Sowing Date On Yield And Yield Components Of Bajra In Rainfed Alfisols Of Andhra Pradesh (kharif 2013-14 trial of PHB-3 and PHB-306). Journal of the SASAP (sasapjas.org) -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-sowing-date-on-yield-and-yield-components-of-bajra-in-rainfed-alfisols-of-andhra-pradesh/
- Authors not shown (2019). Annual Report 2018-2019. ANGRAU, Andhra Pradesh -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/Publications/Annual%20Report%20%20-%202018-2019%20(1).pdf
- No other PHB-3 publications found (no KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or DOI).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for PHB-3 seed from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU sales, or private dealers. A dealer listing for "Govinda" hybrid bajra was found, but it is a different hybrid and is not evidence for PHB-3 -- https://www.puregeneagritech.com/product/govinda-research-hybrid-bajra/

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for PHB-3 notification or recommended states. The Tirupati trial location (Andhra Pradesh) is not a recommendation. The release date of 2013-01-18 could not be confirmed.

---
Process notes:

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HM-12 / HKH 313 (maize) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST

Search coverage: 4 web_search calls (variety/release, seednet name, breeder/contact, research/publications, seed availability). Findings below refer to HM-12 (also written HKH 313 / HKM 313 in sources) unless stated. No evidence was found linking the Seednet name HIM-128 to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no stress-tolerance data (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence) attributed to HM-12. The stress-resilience paper found covers hybrids other than HM-12 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12689321

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for HM-12 resistance ratings. The Karnal station's blight-screening results (93 inbred lines and 26 hybrids screened against BLSB in Kharif 2013) do not name HM-12 -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rakesh-Mehra-2

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- HM-12 (HKH 313) was listed among CCS HAU entries in the AICRP Maize Kharif 2016 report, with a validity entry dated Aug 19, 2016 to Aug 18, 2031; the yield for HM-12 is not shown in the extracted tables -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
- HM-12 was tested under AICRP on Maize across zones after development at CCS HAU RRS Karnal -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rakesh-Mehra-2
- Benchmarking presentation lists HM-12 (CCSHAU, Uchani, Karnal) as white, semi-dent, with a Kharif recommendation for UP, Bihar, Jharkhand and Odisha; maturity text in extraction is ambiguous -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
- Maturity: medium (see RECOMMENDED STATES for the notification-based group); the "86-95 days" figure in the benchmarking extract could not be reliably tied to HM-12 and is not used.

GENETICS AND QTL
- HM-12 parentage: single-cross hybrid derived from a cross of Hki1344 and Hki1378 (the user's parentage field "Not specified" can be updated to this) -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5727
- SSR marker pumc1040 gave a 140 bp amplicon for the male parent of HM-12 and distinguished it from HM-5 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5727
- Other SSR markers (pumc1020 and others) confirmed hybridity of HM-12 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/D-5727
- No QTL mapping study specific to HM-12 was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Regional Research Station, Uchani (Karnal), which developed HM-12 as a white single-cross maize hybrid -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rakesh-Mehra-2
- Lead breeder named in the AICRP Kharif 2016 report: Dr. M.C. Kamboj, Assistant Breeder and In-charge Plant Breeding, CCS HAU RRS Karnal. This is the station's maize breeder; a direct HM-12 breeder attribution is inferred from the station, not stated per variety -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
- Rakesh Mehra, Principal Scientist (Plant Pathology), CCS HAU RRS Karnal, is a station scientist who reported HM-12 screening context; not identified as a breeder of HM-12 -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Rakesh-Mehra-2
- Station background: maize research at this station began in 1979 -- https://hau.ac.in/page/home-18

CONTACT DETAILS

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HQPM-4 (maize)

Note: the search budget ran out during a fifth call, so only the four initial searches returned usable results. Only the first ~700 characters of each result were captured, so the findings below are limited to what those snippets showed. Names match in both fields (variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HQPM-4"), so all evidence below refers to that name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. (Searched; no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for HQPM-4 appeared in the captured snippets.)

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. (Searched; no resistance data appeared in the captured snippets.)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
HQPM-4 is listed as one of four quality protein maize (QPM) hybrids released in India, and it was developed by introgressing the o16 allele into parental lines of commercial maize hybrids -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.12923
A ResearchGate table lists HQPM-4 alongside J-1006 and HQPM-1 in a study on QPM as elite feed and fodder for livestock; the snippet gave no yield or trial values -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/The-cultivars-J-1006-HQPM-1-and-HQPM-4_tbl1_308899920

GENETICS AND QTL
The o16 allele is the QPM modifier introgressed into HQPM-4's parental lines -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.12923
Parentage "HKI-193-2 x HKI-161" comes from the supplied variety record; it was not confirmed by any search result -- source: task input (no URL)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No evidence found. (Searched "HQPM-4 maize breeder institute"; the only hit was the Wiley review, which names no breeder. The HQPM series is generally associated with the Hisar (CCSHAU/HAU) maize programme, but no source here confirms that.)

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone, address, or contact-page URL appeared in the captured results.

PUBLICATIONS
Maqbool (2021). Quality protein maize (QPM): Importance, genetics, timeline of different events, breeding strategies and varietal adoption. Plant Breeding -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/pbr.12923 (DOI 10.1111/pbr.12923)
Authors not captured (n.d.). The cultivars J-1006, HQPM-1 and HQPM-4 (table in a QPM feed/fodder study). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/The-cultivars-J-1006-HQPM-1-and-HQPM-4_tbl1_308899920
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report, or QTL/marker paper specific to HQPM-4 appeared in the captured results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. (Searched; no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listings appeared in the captured snippets.)

RECOMMENDED STATES
The supplied record lists: Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, West and Central UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Orissa, Eastern UP, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamilnadu, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh -- source: task input (no URL; not verified by search)

RELEASE AND MATURITY
Year of release: not found. The record shows "NaT," and the Wiley review confirms only that HQPM-4 was released in India, with no year.

Gaps to close next: seednet.gov.in variety page for code A0207401; the CSC/AICRP-Maize notification minutes; KrishiKosh and ICAR/AICRP-Maize annual reports; and the breeding institute's maize page with contact details.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: HT 17169 (maize)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HT 17169", so every search used that one name. I ran four searches (variety, breeder/institution, research, seed availability). None of the returned pages mention HT 17169, Hytech Seed, or variety code A0207797. Nothing below is attributed to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety search returned only an unrelated US patent for hybrid corn CH101699 (https://image-ppubs.uspto.gov/dirsearch-public/print/downloadPdf/10757879).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The research search returned a PubMed article on Ht genes and northern leaf blight resistance in maize (https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30861770). It concerns the Ht gene family in general and does not name HT 17169.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No search returned yield, maturity, or trial data for HT 17169.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The research search returned no QTL or marker study naming this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The breeder search returned a Crop Breeding Institute maize breeding manual (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390474965_Maize_Breeding_Manual_-_CBI). It is a generic manual and does not mention HT 17169 or Hytech Seed India Pvt. Ltd. as its developer.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, or company contact page for Hytech Seed India Pvt. Ltd. or HT 17169 was returned. I did not find an official email, phone, or address.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming HT 17169 was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The search returned an unrelated Senegal peanut seed news article (https://www.seneweb.com/en/news/Agriculture/kedougou-les-semences-darachide-presque-disponibles-pour-la-campagne-2026-2027-mais-le-retard-des-pluies-i). No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found on the search results. The record's stated recommendation is "Punjab, Haryana, Western UP, Delhi and Plain of Uttarakhand" (from the supplied variety data, not verified by any source). The data also lists a release date of 2020-11-09 and parentage as "Not specified", and neither is confirmed by a source.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) for variety code A0207797 directly, and the CSC/ICAR release notification for the 2020 maize release. Both are outside what these searches could reach.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Maize Hema Hybrid (variety_name) / HYBRID MAIZE DECCAN (seednet_variety_name), variety code NAH-1137, UAS Bangalore, crop: maize

Scope note: Four web searches were run (general variety, breeder/institution, Seednet name, seed availability). No dedicated search for research papers or QTL studies was run, so the PUBLICATIONS and GENETICS headings rest on incidental hits only.

Name check: The Seednet name "HYBRID MAIZE DECCAN" returned only a Hyderabad seed company (Deccan Hybrid Seeds) and an ANGRAU variety called "Deccan" (Deccan 105, Deccan 1961). Both were excluded as different products. Every finding below refers to "Hema (NAH-1137)" under variety_name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The variety-specific searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Hema or NAH-1137. A Karnataka ICAR page notes general downy mildew susceptibility in the state's maize, but it does not name Hema -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/17269
Excluded: the CIMMYT and Mahyco stress-tolerant hybrid pages concern RCRMH2 / MRM4070, a different hybrid -- https://www.cimmyt.org/news/stress-resilient-maize-a-big-relief-for-indian-farmers/

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest reaction was recorded for Hema or NAH-1137 in any result.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Hema (NAH-1137) appears in the Kharif 2016 AICRP maize workshop report with release details (see RECOMMENDED STATES). The report's yield-like figure ("7 .25") is not labelled, so no yield value can be assigned to Hema from it -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
No maturity, plant-height, or multi-location trial data were found for Hema.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No parentage, pedigree, inbred-line information, or marker/QTL study was found for Hema or NAH-1137. The parentage field is "Not specified" and remains unconfirmed.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: University of Agricultural Sciences, Bangalore (UAS-B), which lists Hema (NAH-1137) among its maize releases -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/maize/
Institution context: UAS-B reports releasing 7 maize hybrids since 1965 across its portfolio, without naming them -- https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/director-message/
Breeder name: No evidence found. The CIMMYT article naming a UAS-Bangalore maize breeder (BS Vivek) concerns a doubled-haploid facility agreement, not Hema, so no attribution is made -- https://www.cimmyt.org/news/cimmyt-and-uas-bangalore-to-establish-a-maize-doubled-haploid-facility-in-karnataka-india/
Station/division of development: No evidence found (no station or AICRP centre named specifically for Hema).

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No institute-level email, phone or postal address for the UAS-B maize programme or Hema was found in the results. Institute pages to check directly: https://www.uasbangalore.edu.in/en/list-of-crop-varieties-hybrids-released-by-uasb-during-last-ten-years/ (variety list; no contact details in the retrieved text)

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not stated. (2016). Annual Progress Report, Kharif Maize 2016, AICRP on Maize, Annual Maize Workshop, UAS Bengaluru (ICAR-IIMR). Report -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
Authors not stated. (year not stated, ResearchGate PDF). Maize research and development in Karnataka. Journal/report not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361408536_Maize_research_and_development_in_Karnataka
  (This paper names Hema among the major AICRP hybrids of Karnataka, with NAH-2049, Arjun and GH-0727. Full author and journal details were not retrieved.)
No KrishiKosh thesis, conference paper, or peer-reviewed paper specifically on Hema was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Hema seed sales. The UAS-B maize page lists Hema as a product, but it does not show seed sales -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/maize/
Seednet's producer/marketer page lists other Karnataka-linked maize hybrids but not Hema -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Seed_Producers_Marketers.htm
Karnataka's hybrid seed supply comes mainly from private companies; no Hema-specific dealer was identified -- https://www.cimmyt.org/news/seeds-of-triumph-u-p-farmers-celebrate-breakthrough-in-maize-seed-production/

RECOMMENDED STATES
Karnataka. Hema (NAH-1137) was released in Karnataka and listed under the Kharif season in the AICRP report -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf
Release date discrepancy: the AICRP report gives 29/06/2016 with notification no. 2238(E), while the CSC record gives 2016-08-12. Please verify against the official notification or Seednet before using either date.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Maize Hybrid FH 3605 / HIM-123 (variety code FH 3605, Central Maize VL 55)

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run (variety and release; breeder and institute; research papers and trials; seed availability). No page found described FH 3605 under that name, and no page on seednet.gov.in was returned. The only page naming HIM-123 is a commercial blog, which is noted below. Every other result concerned other maize hybrids, other crops, or unrelated topics, and was discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for FH 3605 or HIM-123. Results were generic maize articles and unrelated US patent claims.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for either name was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial, name match on HIM-123 only: the blog lists "Him-123" under baby corn varieties in a generic maize package of practices, with no yield, maturity or trial data -- https://www.bighaat.com/kisan-vedika/blogs/maize-planting-and-package-of-practices. This conflicts with the "hybrid" category in the record and should be verified against an official source. No FH 3605 trial results were found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No pedigree, QTL or marker study for FH 3605 or HIM-123 was returned. The parentage in the record (CM 202 x CM 205; CM 113 x CM 112) was not confirmed by any source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name was found for FH 3605 or HIM-123. Institution-level only: the Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, is the ICAR institute that works on maize hybrids, as shown on pages about other hybrids -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/SR/article/download/174708/64409/506477. No page links FH 3605 or HIM-123 to VPKAS, so the institution attribution in the record is unverified.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No variety-specific or breeder contact found. Institute-level only:
- Institute name and postal address as printed on a VPKAS paper: "Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora 263601, Uttarakhand" -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105 (also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554)
- Named institute director on a symposium presentation: Dr Lakshmi Kant, Director, ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (no email or phone given) -- https://www.taas.in/Upload/Publications/638815746549978560.pdf
- No email or phone number for VPKAS was found in any result.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for FH 3605 or HIM-123. The papers returned concern other VPKAS maize hybrids (Vivek QPM 9, VL VitA, VLQPM Hybrid 45, VL Madhurima) and were excluded. Searches did not reach KrishiKosh or AICRP maize reports for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or dealers. The only HIM-123 mention is the commercial blog above, which is not a dealer listing.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record's "Not specified" field remains unresolved by these searches.

Suggested next steps: check seednet.gov.in directly for "HIM-123" and its notification details; search the CSC release minutes for "FH 3605"; and check the VPKAS (vpkas.res.in) and KrishiKosh records for "Central Maize VL 55".

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Bajra hybrid / "Hybrid Bajra-3" (Seednet) / "Napier Bajra Hybrid PBN 346" (CSC variety code), PAU, released 2016-08-12**

**NAME AND CROP MATCH:** The only retrieved evidence that names this variety refers to PBN 346, a PAU Napier × bajra fodder hybrid (*Pennisetum*), not a grain pearl millet or maize hybrid. The Seednet crop label "MAIZE (MAKKA)" is not supported by any retrieved page. "Hybrid Bajra-3" matched only a 1968-era "Hybrid Bajra No.3" pearl millet entry, which I discarded as a different variety. All findings below refer to the name "Napier Bajra Hybrid PBN 346" unless stated otherwise.

**STRESS TOLERANCE:**
- Hybrid Napier-type plantings are described as tolerant to mild salinity, and waterlogged soils should be avoided. This is stated for the napier bajra hybrid generally on a page that names PBN 346, not as a variety-specific trial result. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fodder/bajra-napier-hybrid
- Drought, heat and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for PBN 346. Searches for the variety returned only general napier-bajra or other-variety pages.

**DISEASE AND PEST:** No evidence found. The Apnikheti page has a pests-and-diseases heading, but the retrieved text contains no content under it for PBN 346.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:**
- PBN 346 is reported to give an average yield of about 715 quintals per acre, with soft, long and wide leaves. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fodder/bajra-napier-hybrid
- PBN 346 is described as a leafy hybrid with smooth, long, broad leaves. The source is a general review of Napier bajra hybrids. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344124034_Bajra_Napier_Hybrid_An_Ideal_Crop_for_Round_the_Year_Green_Fodder_Production
- Field trial at PAU for PBN 346 specifically: No evidence found. The one PAU fodder-trial abstract retrieved (Goyal, kharif 2016, Forage Research Farm, Ludhiana) covers Napier bajra hybrid generally and does not name PBN 346, so I excluded it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324861585_FODDER_PRODUCTIVITY_AND_QUALITY_OF_NAPIER_BAJRA_HYBRID_PENNISETUM_PURPUREUM_PENNISETUM_GLAUCUM_AND_SUMMER_FODDER_INTERCROPS_WITH_DIFFERENT_SEED_RATES

**GENETICS AND QTL:**
- PBN 346 was one of 34 Napier grass genotypes from the PAU Forage Research Farm, characterised with SSR markers across two locations (PAU Ludhiana and PAU Regional Research Station). This is a diversity study, not a QTL study. -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/download/1375/811/3163
- QTL or marker-trait mapping for PBN 346: No evidence found.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:**
- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, through its Forage Research Farm and Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics. The PAU College of Agriculture page lists PBN 346 among Napier bajra materials for which breeder seed is in demand. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20&intLinkID=9
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s) for PBN 346: No evidence found. The PAU fodder pearl millet breeder named in search results (Dr VS Sohu) is linked to different varieties (PCB 168), so I did not attribute him to this variety.

**CONTACT DETAILS:** No evidence found. No email, phone, postal address or contact page for PAU's forage or plant breeding division appeared in the retrieved text. The only PAU institutional URL retrieved is the College of Agriculture page above. Verify contacts at pau.edu before use.

**PUBLICATIONS:**
- Kaur et al. (year not shown in retrieved text). Elucidating molecular and morpho-agronomic diversity of napier grass. Journal not shown in retrieved text (publications.rmsi.in) -- https://publications.rmsi.in/index.php/rma/article/download/1375/811/3163
- Malhi, G. S.; Sharma, K.; Kaur, M.; Gupta, G. (2020). Bajra Napier Hybrid: An Ideal Crop for Round the Year Green Fodder Production. Journal not named in retrieved text (Vol. 2, Issue 9, Article 31707) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344124034_Bajra_Napier_Hybrid_An_Ideal_Crop_for_Round_the_Year_Green_Fodder_Production (no DOI retrieved)
- AICRP or ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, or peer-reviewed papers naming PBN 346 specifically: No evidence found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY:**
- PAU reports ongoing demand for PBN 346 breeder seed at national level. This is a breeder-seed indent, not a sales channel. -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewMatter&intDepTitleID=20&intLinkID=9
- Napier bajra hybrids are propagated vegetatively, so planting material is slips or stem cuttings rather than true seed. The Apnikheti page gives about 11,000 slips or cuttings per acre. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/fodder/bajra-napier-hybrid
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, PAU seed sales or private dealers for PBN 346: No evidence found. The dealer listings retrieved were for grain pearl millet hybrids, which I excluded.

**RECOMMENDED STATES:** No evidence found for PBN 346 in Punjab or elsewhere. The Punjab pearl millet lists retrieved cover grain hybrids and varieties, not PBN 346. The "Punjab" entry in the input comes from the release record and was not verified by any retrieved source.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IQMH 202 (CSC/release name) / IMH 222 (Seednet name), maize
Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institute, research, Seednet name). Evidence refers to IQMH 202 unless stated. No page matched the Seednet name IMH 222 as a standalone entry.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for IQMH 202. Tolerance statements for TLB/BLSB and Chilo partellus on the IIMR maize-hybrids page belong to other hybrids (IQMH 209 and IQMH 211), so I excluded them. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for IQMH 202. The only pest/disease text retrieved (TLB, BLSB, Chilo partellus tolerance) is attributed to IQMH 209 and IQMH 211 on the same page, so it was discarded. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- IIMR lists IQMH 202 as an early kharif single-cross hybrid, about 96 days maturity in the NWPZ kharif season, with yield of 7.2-8.0 t/ha in the recommended ecology. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- IIMR reports a yield advantage of about 13.35% over the relevant best check in the North Western Plain Zone across three years of testing. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Krishi Jagran reports a grain yield of 72.0 q/ha and 96-day maturity for IQMH 202 (LQMH 2), released in 2020. This differs from the IIMR range (7.2-8.0 t/ha = 72-80 q/ha), so both figures should be kept. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/biofortified-maize-varieties-a-nutritious-sustainable-and-profitable-choice-for-farmers/
- A 2025 preprint evaluated 87 hybrids plus 4 checks, including IQMH 202 and IQMH 203 as QPM checks, in an alpha-lattice design with two replications per location in kharif 2025. Only the entry for IQMH 202 as a check was retained; no yield values were extracted. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11164376/v1

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: IIMR states IQMH 202 is DQL 2209 x DMRQPM 106. This answers the "Not specified" parentage field. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Conflict to note: the 2025 preprint describes inbred QIL-4-2192 as an elite QPM parental line of IQMH 202. This does not match DQL 2209 and should be reconciled against IIMR records. The same preprint also lists QIL-4-2209 and DMRQPM 106 as parental inbreds of IQMH 202 and IQMH 203. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11164376/v1
- IQMH 202 is described as a quality protein maize (QPM) hybrid. No QTL, marker, or genotyping study naming this hybrid was found. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11164376/v1

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/biofortified-maize-varieties-a-nutritious-sustainable-and-profitable-choice-for-farmers/ ; https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-20/
- ICAR's institute profile lists IQMH 202, with LQMH 1 and IQMH 203, among three biofortified maize varieties dedicated to the nation. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found. None of the retrieved pages names a breeder for IQMH 202.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for IQMH 203 (LQMH 3 / IIMRQPMH-1705). Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid.
IMH 223 (Seednet name): the institute's hybrid page lists it as having moderate resistance to stem borers (Chilo partellus and Sesamia inferens) and fall armyworm. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for IQMH 203 disease or pest resistance.
IMH 223 (Seednet name): the same institute page reports resistance to Maydis leaf blight. The snippet was truncated, so the full disease list was not confirmed. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
IQMH 203: a Krishi Jagran article gives a 2020 release, yield of 63.0 q/ha and 90 days to maturity for Kharif sowing. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/biofortified-maize-varieties-a-nutritious-sustainable-and-profitable-choice-for-farmers/
IQMH 203: an Agrifarming article gives yield of 6.3 t/ha and medium maturity of 89 days, for Kharif in the Central Western Zone. This conflicts with the 63 q/ha figure above, which is the same value expressed in a different unit, and with the 90-day figure. Verify against the CSC notification or IIMR release notice. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-varieties-of-maize-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
IQMH 203: the IIMR Maize Hybrids page lists the parentage as DQL 2209 × DMRQPM 106 with Kharif season. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
IQMH 203: a 2025 Kharif alpha-lattice trial (Research Square preprint) used IQMH 203 as one of four checks across two replications per location. It does not report stand-alone yield for this hybrid in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11164376/v1
IMH 223 (Seednet name): the IIMR page gives 10.48 t/ha yield and medium maturity (145–155 days rabi; 115–125 days spring), recommended for irrigated conditions in Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand plains, western UP and Delhi NCR. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
IMH 223 (Seednet name): an Agri Innovate India page gives the same 10.48 t/ha across zones and locations, with a potential of up to 12.0 t/ha. -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=77

GENETICS AND QTL
IQMH 203: described as a Quality Protein Maize (QPM) hybrid. Parental inbreds QIL-4-2209, QIL-4-2192 and DMRQPM 106 are named as the parents of QPM hybrids IQMH 202 and IQMH 203. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11164376/v1
IQMH 203: the Agrifarming page gives the parentage as DQL 2209 × DMRQPM 106.
Parentage conflict: the parentage supplied in the record (female IML 15, male BML 7) matches IMH 223 (Seednet name) on the IIMR page, not IQMH 203. The record's parentage should therefore be checked and assigned to the correct variety.
QTL/marker studies: none found that name IQMH 203 or IMH 223. The IIMR 2022 annual report mentions meta-QTL work for fungal disease resistance, but that work does not name either variety in the retrieved text, so it was excluded. -- https://www.iimr.res.in/frontend/images/publications/annual_reports/2022/annual_report_2022.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
IQMH 203: developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
IQMH 203: an ICAR institute profile says the institute dedicated three biofortified maize varieties, LQMH 1, IQMH 202 and IQMH 203, to the nation. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
IQMH 203: an IIMR-linked trial report describes it as an ICAR-IIMR, Ludhiana QPM hybrid. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2022.963368/pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The searches did not return a breeder name for IQMH 203 or IMH 223.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a named breeder, email, phone or postal address for IQMH 203 or IMH 223.
Institute-level: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research, Ludhiana, is the developing institution named by the IIMR maize hybrids page (https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids). The retrieved text did not include its address, phone or email. Its website is listed in the UAS Bangalore varieties page as iimr.icar.gov.in, and the IIMR domain iimr.res.in appears in the institute's own pages. -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-20/

PUBLICATIONS
Kaur et al. (2022). Improvement in nutritional quality of traditional unleavened flat bread using Quality Protein Maize. Frontiers in Nutrition -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fnut.2022.963368 (IQMH 203 is one of the seven genotypes assessed. Full author list was not retrieved.)
Authors not retrieved (2025). Accelerated generation of inbred lines through DH Technology vs conventional bred QPM germplasm: Inbred and hybrid performance for higher genetic gains. Research Square preprint -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-11164376/v1 (IQMH 203 used as a check hybrid; preprint, not peer-reviewed.)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: IMH-230 (seednet name: IMH 223), maize**

**Name and identity warning:** The evidence does not support the Seednet mapping. Every IMH 223 source found describes a different hybrid (IML 15 × BML 7, code IMHSB 17R-9, NWPZ release, Gazette S.O. 4065(E), 2022). IMH 230 (code IMHSB 20R-6) is a separate hybrid from the eastern zone (NEPZ), with parents IML 23 × HKI 1128. The parentage you supplied (IML 15 × BML 7) matches IMH 223, not IMH 230. Treat the Seednet entry as unverified until the portal record is checked.

**Search coverage:** Four web searches were run (release/notification, breeder/institute, research/publications, seed availability). The seednet.gov.in portal was not reached.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- IMH 230 is reported as having lodging tolerance and responsiveness to high inputs. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- No evidence found for IMH 230 drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance.
- IMH 223 is reported as comparatively tolerant to cold stress (not IMH 230). -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

DISEASE AND PEST
- IMH 230 is reported as moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight, Maydis leaf blight, and charcoal rot, and moderately resistant to stem borer (Chilo partellus) and fall armyworm. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- IMH 223 (not IMH 230) is reported as resistant to Maydis leaf blight and Fusarium stalk rot, and moderately resistant to charcoal rot and turcicum leaf blight. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- IMH 223 (not IMH 230) pest scores: moderately tolerant to Chilo partellus and pink stem borer, moderately tolerant to fall armyworm. -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=77

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- IMH 230: rabi season, medium maturity (142-148 days), yield 9.236 t/ha, long thick cylindrical ears, bold semi-flint yellow kernels, high seed productivity of the female parent. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- A second IIMR listing shows 148 days (140-150) and 9.3 t/ha for a hybrid whose heading is cut off in the snippet; it appears to be IMH 230 but is unconfirmed. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Public-release summary: IMH 230 matures in roughly 145 days in rabi in the eastern zone. -- https://choupalsamachar.in/maize-new-hybrid-variety/
- IMH 223 (not IMH 230): 10.48 t/ha, 21.58% yield superiority over best check in NWPZ across three years of AICRP testing. -- https://www.agrinnovateindia.com/technology.html?id=77
- No multi-location trial data for IMH 230 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage conflict: IIMR lists IMH 230 as IML 23 (MIL 2-164-1) × HKI 1128. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- The supplied parentage (female IML 15, male BML 7) matches IMH 223 (IML 15 × BML 7). -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- No QTL or marker studies for IMH 230 found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana, Punjab. -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2044754&reg=48&lang=2
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s) for IMH 230: No evidence found.
- A VIT Vellore paper acknowledges two IIMR scientists for supplying IMH 223 seed (Dr. Shyam Bir Singh, Principal Scientist; Dr. Chikkappa Gangadhar Karjagi, Senior Scientist). They are seed suppliers in that paper, not confirmed breeders of record. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11883377/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research, Ludhiana, Punjab. Institute website: https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Official email, phone, postal address, and named breeder contacts for IMH 230: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis, or DOI specific to IMH 230 was found.
- Related IMH 223 paper (not IMH 230): Authors not shown in the retrieved snippet (year not shown). "Characterizing diverse maize varieties under organic cultivation: phenotypic, yield, and canopy data from VIT Vellore." -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11883377/
- Official release document (IMH 230): Gazette notification S.O. 4388(E), dated 8 October 2024 (see RECOMMENDED STATES). -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

SEED AVAILABILITY
- IIMR has begun branding and selling its own hybrid seed and has signed more than 40 MoUs with 28 private seed companies. -- https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
- IMH 224 (not IMH 230) has MoUs with private companies; the IMH 230 MoU count is not reported. -- https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
- No seller, KVK, SAU, or state corporation stock listing for IMH 230 was found.
- A generic NDDB list shows National Seeds Corporation (Patna) listed for maize, with no link to IMH 230. -- https://nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/state-wise-list-of-seeds-producer-supplier

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Official list: Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal (NEPZ). -- https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleaseIframePage.aspx?PRID=2044754&reg=48&lang=2
- IIMR lists the same states under irrigated conditions. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Release dates conflict: PIB event date 11 August 2024; IIMR Gazette date 8 October 2024 (S.O. 4388(E)); your record says 2 August 2024. Verify against the official gazette before filing.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: IMH 224 (maize)
Variety name (CSC minutes) and Seednet name are both "IMH 224", so the evidence applies to both names.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. None of the captured pages reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for IMH 224.

DISEASE AND PEST
- A Marathi-language launch article says that the set of ICAR-IIMR hybrids it lists, including IMH-224, carries a low chance of pest and disease attack; this is a general press claim, not a trial result -- https://hellokrushi.com/icar-iimr-launches-4-new-hybrid-varieties-of-maize-beneficial-for-farmers/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The VIT Vellore organic-cultivation study grew IMH 224 among eight maize genotypes, and it reports phenotypic, yield and canopy data for them; the IMH 224 values were not captured -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11883377/
- The same article's data set includes IMH 224 kernel-weight data (total kernel weight 163.00 g in the table row captured) in a machine-learning study that uses it as a genotype; this is a dataset value, not a field-trial result -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/artificial-intelligence/articles/10.3389/frai.2026.1742033/xml
- A Marathi-language launch article gives a yield claim of more than 95 quintals per hectare for the listed hybrids, IMH-224 included; this is a promotional claim, not a verified trial mean -- https://hellokrushi.com/icar-iimr-launches-4-new-hybrid-varieties-of-maize-beneficial-for-farmers/

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on IMH 224. The parentage in the request (female IML 22; male BML 16) was supplied by the user and was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The 2022 IIMR annual report lists IMH 224 among the three field-corn hybrids (with IMH 222 and IMH 223) developed, produced and commercialised in 2022 -- https://www.iimr.res.in/frontend/images/publications/annual_reports/2022/annual_report_2022.pdf
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana, Punjab. Source for the institute: https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- No breeder or scientist name was found for IMH 224 in the captured results.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute: ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Official institute website: https://iimr.res.in
- Breeder name, email, phone and postal address for the division: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2026). Machine-learning study using IMH 224 kernel-weight data (Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence). -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/artificial-intelligence/articles/10.3389/frai.2026.1742033/xml ; DOI 10.3389/frai.2026.1742033
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Characterizing diverse maize varieties under organic cultivation: phenotypic, yield, and canopy data from VIT Vellore (includes IMH 224). Journal not captured. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11883377/
- ICAR-IIMR (2022). Annual Report 2022 (IMH 222, IMH 223, IMH 224 produced and commercialised). ICAR-IIMR, Ludhiana. -- https://www.iimr.res.in/frontend/images/publications/annual_reports/2022/annual_report_2022.pdf
- No AICRP/ICAR trial report, KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed variety-release paper naming IMH 224 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The VIT Vellore study says its IMH-series seed was purchased from IIMR (Punjab) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11883377/
- A Hindi-language article gives MoU counts for IMH 224 with seed companies, reported as 5 (the article lists 6, 5 and 2 for LQMH 1, IMH 224 and IQMH 203 in that order) -- https://www.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/icar-iimr-hybrid-maize-seeds-for-farmers/48234
- No Seednet listing, NSC/State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale page for IMH 224 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found. The search results do not confirm the states given in the request (Eastern UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha). Treat them as unverified input and check the CSC minutes or Seednet notification.

NOTE ON THIS SEARCH
- Four web_search queries were run: variety and release, breeder/institute, research, and seed availability. A fifth call hit the tool-use limit, so the contact, breeder and trial gaps above could not be followed up. The search-result pages cited above are the only sources.
- The searches did not return the official Seednet or CSC notification page for IMH 224.
- The IIMR maize-hybrids page appeared in results, but the captured text did not include the IMH 224 entry, so it is cited only as the institute source.
- Hindi and Marathi news articles are secondary sources; their yield and pest-resistance claims should be checked against IIMR or CSC documents.
