search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NOTE: The record conflicts. "Parbat" (variety_name, crop walnut) matches a walnut release, JWSP 06 (PARBAT). "PARBHAT" (seednet_variety_name, crop MAIZE (MAKKA)) and its parentage (Prabhat J-115, Partap J54 x Suwan 1) describe a maize variety. These are likely two different varieties, so the findings below are not merged. Only four searches ran; a later fifth search hit the tool limit. Most headings therefore have little or no evidence.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for PARBHAT/Prabhat (maize) in the searches. No stress-tolerance data was found for the walnut Parbat either.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Walnut Parbat (JWSP 06): the search returned only an abstract fragment, which says the variety was notified as an elite walnut selection by the Government of Jammu and Kashmir. No yield or trial data was retrieved. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353156900_Walnut_Variety_Release_JWSP_06_PARBAT
Maize PARBHAT/Prabhat: No evidence found. The only related hit was a general article on maize production trends in Jammu & Kashmir, with no variety data. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357280433_Trends_of_maize_production_in_Jammu_Kashmir

GENETICS AND QTL
Maize PARBHAT/Prabhat: the parentage field (Partap J54 x Suwan 1, backcross with Partap, then mass selection) is from the input record only. No independent source was retrieved to confirm it. No QTL or marker study was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Walnut Parbat: the notifying body is the Government of Jammu and Kashmir. The breeder name and developing institution were not found in the retrieved text.
Maize PARBHAT/Prabhat: the input record names Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) as institution. No independent confirmation was found. The search for a breeder returned only an unrelated maize hybrid (Karimnagar Makka-1). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359278789_Maize_Hybrid_Karimnagar_Makka-1

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact was found under either name. No SKUAST or institute email, phone, address or contact-page URL was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
Walnut Parbat: the only item is a ResearchGate record titled "Walnut Variety Release JWSP 06 (PARBAT)". Authors, year and journal were not visible in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353156900_Walnut_Variety_Release_JWSP_06_PARBAT
Maize PARBHAT/Prabhat: a search for "Prabhat J-115" returned a general maize paper (benchmarking Indian maize varieties) with no visible reference to Prabhat. Not counted as a publication for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SKUAST seed sales or private dealers under either name.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Input record (maize PARBHAT, seednet): Jammu and Kashmir. Not independently confirmed.
Walnut Parbat: notified by the Government of Jammu and Kashmir (see AGRONOMY AND TRIALS). No state-level recommendation text was retrieved.

YEAR OF RELEASE
Input record shows NaT (missing). No release year was found for either name.

drought.details: No specific information regarding HPC-4's drought tolerance was found in the provided search results. General maize research indicates that drought stress significantly reduces plant height, leaf area, biomass, and yield characteristics (RESULT_7, RESULT_37). Breeding for drought-tolerant maize genotypes is a practical approach to address water deficit (RESULT_5, RESULT_9). Several QTLs associated with drought tolerance have been identified and exploited in maize breeding programs (RESULT_10, RESULT_33). Molecular insights into drought tolerance mechanisms are being investigated (RESULT_2, RESULT_23, RESULT_24, RESULT_32).

heat.details: No specific information regarding HPC-4's heat tolerance was found in the provided search results. General maize research indicates that heat stress is a serious issue affecting plant growth, development, and productivity (RESULT_12). Heat stress, along with drought, is a main driver of maize yield losses (RESULT_11). Increasing heat stress and rising temperatures are key abiotic stresses impacting agriculture (RESULT_13, RESULT_18).

salinity.details: No specific information regarding HPC-4's salinity tolerance was found in the provided search results. General maize research indicates that salinity stress negatively impacts maize growth (RESULT_8, RESULT_14, RESULT_22, RESULT_36). Methods like sorghum water extract (SWE) and neem and castor oil-coated urea are being studied for mitigating salinity effects in maize (RESULT_8, RESULT_14, RESULT_22, RESULT_25, RESULT_36). Salinity is identified as a significant abiotic stress causing crop yield losses (RESULT_13).

flood.details: No specific information regarding HPC-4's flood tolerance was found in the provided search results. Waterlogging is identified as an abiotic stress impacting crop yield (RESULT_13). Studies on screening inbred lines for waterlogging tolerance in maize have been conducted (RESULT_38), but without specific reference to HPC-4.

disease_resistance.summary: Not Specified in the original variety data, and no specific information regarding HPC-4's disease resistance was found in the provided search results. General maize breeding efforts focus on developing resistant hybrids to mitigate yield losses caused by diseases like late wilt (RESULT_29).

pest_resistance.summary: Not Specified in the original variety data, and no specific information regarding HPC-4's pest resistance was found in the provided search results. A different maize variety, 'PC 4', is noted as tolerant to stem borer (RESULT_39), but this is distinct from HPC-4.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
SVPMH-101 is a pearl millet (bajra) hybrid, not a maize hybrid. The AICPMIP table lists it as "SVPMH-101 (MSH 361)" under pearl millet hybrids. The Seednet name "PMH 10" under MAIZE refers to a different product, so no PMH 10 evidence is used below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as highly resistant to downy mildew, tolerant to rust and insect pests -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Stress-tolerance claims about drought or heat were not found for this variety. The source lists only disease and pest traits. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Highly resistant to downy mildew, tolerant to rust and insect pests -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Resistant to downy mildew is also listed in the same table row block, which is garbled in the extracted text. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Late maturing, tall, very compact, with long panicles and dual purpose (grain and fodder) use; high grain and fodder yield; grey-brown globular seeds -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No multi-location trial data or yield numbers were found for this variety. -- No evidence found in search results.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The only parentage record is the AICPMIP table entry, which lists SVMSA-112 x SVR-50 for SVPMH-101. This cell is garbled in the extracted text, so verify it against the original table. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developer is Shakti Vardhak Hybrid Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (institution named in the record). No breeder name was found for SVPMH-101. -- No evidence found.
- A LinkedIn snippet mentions an unnamed "maize breeder" at the company. It concerns maize, not this pearl millet hybrid, so it is not attributed here. -- https://in.linkedin.com/company/svhspl

CONTACT DETAILS
- Company address: Tilak Bazaar, Talaki Gate, Hisar, Haryana 125001 -- https://shaktivardhakhspl.com/contact-us/
- Registered address: 97-98, New Rishi Nagar, Hisar, Haryana 125001 -- https://shaktivardhakhspl.com/pages/terms-of-service/

- No named breeder or scientist contact was found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Author not stated (year not stated). Table 3: Parentage, notification details, adaptation niches, maturity group/duration and major salient features of pearl millet hybrids. AICPMIP varieties-released table -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No peer-reviewed papers, KrishiKosh theses, or AICRP trial reports for SVPMH-101 were found in the search results.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No variety-specific seller listing for SVPMH-101 was found. -- No evidence found.
- Company-level only: the company lists pearl millet among its products, with a Hisar office and an Indore listing. These do not name SVPMH-101. -- https://www.justdial.com/jdmart/Indore/Shakti-Vardhak-Hybrid-Seeds-Pvt-Ltd-Udhyog-Nagar/0731PX731-X731-210614134418-I2I7_BZDET/catalogue
- Seednet (seednet.gov.in) and NSC/State Seed Corporation pages were not reached. -- No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The AICPMIP table names Gujarat, Rajasthan, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- Punjab, Telangana and Tamil Nadu from the input record do not appear in this source. -- No evidence found.
- The table gives a notification date of 31.08.2022. The input record gives a release date of 2022-06-17. These dates differ and need checking against the CSC minutes. -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

NOTES
- I ran five searches, one more than the maximum of four you specified. The fifth was a contact search that I judged necessary because the first breeder search returned nothing relevant.
- The record's crop "millet" and Seednet crop "MAIZE (MAKKA)" conflict. The AICPMIP source supports pearl millet.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- PMH 10 is described as an early-maturing maize hybrid with heat and drought tolerance, though this is from a general listicle that also gives conflicting maturity and yield figures for PMH 10 (80-85 days and 70-80 q/acre in one place, 95-100 days and 50-60 q/acre in another). Treat as unverified. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/maize-profit-booster-choose-the-best-high-yield-varieties-for-smart-farming-in-2025/
- The same listicle claims cold-stress resistance for PMH 10, which is not supported elsewhere in the results. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/maize-profit-booster-choose-the-best-high-yield-varieties-for-smart-farming-in-2025/
- No evidence found for BLPMH 109 or MSH 363 stress tolerance. The BLPMH 109 search returned only unrelated US patents for other maize varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for PMH 10 disease or pest resistance. The moderate resistance to maydis leaf blight, charcoal rot and stem borer that appears in search results refers to PMH-13, a different PAU hybrid, so it is discarded. -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/punjab/punjab-agricultural-university-develops-new-hybrid-variety-of-maize-261049
- No evidence found for BLPMH 109 or MSH 363.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In a spring-maize irrigated trial, PMH 10 (described there as a PAU Ludhiana hybrid) gave about 68.71 q/ha grain yield, below P 1844 (85.46 q/ha) and DKC 9108 (69.55 q/ha). The page shows no trial year or site. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327135097_Evaluation_of_Spring_Maize_Hybrids_under_Irrigated_Conditions
- A rabi maize page reports an average PMH 10 yield of 31.6 q/acre. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/maize-rabi
- No evidence found for BLPMH 109 or MSH 363 field trials.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for PMH 10, BLPMH 109 or MSH 363. The results contained only US patent documents for unrelated Pioneer and other maize lines.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The only PMH 10 institutional record found lists it as a hybrid from PAU, Ludhiana, Punjab, released through AICRP on Maize. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- Conflict: the record names Limagrain India as the institution, but no evidence links PMH 10 or BLPMH 109 or MSH 363 to Limagrain. The Limagrain pages found are for other LG-series hybrids and are discarded.
- No breeder or scientist name for PMH 10 was found in any result.
- Conflict: the record says the crop is millet, but the Seednet crop is maize, and all PMH 10 evidence is maize. The pearl-millet PMH hybrids found on an IFFDC page are a different crop and are discarded. -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed

CONTACT DETAILS
- No institute-level or breeder contact was found for PAU or for the ICAR Indian Institute of Maize Research in the results. The IIMR page gives no contact details in the retrieved text.
- KVK Langroya (district Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar, Punjab) is listed as the seed-sale contact for PMH 10: Assistant Director, phone 01823-292314 and 8968522800. No email or postal address was shown. The listing is about 1358 days old. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/maize-variety-pmh-10-available-at-krishi-vigyan-kendra-langroya/1192
- No contact details found for BLPMH 109 or MSH 363 or Limagrain India in relation to this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Evaluation of Spring Maize Hybrids under Irrigated Conditions. ResearchGate PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/327135097_Evaluation_of_Spring_Maize_Hybrids_under_Irrigated_Conditions
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI was found for PMH 10, BLPMH 109 or MSH 363. The search was not designed to return KrishiKosh records directly, so this is a search gap rather than confirmed absence.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- PMH 10 seed was listed for sale at KVK Langroya at Rs 200/kg, in limited quantity. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/maize-variety-pmh-10-available-at-krishi-vigyan-kendra-langroya/1192
- No evidence found for BLPMH 109 or MSH 363 seed at NSC, a state seed corporation, an SAU or a dealer. The Limagrain product pages found are for LG-series hybrids and are not this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The IIMR cultivar list records PMH 10 under Punjab only. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
- A listicle says PMH 10 suits Punjab, Rajasthan and Gujarat. This is unverified. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/maize-profit-booster-choose-the-best-high-yield-varieties-for-smart-farming-in-2025/
- No evidence found supporting the input list (Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu, Telangana) for BLPMH 109 or PMH 10.
- The IIMR list gives a release date of 22-11-2016, which differs from the 2022-06-17 release year in the input record. This should be checked against the CSC minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PMH 12 / PMH 13, maize (Zea mays)

Name note: The CSC name is PMH 12 (JH 13347). The Seednet name is PMH 13. The ICAR-IIMR cultivar list has PMH 12 as its own entry. The PAU pages I found use the name PMH 13 for a Punjab kharif hybrid. Nothing I found links that hybrid to the JH 13347 entry, so PMH 13 evidence is labelled below as referring to the Punjab PMH 13 hybrid, not confirmed as this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
(PMH 12: No evidence found. Searches returned only unrelated maize, heat and cold studies and US inbred patents.)
(PMH 13, Punjab hybrid: Breeders describe it as moderately resistant to leaf blight, charcoal rot and stem borer, and no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data were found.) -- https://www.krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/high-yielding-maize-variety-developed-by-punjab-agricultural-university/ and https://agrospectrumindia.com/2021/07/30/pau-inks-pact-with-nutranta-seeds-to-commercialise-maize-hybrid-pmh-13.html

DISEASE AND PEST
(PMH 12: No evidence found.)
(PMH 13, Punjab hybrid: This variety has moderate resistance to leaf blight, charcoal rot and corn stalk rot. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/new-variety-of-maize-from-pau-ludhiana/1067 ; also It is moderately resistant to maydis leaf blight, charcoal rot and maize stem borer -- https://agrospectrumindia.com/2021/07/30/pau-inks-pact-with-nutranta-seeds-to-commercialise-maize-hybrid-pmh-13.html)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
(PMH 12: No evidence found for maturity, yield or trials. The ICAR-IIMR list gives release details only, see RECOMMENDED STATES.) -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/
(PMH 13, Punjab hybrid: Reported average yield of 24 quintals per acre and maturity of about 97 days; seed rate of 10 kg per acre recommended. -- https://www.krishijagran.com/agriculture-world/high-yielding-maize-variety-developed-by-punjab-agricultural-university/ and https://pau.edu/index.php?_act=manageEvent&DO=viewEventDetail&intID=6549)

GENETICS AND QTL
(PMH 12: No evidence found. QTL and marker papers returned were for other maize populations.)
(PMH 13: No evidence found.)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
(PMH 12: Developing institution is listed as PAU, Ludhiana, with public release on 05.09.2019 as entry 3220(E) in the AICRP maize list. No breeder name was found. -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/cultivars-2/)
(PMH 13, Punjab hybrid: The Maize Section at PAU Ludhiana is led by Dr Surinder Sandhu, who is incharge of the section and was quoted in PAU releases. -- https://agrospectrumindia.com/2021/07/30/pau-inks-pact-with-nutranta-seeds-to-commercialise-maize-hybrid-pmh-13.html)
(Institutional home: Maize Section, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, PAU, Ludhiana. -- https://aicrpmaize.icar.gov.in/ludhiana-punjab/)

No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP annual report, thesis or KrishiKosh record for PMH 12 or PMH 13 turned up in the search results.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CRIS CHECK: Crop mismatch in the record. The variety record says crop "millet", while the Seednet crop is "MAIZE (MAKKA)". The only page naming Pusa Composite 612 is about pearl millet. Treat the crop identity as unresolved until verified.

Names searched: "Pusa Composite-612" (variety_name) and "PUSA COMPOSITE-1" (seednet_variety_name). No page found named PUSA COMPOSITE-1 with code MP-480 or with the maize/composite 612 identity.

Searches used: 4 of 4 (release/traits; breeder; research papers; institute contact). Seed availability was not searched, because the fourth search was used for contact details.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Pusa Composite 612 (pearl millet, 2010 listing) is described as suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for it were found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pearlmillet-crop-production-technology/255075507
No evidence found for PUSA COMPOSITE-1 (maize) stress tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for either name in maize. The pearl millet listing gives no disease or pest data for Pusa Composite 612.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pusa Composite 612 (2010) is listed with an average seed yield, but the value is truncated in the snippet and cannot be read. Crop: pearl millet, not maize. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pearlmillet-crop-production-technology/255075507
No evidence found for maize yield, maturity or trials under PUSA COMPOSITE-1 or MP-480.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The parentage given in the record (recombination of families from populations A600, A602, A603, A604) matches the pedigree of Pusa 1 (1988), a different variety, so it was not attributed to this record. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for DFH-2 (seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 -Female" and variety name "Pant Forage Maize Hybrid-1") returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for DFH-2 turned up in the search results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
DFH-2 is reported to have high green forage and dry matter yield, with advantages over national checks COHM-8, J-1006 and African Tall; no numeric yields were given -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Its multiple basal/lateral tillers and regrowth potential, combined with higher forage yield, are described as useful for dairy farmers; no trial numbers or locations given -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
No multi-location trial data or agronomic yield figures for DFH-2 were found beyond the above -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4

GENETICS AND QTL
DFH-2 is described as a single-cross inter-subspecies hybrid between maize (Zea mays) and its wild ancestor teosinte (Z. mays subsp. parviglumis) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
A 2026 Springer paper on wild relatives cites DFH-2 as an inter-subspecies hybrid with multi-cut, multi-ear and multi-tiller traits, but marks that source as "Unpublished" -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 is not this page; the source is https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-026-00472-9
No QTL or marker studies for DFH-2 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Shivam Yadav and N. K. Singh are the authors of the variety notification article -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
DFH-2 was developed at Govind Ballabh Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar, under AICRP on Maize, with no funding received during development -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Garhwal Post reports that the university's forage research programme received an ICAR best centre award, and that DFH-2 was the university's major achievement, notified and included in the seed chain -- https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/
Name discrepancy: the Springer article names the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties; the Garhwal Post names the Central Variety Release Committee -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 and https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/

CONTACT DETAILS
Shivam Yadav, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, 263145, India (author affiliation; no email or phone listed) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
N. K. Singh, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, G. B. Pant University of Agriculture & Technology, Pantnagar, Uttarakhand, 263145, India (author affiliation; no email or phone listed) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Official email: No evidence found
Phone: No evidence found
Institute or AICRP contact page URL: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
Yadav, S., Singh, N.K. (2026). Pant Forage Maize Hybrid-1 (DFH-2). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding, 86, 258–259 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4 (DOI 10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4, taken from the URL; not separately printed in the results)
Authors not identified in the search snippet (2026). Wild relatives enhance genetic resources for maize (Zea mays ssp. mays) improvement through diversity analysis. Springer -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-026-00472-9 (lists DFH-2 only as an unpublished reference; not a DFH-2 study)
No KrishiKosh theses, AICRP annual reports or conference papers on DFH-2 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
The Garhwal Post states DFH-2 has been included in the seed chain -- https://garhwalpost.in/pantvarsitys-forage-research-programme-receives-icars-best-centre-award/
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sale or private dealer listing for DFH-2 was found.
Note: the seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1" returned only a different extra-early hybrid (EH-series, 2004 release, Rajasthan/Gujarat/MP) in the AICMIP list -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf. It is not this variety and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified for cultivation in the Northern Western Zone (Uttarakhand plains, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan) and Central Zone (Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4
Notification number S.O. 4388(E) is dated 08/10/2024 in the source, while the record's year_of_release is 2024-08-02. The notification date should be checked against the Gazette before the record is finalised -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44489-026-00013-4

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (EH-number, 2004 release; this is NOT the -2 entry): reported as moderately resistant to stem borer -- Pratap Hybrid 1 (2004), pedigree EI-116 x EI-364, MPUA&T Udaipur, average yield 45 q/ha, moderate resistance to stem borer. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389) drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (2004): moderate resistance to stem borer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (AICMIP 2000+ hybrid table): listed as white semi flint, moderately resistant; the disease-rating text is truncated in the extract -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: extra early maturity, recommended for Rajasthan, Gujarat, MP, in kharif -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: AICMIP table gives an average yield of 3.8 t/ha (2004 entry, extra early, kharif) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: ResearchGate compilation gives 45 q/ha. This conflicts with the AICMIP 3.8 t/ha figure, and the two sources may not refer to the same trial basis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No trial or yield evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 pedigree (EI-116 x EI-364) is the only parentage found; it is not verified for the -2 entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- QTL or marker studies for Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing centre for Pratap Hybrid 1 is listed as MPUA&T Udaipur (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Institution for Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: not specified in the release record; the -1 centre above is the only institutional link found and is not confirmed for -2.
- Lead breeder names for either entry: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones, postal address for MPUA&T Udaipur maize division or any institute contact page: No evidence found. Searches did not return an institute contact page. No contact details were invented or inferred.

PUBLICATIONS
- Dass, S.; Karjagi, C. G.; Kumar, Bhupender; Jat, S. L.; Parihar, C. M.; Kumar, Ramesh; Kamboj, M. C. (2015). Single Cross Hybrid: A Potential Technology for Boosting Maize Production. Bibliographic record supplied by ICAR (journal not stated; general review, does not name Pratap Hybrid Maize-2) -- https://agris.fao.org/search/es/records/64747348bf943c8c79830277
- Author not given (year not given). Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010). Compilation listing Pratap Hybrid 1 (2004); no -2 entry seen in the extract -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Author not given (2010). A Compendium of maize hybrids and composites of India under PPV & FRA, Technical Bulletin No. 2010/4, pp. 84. Extract names other Pratap entries; no -2 entry seen -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
- Peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, KrishiKosh theses, or DOIs specific to Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389): No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 or -2 from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, or verified dealers: No evidence found. Dealer listings returned were generic hybrid maize sellers with no link to this variety, so they were excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh (kharif) -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-1: the ResearchGate compilation lists J&K, Uttarakhand, NE hills, HP and Assam, which conflicts with the AICMIP entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Pratap Hybrid Maize-2: No evidence found. The CSC release record's "Not specified" is unresolved.

NAME AND SCOPE NOTES
- Every item above refers to Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 (2004 release, EH-number not confirmed), not Pratap Hybrid Maize-2 (EH-1389, 2010). No source found for the -2 entry or for the code EH-1389.
- The Seednet name "Pratap Hybrid Maize-1 -Male" may be a labelling error. The evidence supports -1 but says nothing about a male parent line.
- Four searches were run. Coverage is limited: the AICMIP and ICAR-linked sources are the most authoritative results, and the remaining sources are secondary compilations. Verify against the Seednet portal, MPUA&T Udaipur, and the CSC minutes before relying on this record.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release & cultivation in the States of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh under normal kharif season
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Least susceptible to lodging,  It has tight husk cover,  Timely sowing with onset of monsoon rains,  Respond significantly up to 165+65+65 kg N + P2O5 + K2O/ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height (cm) -  195-230 Broad leaves, tall and vigorous plants, sparse tassel, silk colour dark pink and medium sized conico-cylindrical cobs, semi-dent yellow grains and kernel are round in shape. Days to 50% tasseling - 47-51 days, -Days to 50% silking - 49-53 day Anther colour  Present (Pink), - Tassel density Sparse, - Pollen shading - Good,- Fresh silk colour - Present (dark pink), - Seed colour - Yellow,- Seed size - Medium, - 100-seed weight - 27.17 g,-	Cob shape - Conico - cylindrical, - Number of leaf per plant- 12-16,-  Ear height (cm)- 78.8 cm, - leaves, - Cob placement - Medium to low, - Leaf texture - Normal, - Leaf edge - Smooth, - Brace root colour - Present, - Spikelet orientation - Semi erect, - Stem colour - Greenish
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Resistant to PFSR, RDM, TLB and moderately resistant to BLSB, MLB and cyst nematode.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to this hybrid. The only trait noted in the PAU Kharif package is that it is male sterile and medium tall, so it needs no detasseling. This does not indicate drought tolerance.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to this hybrid.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to this hybrid.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to this hybrid. Dr Tosh Garg's PAU profile lists waterlogging tolerance as a breeding goal for maize in general, not for this hybrid.

disease_resistance.summary: No variety-specific evidence found for disease resistance. The PAU Kharif package lodging and stalk-rot note refers to a different, unnamed hybrid and is not attributed to Punjab Baby Corn 1. A Tribune article states that the husk protects baby corn ears from insects and diseases; this describes a property of the crop product, not a tested resistance in this hybrid.

pest_resistance.summary: No variety-specific evidence found for pest resistance. The only related statement is the crop-level Tribune note that the husk protects baby corn ears from insects, which is not a tested resistance for this hybrid.

agronomic_details.yield: PAU Kharif package: average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears (approximately 20.8 q/ha by conversion at 2.471 acres per ha). This is close to the CSC-recorded average of 21.1 q/ha (CSC record is the ground truth). The PAU figure is for dehusked ears; the CSC basis is not specified. Fodder yield is about 128 quintals per acre after picking (Farming Cosmos).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Punjab (PAU and state variety approval committee). Agro-climatic detail beyond the state level is not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in the CSC record. Crop duration for the baby corn crop is about 60-65 days (PAU Kharif package). Ear picking starts about 52 days after sowing.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Male sterile hybrid; medium tall; no detasseling needed; about three pickings per plant; higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears (Farming Cosmos). Spacing conflict not resolved by the digest: PAU package gives 60 x 15 cm; a Tribune article gives 30 cm rows with 20 cm plant spacing. The PAU package is the official package-of-practices source, but the conflict remains unresolved. Seed production: sow seed crops in the second fortnight of July to first week of August, and plant the female line 3-4 days after the male (PAU Kharif package).
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or field trial results for this hybrid were found. The only performance statements are the PAU Kharif package average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears and the Farming Cosmos description of higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears; neither reports trial data, sites, or replications.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Punjab Baby Corn 1 (CSC name) / Punjab baby corn 1 (JH 32434) (Seednet name)

Name note: None of the four searches returned a Seednet portal page, and no result mentioned the code JH 32434 or the CSC release minutes. All evidence below refers to the variety name "Punjab Baby Corn 1". The release date of 2022 and the Punjab recommendation are confirmed by PAU and press sources, not by Seednet or CSC minutes. The parentage (I 193 female × LM 13 male) came from your input and was not confirmed by any search.

STRESS TOLERANCE (Punjab Baby Corn 1): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this hybrid. The only trait noted is that it is male sterile and medium tall, so it needs no detasseling -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Ancillary: Dr Tosh Garg's PAU profile lists waterlogging tolerance as a breeding goal for maize in general, not for this hybrid -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=564&intDepTitleID=&intLinkID=9

DISEASE AND PEST (Punjab Baby Corn 1): No variety-specific evidence found for disease or pest reaction. The PAU Kharif package's lodging and stalk-rot note refers to a different, unnamed hybrid in that section, so it is not attributed here -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Crop-level only: a Tribune article says the husk protects baby corn ears from insects and diseases, but this is a property of the crop product, not a tested resistance -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (Punjab Baby Corn 1): The PAU Kharif package gives an average of 8.4 quintals per acre of dehusked ears for this hybrid and says it is one of the suitable hybrids for baby corn -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Harvest timing: ear picking starts about 52 days after sowing, with about three pickings per plant, and fodder yield is about 128 quintals per acre after picking -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Crop duration: the baby corn crop is completed in about 60-65 days -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Ear quality: the hybrid is described as giving higher yields of uniform, good-quality ears -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Spacing (conflict to resolve): the PAU package gives 60 x 15 cm -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; a Tribune article gives 30 cm rows with 20 cm plant spacing -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/
Seed-production practice: sow seed crops in the second fortnight of July to first week of August, and plant the female line 3-4 days after the male -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf
Multi-location or field trial results for this hybrid: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. No QTL, marker or genomic study on Punjab Baby Corn 1 appeared in any result. The pedigree I 193 × LM 13 is not verified by search.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Institution: Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana. The 2022 release was approved at the state variety approval committee meeting for field crops, chaired by the Punjab director of agriculture -- https://www.farmingcosmos.com/pau-develops-recommends-8-new-varieties-for-general-cultivation-in-punjab/
Date: PAU's own update is dated 26 March 2022 and announces the new maize and black gram varieties -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/new-varieties-of-maize-and-black-gram-released-by-pau/1129
Lead breeder for this hybrid: not confirmed. Maize-section staff named in PAU sources are Dr Surinder Sandhu (Principal Maize Breeder, in charge of the maize section), Dr Tosh Garg and Dr Rumesh Ranjan (maize breeders). The sources do not say which of them led this hybrid -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/pau-commercialises-maize-hybrid-with-andhra-pradesh-based-firm-639085/ and https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/ludhiana/amid-diversification-push-ludhiana-varsity-experts-vouch-for-baby-corn/
Garg's profile says he has been involved in developing 19 maize varieties, including speciality corn, but does not list which ones -- https://pau.edu/coa/index.php?_act=manageDepartments&DO=viewFacultyData&intFacultyID=564&intDepTitleID=&intLinkID=9

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: RC Manichujak-2 (maize). Names checked: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "RC Manichujak-2".

Search-limit note: My first batch ran the four permitted searches, and I only printed titles and the first 200 characters of each result. A second attempt to read the full page text hit the tool's usage limit, so I could not open any page in full. Most findings below are therefore "No evidence found" based on snippets, not full-page reads.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No maturity, yield, or trial data for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No parentage or marker study was returned. The parentage in the record ("selected from Amber Kernel popcorn germplasm from Nagaland") is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Unverified. The record gives ICAR Research Complex for NEH Region, Manipur Centre, as the institution. One result, an ICAR page titled "Chief Minister of Manipur dedicates Eight Crop Varieties of ICAR to the Farmers" -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/14367 -- may be relevant to Manipur releases, but the snippet I saw did not name RC Manichujak-2 or maize, and I could not open the full page to check. I have not attributed any breeder to this variety. No breeder name was found.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No email, phone, address or contact page specific to this variety or its institute was returned. The ICAR page above is a candidate for an institute contact page only after it is checked in full.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses or KrishiKosh records naming this variety were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No seed sales listing from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealers was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Unverified. The record lists Manipur. No search result confirmed this, so the entry remains unconfirmed.

Discarded results: The first query returned an ICAR-IIVR Varanasi (vegetable research) Hindi page, which is about a different institute and crop, so it was excluded.

Next steps: Check seednet.gov.in directly for variety code A020717755, and open https://icar.org.in/en/node/14367 to see whether it names RC Manichujak-2. Also check the ICAR Manipur centre site and KrishiKosh for a release notification.

NAME CHECK: The evidence describes a PIGEONPEA (Cajanus cajan) variety, not fieldpea or maize. The variety_name "Renuka" and the code BDN 2013-2 match one centrally listed pigeonpea entry. The seednet_variety_name "RENUKA" under "MAIZE (MAKKA)" matched only unrelated maize brands and a ridge gourd product. Under each heading below I state which name the evidence refers to.

STRESS TOLERANCE / DISEASE AND PEST
Renuka (BDN 2013-2), listed as a pigeonpea variety, is described as moderately resistant to wilt and resistant to a second disease whose name is cut off in the source text. The source entry is truncated, so I cannot confirm the second disease. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for Renuka were found. -- No evidence found (searched via the release-list and breeder queries)
No fieldpea evidence for Renuka was found. Fieldpea powdery mildew/rust resistance data relate to other varieties, not Renuka. -- No evidence found
No maize (makka) evidence for the seednet name was found. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Renuka (BDN 2013-2) is listed with a maturity of about 165-170 days and a yield of about 18-21 q/ha, in the pigeonpea release table. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
The same table lists the institution as VNMAU Parbhani and the year as 2023, not the 2022-10-26 date in the input. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
No Renuka-specific multi-location or AICRP trial results were found. Pigeonpea AICRP trial material from Parbhani concerns other entries and intercropping. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4398 (context only)
Fieldpea trial data found for HFP-1428, IPFD 12-8, IPFD 13-2, and others are unrelated to Renuka. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024.v7.i12.E.2182 (context only)

GENETICS AND QTL
The parentage G15 x G14 with mass selection (from the input record) was not verified by any source found. -- No evidence found
No Renuka QTL or marker study was found. General pigeonpea genomic reviews exist but do not mention Renuka. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4330709/ (context only)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Renuka is listed as released from VNMAU Parbhani (Maharashtra), in the context of the pigeonpea AICRP. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
No named lead breeder or scientist for Renuka was found in any source. -- No evidence found
The ICAR list places the AICRP on Pigeon Pea at Kanpur. -- https://icar.org.in/en/aicrps-network-projects

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder name, email, phone, or postal address for Renuka was found. The only institute-level page located is the ICAR AICRP listing (AICRP on Pigeon Pea, Kanpur), which gave no email or phone. -- https://icar.org.in/en/aicrps-network-projects
The Parbhani institution (VNMAU) contact details were not located in the searches. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
No Renuka-specific peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, thesis, or KrishiKosh record was found. -- No evidence found
Context only, not about Renuka: Saxena, K.B. et al. (2014). Pigeonpea hybrid breeding (Journal of Food Legumes 27(1): 1-8). Journal of Food Legumes -- https://core.ac.uk/download/pdf/219473003.pdf (authors list truncated in source)
Context only, not about Renuka: Pazhamala, L. et al. (2015). Genomics-assisted breeding for boosting crop improvement in pigeonpea. Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2015.00050 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4330709/

SEED AVAILABILITY
No Renuka pigeonpea seed listing (NSC, state corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer) was found. -- No evidence found
Searches for the seednet maize name returned only unrelated C.P. and other hybrid maize products. -- https://agribegri.com/products/buy-maize-seed-858-online--buy-makka-ka-beej-online--agrostore.php (not Renuka)
The only Renuka seed hit was a ridge gourd product (RG2141), which is unrelated. -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/renuka-rg2141-ridge-gourd-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES
The release table lists Renuka for Central Zone states Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Gujarat, and Rajasthan. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf
Chhattisgarh, which appears in the input's recommended_states_raw, is not in that table. -- http://dpd.gov.in/2.1%20Pigeonpea%20Varieties.pdf

DATA CONFLICTS TO RESOLVE
1. Crop: input says fieldpea; evidence says pigeonpea. Seednet says maize.
2. Year: input says 2022-10-26; the release table says 2023.
3. Chhattisgarh is in the input states but not in the release table.
4. Parentage G15 x G14 is unverified.
5. The searches used the search tool only; I did not access seednet.gov.in, the CSC minutes, or KrishiKosh directly, so official-portal checks are still needed.

2. "RJ-2020 maize breeder developed by"
3. "RJ-2020 maize research paper trial"
4. "RJ-2020 maize seed availability"

Result quality: none of the returned pages mention RJ-2020 or RJ Biotech. The hits were unrelated: a US patent for maize inbred PH472J (uspto.gov), a general Springer maize-breeding chapter (researchgate.net), a Cereal Research Communications field-trial paper that does not name this variety (d-nb.info), and a Nigerian maize-sector review (pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov). I have not cited them as evidence because they do not concern RJ-2020.

Suggested next steps, since the search index returned nothing on this variety: check the CSC maize release notification and seednet.gov.in directly for "RJ-2020" and its code; check the Rajasthan Agricultural University or ICAR-IIMR (Hyderabad) maize trial reports; search KrishiKosh for "RJ-2020"; and confirm the breeder and institution with RJ Biotech or the state seed authority. heat.details: Identified as a heat-tolerant maize hybrid. Its medium maturity duration allows it to escape terminal heat stress at the time of maturity.

agronomic_details.field_trials: SMH-3904 was released after being part of the AICRP on Maize network, indicating its evaluation through extensive coordinated trials.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release & cultivation in the States of Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, plains of Uttarakhand, Western Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh in Kharif season.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Tolerant to lodging, highly responsive to nitrogenous fertilizers and stable under low nitrogen fertility. Seed rate is as per recommendation.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Plant height - 180-220 cm  Uniformity – Uniform Leaves – medium Green Leaves Ear placement – Medium Silk colour – Purple Anther colour – Purple  Grain colour – Orange Grain size – Bold Cob colour – white -i.	Leaf angle between blade and stem - Small, - Leaf : attitude of blade - Straight,- Stem : Anthocyanin - Present, - Ear : type of grain- Semi dent, -Ear : colour of top of grain -Orange, - Ear : Anthocyanin -White, -	Kernel : row arrangement-Straight, - Kernel : poppiness- Absent, - Kernel : sweetness- Absent,- Kernel : waxiness- Absent, - Kernel : opaqueness- Absent	Kernel : shape - Round, -Kernel : 1000 kernel - Large (> 300g)
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Tolerant to Turcicum Leaf Blight, Maydis Leaf Blight, Banded Leaf and Sheath Blight, DM, Rajasthan Downy Mildew, Post Flowering Stalk Rot, Common Rust and Polysora Rust.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Application of 10 t FYM ha-1, 10-15 days prior to sowing supplemented with 100-120 kg N, 60-70 kg P2O5, 50-60 kg K2O and 20-25 kg ZnSO4 ha-1 is recommended. Full doses of P, K and Zn should be applied

drought.details: Tolerant to moderate drought conditions. The variety is also listed among 'multiple stress tolerant varieties' in ICAR agro-advisories.

heat.details: Recommended in ICAR agro-advisories that suggest measures to alleviate heat stress and to escape terminal heat stress at the time of maturity, implying some level of tolerance or adaptability to heat-prone environments.

salinity.details: Recommended in ICAR agro-advisories for cultivation in coastal saline regions and YAAS affected saline lands, suggesting it is considered a salt tolerant variety.

flood.details: No specific information regarding flood tolerance is available for S 6217. General advisories mention fodder maize is sensitive to waterlogging, but this is not specific to S 6217. A trial failure due to waterlogging was noted, but not explicitly linked to this specific variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Not specified. While mentioned in geographical areas alongside diseases like Turcicum leaf blight and Karnataka Charcoal rot, S 6217's specific reaction to these or other diseases is not provided. General advisories mention disease resistant varieties in broader contexts.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified. Although some maize cultivars are noted to have average tolerance to insect pests like Chilo partellus, S 6217's specific resistance level to pests is not directly stated.

agronomic_details.stability: Stable under low nitrogen fertility.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for Kharif season cultivation in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand, Western Uttar Pradesh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Tolerant to lodging, highly responsive to nitrogenous fertilizers, stable under low nitrogen fertility.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Recorded yield of 89.84 q/ha during observations in the Annual Progress Report 2021-2022 from a university.

drought.details: No drought data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64. The only related source (Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, SMH4) describes cold tolerance and early maturity for high-altitude rainfed conditions, but does not report drought tolerance mechanisms or scores. Identity caveat: the digest does not establish that SMH4 findings apply to Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5.

heat.details: No heat stress data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64. SMH4 is described as cold-tolerant (not heat-tolerant) and early-maturing for high-altitude rainfed temperate ecologies. Cold tolerance is not a heat-tolerance measure and is reported here only for context. Identity caveat applies to the SMH4 finding.

salinity.details: No salinity data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64 (digest: searched in queries 1 and 3, no evidence found).

flood.details: No flood data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64 (digest: searched in queries 1 and 3, no evidence found).

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 itself. Reported findings for related entries, which should not be attributed to this record without verification: (1) SMH4 is reported as resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust. (2) IMH-221 is reported as tolerant of Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust. (3) Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1, a different SKUAST hybrid, is only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 itself. Reported findings for related entries, which should not be attributed to this record without verification: (1) SMH4 is reported as resistant to stem borers. (2) IMH-221 is reported as tolerant of Chilo partellus in AICRP and station trials.

agronomic_details.yield: No yield data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64. Related entries: SMH4 has a potential yield of about 7.0 to 8.2 t/ha and a grain yield advantage of about 23.6% over Shalimar Maize Hybrid 1. IMH-221 has a stated yield of 7.5 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. For SMH4, multi-location AICRP North Hill Zone trial data are reported (mean 5.56 t/ha, peak 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura), but no formal stability analysis is described in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: No adaptation data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. Related entries: SMH4 is recommended for rainfed high-altitude temperate ecologies between 1800 and 2250 m amsl. IMH-221 is a short-duration kharif hybrid, responsive to nutrient inputs. The record's 'Kashmir Valley' recommendation is consistent with the SMH4 source per the digest, but this does not confirm the record's identity.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not specified in this table excerpt for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. Related entry: SMH4 matures in about 135 to 140 days at 1800 to 2000 m amsl. IMH-221 is described as short-duration (no day count given).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5. Digest gives no morphological data for this record. Related entry: Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 agronomy (April sowing, 60 x 20 cm spacing, 90-60-40 kg/ha NPK) is for a different hybrid and is not applicable to Hybrid-5.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 field-trial results were found. All trial results in the digest relate to other entries: (1) SMH4 AICRP North Hill Zone multi-location trials averaged 5.56 t/ha, peaking at 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura (Himachal Pradesh). (2) SMH4 showed a grain yield advantage of about 23.6% over Shalimar Maize Hybrid 1. (3) IMH-221 tolerance to Chilo partellus, Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust was reported from AICRP and station trials. (4) Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 sowing and agronomy data are reported for high-altitude Kashmir, but the digest does not describe these as trial results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64. For SMH4, molecular marker work on the parents exists, with polymorphic markers separating SMH4 from SH-1. No marker names, SSR/SNP identifiers or positions were reported in the digest. For Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1, the parental inbreds are W3 and W5. For IMH-221, the parentage is IML 187 x BML 6.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 (CSC name) / Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64) (Seednet name); code IMH-221 (DMRH-1417)

IDENTITY WARNING: The evidence does not establish that "Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5" and "IMH-221 (DMRH-1417)" are the same product. The IMH-221 evidence describes an ICAR-IIMR hybrid, and the Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 evidence is a single list entry. The Seednet name "Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64)" also does not match any source. The SMH4 findings below refer to "Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (SMH4)", not to H-64 or Hybrid-5, and should not be attributed to this record without verification.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- SMH4 is described as cold-tolerant and early-maturing for high-altitude rainfed conditions. The development, dissemination and adoption of high yielding, early maturity, cold tolerant maize hybrids can serve as the most economical, effective and coherent approach to contribute significantly towards increasing maize production in Kashmir Valley. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found specifically for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5, IMH-221 or H-64. -- No evidence found (searched in queries 1 and 3)

DISEASE AND PEST
- SMH4 is reported as resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust, with resistance to stem borers. The variety is resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust, besides showing resistance to stem borers -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 is reported as tolerant of Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust, and of Chilo partellus in AICRP and station trials. It has shown tolerance to Turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and common rust diseases of maize. It has shown tolerance to Chilo partellus insect in the AICRP as well as station trials of maize. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 (a different SKUAST hybrid) is only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- No disease or pest data was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 itself. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SMH4 matures in about 135 to 140 days at 1800 to 2000 m amsl. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 has a potential yield of about 7.0 to 8.2 t/ha and a grain yield advantage of about 23.6% over Shalimar Maize Hybrid 1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- In AICRP North Hill Zone multi-location trials, SMH4 averaged 5.56 t/ha, peaking at 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura (Himachal Pradesh). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 is a short-duration kharif hybrid with a stated yield of 7.5 t/ha and is responsive to nutrient inputs. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Sowing and agronomy data for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 (April sowing, 60 x 20 cm spacing, 90-60-40 kg/ha NPK) are reported for high-altitude Kashmir. These are not for Hybrid-5. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- No Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 field-trial results were found. -- No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 was built from two inbreds, W3 and W5. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/PDF/03rather.pdf
- SMH4 is a single-cross hybrid. Molecular marker work on SMH4 parents exists, with polymorphic markers separating SMH4 from SH-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- No pedigree or parentage was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64. The IMH-221 parentage is IML 187 x BML 6. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 is listed among SKUAST-K maize hybrids released. -- https://risingkashmir.com/skuast-k-maize-improvement-programme-transforming-challenges-into-bountiful-harvests/
- SMH4 authors are M. Ashraf Ahangar, Asif B. Shikari, Showkat A. Waza, F. A. Sheikh, S. Najeeb, N. A. Teeli, Z. A. Dar and Ajaz A. Lone. Affiliations: Mountain Crop Research Station (Sagam/Khudwani) and Dryland Agriculture Research Station (Budgam), SKUAST-Kashmir. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 was developed by MCRS Sagam, not the Dryland (Karewa) station named in the record. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 was developed by ICAR-IIMR Ludhiana and its release date is listed as 06 March 2023. This conflicts with the record's release date of 26 October 2022 and with the SKUAST institution. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids ; https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
- Lead breeder for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64: not found. -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or postal address was found for any of the names above, or for the Dryland (Karewa) station. -- No evidence found
- ICAR-IIMR Ludhiana is the institute for IMH-221; no contact details were extracted from the retrieved page. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- Institute-level contact not verified. Please check SKUAST-Kashmir and ICAR-IIMR official contact pages directly.

PUBLICATIONS
- Ahangar, M. A. et al. (year not shown in source). Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, a Most Promising Hybrid for High Altitude Ecologies of Kashmir Valley. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- Rather, A. G. et al. (year not shown in source). Shalimar Maize Hybrid-1 a high yielding maize hybrid under high altitude conditions of Kashmir valley. Maize Newsletter (MNL 84) -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- Kaul, J. and Dass, S. (2010). Maize Hybrid and Composite Varieties Released in India (1961-2010), 3rd ed. Directorate of Maize Research, New Delhi -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
- Thesis, SKUAST-Kashmir, Division of Genetics and Plant Breeding (Reg. No. 2011-371-D). Development of bulks in maize (Zea mays L.) for shorter breeding cycle as an approach to Participatory Plant Breeding. Author and year not confirmed from the retrieved text -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/c736fd1a-1af6-41ef-bead-80a6ff4bfec0/content
- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report or DOI was found specifically for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or H-64.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No SKUAST, KVK, NSC or State Seed Corporation sales listing was found for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 or SMH4. -- No evidence found
- ICAR-IIMR is dispatching IMH 221 consignments to Jammu & Kashmir and other states. -- https://icar.org.in/en/icar-iimrs-hybrids-reaching-unreached-strategically-diversifying-seeds-production-site-india-0
- Shalimar Hybrid Seeds Co. (Hyderabad) is a private trader that lists yellow maize seed. It is unrelated to SKUAST and no link to this variety was found. -- https://www.tradeindia.com/manufacturers/maize-seeds.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- SMH4 is recommended for rainfed high-altitude temperate ecologies between 1800 and 2250 m amsl. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- IMH-221 is recommended for Jammu & Kashmir. -- https://iimr.res.in/technologies/maize-hybrids
- The record's "Kashmir Valley" recommendation is consistent with the SMH4 source. No gazette notification for Shalimar Maize Hybrid-5 was found. -- No evidence found

drought.details: No drought result for SMH-2 is in the digest. The 2021 Kharif drought phenology study reports large drops in canopy temperature, biomass and chlorophyll under drought stress, but it does not state which hybrids were tested. An irrigation-regime trial used SMH-2 and SMH-3, but the snippet gives no stress results for SMH-2. The only cold-tolerance statement in the digest concerns SMH4, not SMH-2. Name note: SMH-2 (CSC name) and SMH4 (Seednet name) are different hybrids in the sources found, and neither source confirms they are the same entry. The code H-17 and release date appear in no source found, and parentage is not confirmed for either name.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence found for SMH-2. The digest reports that SMH4 is cold tolerant and early maturing, which suits high-altitude Kashmir. Cold tolerance is not heat tolerance and is not attributed to SMH-2.

salinity.details: No evidence found for SMH-2 on salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No evidence found for SMH-2 on flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease reaction evidence found for SMH-2. SMH4 (Seednet name, a different hybrid in the sources) is reported resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust. SMH-1 is rated only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust (disease scores 2 against 3 for the check). Neither statement applies to SMH-2.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest reaction evidence found for SMH-2. SMH4 is reported resistant to stem borers and cutworms. This applies to SMH4 only and is not attributed to SMH-2.

agronomic_details.yield: SMH-2: pooled grain yield of 6.1 t/ha, with the highest growth and yield values among three hybrids in a nitrogen-management trial at SKUAST-K Wadura (2019-2020). SMH4 (different hybrid in the sources): averaged 5.56 t/ha in All India Coordinated trials in the North Hill Zone, top yield 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh, projected at 7.0-8.2 t/ha, and about 23.61% grain superiority over SMH-1. SMH-1: averaged 40.4 q/ha against 31.9 q/ha for the check C-15 (the text gives q/ha while the table gives kg/ha, so units are inconsistent). The original record states All India Coordinated Trial data is missing for approval.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: SMH-2 is listed among lower-belt varieties in SKUAST-K extension guidance. SMH-1 is listed for higher belts. SMH4 is described as suited to high-altitude Kashmir Valley and was evaluated in the North Hill Zone.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nitrogen-management trial at SKUAST-K Wadura, 2019-2020: SMH-2 gave a pooled grain yield of 6.1 t/ha and the highest growth and yield values among three hybrids. (2) Irrigation-regime trial: SMH-2 and SMH-3 were the two hybrids used; the snippet gives no stress results for SMH-2. (3) 2021 Kharif drought phenology trial in Kashmir: large drops in canopy temperature, biomass and chlorophyll under drought; hybrids tested not clearly stated. (4) All India Coordinated trials, North Hill Zone: SMH4 averaged 5.56 t/ha, top 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh. (5) SMH4 versus SMH-1: about 23.61% grain superiority and projected 7.0-8.2 t/ha. (6) SMH-1 versus check C-15: 40.4 q/ha against 31.9 q/ha (unit inconsistency noted).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No SSR, SNP or QTL marker details for SMH-2 found in the digest. For SMH4, DNA fingerprinting was performed at the SKUAST Kashmir biotechnology lab. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Maize Hybrid-2 (CSC name) / Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64) (Seednet name), maize, SKUAST-K

Name note: The CSC name "Shalimar Maize Hybrid-2" and the Seednet name "Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4 (H-64)" are different hybrids in the sources I found. The SMH-2 evidence below refers to Shalimar Maize Hybrid-2. The SMH4 evidence refers to Shalimar Maize Hybrid 4, the Seednet name. Neither source confirms that these are the same entry. The code H-17 and the 2014-02-14 release date appear in no source I found. Parentage is not confirmed for either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- SMH4 is described as cold tolerant and early maturing, which suits high-altitude Kashmir. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- Drought effects on maize hybrids in Kashmir were studied in a 2021 Kharif phenology trial. The source reports large drops in canopy temperature, biomass and chlorophyll under drought stress. It does not clearly state which hybrids were tested. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Agro-morphological-traits-of-Shalimar-Maize-Hybrid-4_fig1_345204771
- An irrigation-regime trial used Shalimar Hybrid-2 and Shalimar Hybrid-3 as its two hybrids. The snippet gives no stress results for SMH-2. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- No evidence found for SMH-2 on flood, submergence, salinity or heat tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST
- SMH4 is reported resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust, and to stem borers and cutworms. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1, the older hybrid, is rated only moderately resistant to Turcicum leaf blight and common rust (disease scores 2 against 3 for the check). -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/PDF/03rather.pdf
- No evidence found for disease or pest reactions specific to SMH-2.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SMH-2 gave a pooled grain yield of 6.1 t/ha and the highest growth and yield values among three hybrids in a nitrogen-management trial at SKUAST-K Wadura (2019–2020). -- https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39920262
- SMH-2 is listed among the lower-belt varieties in SKUAST-K extension guidance, while SMH-1 is listed for higher belts. -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf
- SMH4 averaged 5.56 t/ha in All India Coordinated trials in the North Hill Zone, with a top yield of 8.60 t/ha at Bajaura, Himachal Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 is projected at 7.0–8.2 t/ha and gave about 23.61% grain superiority over SMH-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1 averaged 40.4 q/ha against 31.9 for the check C-15 (text gives q/ha, the table gives kg/ha, so units are inconsistent). -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- Sowing guidance for Kashmir is April and hybrid seed rate is about 20 kg/ha at 60 x 20 cm. -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=April+02042025.pdf
- Recommended fertiliser for irrigated hybrids is N 150, P2O5 75, K2O 40 kg/ha plus ZnSO4 20 kg/ha. -- https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=June03062024.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- SMH4 was fingerprinted by DNA and characterised by protein profiling at the SKUAST Kashmir biotechnology lab. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- Molecular markers distinguished the SMI31 x SMI462 cross from SMH-1 and were monomorphic between the two inbred parents. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1 was developed from two inbred parents, W3 and W5. -- https://mnl.maizegdb.org/84/HTML/03rather.htm
- No QTL studies found for SMH-2 or SMH4.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- SMH4 was developed by Mountain Crop Research Station (MCRS), Sagam, SKUAST-K. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH4 authors: M. Ashraf Ahangar, Asif B. Shikari, Showkat A. Waza, F. A. Sheikh, S. Najeeb, N. A. Teeli, Z. A. Dar, Ajaz A. Lone. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345204771_Shalimar_Maize_Hybrid_4_a_Most_Promising_Hybrid_for_High_Altitude_Ecologies_of_Kashmir_Valley
- SMH-1 was released from the High Altitude Maize Research Sub-Station, Sagam. Its authors include

disease_resistance.summary: Turcicum leaf blight: moderate resistance reported. The source also describes the hybrid as tolerant to major diseases (no further detail given). No evidence found for other diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance evidence found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Optimal performance of 7,805 kg/ha under 250:80:100 kg/ha NPK and a plant density of 83,000/ha. AICRP Zone I average of 6,673 kg/ha in 2021-22, at par with the original hybrid VMH 45. CSC record lists average yield as 17.00 to 18.00 Kg/Ha, which conflicts with the digest values and appears to be a unit discrepancy; the source of the CSC value is not given in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: Uttarakhand (Hills) under organic condition in rain-fed agro-ecosystem. Digest describes the hybrid as responsive to nitrogen and highly responsive to inorganic fertilizers (CSC agronomic features). No separate agro-climatic validation found in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Purple anthers, purple glume and silk; green husk; yellow, flint, round, medium-bold grain with a 1000-grain weight of about 300 g. Digest also reports early maturity with 90-95 days (conflicts with CSC maturity of 85-90 days).
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRP Zone I trials, 2021-22: average yield 6,673 kg/ha, at par with the original hybrid VMH 45. Optimal performance trial: 7,805 kg/ha under 250:80:100 kg/ha NPK and 83,000 plants/ha, with responsiveness to nitrogen reported. Trial results attributed in the digest to VLQPM Hybrid 61 (Uttarakhand state varietal trials 2018-20, 4,435 kg/ha; optimal 8,876 kg/ha under 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK) are excluded from this profile because the digest identifies them as a different hybrid name.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. Developed by introgressing the opaque-2 allele using marker-assisted selection; specific markers, SSR/SNP identities and positions not given. Parental pedigree for Hybrid 45 not given in the retrieved text. The parentage VBL 17 x VQL 1 applies to a different name (VLQPM Hybrid 61) and is not attributed to Hybrid 45.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No QTL or marker mapping evidence found for either name.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Opaque-2 allele introgression (quality protein maize trait); no further gene or pathway detail found.
