search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VLQPM Hybrid 45 / VLQPM Hybrid 61 (maize, FQH165), evidence digest

Name note: the CSC name "VLQPM Hybrid 45" and the Seednet name "VLQPM Hybrid 61" are two different hybrids in the retrieved sources. Each finding below states which name it refers to. The parentage VBL 17 x VQL 1 appears in the source only for VLQPM Hybrid 61, not for Hybrid 45. Searches 1 to 4 were run; no separate seed-availability search was run within the query budget.

STRESS TOLERANCE

VLQPM Hybrid 45: Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight was observed, and the source describes the hybrid as tolerant to major diseases. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61: It also exhibited moderate resistance to turcicum and maydis leaf blight. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found for either name in the retrieved text.

DISEASE AND PEST

VLQPM Hybrid 45: Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight (see Stress Tolerance above). No pest resistance evidence found. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61: Moderate resistance to turcicum and maydis leaf blight (see Stress Tolerance above). No pest resistance evidence found. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

VLQPM Hybrid 45 (maturity): Early maturing, with 90-95 days reported. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (yield): Optimal performance of 7,805 kg/ha under 250:80:100 kg/ha NPK and a plant density of 83,000/ha, and the hybrid is described as responsive to nitrogen. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (AICRP Zone I): Average yield of 6,673 kg/ha in AICRP trials during 2021-22, at par with the original hybrid VMH 45. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (grain): Purple anthers, purple glume and silk; green husk; yellow, flint, round, medium-bold grain with a 1000-grain weight of about 300 g. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (maturity): Described as early maturing (85-90 days in mid-hills) and also as 95-100 days to maturity. The source is internally inconsistent; both values are reported. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (yield): Average of 4,435 kg/ha in state varietal trials in Uttarakhand hills during 2018-20, with 10.9% superiority over the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions. Optimal performance of 8,876 kg/ha under 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (quality): 0.76% tryptophan, 3.30% lysine and 9.16% protein. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (grain and plant): Yellow, semi-flint, flat, medium-bold grain (1000-grain weight about 260 g); plant height 200-210 cm. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

GENETICS AND QTL

VLQPM Hybrid 61 (parentage): Developed by crossing QPM lines VBL 17 (female) and VQL 1 (male). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (line origin): VBL 17 and VQL 1 were developed by introgressing the opaque-2 allele using marker-assisted selection. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
VLQPM Hybrid 45 (genetics): Developed by introgressing the opaque-2 allele using marker-assisted selection; the parental pedigree is not given in the retrieved text. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
QTL or marker mapping studies for either name: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

Developing institution (both names): ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora, Uttarakhand. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Named corresponding author (VLQPM Hybrid 45 and 61 variety bulletin): Rajesh Khulbe, ICAR-VPKAS, Almora. Full author list is not visible in the retrieved text. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Almora AICRP maize directory: Dr. R.K. Khulbe is listed as Senior Scientist & I/C, Plant Breeding. Other breeders are also listed at the centre, but none is confirmed as a developer of this hybrid. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Directory/Directory_2025.pdf
Institute profile: VPKAS is recognised as a pioneer maize breeding centre, and the centre reports 32 released varieties (9 composites and 23 hybrids). -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/hindi/almora-uttarakhand/

CONTACT DETAILS

Corresponding author: Rajesh.Khulbe@icar.gov.in (email as printed in the bulletin). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Dr. R.K. Khulbe, Sr. Scientist & I/C (Plant Breeding), AICRP Maize Almora: rkkhulbe@gmail.com; rajesh.khulbe@icar.gov.in; +91-9411354346. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Directory/Directory_2025.pdf
AICRP Maize Almora centre: Crop Improvement Division, VPKAS, Almora-263601; Ph. 05962-230208; Fax 05962-231539; aicrp_maize.alm@icar.gov.in. -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Directory/Directory_2025.pdf
Institute address: ICAR-VPKAS, Mall Road, Almora-263601, Uttarakhand; phone +91-5962-230208. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
Director (Dr. Lakshmi Kant): Director, Almora; director.vpkas@icar.gov.in (as listed); vpkas@nic.in; lakshmi.kant@icar.gov.in; phones 05962-230208, 9389669695. -- https://www.indiacustomercare.com/vivekananda-parvatiya-krishi-anusandhan-sansthan-icar-vpkas-no
Dr. Lakshmi Kant profile (Director (A) since 2020; Head, Division of Crop Improvement): Email lakshmi.kant@icar.gov.in; Cell 9412044391. -- https://naas.org.in/detail.php?id=719
Institute-level contact (VPKAS main): +91-5962-230208; director.vpkas@icar.gov.in. -- https://www.facebook.com/www.vpkas.icar.gov.in/

PUBLICATIONS

Authors not fully visible (corresponding author R. Khulbe) (year not shown in retrieved text). Maize Variety VL VitA VLQPM Hybrid 45 (variety notification bulletin). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
Sources for VLQPM Hybrid 61 and the 2021-22 AICRP trial data appear in the same bulletin; no separate journal article was found for either name. No DOI found.
Excluded: Vivek Maize Hybrid 45 (VMH 45, 2013 notification) is a different hybrid. Vivek QPM 9 (VQL1 x VQL2) is a different hybrid. Both were discarded despite name resemblance.

SEED AVAILABILITY

No evidence found. Searches 1 to 4 returned no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VLQPM Hybrid 61 (maize) evidence digest

Name check: the CSC release minutes name and the Seednet name are identical ("VLQPM Hybrid 61"). The evidence below refers to that name, which the source also writes as "VLQPMH 61." No Seednet portal page was returned, so the Seednet record itself is unverified. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this hybrid. The waterlogging and drought studies returned (e.g., the Asia AWDT multi-location trial and the waterlogging multi-environment trial) involve other hybrids, so I excluded them. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358285361_Multi-environment_field_testing_to_identify_better_performing_and_stable_genotypes_for_water_logging_stress_tolerance_in_tropical_maize (excluded, other hybrids); https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12554654/ (excluded, other hybrids)

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight and maydis leaf blight is reported for this hybrid. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
No pest-resistance data were found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Single-cross QPM hybrid, released and notified by the CSC on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties (S.O. 4065(E), dated 31.08.22) for Uttarakhand hills. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Maturity: the same source gives both 85-90 days in mid-hills and 95-100 days to maturity, which conflict; both are recorded here. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Average yield of 4,435 kg/ha in state varietal trials (2018-20, Uttarakhand hills), 10.9% above the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Yield of about 8,876 kg/ha under 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK; the hybrid responds to nitrogen. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Plant height 200-210 cm. Grain is yellow, semi-flint, flat and medium-bold, with 1000-grain weight of about 260 g. Purple anthers, glume and silk; green husk with good cover. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Grain quality: 9.16% protein, 0.76% tryptophan, 3.30% lysine. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Parentage: the source says it was developed by crossing QPM lines including VBL 17; the second parent is truncated in the retrieved text, so VQL 1 could not be confirmed from the source. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or MAS studies specific to VLQPM Hybrid 61. The MAS-derived QPM work returned concerns Vivek QPM 9 and is excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/263374947_Accelerated_development_of_quality_protein_maize_hybrid_through_marker-assisted_introgression_of_opaque-2_allele (excluded, other hybrid)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- The VPKAS maize listing gives the release as 2022 (SVRC), area Uttarakhand, which differs from the CSC notification route in the publication above. -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
- No lead breeder name for this variety was found in the retrieved text. Names on other VPKAS maize releases were not transferred to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora 263 601 (263601), Uttarakhand, India. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute website: https://vpkas.icar.gov.in (official ICAR-VPKAS site, from the maize listing page).
- No breeder name, email or phone number for this variety was found in the search results. Institute contact details were not visible beyond the address and website.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured in the retrieved text (year not confirmed). "Maize Variety VL VitA VLQPM Hybrid 45" (release notification compilation, includes a VLQPM Hybrid 61 entry). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding (IJGPB). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Authors not captured (year not confirmed). "Vivek Maize hybrid 51 (FH 3554)" (release notification) lists VPKAS as developer, but does not mention VLQPM Hybrid 61 in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554 (excluded, other hybrid)
- No peer-reviewed field-trial papers, AICRP/ICAR reports or KrishiKosh theses specifically on VLQPM Hybrid 61 were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this hybrid was returned. The only related statement is that the publication expects the high-yielding parents to keep seed prices reasonable, which is a projection, not a seed-sale record. -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105

RECOMMENDED STATES
Uttarakhand (hill regions). -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105 ; https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 215-225 cm; 1000-grain weight about 280 g; semi-flint, yellow grain with purple anthers and glume. Early maturing (90-95 days in mid-hills).
agronomic_details.field_trials: State varietal trials in Uttarakhand hills, 2018-20: mean yield 4,675 kg/ha, 16.9% above the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions. Nitrogen response trial: 9,671 kg/ha at 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK. Grain quality: 9.22% protein, 0.72% tryptophan, 3.20% lysine. Disease observations: moderate resistance to turcicum and maydis leaf blight in the same 2018-20 state trials.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Opaque-2 allele (carried by female parent VQL 398), introgressed by marker-assisted backcross breeding. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME CHECK
variety_name (CSC minutes) = "VLQPM Hybrid 63"; seednet_variety_name = "VLQPM Hybrid 63". Both names are identical, so all evidence below refers to both. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved; the Seednet crop label was not checked against a live page.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight and maydis leaf blight, reported in the 2018-20 state trials -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for this hybrid under those conditions.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate resistance to turcicum leaf blight and maydis leaf blight (same finding as above) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Early maturing, 90-95 days in mid-hills; plant height 215-225 cm; 1000-grain weight about 280 g -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- State varietal trials in Uttarakhand hills, 2018-20: mean yield 4,675 kg/ha, 16.9% above the QPM check Vivek QPM 9 under organic conditions -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Responsive to nitrogen; 9,671 kg/ha at 150:60:60 kg/ha NPK -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Grain quality: 9.22% protein, 0.72% tryptophan, 3.20% lysine; semi-flint, yellow grain with purple anthers and glume -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute variety listing (SVRC, 2022, Uttarakhand) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: VQL 398 (female) x V 467 (male). VQL 398 carries the opaque-2 allele introgressed by marker-assisted backcross breeding; V 467 is a high lysine and tryptophan line -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- QPM (quality protein maize) single-cross hybrid -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- QTL or marker-validation studies specific to this hybrid: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Named lead breeder or scientist for VLQPM Hybrid 63: No evidence found. The retrieved pages name only the institute. Names associated with other VPKAS QPM hybrids (Vivek QPM 9, Vivek Maize Hybrid 9) were found in other pages and were not attributed to this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute name and postal address as printed: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora 263 601, Uttrakhand, India -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute website: https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize (official ICAR-VPKAS site)
- Official email: No evidence found
- Phone: No evidence found
- Breeder name, role, email or phone: No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not confirmed in retrieved text (2022 variety notification compilation). Maize Variety VL VitA and VLQPM Hybrid 45 (includes VLQPM Hybrid 63 entry). Indian Journal of Genetics and Plant Breeding (ISGPB) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105 (Year: not confirmed in retrieved text; DOI: not found)
- The author names "H. Rajashekara" and "D. Mahanta" appear in the retrieved text near this entry, but their role for this variety is not confirmed, so they are not attributed here.
- Other QPM or VPKAS publications were found but do not name VLQPM Hybrid 63, so they are excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Searches returned only generic seed-company, CIMMYT and seed-production pages, none naming this hybrid. Check the VPKAS Almora seed unit, the Uttarakhand State Seed Corporation or a KVK directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Notified for cultivation in Uttarakhand hills (S.O. 4065(E), dated 31.08.22) -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- VPKAS maize listing gives area of adaptation as Uttarakhand (SVRC, 2022) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
- Discrepancy: the notification text refers to the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards (CSC). The VPKAS listing shows an SVRC (state) release. Verify the release body before citing it as a central release.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: VL QPM Hybrid 59 (seednet name: VL QPM Hybrid 59 (FQH 106)), maize. Four web searches were run. Most findings below refer to the CSC name "VL QPM Hybrid 59". FQH 106, the seednet code, appears only in one conference abstract.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. None of the searches returned stress-tolerance data for this variety. Results about other QPM hybrids and African trials were discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Pages on other hybrids (VL VitA / VLQPM Hybrid 45, VLQPM Hybrid 61, Vivek Maize Hybrid 57) were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for VL QPM Hybrid 59 or FQH 106 (maturity, yield, or multi-location results). The only FQH 106 mention is in a conference abstract, listed under PUBLICATIONS.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No retrieved page links this variety or FQH 106 to QTL, markers or MAS. The parentage in the record (VQL 373 x VQL 1) is not confirmed by any retrieved page. Vivek QPM 9, Pusa Vivek QPM9 and VLQPM Hybrid 63 marker and MAS pages were discarded as other varieties.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (name used: VL QPM Hybrid 59)
- The 98th Foundation Day page of ICAR-VPKAS, Almora, says the Director-General dedicated VL QPM Hybrid 59 with two other new varieties to farmers -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127
- The 97th Foundation Day page (dated 4 July 2020) lists VL QPM Hybrid 59 among the releases and calls it a QPM maize variety -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/12335 (Note: this date is earlier than the 2020-11-09 release date in the record. The discrepancy is not resolved here.)
- Lead breeder: No evidence found. The name "D. Mahanta" appears only as an author on papers about other varieties, so it is not attributed here.
- Institute director (institute-level, not a breeder): Dr. Lakshmi Kant, named as Director of ICAR-VPKAS, Almora -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address (institute-level; taken from an affiliation line in a paper on another variety): ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Almora 263 601, Uttarakhand, India -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/4883/3105
- Institute seed portal page (contact-type URL): https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
- Director: Dr. Lakshmi Kant, Director (role only; no email or phone found) -- https://www.icar.org.in/en/node/3127
- Breeder name, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Official email and phone for the institute: No evidence found in the retrieved pages.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated; the file path suggests a 2018 upload). Book of Abstracts, 13th Asian Maize Conference and Expert Consultation. Abstract on haploid induction at ICAR-VPKAS, Almora, kharif 2016–2017, in which FQH 106 was used as a QPM female parent and reported seed set per ear -- https://archive.maize.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/76/2018/09/13thAMCBookofAbstracts.pdf
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP/ICAR report or DOI naming VL QPM Hybrid 59 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The ICAR-VPKAS seed portal lists VL QPM Hybrid 59 under Maize Hybrids with an "Add to Cart" option. Price and stock were not visible -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- The seed portal gives the area of suitability as Uttarakhand Hills -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93

EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vivek Maize Hybrid-27 (release-minutes name, variety_code FH 3288) and Vivek Hybrid Maize-53 (Seednet name, "Vivek Hybrid Maize - 53")

NAME NOTE: Every page that names "Vivek Maize Hybrid-27" or "Vivek Hybrid 27" points to the VPKAS Almora hybrid with pedigree V 335 x V 345. The Seednet name "Vivek Hybrid Maize - 53" points to a different hybrid, Vivek Maize Hybrid 53 (FH 3556), with parents V 407 x V 409. I found no page linking Vivek-53 to Vivek-27, so the Seednet-name findings are listed separately below and are not attributed to Vivek-27. The FH 3288 code appears on no page I retrieved. The input release year (2011-06-28) conflicts with the 2007 notification evidence (1703(E), 05/10/2007).

STRESS TOLERANCE
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: the 1961-2010 release compendium lists resistance to turcicum leaf blight (TLB) and common rust for Vivek 27 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was stated for this hybrid in any retrieved page. No evidence found for those stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: TLB and common rust resistance as listed in the 1961-2010 compendium -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no pest-resistance data (stem borer, fall armyworm) was found. No evidence found for pests.
Seednet name (Vivek Hybrid Maize-53, not Vivek-27): tolerance to turcicum leaf blight, maydis leaf blight and a moderate rust reaction, reported over three years of multilocation trials -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: extra-early maturity and 5.0-5.5 t/ha yield in the 2000-era hybrid list -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: a yield of 85 q/ha is printed beside the Vivek 27 entry in the 1961-2010 compendium, but the layout is ambiguous and this conflicts with the 5.0-5.5 t/ha figure -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: the Vivek 27 entry in the 2010 compendium lists a leaf-angle trait score; no trial data was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
Seednet name (Vivek-53, not Vivek-27): 12 multilocation trials in Zone I gave 7676 kg/ha, 26.08% above the Vivek QPM 9 check; plant height 185-195 cm; maturity 85-90 days in mid hills and 80-85 days in plains -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554
Seednet name (Vivek-53, not Vivek-27): a benchmarking table lists VMH 53 as a 7.6 t/ha, extra-early hybrid for Kharif in Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, Uttarakhand and UP -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties

GENETICS AND QTL
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: single cross with pedigree V 335 x V 345 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010 and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no QTL, marker or molecular study naming this hybrid was found. No evidence found.
Seednet name (Vivek-53, not Vivek-27): parents V 407 (female) and V 409 (male) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: developed by ICAR-VPKAS, Almora (Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan, Uttarakhand), notified 2007 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: no named breeder or lead scientist was found on any page. No evidence found for breeder names.
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: release-year conflict. The input says 2011-06-28, but the compendium gives 05/10/2007 under notification 1703(E) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290899665_A_Compendium_of_maize_hybrids_and_composites_of_India_under_PPV_FRA_Technical_Bulletin_No_20104_pp_84
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: FH 3288 code not found on any page. No evidence found for the variety code.
Seednet name (Vivek-53): developed by VPKAS Almora, identified by the Varietal Identification Committee -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/298045597_Vivek_Maize_hybrid_51_FH_3554

CONTACT DETAILS
Vivek Maize Hybrid-27: No evidence found. No breeder contact, email, phone or address appeared on a page that names this variety. The VPKAS Almora address seen on Gupta et al. pages concerns a different QPM hybrid (Vivek Maize Hybrid 9 / QPM 9), so it was excluded.
Seednet name (Vivek-53): the seed-portal page lists "VPKAS" as brand but gives no contact details -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/VivekMaizeHybrid53_%E0%A4%B5%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%B5%E0%A5%87%E0%A4%95%E0%A4%AE%E0%A4%95%E0%A

disease_resistance.summary: High tolerance to Turcicum leaf blight (Helminthosporium turcicum) and high tolerance to Maydis leaf blight (Helminthosporium maydis) under natural infection over three years of station trials; the parents were also rated tolerant. agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of 6686 kg/ha across trials, with consistent superiority over checks Prakash (15.4-29.2%) and JH3459 (14.1-32.9%). Assam package lists a potential yield of 69 q/ha (about 6900 kg/ha); this is a package-level figure and its variety attribution is not explicit in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Consistent superiority over the checks Prakash and JH3459 across trials. The digest gives no further across-environment stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to rainfed hill agro-ecosystems and the marginal Himalayan environment (mid hills). The digest lists the adaptation ecology as NEH Region in the original data, but no NEH-specific trial evidence was found in the digest. Hybrid seed should not be saved for resowing because of segregation (Assam package).

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height about 200-210 cm in the hills; semi-flint grain, yellow with purplish glume and brown anther. Assam package: yellow cob with white cap.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials over three years under natural infection rated high tolerance to Turcicum and Maydis leaf blights (see disease_resistance). (2) Multi-trial average yield of 6686 kg/ha, with superiority over Prakash by 15.4-29.2% and over JH3459 by 14.1-32.9%. (3) Agronomy trials showed 21.8% yield superiority over JH3459 and 22.7% over Prakash. (4) Identified by the Varietal Identification Committee at the 56th Maize Workshop, ANGRAU Hyderabad, 6-8 April 2013. (5) A benchmarking table lists Hybrid 47 at 6.9 t/ha under a Uttar Pradesh Kharif row, but the digest marks this attribution as unverified and the table layout as ambiguous; it is excluded from the yield figures above. Fertilizer, seed rate and sowing schedule data specific to this hybrid were not found beyond the generic Assam package.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Note: the search tool hit its usage limit during my second batch, so I could not run the remaining checks. The four searches that did run returned no page that names Vivek Hybrid 27 or Vivek Maize Hybrid-27 (FH3288) in the text I captured. The snippets I saw were truncated to about 300 characters, so the full pages were not checked for this name.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched "Maize Hybrid Vivek Hybrid 27 maize variety"; returned general lists of Indian maize releases, not this variety's tolerance data.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No returned page named this variety with disease or pest data.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Searched "Vivek Hybrid 27 maize research paper trial"; the results named other Vivek hybrids (for example Vivek Hybrid 33) but not Vivek Hybrid 27. Source: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290911638_Maize_Hybrid_and_Composite_Varieties_Released_in_India_1961-2010

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage in the record (V335 x V345) could not be confirmed from any returned page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for this variety. Searched "Vivek Hybrid 27 maize breeder developed by VPKAS Almora." The results showed VPKAS Almora developing other maize hybrids (e.g., 'Vivek QPM9', 2008) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/SR/article/download/174708/64409/506477. These are different varieties and are not attributed to Vivek Hybrid 27.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact details were returned for this variety. Recommended institute-level starting point, unverified in this session: VPKAS, Almora (ICAR), via icar.org.in.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis naming this variety was returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Searched "Vivek Maize Hybrid-27 FH3288 seed availability." The AICMIP list of released maize hybrids (https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/Documents/Hybrids%20of%20maize%20released-1.pdf) includes Vivek Maize Hybrid 39 (2012), which is a different variety and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found on the listed states for this variety. The record lists Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Odisha, Tamil Nadu, Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal, but these are unverified by any returned source.

Suggested next steps: open the AICMIP released-hybrids PDF and check its entry for Vivek Hybrid 27 (the search snippet was cut off before reaching it); check the full ResearchGate PDF; search seednet.gov.in directly for "FH3288"; and when the search tool is available again, run the contact and publication searches with the spelling "Vivek Hybrid-27" and the ICAR-VPKAS website.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Chhattisgarh Nandiraj (mango, variety code H060216782)

Name note: The CSC variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Chhattisgarh Nandiraj"). I did not find a Seednet portal entry, so all Seednet-related evidence below is absent. Searches used: 4 (variety, breeder/institution, research, seed availability).

Release-year discrepancy: The record says 2013-06-04. An ICAR Indian Horticulture article says the variety was released in 2015 by IGKV, Chhattisgarh. Flag this for verification against the CSC minutes.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Variety is a clonal selection of local mango from Nayapara, Jagdalpur, Chhattisgarh. Described as having attractive shape, appearance and pleasant aroma. -- https://mangifera.res.in/varieties.php (also https://www.hortportal.org/mangifera_res/site/varieties.php)
- Under rainfed Chhattisgarh plains conditions, this cultivar had the highest share of male flowers (88.56%) and hermaphrodite flowers (48.40%) per panicle, and the highest sex ratio (7.76), in a flowering/fruiting comparison. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329513272_Assessing_the_Flowering_and_Fruiting_Behaviour_in_Some_Important_Cultivars_of_Mango_Mangifera_indica_L
- In a Bilaspur-region germplasm evaluation (Chhattisgarh Plain Agro-climatic Zone), the variety was among collected material evaluated; yield and trial figures were not confirmed from the retrieved text. -- https://zenodo.org/records/5723045
- In a South Gujarat coloured-variety study, this cultivar showed the minimum fruit breadth (5.61 cm) among compared cultivars. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313369324_Studies_on_Fruit_and_Yield_Traits_in_Indigenous_Coloured_Varieties_of_Mango_Mangifera_indica_L_in_South_Gujarat_India
- In a Malda (West Bengal) cultivar characterization, this cultivar appeared in the results, but the snippet did not give a clear value for it. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/315713567_Characterization_of_Different_Cultivars_of_Mango_Commercially_Grown_in_Malda_India
- In a Bihar study, this cultivar recorded the lowest peel weight (21.80 g) and lowest peel percentage among compared cultivars... (the snippet names Nandiraj with peel weight 21.80 g and Raj with the lowest peel percentage (10.81%)). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/385273170_Characterization_of_Some_Leading_Mango_Mangifera_indica_L_Cultivars_in_Bihar_Condition_Based_on_Yield_and_Chemical_Quality_Parameters

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. Searches returned no parentage, marker, or QTL studies. The record lists parentage as "Not specified"; the source describes it as a clonal selection, so parentage is not a cross.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by Indira Gandhi Krishi Vishwavidyalaya (IGKV), Raipur. -- https://mangifera.res.in/varieties.php
- ICAR article attributes release to IGKV, Chhattisgarh, and describes the variety as a clonal selection from Nayapara, Jagdalpur. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndHort/article/download/117187/45388
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found. No breeder name was found in any retrieved source.
- Station/division: No evidence found beyond the university and the Nayapara (Jagdalpur) origin of the selection.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search budget note: the first batch ran four searches. A second attempt to re-read the full page text was blocked by the tool-use limit, so I could not open the pages. Most headings below rest only on the short search snippets, and several are incomplete.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: "Pusa Soumya" (CSC/variety_name) is the name used for the evidence below. "Pusa Surya" (Seednet name, listed under MANGO) returned no onion evidence. Its only hit was an Amazon listing for "Pusa Red Onion Seed", which is a different product, so it was discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- A 2022 Frontiers in Plant Science article's introduction says a 2019 study reported Pusa Soumya (described as a bunching-type onion) as moderately resistant. The snippet does not name the stress or pathogen, so I have not attributed it to any specific disease. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.1063685/xml
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. These were not in the retrieved snippets.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Same Frontiers source as above: Pusa Soumya reported as moderately resistant in a 2019 study. The disease is not named in the retrieved text. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.1063685/xml
Possible relevance only (not confirmed for this variety): an IARI-affiliated PDF on purple blotch resistance screening of 34 onion genotypes. Its snippet does not mention Pusa Soumya. -- https://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/58bb/1c25254827ff036ce05200ed3bb62d835c52.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. The searches did not return yield, maturity or trial data naming Pusa Soumya. The ResearchGate onion breeding-for-quality review did not name the variety in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359705125_Onion_Allium_cepa_L_Breeding_for_quality_traits_and_export

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. No QTL or marker study naming Pusa Soumya was retrieved.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution per input record: Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi. Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The search results did not name a breeder or developing scientist for Pusa Soumya. Release year 2015-04-07 and parentage "An introduction from Brazil" come from the input record only and were not verified by search. CSC release minutes were not retrieved.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address or contact-page URL for Pusa Soumya was retrieved. I have not filled these in from memory. Verify via the IARI website and the Seednet portal.

PUBLICATIONS
Frontiers in Plant Science (2022). Introduction section citing a 2019 onion resistance study that mentions Pusa Soumya. Full title, authors and journal volume were not visible in the retrieved text. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2022.1063685/xml (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2022.1063685)
Note: this is a citing source, not the 2019 study itself. The 2019 study's authors and title are not identified.
Research search returned no other paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper that names Pusa Soumya. The Semantic Scholar IARI PDF is a candidate only; its snippet does not name the variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Pusa Soumya. The "Pusa Surya" query returned only an Amazon listing for "Pusa Red Onion Seed" (https://www.amazon.in/Pusa-Onion-Seed-450-SEED/dp/B09JNV6CXQ), a different product, so it is excluded. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was retrieved. The Seednet record for Pusa Surya under MANGO was not retrieved.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Only the input record states "NCT of Delhi". The search did not confirm it. No evidence found in search results.

Suggested next steps: open the Frontiers article to identify the 2019 study and the disease named; check the CSC minutes and Seednet record for the variety, release year and states; and check the IARI Division of Vegetable Science contact page for breeder and contact details.

drought.details: Pusa Surya (mango) is often mentioned in contexts where rootstocks ('K-2', 'K5', general tolerant rootstocks) are used to manage water or drought stress. This suggests the scion benefits from the rootstock's tolerance rather than possessing inherent drought tolerance itself, as rootstocks tolerant to drought have been recommended for mango varieties including Pusa Surya.

heat.details: Pusa Surya (mango) is noted for its pollination not being affected by increasing atmospheric temperature (during the season without affecting pollination). It is also mentioned in the context of post-harvest heat treatments. No direct evidence on the plant's specific field heat stress tolerance was found.

salinity.details: Pusa Surya (mango) is frequently discussed in relation to salt-tolerant rootstocks ('Kurukkan', 'Olour', '13-1') for mango, indicating that the variety can be successfully grown in saline conditions when grafted onto such rootstocks. Its intrinsic scion tolerance is not explicitly stated.

agronomic_details.adaptation: While the original variety data lists adaptation for wheat, the provided search results overwhelmingly identify 'Pusa Surya' as a mango (Mangifera indica L.) variety developed by ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute. As a mango variety, it is described as a 'new promising variety'. Its commercial suitability implies adaptation to typical mango growing regions, consistent with its release by IARI. agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Pusa Surya is a mango variety producing apricot yellow coloured fruit with prominent dots and broadly bused wrinkled leaves. It is characterized by medium-sized fruit, yellow peel color, good shelf life, and long self life. The tree is described as moderate vigorous, with its growth potentially inhibited by certain rootstocks like 'K-2' and 'K5'. Pusa Surya is also identified as a selection, synonymous with 'Eldon', which was an introduction from Brazil.

agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Pusa Surya is a mango variety producing apricot yellow coloured fruit with prominent dots and broadly bused wrinkled leaves. It is characterized by medium-sized fruit, yellow peel color, good shelf life, and long self life. The tree is described as moderate vigorous, with its growth potentially inhibited by certain rootstocks like 'K-2' and 'K5'. Pusa Surya is also identified as a selection, synonymous with 'Eldon', which was an introduction from Brazil.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: Arka Pradhan / ARKA RAJHANS (IIHR-15-5)**

**Name mismatch:** The record lists "Arka Pradhan" (crop "indian bean", code IIHR-15-5), but the Seednet name is "ARKA RAJHANS" (crop "MUSK MELON"). My searches found no source for "Arka Pradhan" or for an Indian bean variety with that code. Every finding below refers to **Arka Rajhans (muskmelon, Cucumis melo)**, the name on Seednet. The parentage text in the record (IIHR-107, a Rajasthan collection) matches Arka Rajhans's known origin, so the record appears to mix a muskmelon origin with a bean name. Verify the crop and name against the CSC notification before using this record.

**Search coverage:** I ran three searches successfully. A fourth-search batch failed with a tool limit error, so I did not run the seed-availability search. The searches returned mostly secondary sources (ResearchGate and SlideShare compilations), not official ICAR or Seednet pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for Arka Rajhans on drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343819994_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L

DISEASE AND PEST -- No specific resistance data found for Arka Rajhans. A related IIHR muskmelon, Arka Jeet, is described as field resistant to powdery mildew and root rot, but this does not apply to Arka Rajhans. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296835410_Muskmelon_genetics_Breeding_and_Cultural_Practices

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Secondary compilations describe Arka Rajhans as a melon with round to slightly oval, medium-large fruit, selected in 1975 for better fruit quality and yield attributes. Quantitative yield data were not found. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/muskmelon-breeding/140193677
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A DUS characterization study lists Arka Rajhans among muskmelon varieties with an elongated globe fruit shape and a creamy suture colour. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286933870_DUS_characterization_of_muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L_varieties
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A general muskmelon review gives 90–110 days to harvest for varieties in general, not specific to Arka Rajhans. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343819994_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on Arka Rajhans. Its origin is given as a selection from local collection IIHR-107 from Rajasthan. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296835410_Muskmelon_genetics_Breeding_and_Cultural_Practices

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Arka Rajhans is attributed to the Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR), Bengaluru, as a selection from the IIHR-107 local collection of Rajasthan. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296835410_Muskmelon_genetics_Breeding_and_Cultural_Practices
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- A second compilation gives the same origin, a selection from a local Rajasthan collection (IIHR-107) at IIHR Bangalore, identified in 1975. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/muskmelon-breeding/140193677
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the lead breeder or scientist names for Arka Rajhans or for "Arka Pradhan".

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. The developing institute is IIHR, Bengaluru, but no official IIHR email, phone, address, or contact-page URL was retrieved in these searches. Verify at the IIHR website (iihr.res.in) before use.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis specifically on Arka Rajhans was retrieved. The following are secondary compilations that mention it:
Goutam et al. (2020). Cited in: Scientific Cultivation of Muskmelon (Cucumis melo L.). Compilation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/343819994_Scientific_Cultivation_of_Muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L
Author not identified. Muskmelon genetics, breeding, and cultural practices. Book chapter compilation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296835410_Muskmelon_genetics_Breeding_and_Cultural_Practices
Author not identified. Muskmelon breeding. SlideShare presentation -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/muskmelon-breeding/140193677
Author not identified. DUS characterization of muskmelon (Cucumis melo L.) varieties. Compilation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286933870_DUS_characterization_of_muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L_varieties

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The fourth search (NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, dealers) was not completed.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, or Jharkhand for Arka Rajhans. The record's state list could not be verified.

**Release year:** The record gives 2023-05-04. The sources retrieved are older compilations and do not confirm a 2023 release or a CSC notification.

drought.details: Information regarding drought tolerance for Arka Madhu marigold is not available in the provided search results. The search results frequently mention 'Hara Madhu' muskmelon as a variety with less water requirement and drought-tolerant accessions (RESULT_2, RESULT_4). 'Arka' (without 'Madhu') is also listed among muskmelon varieties in the context of water stress (RESULT_3).

heat.details: Information regarding heat tolerance for Arka Madhu marigold is not available in the provided search results. The search results mention 'Hara Madhu' muskmelon as heat-tolerant (RESULT_11, RESULT_14, RESULT_15, RESULT_17, RESULT_20) and discuss genes involved in melon plant physiology under temperature stress (RESULT_13).

salinity.details: Information regarding salinity tolerance for Arka Madhu marigold is not available in the provided search results. The results indicate that alkaline soils with high salt concentration are not suitable for muskmelon cultivation, and 'Hara Madhu' muskmelon showed the highest rate of yield drop per unit salinity increase (RESULT_21, RESULT_22, RESULT_24, RESULT_26, RESULT_27, RESULT_30, RESULT_34).

flood.details: Information regarding flood tolerance for Arka Madhu marigold is not available in the provided search results. General references to 'water stress' include both drought and flooding (RESULT_3). Over flooding is advised to be avoided in muskmelon fields (RESULT_32).

disease_resistance.summary: Information regarding disease resistance for Arka Madhu marigold is not available in the provided search results. For muskmelon, 'Punjab Sunehri' (a selection from Hara Madhu x Edisto) is noted as tolerant to downy mildew (RESULT_12). Some muskmelon varieties are resistant to DM, PM, and CGMMV (RESULT_39).

pest_resistance.summary: Information regarding pest resistance for Arka Madhu marigold is not available in the provided search results. For muskmelon, Cucumis melo var. callosus is noted as resistant to fruit fly (RESULT_16, RESULT_39).

agronomic_details.yield: Unknown. No yield information is available for Arka Madhu marigold. For 'Hara Madhu' muskmelon, an average yield of 8–10 tonnes/ha is reported (RESULT_12).
agronomic_details.stability: Unknown.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Unknown for Arka Madhu marigold. The original data recommends Chhattisgarh and Karnataka. For 'Hara Madhu' muskmelon, it is mentioned in the context of promising climate-resilient technologies for Madhya Pradesh (RESULT_2, RESULT_15, RESULT_38). It is also listed as a variety for North West India and hot valleys of Iran (RESULT_48).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified for Arka Madhu marigold. For 'Hara Madhu' muskmelon, it is described as a late maturing variety with large, round fruits (RESULT_18, RESULT_22, RESULT_27, RESULT_32, RESULT_47). Vines are vigorous and 3-4m long (RESULT_47). Harvest is recommended when fruits turn yellow (RESULT_9, RESULT_26, RESULT_40). 'Hara Madhu' is also noted for high Brix and sweet, aromatic, high-sugar melons (RESULT_11, RESULT_25).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
CONFLICT FLAG: The record mixes two different varieties. "PMH 5 (JH 3110)" is a maize hybrid from PAU Ludhiana/ICAR-IIMR (AICRP and PPV&FR records). "MHY-5" is a muskmelon variety from ARS/RARI Durgapura, and its parentage (Durgapura Madhu x Hara Madhu) and institution match the muskmelon record. Evidence is reported under each name below, and no muskmelon fact is attributed to the maize hybrid. The maize release year in the source tables is 2011 and the record says 2010-12-23. Searches run: 4 (one on the maize name, one on breeders, one on research, one on the MHY-5 seednet name). No separate seed-availability search was run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Maize PMH 5 / JH 3110: No evidence found. The drought-tolerance pages returned covered other maize varieties (for example Sammaz 52 and TZPB), so they were discarded.
Muskmelon MHY-5 (seednet name): RARI describes MHY 5 as having moderate resistance to root rot, powdery mildew and virus, grouped with RM 50 and MHY 3 -- https://raridurgapura.org/varieties-developed.htm

DISEASE AND PEST
Maize PMH 5 / JH 3110: No evidence found for disease or pest resistance of this hybrid. The resistance tables returned named PMH-1 and other hybrids, which were discarded.
Muskmelon MHY-5: Classed as moderately resistant to melon fruit fly (Bactrocera cucurbitae) in field screening of eleven genotypes in the hot arid region of Rajasthan -- https://zenodo.org/records/6812561 ; same finding also reported -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252322970_Allelochemical_resistance_traits_of_muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_against_the_fruit_fly_Bactrocera_cucurbitae_in_a_hot_arid_region_of_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maize PMH 5 / JH 3110: Listed as an entry in the Kharif 2016 AICRP maize report, PAU Ludhiana, with PPV&FR registration dated August 2016 -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf ; a PMH5 (C) trial entry from PAU Ludhiana appears in the same report, but its yield figures are not labelled in the retrieved text -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf ; benchmarking table lists PMH 5 (PAU Ludhiana), white/orange flint with an early maturity class and a yield value of 5.9 (unit not shown) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290428916_benchmarking_indian_maize_varieties
Muskmelon MHY-5: Ovate fruit shape and medium flesh thickness in DUS characterization -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/286933870_DUS_characterization_of_muskmelon_Cucumis_melo_L_varieties ; MHY-5 showed the highest marketable fruits per plant and early fruit harvesting in a Durgapura trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391810627_As_sess_ment_of_Ge_netic_Vari_abil_ity_Among_Musk_melon_Cucumis_melo_Ge_no_types_in_the_Hot_Arid_Re_gions

GENETICS AND QTL
Maize PMH 5 / JH 3110: No evidence found for QTL or marker studies. Parentage was not found for the maize hybrid.
Muskmelon MHY-5: Produced at ARS Durgapura by pedigree selection combined with hybridization, from Durgapura Madhu x Hara Madhu -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384438288_Advances_in_Breeding_of_Muskmelon ; same cross listed under heterosis breeding -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384438288_Advances_in_Breeding_of_Muskmelon ; cross also listed -- https://www.horticultureguruji.in/muskmelon-cultivation/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Maize PMH 5 / JH 3110: Registered for PPV&FR protection by ICAR-IIMR Ludhiana; the Department of Plant Breeding, PAU Ludhiana is listed as an affiliation -- https://www.ijcmas.com/10-8-2021/Dhirendra%20Singh,%20et%20al.pdf ; developed by PAU plant breeders per a 2006 press item on the earlier PMH-1 hybrid, which does not confirm PMH 5 -

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Punjab Sindhuri (CSC name) / Panjab Sinduri (Seednet name), chilli
Searches run: 4 web_search queries (variety traits; breeder and institution; research papers; seed availability).
Name note: The release-era evidence uses "Punjab Sindhuri" (PAU spelling). No page I found uses "Panjab Sinduri." The Seednet record lists the crop as MUSK MELON, but every chilli page found is about chilli, so the Seednet crop entry is unverified and conflicts with the sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Described as moderately resistant to leaf curl virus, dieback and root-knot nematodes, and tolerant of aphids, thrips and yellow mites (PAU factsheet; the bullets sit under the Sindhuri block, but the layout is ambiguous) -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance data found for this variety -- No evidence found (searched)

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderate resistance to leaf curl virus, dieback and root-knot nematode, and tolerance to aphids, thrips and yellow mites -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf
Leaf curl resistance is mentioned in a PAU adoption study only for CH-27, not for Sindhuri -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380081136_An_appraisal_of_Chilli_production_technology_adopted_by_the_farmers_of_Punjab (discarded for this variety)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Early maturing; first picking of red fruit about 75 days after transplanting; fruit about 7.14 cm long, thick-skinned, dark green immature and deep red ripe; about 1% capsaicin; about 155 mg/100 g vitamin C -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
Average yield about 190 q/ha, about 206% above check Punjab Surkh (62 q/ha); multilocation trial mean about 176 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287935720_Punjab_Sindhuri_and_Punjab_Tej_New_Varieties_of_Chilli
Potential of about 76 q/acre red ripe fruit; farmers can save seed -- https://pau.edu/content/research/32_3.pdf
Average about 96 qtl/acre cited in a general chilli farming guide -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/horticulture/vegetable-crops/chilli
Good Agricultural Practices guide for NE India lists about 100 q/acre yield for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373629483_Good_Agricultural_Practices_for_Important_Spices_of_North_East_India_-_Chilli
Fresh red fruit used in a drying study at PAU -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/322419835_Study_of_drying_behavior_in_red_chillies
Honey chilli sauce study using Punjab sindhuri red chilli -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/jfpp.15734

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found (searched; no QTL, marker or parentage study for this variety; parentage in the CSC record is "Not specified")

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

The 109-variety list entry describes it as moderately tolerant to drought. The digest also states it is suitable for timely sown, restricted irrigation conditions. The sensitivity index value and the 'tolerant' wording are not consistent with each other, so the level is set to medium. No mechanism-level data was found.

heat.details: The release-level claim describes the variety as tolerant to heat, with a heat sensitivity index of 0.98 (CSC list). The 109-variety list entry describes it as tolerant to high temperatures. The index value is not consistent with the tolerance description, so the level is set to medium. No mechanism-level data was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Release-level claim (name: Pusa Gehun Sharbati / HI 1665, CSC list; Seednet name "Pusa Sharbati" not located): heat sensitivity index 0.98 and drought sensitivity index 0.91, described as tolerant to heat and drought -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/pm-modi-unveils-new-climate-resilient-wheat-variety-pusa-gehun-sharbati-hi-1665/
Moderately tolerant to bacterial blight and drought, and tolerant to high temperatures (list entry for the wheat row) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/list-of-109-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/
Suitable for timely sown, restricted irrigation conditions (no full-irrigation or saline/flood/submergence data found) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-gehun-sharbati-hi-1665/
Salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to leaf rust and stem rust (release reports) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-gehun-sharbati-hi-1665/
Moderately tolerant to bacterial blight (list entry) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/list-of-109-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/
Yellow rust, Karnal bunt, insect pest reaction: No evidence found for this variety
Note: the same list entry carries red-aril, anthocyanin and anardana text that appears to belong to a pomegranate profile, not wheat. Excluded as unreliable -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/list-of-109-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Grain yield 33.0 q/ha and maturity about 110 days (release) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-gehun-sharbati-hi-1665/
Tribune report of IIWBR recommendation gives average 33 q/ha and 110 days maturity -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/karnal-scientists-behind-barley-variant/
Excluded as wrong: "average yield is 351 q/ha" in the 109-variety list (implausible, likely a typo) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/list-of-109-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/
Excluded as outdated and not this variety: a 2011 blog citing about 23 q/acre -- https://agroconsultants.blogspot.com/2010/12/agroconsultancy.html
Multi-location trial data, AICRP entry data, plant height: No evidence found (only a 85-90 cm plant height figure for a different Oswal SHARBATI-14001 product was seen, so not used) -- https://www.oswalseeds.com/shar.html
Zinc content 40.0 ppm (biofortified) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-gehun-sharbati-hi-1665/

GENETICS AND QTL
Open pollinated variety (release classification, not a pure line) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/list-of-109-climate-resilient-and-biofortified-varieties-released-by-pm-modi/
Pedigree, marker, QTL or gene-postulation studies for HI 1665: No evidence found. The IARI newsletter QTL material concerns durum and rust-gene lines, not this variety -- https://pusakrishi.in/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/IARI-News_letter_english_jul_sept_2024.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Regional Station, Indore, Madhya Pradesh -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/pm-modi-unveils-new-climate-resilient-wheat-variety-pusa-gehun-sharbati-hi-1665/
Recommended by the ICAR-IIWBR Karnal (AICRP wheat and barley nodal centre) -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/karnal-scientists-behind-barley-variant/
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The scientist names in the Tribune article (Lokendra Singh, Joginder Singh, Chuni Lal, RPS Verma) belong to a barley variety story and are not attributed here -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/haryana/karnal-scientists-behind-barley-variant/
Name note: CSC/PM-release name is "Pusa Gehun Sharbati" (code HI 1665, also written HI-1665). The Seednet name "Pusa Sharbati" did not appear in any search result. The Seednet crop field reads "MUSK MELON", which conflicts with wheat and should be treated as a portal data error -- https://www.scribd.com/document/765228880/Final-109-Varieties-for-Release-by-Honble-PM-watermark

drought.details: BIO 9544 is identified as a drought-tolerant or water stress-tolerant variety. It is explicitly recommended as a drought-tolerant choice for maize cultivation and is listed among varieties for 'climate-smart agricultural technologies' in contexts of low-water input management. Evaluation reports also identify it as tolerant to drought stress.

heat.details: The variety is listed in documents discussing 'High-temperature and heat wave stress' in climate-smart agricultural technologies. Field days and evaluations associated with BIO 9544 have also touched upon 'Heat-stress-induced changes'.

salinity.details: BIO 9544 is listed within documents that address 'developing salt-tolerant varieties for coastal salinity'. While not explicitly stated as salt-tolerant, its inclusion in such contexts suggests its potential or evaluation for this trait.

flood.details: Maize, in general, is susceptible to waterlogging. While BIO 9544 has been subject to phenotyping for 'Waterlogging Stress', the provided results do not confirm its tolerance to flood or waterlogging. Some documents state that maize cannot tolerate water logging and requires well-drained soil.

disease_resistance.summary: BIO 9544 was found to be moderately resistant to an unspecified disease, compared to a check variety, Kaveri-50.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: BIO 9544 is characterized as a high-yielding variety and is frequently used as a check variety in yield performance assessments. Reported yields include 12.772 t/ha (for fodder maize) and 63.25 q/ha (6.325 t/ha) and 49.71 q/ha (4.971 t/ha) for grain in different zones and evaluations.
agronomic_details.stability: The variety is used as a 'best check' in heterosis studies for yield across locations and evaluated at multiple locations, suggesting good stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for cultivation during the Kharif season and also suitable for the Summer season (February–June) and summer fodder cultivation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Grains are orange-yellow and semi-dent type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensively evaluated in multi-location trials across various zones (e.g., Zone-I, Zone III) and states including Himachal Pradesh and Delhi, often serving as a check variety for both grain and fodder maize hybrids.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2 or FSCH 75 with drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. The only sweet corn stress hits were unrelated hybrids (for example, Sugar 75 and Pusa Super Sweet Corn).

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page named this variety with disease or pest resistance. Results for rust, leaf blight and virus resistance were about other sweet corn hybrids.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. No yield, maturity or trial data for VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2 or FSCH 75 was returned. The "Sugar 75" front-line demonstration study (florajournal.com) is a different variety and was discarded.

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The parentage VSL 26 x VSL 27 appears only in the request record and was not confirmed by any search result. The VPKAS sh2 backcross paper (researchgate.net/publication/332760677) names other parental lines (VLS3, VQL373) and does not name this variety, so it was discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-Vivekananda Parvatiya Krishi Anusandhan Sansthan (VPKAS), Almora -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/12335
Institution: The VPKAS seed portal lists "VL Sweet Corn 2" under Maize Hybrids -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
Notification: At its 97th Foundation Day (4 July 2020), the Director said the institute had notified "VL Sweetcorn 2" in maize -- https://icar.org.in/en/node/12335
Breeder names: No evidence found. No page named the lead breeder or scientist for this variety. "VL Sweetcorn Hybrid 202" in the same article is a different variety and was not attributed.

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level only; no breeder contact found)
ICAR-VPKAS, Mall Road, Almora-263601, Uttarakhand (India); phone +91-5962-230208 -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/sub-cat-details/3/Maize
Email: No evidence found.
Institute contact page: No evidence found beyond the maize page above.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP report or KrishiKosh record naming VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2 or FSCH 75 was returned. The VL Madhurima (isgpb.org) sweet corn paper and the VL VitA paper are different varieties and were discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
VPKAS seed portal, Maize Hybrids category, lists "VL Sweet Corn 2 / स्वीटकाॅर्न हाईब्रिड 2" (listing only; no price or stock detail in the snippet) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings: No evidence found. The FSCH 75 name returned no seed listing.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Listed on VPKAS seed portal as: Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand (hills), Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya (listing truncated after this point) -- https://vpkas.icar.gov.in/seed-portal/index.php?route=product/category&path=59_93
The request's full list (Mizoram, Nagaland, Sikkim, Tripura) was not confirmed by a search result.

NAME NOTE
"VL Sweet Corn Hybrid-2" and "VL Sweet Corn 2" / "VL Sweetcorn 2" appear to refer to the same variety. No search result contained the Seednet name "FSCH 75 VL Sweet Corn Hybrid 2," so all findings above refer to the CSC-style name.

drought.details: GPMH-1101 appears as a local check in a study of parental lines and hybrids evaluated under rainfed conditions (ResearchGate). A separate morpho-physiological study lists GPMH-1101 among hybrids that increased maize yield in a water-stress context, but the snippet does not report tolerance indices or stress-specific yield data for this variety. No quantitative drought tolerance rating is available in the search results.

heat.details: No GPMH-1101-specific heat stress data found. The ICAR Annual Report 2020 lists heat stress tolerance as a general research theme, but does not link it to this hybrid.

salinity.details: No GPMH-1101-specific salinity data found in the search results.

flood.details: No GPMH-1101-specific flood tolerance data found. Karnataka SDG vision documents mention flood-resistant varieties only as a general strategy.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance data specific to GPMH-1101 were found in the search results. The Karnataka SDG documents and ICAR report name the variety but do not report disease reactions.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance data specific to GPMH-1101 were found. A TNAU meeting report describes resistance to downy mildew and moderate resistance to shoot fly and stem borer, but the snippet does not clearly attribute these traits to GPMH-1101 and may refer to a different entry.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Zone 3, Kharif season, as listed in the Karnataka Legislative Assembly paper. Adaptation is recorded only for Karnataka.

seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Plant growth habit; plant height (range)- Medium, 166-170 cm. 2.	Important morphological features (4-5) of the proposed variety/hybrid which distinguish it from other important commercial varieties under field condition. GSCH-0913 1.	Yellow kernel colour. 2.	High tassel density of spikelets. 3.	Tassel and silk colour is green. 4.	Ear placement-Medium. 5.	Plant height is comparatively more than parents. 6.	Angle between main axes and lateral branches is wide as compared to parents. 7.	Ear length is long as compared to parents. 8.	Ear diameter is medium as  compared to parents.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RECORD CONFLICTS (read first): The input record describes this as a millet with a 2010 release year, but the sources split it into two different hybrids that share the code 86M64. The pearl millet record (MH 1540, notified 7.2.2011, S.O. 283(E)) matches the input's crop, states and parentage-style code. The IIMR maize record (LPCH 3 = IMHP 1540, popcorn, gazette S.O. 3482(E), 7 October 2020) matches the Seednet name and the parentage Dpcl 15-90 x Dpcl 117. Neither matches the 2010-10-10 release date. Evidence for each heading below says which name it refers to. Four searches were used (the maximum), so seed availability got only incidental coverage.

STRESS TOLERANCE
MH 1540 (pearl millet, 86M64): listed as resistant to downy mildew -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
IMHP 1540 (maize): No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance -- searched via https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

DISEASE AND PEST
MH 1540 (pearl millet): downy mildew resistance noted -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
IMHP 1540 (maize): No evidence found for disease or pest resistance -- searched via https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
IMHP 1540 / LPCH 3 (maize): kharif yield 3.5-4.0 t/ha, also suited to rabi, maturity not stated -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
IMHP 1540 / LPCH 3 (maize, secondary blog): kharif yield 3.5-4.0 t/ha; listed for several eastern and northern states -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/exploring-varieties-of-maize-in-india
MH 1540 (pearl millet): late maturing, with conical compact earheads and light grey obovate seeds -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Multi-location trial data for either hybrid: No evidence found in the retrieved AICRP kharif maize 2016 excerpt -- https://aicmip.naarm.org.in/AnnualReports/Maize%20AICRP%20REPORT%20KHARIF%202016.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
IMHP 1540 (maize) parentage: Dpcl 15-90 x Dpcl 117 -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
MH 1540 (pearl millet) parent listing is ambiguous in the table: 86M64 appears alongside "M096F x M" and 117R -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
QTL or marker studies for either hybrid: No evidence found. Maize QTL papers returned by the search used unrelated populations and were not listed.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
IMHP 1540 (maize): developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Maize Research (IIMR), Ludhiana, PAU Campus; no lead breeder name found -- https://iimr.icar.gov.in/?page_id=150
MH 1540 (pearl millet): notified under Pioneer Overseas Corp., Hyderabad; no breeder name found -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Unlinked IIMR scientists (not confirmed as breeders of this hybrid): G. K. Chikkappa, N. Sunil, Vinay Mahajan, Bhupender Kumar -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/node/120825

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: J 1009 / J-1006 (maize, fodder)

Name note: All four searches returned evidence only for "J-1006", the Seednet name. I found nothing that names "J 1009" or the code "PFM 13". I cannot confirm that J 1009 and J-1006 are the same entry. The findings below refer to J-1006 unless stated otherwise. Searches used: 4 (the maximum).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of J-1006 or J 1009 in the four searches. -- No URL with relevant content

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for disease or pest resistance of J-1006 or J 1009. The Krishi Bazaar handbook recommends fodder maize varieties generally and mentions disease resistance only for hybrids, not for J-1006. -- https://krishibazaar.in/blog/maize-cultivation-in-india-a-farmers-handbook

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A Kashmir field trial (2009 and 2010) tested seed rate and nitrogen/zinc on J-1006. It reported that 120 kg N/ha gave the highest green fodder yield, crude protein and plant height. -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4604/4279
- A Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana study tested planting methods and N levels for J-1006 seed yield (zero tillage, conventional tillage, bed planting). -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/Rupinder%20Kaur%20Jassal,%20et%20al.pdf
- A forage-quality trial lists J-1006 alongside other maize types, with green fodder figures. The table units are unclear, so I have not used the numbers. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/forage-quality-of-maize.pdf
- A Kalyani centre variety page lists J-1006 with sowing window May to August, seed rate 50 to 60 kg/ha and spacing 45 x 50 cm. -- https://rsfpdkalyani.com/varietymain.php?id=70&category=Maize+(J-1006)
- The Indiamart listing describes J-1006 as tall (about 7 to 8 feet) with 8 to 11 percent crude protein and a seed rate of 10 to 15 kg/acre. This is seller copy, not trial data. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-maize-j-1006-2856922031312.html

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. No QTL, marker or pedigree data for J-1006 or J 1009 were returned. Parentage is not specified in the input, and no source gave it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist for J 1009 or J-1006.
- The NDDB page lists J-1006 among improved fodder maize varieties, without a developer. -- https://www.nddb.coop/farmer/animal-nutrition/fodder/cereals/maize
- The Kalyani centre page lists J-1006 among its varieties, but does not say it was developed there. -- https://rsfpdkalyani.com/varietymain.php?id=70&category=Maize+(J-1006)
- Institution per input only: ICAR-AICRP on Forage Crops, Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana. Not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone or postal address for PAU's AICRP on Forage Crops appeared in the results. The Kalyani centre page is a different forage centre and I have not treated its details as PAU contacts. Please check the PAU and AICRP Forage Crops websites directly for an institute contact page.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in the source (year not stated). Evaluation of maize cultivars for herbage yield and silage quality, with a J1006 composite silage comparison. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354947120_Maize_Zea_mays_cultivars_evaluation_for_herbage_yield_and_silage_quality
- Jassal, R. K. et al. (2017, from the issue number in the URL). Growth, phenology and seed yield of fodder maize (J-1006) in relation to planting method and nitrogen level. Int. J. Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences (ijcmas) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/Rupinder%20Kaur%20Jassal,%20et%20al.pdf
- Authors not stated in the source (2012, from the page header). Seed rate and nutrient management in fodder maize (var. J-1006). Indian Journal of Agronomy -- https://pub.isa-india.in/index.php/ija/article/download/4604/4279
- Authors not stated in the source (year not stated). Forage quality of maize, with J-1006 yield comparisons. Forage Research -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2013/07/forage-quality-of-maize.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report or DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Amar Seeds Private Limited (Pune, Maharashtra) lists "Fodder Maize J-1006" as in stock, with a note that it is notified for fodder cultivation. This is a private dealer listing, not an NSC, State Seed Corporation or SAU source. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-maize-j-1006-2856922031312.html
- No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sale for J 1009 was found. Seednet listings were not reachable in these searches.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found for Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra or Uttar Pradesh for J 1009 or J-1006. The Indiamart seller says J-1006 is recommended across the country, but this is a commercial claim and does not match the four states in the input. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/fodder-maize-j-1006-2856922031312.html

RELEASE RECORD
The 2024-08-02 release date and the CSC minutes could not be checked. No search result confirmed a 2024 release for J 1009 or PFM 13. The J-1006 evidence points to an older Punjab fodder variety, so the two records may not describe the same variety.
