drought.details: The variety is explicitly stated to be tolerant against drought. It has been studied under varying levels of moisture stress, with research noting its characteristics in relation to chlorophyll and anthocyanin content under such conditions.

heat.details: While the variety is mentioned in documents discussing temperature stress, there is no direct evidence confirming HFO 529's specific level of heat tolerance. Studies on temperature stress in other crops like mustard and flax are noted in the same reports.

salinity.details: HFO 529 is listed among oat varieties tested under salt stress conditions. Oats are generally considered a moderately salt-tolerant crop, and HFO 529 is part of research efforts aimed at developing salt-tolerant varieties.

flood.details: No specific evidence regarding HFO 529's tolerance to flood stress was found. Mentions of water-logging tolerance refer to sugarcane clones in the provided results, not oats.

disease_resistance.summary: HFO 529 is reported to be resistant against Alternaria Leaf Spot and moderately resistant to Helminthosporium leaf blight disease.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety has been studied in contexts related to resistance against insect pests, though specific pests are not detailed for HFO 529.

agronomic_details.yield: HFO 529 recorded a maximum green fodder yield of 397 q/ha and dry matter yield of 79.24 q/ha in the Varietal Trial on IVT Oat (SC) in 2018-19. Earlier trials in 2017-18 reported a dry matter yield of 383 q/ha, where it outyielded other test entries like OS-6. Another report indicates a green fodder yield of 223 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for multiple states (Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Jammu and Kashmir) and tested under varying moisture and salt stress conditions, indicating adaptability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for timely-sown conditions with normal fertility. Adapted for cultivation in Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Jammu and Kashmir.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Found promising for green fodder yield per plant.
agronomic_details.field_trials: HFO 529 has been extensively tested in Varietal Trials on IVT Oat (SC) by Dr. Rajendra Prasad Central Agricultural University, Samastipur, as well as under varying levels of moisture and salt stress conditions by Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University and other institutions.

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to HFO 607. The search returned only general oat or other-variety pages.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to HFO 607. The search returned only general oat or other-variety pages.

salinity.details: In a pot and screenhouse salinity screen at 10 dS/m (Devi, Singh and Goyal, CCS HAU, year not shown), HFO 607 had the lowest dry weight per plant (2.93 g) and the lowest relative water content (51.36%) among the genotypes tested. Maximum dry weight was in HJ-8 (6.20 g), followed by HFO 716 (5.37 g) and HFO 529 (5.30 g). The digest reads this as comparatively poor salt tolerance.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to HFO 607.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The review table lists HFO-607 as a 2019 CCS HAU pedigree release, but the text mentioning powdery mildew, leaf blight, aphid and armyworm resistance is not clearly attached to HFO-607 in the extracted text, so no resistance is attributed to this variety. No variety-specific rust, smut or leaf blight rating for HFO 607 was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Aphid and armyworm resistance mentioned in the review text is not clearly attributed to HFO 607, so none is recorded.

agronomic_details.yield: Release trial average of 615.7 q/ha green fodder across North West Zone locations over three years (input average_yield field gives only the unit Kg/Ha; 615.7 q/ha corresponds to 61,570 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Yield reported as an average across North West Zone locations over three years. No further stability analysis (e.g., per-environment or GxE data) was found in the searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released and notified for timely-sown, normal-fertility, irrigated conditions in the North West Zone of India, including Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, the Terai region of Uttarakhand and Western Uttar Pradesh.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Not found in searched sources. No maturity or sowing-date data specific to HFO 607 were found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Described as a single-cut oat variety (AICRP on Forage Crops listing, 2019-20). Parentage and breeding method are recorded under genetics. The general single-cut oat recommendation of a first cut at about 50-55 days is a crop-level recommendation, not a HFO 607 trial result. Morphological characteristics: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Release trial in North West Zone: 615.7 q/ha green fodder, 11.9% higher than national check Kent and 17.4% higher than national check OS 6. (2) Same NWZ trials: 8.8% higher green fodder yield than zonal check OL 125. (3) ICAR-NDRI Karnal, rabi 2021-22: HFO-607 evaluated under single cuts at 45, 55 and 65 days after sowing and no cut; yield results were not extracted. (4) Salinity screen at 10 dS/m (pot and screenhouse, CCS HAU): lowest dry weight per plant (2.93 g) among genotypes tested; see stress_tolerance.salinity.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
HFO 607 (fodder oat). Variety name in CSC minutes and Seednet name are both "HFO 607", so the evidence below applies to both headings.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Salinity screen (pot and screenhouse, 10 dS/m): HFO 607 had the lowest dry weight per plant (2.93 g) and the lowest relative water content (51.36%) among the genotypes tested, which points to comparatively poor salt tolerance. Source is a study by Devi, Singh and Goyal of CCS HAU, year not shown. Maximum dry weight (g) plant-1 was noticed in HJ-8 (6.20) followed by HFO 716 (5.37), HFO 529 (5.30) and minimum in HFO 607 (2.93) at 10 dS m-1 of salinity. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394327520_Effect_of_Salinity_on_Six_Genotypes_of_Avena_Sativa_during_Germination_and_Seedling_Growth
- No evidence found for drought, heat, flood or submergence tolerance specific to HFO 607. The search returned only general oat or other-variety pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The review table lists HFO-607 as a 2019 CCS HAU pedigree release, but the text in the snippet that mentions powdery mildew, leaf blight, aphid and armyworm resistance is not clearly attached to HFO-607 in the extracted text. I have not attributed any resistance to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
- No variety-specific rust, smut or leaf blight rating for HFO 607 was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Release trial yield: average green fodder of 615.7 q/ha across North West Zone locations over three years. This variety gave 615.7 q/ha green fodder yield in North West Zone which was 11.9% and 17.4 % higher than the national checks Kent and OS 6, respectively. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- The same article reports 8.8% higher green fodder yield than the zonal check OL 125 in NWZ trials. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- AICRP on Forage Crops technology listing of HFO 607 as a single-cut variety, 2019-20, from CCS HAU Hisar, with a recommended area. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382887644_Fodder_Crops_Technologies_A_Five_Years_2019-2023_Journey_of_AICRP_on_Forage_Crops_and_Utilization
- A field experiment at ICAR-NDRI Karnal (rabi 2021-22) evaluated HFO-607 under single cuts at 45, 55 and 65 days after sowing and no cut. Reported yield results were not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230132091_Prediction_of_fibre_components_in_oat_hulls_by_near_infrared_reflectance_spectroscopy
- Single-cut oat varieties generally: first cut at about 50–55 days. This is a general crop-level recommendation, not a HFO 607 trial result. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
- Maturity and sowing-date data specific to HFO 607: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from a review table, not from the release article): HJ-8 × UPO-04-1, developed by pedigree method, 2019, CCS HAU Hisar. This conflicts with the input field "Not specified", so it is recorded as a secondary-source finding. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/365785271_Health_benefits_of_oat_Avena_sativa_and_nutritional_improvement_through_plant_breeding_interventions
- Breeding method: pedigree method. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- QTL or marker studies for HFO 607: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing team: Forage Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar. Named authors of the release article: D. S. Phogat, Yogesh Jindal, Minakshi Jattan, Naveen Kumar, Dalvinder Pal Singh, Jayanti Tokas. The individual lead breeder is not explicitly designated. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar-125 004 (Haryana). -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Institution-level description (CCS HAU, Hisar): Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University is one of the biggest Agricultural University in Asia, established on February 2, 1970 and located at Hisar in the Indian state of Haryana. -- https://hau.ac.in/storage/app/uploads/VG6dQAaSUuipIFlVp92JI4OWkBCKQz7JZcEuxqgg.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Corresponding-author e-mail printed in the release article for the Forage Section team: jattanmina@gmail.com (Minakshi Jattan, listed as corresponding author). This is a personal address shown in the paper, not a verified official institute address. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Postal address (institute-level, from the release article): Forage Section, Department of Genetics & Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar-125 004 (Haryana), India. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Institute phone and official email: No evidence found in the search results. An institute contact page URL was not retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Phogat, D. S., Jindal, Y., Jattan, M., Kumar, N., Singh, D. P., Tokas, J. (year not shown; received 15 March 2021). HFO 607: A new single-cut oat variety for North West Zone of India. Forage Research -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- Dwivedi, R., Meena, V. K., Sharma, D., Singh, M., Chand, S. (2025). Oats (Avena sativa): A potential winter fodder crop for better livestock production. Indian Farming, September 2025 issue. Lists HFO 607 in its table of recent fodder oat varieties -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
- Chand, S., et al. (2025). Analyzing trends and future projections in fodder oats (Avena sativa L.) for quality seed production in India. Frontiers in Plant Science. DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422. The variety-level text for HFO 607 was not visible in the retrieved extract, so this is recorded as a source only, not as HFO 607 evidence. -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422
- Devi, S., Singh, S., Goyal, V. (year not shown). Responses of oat (Avena sativa L.) genotypes under salt stress. Journal not identified in the extract. Contains the HFO 607 salinity data above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394327520_Effect_of_Salinity_on_Six_Genotypes_of_Avena_Sativa_during_Germination_and_Seedling_Growth
- Field trial at ICAR-NDRI Karnal (rabi 2021-22), HFO-607 among four oat varieties. Authors, year and journal not extracted. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230132091_Prediction_of_fibre_components_in_oat_hulls_by_near_infrared_reflectance_spectroscopy
- KrishiKosh thesis search: not run, as the four allowed searches were used.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found for HFO 607 seed. The searches returned general sources only: CCS HAU RDS Seed Farm sale counters for oat (no variety named) -- https://hau.ac.in/page/seed-sale-information ; Haryana certified oat seed statistics naming other varieties (HJ-8, OS-6, OS-377, OL-10, Kent) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368786506_STATUS_OF_CERTIFIED_SEED_PRODUCTION_OF_FORAGE_CROPS_IN_HARYANA ; a private hybrid oat seed trader in Hisar -- https://www.indiamart.com/evergreenseedco/oat-seeds.html. None of these names HFO 607, so none is recorded as evidence for it.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Released and notified for timely-sown, normal-fertility, irrigated conditions in the North West Zone: Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Terai region of Uttarakhand and Western Uttar Pradesh. -- https://forageresearch.in/hfo-607-a-new-single-cut-oat-variety-for-north-west-zone-of-india/
- The review table gives the same adoption area. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308
- Release-date discrepancy: input says 2020-11-09. Sources give identification 2019 (review table) and AICRP entry 2019-20. The notification date should be confirmed against the CSC minutes or the Gazette.

The ICAR Indian Farming article lists CCS HAU Hisar among the major oat breeding institutions, and it lists HFO 707 as a CCS HAU, Hisar release -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/166826/64546/507308

Institution: Chaudhary Charan Singh Haryana Agricultural University; address as listed: "CCS HAU NEAR MADUBAN PARK HISAR"; Pincode 125001; website http://www.hau.ernet.in -- https://hisar.gov.in/public-utility/chaudhary-charan-singh-haryana-agricultural-university/
Email: not found. Phone: not found. Divisional contact (Forage Section, Dept. of Genetics and Plant Breeding): not found for HFO 707. The email jattanmina@gmail.com appears only on the HFO 607 paper, so it was excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for HFO 707 at NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for JHO-2009-1 / JHO 2009-1 / Bundel Jai-2009-1 returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-025-00106-6 (returned for the name search, but no stress data for this variety)

DISEASE AND PEST
Unattributed: an IGFRI forage variety table lists "Tolerant to root rot, crown rust, leaf blight and powdery mildew" for one oat variety. The row sits between the Bundel Jai-822/851 section and the Bundel Jai-2004 section, and the page does not make clear which variety it belongs to, so it is not attributed to JHO-2009-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
No evidence found for this variety's pest or disease reaction. The pest-resistance page returned is about Bundel Jai 991 (JHO 991), a different variety. -- https://www.merikheti.com/en/blog/oats-cultivation-in-india-its-varieties-and-health-benefits (discarded for relevance)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
JHO-2009-1 was one of eight ICAR-IGFRI oat varieties (JHO-822, JHO-851, JHO-99-1, JHO-99-2, JHO-2000-4, JHO-2010-1, JHO-2009-1, JHO-2012-2) compared for forage and grain yield, milling recovery, nutrition and grain physical properties; green fodder yield across the set ranged from 34.5 to 57.3 t/ha. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277746468_Oat_Production_in_North_Dakota (page title is unrelated to oats in India; the text itself names ICAR-IGFRI and JHO-2009-1)
In that study JHO-2009-1 was judged the best dual-purpose variety on green fodder yield, seed yield and early maturity. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277746468_Oat_Production_in_North_Dakota
In a separate ranking, JHO-2009-1 was listed among the top-yielding varieties for green fodder, at 550 to 600 q/ha, behind HJ-8 (600 to 680 q/ha). -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422/full (same data in https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/)
Quality trial (semi-arid India): JHO-2009-1 had higher palmitic acid (about 21%) and stearic acid (about 3.97%), and the authors describe its quality as poor because of high saturated fatty acid content (about 25.42%). -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-025-00106-6
Maturity: no days-to-flowering or days-to-maturity figure was found for JHO-2009-1 specifically. Early maturity is noted only in the comparison above.
Release and notification: no evidence found for a 2016-08-12 release date or any CSC/CVRC notification number for JHO-2009-1. The IGFRI forage variety table has a notification entry for a different variety (CVRC No. 1572 dated 20.09.2006), and its variety-to-row alignment is unclear, so it is not attributed. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: individual plant selection from exotic collection EC 498707, per the IGFRI variety table (this conflicts with the "Not specified" parentage field in the record). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
Breeding method: the same table names mass selection as the method used, though the text is garbled in the source. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
QTL or marker studies: No evidence found for this variety. The marker-assisted breeding review returned covers oat generally and does not name JHO-2009-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/397086699_Accelerated_Breeding_Approaches_for_Improved_Productivity_and_Quality_in_Dual-Purpose_Oats (discarded for relevance)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: ICAR-Indian Grassland and Fodder Research Institute (IGFRI), Jhansi, UP. The IGFRI variety table lists JHO-2009-1 as "Bundel Jai-2009-1 (JHO-2009-1)" under the oat section. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/323305621_Improved_Forage_Crop_Varieties_of_IGFRI
Breeder names: No evidence found. A 2020 AICRP database lists breeder names (R.K. Jain, R.P. Nagar, Jiban Mitra, U.P. Singh, S. Natrajan, G.P. Shukla), but the listing is not tied to this variety on the page, so these names are not attributed to JHO-2009-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020
Name conflict (seednet name JHO 2015-1): the evidence refers to a different variety. JHO-2015-1 is described as a derivative of UPO 90 × IGO2-70, released as Bundel Jai-2015-1 in 2018 for irrigated, timely-sown tropical and subtropical conditions. It is not this variety. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/932 (discarded for relevance; shown only to document the name conflict)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: JO 03-91 (variety_name, CSC minutes) / JO-03-91 (SC) (seednet_variety_name), oat (Avena sativa)**

Naming: The sources spell it "JO 03-91", "JO-03-91" and "JO-03-91" with a hyphen. All of them are read as the same variety. The Seednet portal search (seednet.gov.in) returned only unrelated Seednet companies in Australia and Taiwan, so no evidence under the seednet_variety_name was found. Searches returned no evidence for JO-03-93, JO-01, JO 05-304 or other varieties, which were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. Searches for these traits returned no JO 03-91 results. -- (searched in the variety and research queries; no matching page)

DISEASE AND PEST
- The JO 03-91 entry, notified in 2010 from the cross OS 6 x JHO 822, is listed with JNKVV and as tolerant to leaf blight. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/67533/28817/169501
- No evidence found for rust, smut, insect or nematode resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Central Gujarat fodder trial: JO-03-91 recorded 39.65 t/ha green fodder, 9.01 t/ha dry matter, 1.18 t/ha crude protein and 23.15% dry mat

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JWGO-01 (Jawahar Wellington Grain Oats-01) (V8), oats

Name check: The CSC release name "JWGO-01 (Jawahar Wellington Grain Oats-01)" appears in the release listings below. The Seednet name "JWGO-01 (Jawahar Wellington Grain Oats-01) (V8)" and code "V8" appear in those same listings. I found no Seednet portal page of its own, so no Seednet-portal evidence is cited. Four searches were run in total.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No oat-specific evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only related note is a 2023 IARI annual report passage on rust resistance, but it describes a wheat variety, so I have not attributed it to JWGO-01. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No oat-specific evidence found for disease or pest resistance. The IARI 2023 annual report passage on rust resistance is wheat-specific and is excluded here. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No maturity, yield or trial data for JWGO-01 found in the search results. The Jabalpur (JNKVV) report says two oat varieties were tested for three years across agro-climatic zones, but it does not name JWGO-01, so the link is unconfirmed. -- https://eastmojo.com/national/2022/01/16/mp-agri-varsity-develops-new-varieties-of-oats-wheat-rice/
Release type: 88 · Oats · Open Pollinated Variety · JWGO-01 (Jawahar Wellington Grain Oats-01) (V8) · Madhya Pradesh -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-106-new-varieties-of-31-major-crops-for-farmers/

GENETICS AND QTL
No parentage, marker or QTL evidence found. Parentage remains "Not specified" in the record. -- No evidence found (searched: release, breeder, research and seed queries)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed and released as the first grain oat variety in India, notified for Madhya Pradesh under timely sown irrigated conditions. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf
The developing centre is the ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Wellington (Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu). The station was set up in 1954 under the ICAR wheat rust scheme. -- https://www.iari.res.in/en/introduction.php?div_id=34
An ICAR-IARI Wellington call for a Senior Research Fellow names a CRP project on high-yielding, nutrient-rich oat varieties for value addition. This is the oat breeding programme context. -- https://ekalvi.com/senior-research-fellowsrf/
The JNKVV Jabalpur co-developer role is reported but not tied to JWGO-01 by name. -- https://eastmojo.com/national/2022/01/16/mp-agri-varsity-develops-new-varieties-of-oats-wheat-rice/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only (no breeder contact found):
ICAR-IARI Regional Station, Wellington, 643 231, The Nilgiris, Tamil Nadu -- https://www.helpbiotech.co.in/2020/01/iari-wellington-technical-assistant.html
ICAR-IARI headquarters: Director Dr. Ashok Kumar Singh; postal address Pusa Campus, New Delhi 110012; email director@iari.res.in; phone +91-11-25842367 (fax +91-11-2584642) -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-12/ICAR-INSTITUTE-PROFILE_.pdf
Regional Station Wellington direct email, phone or breeder email: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No peer-reviewed or institutional publication specific to JWGO-01 found in the search results.
Context only (not about JWGO-01): Chand, S. et al. (2025). Analyzing trends and future projections in fodder oats (Avena sativa L.) for quality seed production in India. Frontiers in Plant Science -- https://doi.org/10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422
Context only: Authors not shown in results (2025). Comparative evaluation of quantitative and qualitative attributes of oat (Avena sativa L.) varieties grown in semi-arid India. Springer -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s44372-025-00106-6
Annual report: ICAR-IARI (2023). Annual Report 2023. ICAR-IARI -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/Annual_English_2023_15072024.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
No JWGO-01 seed source (NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer) found. The Seednet portal page for this variety was not in the results. -- No evidence found
General seed chain context (state corporations, departmental outlets, cooperatives and private dealers): https://seednet.gov.in/Material/IndianSeedSector.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
Madhya Pradesh only. Notified for sale in Madhya Pradesh. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-23-new-varieties-of-13-crops-for-madhya-pradesh-farmers/
Notified by the Government of India after Central Seed Committee consultation, with the notification issued on 25 September 2023 by the Joint Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/india-region/indian-government-released-23-new-varieties-of-13-crops-for-madhya-pradesh-farmers/
Hindi report of the same notification, dated 1 November 2023 (open-pollinated, sale in Madhya Pradesh). -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/oat-variety-jwgo-01-jawahar-wellington-grain-oats-01-v8/

DATA DISCREPANCY
The release year in the record (2023-05-02) differs from the notification date found (25 September 2023). Please check the CSC minutes before finalising.

drought.details: No search result mentions OL-1931. General oat literature describes drought mechanisms (photosynthetic carbon assimilation genes, the transcription factor AsHSFA2c that balances drought tolerance and growth, SPL13 under miR156 regulation, and root architecture traits). None of these are linked to this variety, so no variety-specific rating can be given.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat data were found. A general oat study notes a possible protective gene and markers on chromosome 6B under heat stress, but it is not linked to OL-1931.

salinity.details: No data on OL-1931. Studies on other oat genotypes (the salt-alkali resistant 'Qinqiong', the naked oat line Bayou1, and a screen of 11 cultivated and 9 wild Avena species) show genotypic variation in salt tolerance. This cannot be attributed to OL-1931.

flood.details: No variety-specific data. A review states that few or no published data exist on waterlogging tolerance of oat varieties, though oats are considered more tolerant than some other cereals.

drought.details: No search result mentions OL-1949. Its drought reaction is therefore unknown. General oat literature covers drought screening and physiology (morpho-physiological traits under water withholding, root architecture, AsHSFA2c co-expression network balancing drought tolerance and growth, drought-perturbed genes), but none of it can be attributed to this variety.

heat.details: No variety-specific heat data were found. A Frontiers paper on spike fertility notes a possible protective gene role in oat during heat stress, which is general and not variety-specific.

salinity.details: No data on OL-1949. General sources state that oats are nearly as salt tolerant as barley, with cultivar differences, and that wild and cultivated Avena genotypes differ in salinity response.

flood.details: No data on OL-1949. A review notes that few or no published data exist on waterlogging tolerance of oat varieties, though oats are considered more waterlogging tolerant than wheat and barley.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to Helminthosporium (leaf blight) is reported for OL 1874-1. A separate ICAR Annual Report 2022-23 entry describes OL 1874-1 as resistant to powdery mildew. The ICAR entry is a brief table excerpt and its context could not be confirmed, so it is treated as single-source evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest-resistance data for OL 1874-1 were found in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.yield: The ANRCM 2022 abstract reports that OL-1874-1 gave the highest herbage yield among the oat entries tested, at 448.9 q (unit as printed in the abstract, presumably q/ha). Trial location and season are not clear from the excerpt.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis was found in the provided search results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The ICAR Annual Report 2022-23 lists OL 1874-1 with the states Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka and describes it as suitable for irrigated, rabi-season, single-cut use. This conflicts with the ground-truth recommended states (Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, Terai Uttarakhand), so the ICAR entry should be verified before use. The ICAR entry is a table excerpt and may refer to a different variety or context.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: The Sabour Sampanna Dhan publication excerpt states that the crop is ready for fodder cutting 128 days after sowing. The excerpt does not clearly attribute this to OL 1874-1, so it is treated as indicative only.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: OL 1874-1 is described as a single-cut oat (Avena sativa L.) variety. Other morphological traits were not found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: A 2022 ANRCM abstract reports OL-1874-1 among ten promising oat entries, with the highest herbage yield noted. A 2025 study of 30 fodder oat genotypes at the Regional Agricultural Research Station grouped OL-1874-1 into Cluster I with other genotypes based on multivariate analysis.

seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Timely sown, normal fertility and irrigated conditions in the Central zone, suitable for single cut system.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for single cut system, In agronomic trials, the proposed variety OS 377 (522.1 q/ha) showed its superiority for GFY over both the national checks, OS 6 (471.7 q/ha) and Kent (476.9 q/ha) as well as to the zonal check JHO 822 (479.6) whereas, for DMY it was statistically at par (84.1 q/ha) with the national checks Kent (86.3 q/ha) and OS 6 (85.7 q/ha) and the zonal check, JHO 822 (85.5 q/ha). The variety responded significantly up to 120 kg N/ha for GFY at Jabalpur and for DMY at Jhansi. At Jhansi location the highest GFY (688.7 q/ha) and DMY (98.5 q/ha) was recorded by the proposed variety OS 377.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: High number of leaves, tall and high number of tillers
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The proposed variety is moderately resistant to Heliminthosporium leaf blight.

agronomic_details.stability: The CSC record states the variety responded significantly up to 120 kg N/ha for green fodder yield at Jabalpur and for dry matter yield at Jhansi. Stability across environments beyond these locations was not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Timely sown, normal fertility and irrigated conditions in the Central zone; suitable for single-cut system (CSC record). The release article describes it as a single-cut forage oat for the central zone of India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Tall, single-cut forage oat with a leaf:stem ratio of 0.65 and bold seed. Parentage per CSC record is HJ 8 x Kent, but the release article does not give the cross parents, so this parentage is unverified. Heterosis studies used OS-377 as a female parent in crosses OS-377 x JHO-851 and OS-377 x PLP-1, which were flagged for earliness, seed yield, fodder yield and plant height.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Release-article agronomic trials: OS-377 gave 522.1 q/ha green fodder yield, superior to national checks OS 6 (471.7 q/ha) and Kent (476.9 q/ha) and zonal check JHO 822 (479.6 q/ha). For dry matter yield, OS-377 (84.1 q/ha) was statistically at par with Kent (86.3 q/ha), OS 6 (85.7 q/ha) and JHO 822 (85.5 q/ha). CSC record (no URL): at Jhansi, OS-377 recorded the highest green fodder yield (688.7 q/ha) and dry matter yield (98.5 q/ha). Heterosis evaluation flagged OS-377 x JHO-851 and OS-377 x PLP-1 for earliness, seed yield, fodder yield and plant height.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found. Searches for OS-377 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance returned only unrelated oat trials (Iowa, Kansas, South Dakota, Georgia, Texas, Minnesota) and other oat cultivars. -- https://practicalfarmers.org/research/oat-variety-trial-2025/ ; https://extension.k-state.edu/historicpublications/pubs/SRP806.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- An agronomy article lists OS-377 among newer releases for specific agroecological zones and says it has improved disease resistance. It names no pathogen, resistance rating or test. This is a secondary source. -- https://agriculture.institute/agriculture-fundamentals/growing-oats-essential-tips-fodder/
- No evidence found for a specific rust, smut or blight reaction of OS-377 in a field or screening trial. -- (searched; see the URLs above)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- OS-377 is described as a tall, single-cut forage oat with a leaf:stem ratio of 0.65 and bold seed, suited to single-cut use. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/242-245.pdf
- In agronomic trials OS-377 gave a green fodder yield of 522.1 q/ha and was reported as superior to the check cultivars. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/242-245.pdf
- The Haryana forage seed-chain report keeps OS-377 among five oat varieties in certified seed production. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368786506_STATUS_OF_CERTIFIED_SEED_PRODUCTION_OF_FORAGE_CROPS_IN_HARYANA
- Breeder-seed allocation and production figures for OS-377 (CCS HAU Hisar) are tabulated; production of 71.0 q against an allocation of 41.2 q. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/
- Heterosis and hybrid evaluation: OS-377 was used as a female parent, and the crosses OS-377 x JHO-851 and OS-377 x PLP-1 were flagged for earliness, seed yield, fodder yield and plant height. -- https://hjar.org/index.php/hjar/article/download/172540/116692 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/381550724_Heterosis_for_fodder_and_seed_yield_traits_in_common_oat_Avena_sativa_L

GENETICS AND QTL
- The release article states OS-377 was produced by pedigree selection from a cross. The cross parents are not given in the retrieved text, so the user-supplied parentage "HJ 8 x Kent" is unverified. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/242-245.pdf
- The release article reports registration of the variety with NBPGR under an IC accession number (599579). -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/242-245.pdf
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies of OS-377.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "OS-377", so one name was searched. No Seednet portal page was retrieved; the Seednet entry and variety code A0609031 are unverified.
- OS-377 was developed at the Forage Research Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, under AICRP (Forage Crops & Utilization). -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/242-245.pdf
- Authors of the release article: Yogesh Jindal, R. N. Arora, D. S. Phogat, S. K. Pahuja, L. K. Midha, S. K. Gandhi and U. N. Joshi. The article does not label each as breeder; Jindal is the Forage Section scientist listed in the department contact sheet. -- https://forageresearch.in/wp-content/uploads/2016/05/242-245.pdf ; https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1689650060.pdf
- Institute context: CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, lists OS 377 among its released oat varieties (Forage Section, Dept. of G&PB). -- https://hau.ac.in/public/pages-pdf/1552632509.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 (variety_code SKO-108; Seednet name "Shalimar Fodder Oats-3")

Search summary: I ran four web searches covering the variety, breeders, research papers and seed sources. None of the results mention "Shalimar Fodder Oat-4" or SKO-108 directly. The name "Shalimar Fodder Oats-3" appears only in a variety table, where it is tied to code SKO-96, not SKO-108. Findings below are therefore either about the Seednet name, a different SKUAST oat variety, or the wider fodder-oat context. Each heading says which.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3. -- searched across all four queries
- A SKUAST-K forage oat released nationally under the name Shalimar Fodder Oats-7 (a different variety) is described as showing response to high doses of inputs and resistant reaction to various diseases and pests. This does not apply to SKO-108 or the Seednet name. -- https://kashmirreader.com/2023/10/06/skuast-ks-high-yielding-quality-enhanced-forage-oats-variety-released-at-national-level/

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3.
- A different SKUAST variety, SKO-7 (released 2005), is listed as resistant to Downy mildew and Crown rust diseases and to aphids and Armyworm, dual type. This is not the variety in question. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for yield or maturity of Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3.
- A SKUAST Shalimar field trial from 1995–96 found that maximum green and dry fodder was recorded with two cuts (one each in autumn and spring). The trial used unnamed oat material, so it does not identify the variety. -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF03543594
- National context: The green and dry fodder productivity and seed yield range from 50 to 60, 12 to 15, and 2–3 t/ha, respectively. These figures cover fodder oats generally, not this variety. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/ (DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422)

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found for parentage, marker or QTL studies of Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3. The parentage field is "Not specified", and no source fills it.
- Broad context: analysis reveals a narrow genetic base at the varietal level, with a few old and popular varieties (Kent, OS-6, and OS-7) sharing > 70% of the genome in varietal development. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12009856/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Shalimar Fodder Oats-3 (SKO-96) is listed in the Frontiers table of Indian fodder oat varieties without breeder names. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/
- The variety most closely linked to SKUAST's fodder-oat programme in the results is Shalimar Fodder Oats-7, which was developed under AICRP on Forages operational at Dryland Agriculture Research Station, Rangreth (A constituent unit of SKUAST-K). The named scientists are Dr. N. S. Khuroo (Professor/OIC, AICRP-FCU Srinagar Centre) as Principal Breeder, Dr. Z. A. Dar (Professor GPB), Dr. GulZaffar (Professor-retd) as Co-Breeders and Dr. Zahida Rashid, Dr. Syed Ansar-ul-Haq. This is a different variety, and no breeder is recorded for SKO-108 or Shalimar Fodder Oat-4. -- https://kashmirreader.com/2023/10/06/skuast-ks-high-yielding-quality-enhanced-forage-oats-variety-released-at-national-level/
- The Seednet-related SKO-96 entry is not linked to a breeder in the results. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or direct contact found for Shalimar Fodder Oat-4, SKO-108 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3.
- Institute-level address found for SKUAST-Kashmir: University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology of Kashmir, Shalimar, Srinagar -190 025. Source: https://skuastkashmir.ac.in/frmPDF.aspx?FN=April+2026+06-04-2026.pdf
- Address for the Division of Genetics and Plant Breeding, SKUAST-K, Shalimar: P.O. Box 706 GPO, Srinagar Jammu and Kashmir, India, 190 001. Source: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF03543594 (this is the Division of Agronomy address from a 2000 paper, so confirm it is current before use).
- No official email or phone for SKUAST-K was found in the results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Chand, S., Kumar, S., Roy, A. K., et al. (2025). Analyzing trends and future projections in fodder oats (Avena sativa L.) for quality seed production in India. Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2025.1525422; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12009856/ (covers the seed chain and variety list, including Shalimar Fodder Oat-3 as SKO-96)
- Hasan, B. & Shah, W. A. (2000). Biomass, Grain Production and Quality of Oats (Avena sativa) Under Different Cutting Regimes and Nitrogen Levels. Journal (Springer, vol. 28, pp. 203–210) -- DOI 10.1007/BF03543594; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF03543594 (SKUAST Shalimar field trial; does not name the variety)
- Ahmad, M., Gul-Zaffar, Dar, Z. A. & Habib, M. (2014). A review on Oat (Avena sativa L.) as a dual-purpose crop. Vol. 9(4), pp. 52–59 -- DOI 10.5897/SRE2014.5820; https://www.academicjournals.org/app/webroot/article/article1393509309_Ahmad%20et%20al.pdf (review by SKUAST-K authors; journal name not stated in the retrieved text)
- Khuroo, N. S. et al. (2023). Shalimar Fodder Oats-7 release (news report, not a peer-reviewed paper). -- https://kashmirreader.com/2023/10/06/skuast-ks-high-yielding-quality-enhanced-forage-oats-variety-released-at-national-level/
- KrishiKosh: no thesis or report on Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3 was found. The KrishiKosh hit was an unrelated Navsari oat seed-production thesis. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/39dd8110-92e7-4a86-9f7b-9f779dcbccda/content

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No direct seed-sale listing for Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or Shalimar Fodder Oats-3 was found.
- KVK Bandipora distributed seed of Shalimar Fodder Oats: 20 quintals of Shalimar Fodder Oats seed were distributed among tribal farmers. The variety in that distribution is not named. -- https://thekashmirhorizon.com/2024/11/30/skuast-k-organises-training-seed-distribution-progat-kvk-bpora/
- SKUAST-K signed an MoU for large-scale fodder seed production with a private firm, expected to produce 5000q seed of oats after two cycles of multiplication. This refers to the newer variety, not SKO-108. -- https://kashmirreader.com/2023/10/06/skuast-ks-high-yielding-quality-enhanced-forage-oats-variety-released-at-national-level/
- Suggested next checks (not searched): SKUAST-K Seed Unit, NSP Shalimar, and the Seednet portal entry for "Shalimar Fodder Oats-3".

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found that Shalimar Fodder Oat-4 or SKO-108 was recommended for Jammu and Kashmir or any other state. The recommended_states_raw entry is unverified.
- The newer SKUAST forage oat (Shalimar Fodder Oats-7) is suitable for cultivation in J&K, HP, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab. This refers to a different variety. -- https://kashmirreader.com/2023/10/06/skuast-ks-high-yielding-quality-enhanced-forage-oats-variety-released-at-national-level/

RELEASE AND NAME RECONCILIATION (not a listed heading, but needed)
- Year of release (2014-02-14): no evidence found. The variety table in the Frontiers paper lists the Shalimar Fodder Oat-3 entry (SKO-96) without a release year in the retrieved text.
- Name check: the Seednet name "Shalimar Fodder Oats-3" maps to SKO-96 in the Frontiers table, not SKO-108. The variety_code in the record may therefore be wrong, or the record may refer to a different entry. Verify on seednet.gov.in before using this record.

The page lists them as article authors; it does not confirm them as the breeders of this variety -- https://dogr.icar.gov.in/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=375:high-yielding-onion-variety-bhima-light-red-a-success-story&catid=2:abt1&lang=en

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: National Research Centre for Onion and Garlic, Rajgurunagar, Pune-410 505
seednet_fields.Resemblence to Variety: Dark red colour and duration resembles with Baswant 780, A.Kalyan and N-53.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in Kharif season in the State of Haryana, Delhi, Rajasthan and Gujarat.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Erect Plant habit, less pseudostem length, minimum neck thickness of the bulb, uniform neck fall during Rabi, early in maturity.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: - Number of leaves: 8-12/plant, - Polar Diameter (P): 42-45 cm, - Equatorial Diameter (E): 45-50 cm, - P.E.: 0.85-0.95, - Neck thickness: 0.6-0.8cm, - % Total solube solids: 10-10.5, - Days to havest after transplanting: 100-105 days in Kharif and 115-120 day in Rabi, - CHaracters different from those of the parents: Bulbs oval in shape and single centred.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 45-50 cm, b) Distinguishing morphological characters: Dark red coloured bulbs, stripes on bulb, oval shape, very less number of bolters and doubles in Rabi, thin neck, number of leaves ranged from 8-12, TSS 10-10.5%.

disease_resistance.summary: Described as moderately tolerant to diseases in the DOGR variety listing; specific diseases are not named. ICAR release notice reports less than 5 percent doubles and bolters (a bolting-related trait, not a disease resistance). A research preprint's comment that white bulbs such as Bhima Safed are more prone to pest and storage losses is a general comment without Bhima Safed trial data and is not treated as resistance evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately tolerant to thrips per the DOGR variety listing. The preprint note on higher pest and storage losses in white bulbs is general and not specific to Bhima Safed trial data.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC data: 25000.00 to 30000.00 Kg/Ha. ICAR release notice: average multi-location yield 185 q/ha (18.5 t/ha) in recommended zones. Secondary page (asiafarming): mean yield about 19 t/ha in recommended zones. Kharif preprint: marketable yield 19.96 t/ha and total yield 26.22 t/ha, the lowest total yield in a nine-variety set. These values differ across sources and were not reconciled.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Bhima Safed is described as moderately tolerant to thrips and diseases, but no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety were found. -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Bolting is reported as under 5 percent, and the ICAR release notice says the line has less than 5 percent doubles and bolters. -- https://icar.org.in/node/7564
The searched ICAR-DOGR page on excess-water tolerance names Phule Safed, Palampur, Bhima Shweta and other lines, not Bhima Safed, so it was discarded. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately tolerant to thrips and diseases (DOGR variety listing; see Stress Tolerance). -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
A research preprint notes that white bulbs such as Bhima Safed are more prone to pest and storage losses than red types, as a general comment without Bhima Safed trial data. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-7103859/v1

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Released from the white line NRCWO-3; medium maturing at 110-120 days, white round to oval bulbs of 70-80 g, 11-12 percent TSS, suitable for table and processing; average multi-location yield 185 q/ha in recommended zones. -- https://icar.org.in/node/7564
Same ICAR-DOGR release figures repeated on a secondary page (mean yield about 19 t/ha in recommended zones). -- https://www.asiafarming.com/hybrid-high-yield-onions-varieties-in-india-for-rabi-kharif-late-and-early-kharif
Kharif comparison of nine varieties: Bhima Safed had marketable yield 19.96 t/ha and total yield 26.22 t/ha, the lowest total yield in the set; polar diameter 3.91 cm; days to harvest 95.83; TSS 13.18 percent (preprint, not peer reviewed). -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-7103859/v1
Bulb traits from the same preprint: attractive whitish globe bulbs, medium neck, semi-erect foliage, single-centred bulbs. -- https://www.researchsquare.com/article/rs-7103859/v1
Bulb morphology on the DOGR listing: attractive white, globe-shaped, medium neck, flat root disc, single axis, non-splitting. -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Bulb storage on the DOGR listing: kharif harvest stores 30-45 days and late kharif up to 3 months (listed under the onion page; see Publications for scope). -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Bhima Safed is listed among improved onion varieties released after 1986 in a GAP manual. -- https://www.manage.gov.in/publications/eBooks/Good%20Agricultural%20Practices%20in%20Onion%20and%20Garlic.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL or marker study for Bhima Safed was found.
Origin: a compendium table attributes Bhima Safed to selection of a white segregating bulb from the red variety Bhima Super, followed by mass selection of white populations for kharif (Mahajan et al. 2019). -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ashwini-Benke/publication/335690512_Compendium_for_Recent_Research_Strategies_in_Onion_and_Garlic_ICAR-Directorate_of_Onion_and_Garlic_Research_Rajgurunagar-410505_Pune_MS/links/5d75f48aa6fdcc9961ba597c/Compendium-for-Recent-Research-Strategies-in-Onion-and-Garlic-ICAR-Directorate-of-Onion-and-Garlic-Research-Rajgurunagar-410505-Pune-MS.pdf
Parentage field "--" is therefore not formally confirmed; the origin above is from a training compendium table only.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR), Rajgurunagar, Pune, Maharashtra, which developed and released the line NRCWO-3 as Bhima Safed. -- https://icar.org.in/node/7564
DOGR lists Bhima Safed among its ten onion varieties developed through genetic improvement in its review period. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name: No named breeder for Bhima Safed was found in the sources; the ICAR release notice and DOGR listing name the institute only.
Mahajan et al. 2019 is named only as the author of the selection step in a compendium table (see Genetics); this is not a confirmed breeder attribution.

CONTACT DETAILS
DOGR institute contact page: ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research, Chandoli, Tal. Khed, Dist. Pune (Maharashtra)-410 505. Phone: 02135-222026, 02135-222697, 02135-224056. Email: director[dot]dogr[at]icar[dot]org[dot]in (as printed). -- https://www.dogr.res.in/index.php/research/varieties-developed?layout=edit
Institute directory (ASTI): Rajgurunagar, Pune-410 505 (MS). Tel +91 2135 222 026, Fax +91 2135 224 056, Email director@dogr.res.in. -- https://www.asti.cgiar.org/india/directory/directorate-onion-and-garlic-research-dogr
Postal address on ICAR-DOGR report: Rajgurunagar, 410 505, Pune, Maharashtra. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could not complete the research. The search tool's limit was reached after the first four queries, so the digest below is thin and several headings have no supporting evidence. Anything marked "not verified" comes from the input metadata, not from a source I found.

Name note: the CSC name is "Bhima Super" and the Seednet name is "Bhima Super (R&N)". The search evidence refers to "Bhima Super" only. I found no source confirming the "(R&N)" code.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Bhima Super.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for Bhima Super.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial. A ResearchGate paper on onion and garlic research in India (2000-2008) includes a table of exotic onion hybrids and varieties under Indian plains, reporting late kharif and rabi yields as percentage increases over Bhima Super. It gives no absolute yield for Bhima Super itself. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332143333_Onion_and_garlic_research_in_India
A commercial seed listing describes Bhima Super as an early-maturing red onion with deep purple-red colour. This is a retailer claim, not an official trial result. -- https://www.amazon.in/Seeds-Company-Early-Onion-Packet/dp/B0DDCPFKWJ

GENETICS AND QTL -- Partial. The NHB recommended-varieties document says Bhima Super (IC No. 561259) was developed from base population B-780 by selection. It gives no parentage beyond that and no QTL or marker studies. -- https://nhb.gov.in/pdf/vegetable/onion/oni013.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Partial. ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (ICAR-DOGR) is listed among the developers of ten onion varieties, including Bhima Super. No individual breeder name was found. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf
The NHB document also lists Bhima Super among recommended onion varieties. -- https://nhb.gov.in/pdf/vegetable/onion/oni013.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No institute email, phone or postal address was found in the snippets. The ICAR document (https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf) is the closest institutional source, but I did not see its contact section. Check icar.org.in for DOGR's official page.

PUBLICATIONS -- Partial, with no full citations:
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Onion and garlic research in India. ResearchGate (contains Bhima Super comparator yield data) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332143333_Onion_and_garlic_research_in_India
- ICAR QRT review of ICAR-DOGR (year not captured; URL path suggests 2022). ICAR-Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research profile -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2022-07/QRT-DOGR-01.pdf
- No DOI or KrishiKosh thesis located.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Partial. A private online retailer (CPM Seeds Company) lists Bhima Super early red onion seed on Amazon.in. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet availability was found. -- https://www.amazon.in/Seeds-Company-Early-Onion-Packet/dp/B0DDCPFKWJ

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified by search. The input metadata lists Chhattisgarh, Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana, Jammu, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Punjab, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu. The NHB document confirms only that Bhima Super is a recommended variety. Release year 2015-04-07 is from the metadata and was not verified.

Suggested follow-up when the search limit resets: the Seednet portal entry for "Bhima Super (R&N)", the DOGR Rajgurunagar, Pune website for contacts and release notification, and KrishiKosh for trial reports.

agronomic_details.yield: Station and on-farm trials (ejplantbreeding abstract): overall mean green fodder yield 192 t/ha/yr, about 14.9% above the check CO (FS) 29. Dry matter yield 49.73 t/ha/yr. Seed yield about 19.1% higher than CO (FS) 29. Discrepancy: the CSC record gives average yield as 158 Q/HECT Kg/Ha, which is not reconciled with the 192 t/ha/yr green fodder figure in the digest; the two measures may differ in basis and were not verified.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources, except the three-year on-farm study at Raichur KVKs (Karnataka) described under field_trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Raichur KVKs (Karnataka) on-farm evaluation over three years. No agro-climatic adaptation or ecology data found for CO 31 in the searched sources. The CSC adaptation_ecology field is 'Not specified'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified. Digest findings: multicut fodder sorghum type (not grain sorghum); seeds stay intact after physiological maturity; fibre 19.80%; dry matter 25.9%. Dealer listing: 5-6 cuts a year, reflowering at about 50-day intervals.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials: mean green fodder yield 201 t/ha/yr vs 172.8 t/ha/yr for check CO (FS) 29. (2) On-farm trials: 183 t/ha/yr vs 161.2 t/ha/yr for check. (3) Overall green fodder yield 192 t/ha/yr, about 14.9% above check. (4) Dry matter 25.9%, dry matter yield 49.73 t/ha/yr, fibre 19.80%. (5) Seed yield about 19.1% higher than CO (FS) 29. (6) HCN 172 ppm after flowering vs 185 ppm in CO (FS) 29. (7) Three-year on-farm study at Raichur KVKs (Karnataka): CoFS-31 judged superior to CoFS-29 and SSV-74 for fodder and seed. (8) Dealer listing (not an official source): first fodder harvest 65-70 days, 50% flowering at 65-70 days, seed harvest at 105-110 days.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 31 (sorghum)

Name note: The CSC name "CO 31" and the Seednet name "CO. 3" differ. I searched only "CO 31 sorghum". No search covered "CO. 3" or Seednet's crop field, which lists ONION, so nothing below is evidence about Seednet's record. Every finding refers to CO 31 as a multicut fodder sorghum, not grain sorghum.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches on CO 31 returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. Results on drought tolerance concerned other sorghum varieties (K 12) and were discarded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/pdf/TNAU%20Variety%20release%20-%20Eng.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for CO 31 disease or pest resistance. Hits on shoot fly, downy mildew and rice weevil concerned other genotypes and were discarded. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/92b2c634-f12e-414e-90a5-f4e524a61ccc/content
Hydrogen cyanide (HCN) content of CO 31 was measured at several growth stages against CoFS 29 and Co 30. This is a toxicity trait, not resistance. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/hrd/pdf/Millet%20program.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
CO 31 was released in 2014 as a fodder sorghum from a gamma-ray (400 Gy) mutant of CO (FS) 29. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
Station trials gave a mean green fodder yield of 201 t/ha/yr, against 172.8 t/ha/yr for the check CO (FS) 29. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
On-farm trials gave 183 t/ha/yr, against 161.2 t/ha/yr for the check. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
Overall green fodder yield was 192 t/ha/yr, about 14.9% above the check. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
Dry matter was 25.9% and dry matter yield 49.73 t/ha/yr. Fibre was 19.80%. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
Seeds stay intact after physiological maturity, and seed yield was about 19.1% higher than CO (FS) 29. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
HCN content was 172 ppm after flowering, against 185 ppm in CO (FS) 29. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
In a three-year on-farm study at Raichur KVKs (Karnataka), CoFS-31 was judged superior to CoFS-29 and SSV-74 for fodder and seed. -- https://chemijournal.com/archives/?ArticleId=10231&issue=4&si=false&vol=8&year=2020
Dealer listings (not official sources) give first fodder harvest at 65–70 days, reflowering at about 50-day intervals, 5–6 cuts a year, 50% flowering at 65–70 days and seed harvest at 105–110 days. -- https://www.jiomart.com/p/homeandkitchen/iagrifarm-cofs-31-fodder-sorghum-seed-1-kg-multicut-for-fodder-cultivation/609479111

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. A TNAU breeder profile lists shoot-fly QTL and KASP marker work, but it does not name CO 31, so it was discarded. -- https://tnau.irins.org/profile/157306
Parentage conflict (unresolved): the CSC input says "clonal selection from open pollinated progenies of CS-450", which no retrieved source supports. The ejplantbreeding abstract gives a gamma-ray mutant of CO (FS) 29. A dealer listing gives interspecific hybridization of TNS 30 × S. sudanense followed by pedigree selection. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231 ; https://www.jiomart.com/p/homeandkitchen/iagrifarm-cofs-31-fodder-sorghum-seed-1-kg-multicut-for-fodder-cultivation/609479111

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed at the Department of Forage Crops, Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Coimbatore. -- https://www.ejplantbreeding.org/index.php/ejpb/article/view/2231
The Department of Forage Crops at TNAU released the variety, which is also described on the CPBG forage-crops page. -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/forage-crops
No individual breeder name was found for CO 31. -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Department of Forage Crops, TNAU, Coimbatore. Phone 0422-6611228, from the TNAU Seed Centre stock list (2021), which names this department beside a CO 31 entry. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
Institute-level postal address: Centre for Plant Breeding and Genetics, TNAU, Coimbatore-641 003, Tamil Nadu. This is an institute address from a sorghum germplasm paper, not a CO 31 contact. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-D-5896-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
No official email for the Forage Crops department was found.
Dealer contact (not institutional): Indian Agri Farm, Chettikulam, Tirunelveli 627120, email indianagrifarm2015@gmail.com. -- https://www.jiomart.com/p/homeandkitchen/iagrifarm-cofs-31-fodder-sorghum-seed-1-kg-multicut-for-fodder-cultivation/609479111

PUBLICATIONS

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to CO 3. Searches returned only general tomato material.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to CO 3. Heat-tolerance trial papers returned by the research search did not concern CO 3 and were excluded.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to CO 3.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to CO 3.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial wilt: a non-official grower guide (secondary source) names CO 3 as a resistant variety, alongside PKM 1, and states that prevention is the only real solution against bacterial wilt. No pathogen-level testing or resistance data for CO 3 was found. The TNAU statements on TLCV resistance and moderate resistance to root knot nematodes refer to the hybrid 'Tomato Hybrid CO 3' and were excluded. No other disease resistance for the open-pollinated CO 3 was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. Resistance to TLCV and root knot nematodes was documented only for the hybrid and was excluded.

agronomic_details.yield: TNAU AAS page reports 40 t/ha for CO 3, compared with 30-35 t/ha for PKM 1 and 30 t/ha for Paiyur. The variety record gives an average yield of 158 Q/HECT (Kg/Ha), which is about 15.8 t/ha and does not match the 40 t/ha figure; this discrepancy is unresolved. Hybrid yield figures (96.2 t/ha) were excluded.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: A grower guide states CO 3 is suited to Coimbatore, Salem and Dharmapuri districts (secondary, non-official source). No agro-climatic or ecological data were found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Determinate type; can be planted as close as 30 cm x 30 cm; fruits round with four light grooves; fruit colour capsicum red. Seed production spacing is 60 x 30 cm.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No trial reports specific to CO 3 were found. The only performance data are the TNAU AAS comparison (CO 3 at 40 t/ha versus PKM 1 at 30-35 t/ha and Paiyur at 30 t/ha) and the variety record average yield of 158 Q/HECT. Trial sites, seasons and replication details were not reported.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No marker study specific to CO 3 was found. Origin conflict: TNAU describes CO 3 (Marutham) as an induced mutant derived from CO 1, whereas the variety record gives parentage as a clonal selection from open pollinated progenies of CS-450.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL study specific to CO 3 was found; QTL results from the research search concerned other tomato lines and were excluded. Paiyur-1 was bred by crossing Pusa Ruby with CO 3; this confirms CO 3 as a parent but does not describe its traits.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CO 3 (tomato)

Name note: the release-minutes name is "CO 3" and the Seednet name is "CO. 3". I did not run a Seednet-specific search, so no finding below comes from seednet.gov.in. Most evidence refers to the open-pollinated "CO 3 (Marutham)". Several TNAU pages also list a separate F1 hybrid named "Tomato Hybrid CO 3" (released 2010). I excluded hybrid-only findings. Crop note: the Seednet crop field says "ONION", which conflicts with the tomato record. No onion evidence was found, and the findings below treat the crop as tomato.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to CO 3. Searches returned only general tomato material, and the one TNAU statement about TLCV resistance applies to the hybrid, so I excluded it. Source checked: https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_tomato_varieties.html

DISEASE AND PEST -- Prevention is the only real solution against bacterial wilt, and resistant varieties such as PKM 1 and CO 3 are recommended. (This is a non-official grower guide, so treat it as secondary.) -- https://growsmartfarm.org/crops/tomato-en
Pest/disease resistance for the open-pollinated CO 3 is otherwise not documented. The "resistant to TLCV / moderately resistant to root knot nematodes" statements on the TNAU variety page refer to the hybrid "TNAU Tomato Hybrid CO 3" and were excluded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_tomato_varieties.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS --
- CO 3 (Marutham) is described as a determinate type that can be planted as close as 30 cm x 30 cm, with fruits round, four light grooves, capsicum red. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
- Yield reported for CO 3 as 40 t/ha, compared with 30-35 t/ha for PKM 1 and 30 t/ha for Paiyur. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
- Seed production spacing for CO 3 is 60 x 30 cm. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed_veg_tomato.html
- Yield and duration figures from the TNAU variety table (96.2 t/ha, 145 days) belong to the hybrid and were excluded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_tomato_varieties.html

GENETICS AND QTL -- Origin: CO 3 (Marutham) is described as an induced mutant derived from CO 1, which conflicts with the record's parentage of a clonal selection from CS-450. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
Paiyur-1 was bred by crossing Pusa Ruby with CO 3. This confirms CO 3 as a parent but does not describe CO 3 itself. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/govt_schemes_services/aas/tomato.html
No QTL or marker study specific to CO 3 was found. The QTL and marker results returned in the research search concerned other tomato lines and were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No named breeder for CO 3 was found. The releasing body is the Horticultural College and Research Institute, Coimbatore, TNAU. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-technologies-developed/
The Department of Vegetable Crops (established 1979 within the institute) runs tomato breeding for yield and stress resistance. This is institute-level only and not specific to CO 3. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-about-department/
TNAU's release table lists CO 3 (Marutham) with a release year of 1980 (also CO1 1969 and CO2 1974). This conflicts with the 2015-04-07 release date in the record. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/hcri-coimbatore/department-of-vegetable-crops-technologies-developed/

CONTACT DETAILS --
- Dr. L. Pugalendhi, Dean (Horticulture), Horticultural College and Research Institute, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore - 641 003, Tamil Nadu, India. E-mail: nextgenhort2021@tnau.ac.in. This is an institute-level contact taken from a 2021 event page, not a CO 3 breeder contact. -- https://sites.google.com/tnau.ac.in/ihc2021/contact
- A third-party listing gives the address as Lawley Road, Coimbatore - 641003, and names the Dean as Dr. S. Mariappan. This conflicts with the event page and is unverified. -- https://www.collegebatch.com/11967-horticultural-college-and-research-institute-in-coimbatore
- TNAU Seed Centre vegetable stock contact: 0422-6611283 / 6611374; vegetables@tnau.ac.in. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Department of Seed Science & Technology, TNAU, Coimbatore-641003: Phone 0422-6611363; Email seed@tnau.ac.in. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed_veg_tomato.html

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research-focused search returned only unrelated tomato papers (cadmium GWAS, Ethiopian germplasm, heat-tolerance trials, fruit-mass genetics) and no CO 3 paper, AICRP report, thesis or KrishiKosh record. No KrishiKosh or journal search was run beyond that query.

SEED AVAILABILITY --
- A TNAU seed stock position dated 13.08.2019 lists CO 3 with a quantity of 35.79, unit not shown in the extracted table. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/pdf/seedavailabilityon13.08.2019.pdf
- A TNAU seed production page says CO 3 is among tomato varieties kept on sale at the Horticultural College and Research Station, Coimbatore (contact 0422 6611283). The page is undated. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/seed_certification/seed%20Centre_Seed%20Productions.html
- The 31.07.2021 TNAU stock list shows PKM 1 and hybrid CO 4 but no visible CO 3 entry. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- Papaya "Co 3" and bhendi hybrid "Co 3" appear in TNAU price lists, but those are other crops and were excluded. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/input_source/input_source_tnau_seed.html
- Availability is subject to stock at the time of enquiry. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or private dealer listing for CO 3 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The record's recommended-states field is "Not specified". A grower guide says CO 3 is suited for Coimbatore, Salem & Dharmapuri districts. This is a secondary source and is not an official notification. -- https://growsmartfarm.org/crops/tomato-en
No official Central Sub-Committee notification or recommended-state list was found. Seednet was not checked directly.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest on drought tolerance or related mechanisms.

heat.details: No evidence of heat tolerance was found. The Sharmila Bharathi and Mohan (2018) source contains agronomic notes on planting dates and temperature responses, but no tolerance rating.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest on salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest on flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: No disease resistance is documented. The variety is moderately susceptible to purple blotch (Alternaria porri).

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance is documented. The variety is susceptible to onion thrips (Thrips tabaci).

agronomic_details.yield: Bulb yield of about 18.9 t/ha in about 90 days, reported as about 18.8% above CO 4 (Saraswathi et al., 2017). The WorldVeg record reports 18.91 t/ha, 18.78% above COA. The comparator varieties differ between sources.
agronomic_details.stability: No evidence found in the digest on performance across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Best suited to January planting for economic yield in fertile loamy irrigated soils. A Coimbatore-area study found December planting gave the highest bulb yield.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 90 days seed-to-bulb; bulb-to-seed 95-100 days (per digest). The input table lists maturity as not available.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Free-flowering and seed-setting type. Produces true seed of roughly 250-300 kg/ha. Pink to light-pink bulbs of about 60-90 g per clump. TSS about 13.2 degrees Brix. Storage life reported over 150 days, although a 2020 TNAU release note describes a short shelf life for CO 5.
agronomic_details.field_trials: A 2015 Journal of Plant Sciences trial in Coimbatore found the lowest post-harvest weight loss and storage rot among CO (On) 5, CO-6 and Aca-15. KVK Namakkal ran a staggered seed nursery of CO (On) 5 for 20 farmers and a demonstration showing improved small onion production. The release year of 2015 is not confirmed by the digest sources.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No evidence found in the digest on QTL, SNP, or SSR markers.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: No evidence found in the digest on genes or pathways. The variety was developed via mass pedigree selection in a seed-propagated aggregatum (multiplier) onion, with parental line AC (SP.l) collected from Gnanamedu village, Cuddalore district.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TOPIC: Identity and breeder: Developed by Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) Horticultural College & Research Institute, Coimbatore, as a seed-propagated aggregatum (multiplier) onion via mass pedigree selection; the input's "Indian Agricultural Research Institute" attribution is not supported by these sources -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf

TOPIC: Release and development: The 2006 WorldVeg record describes the variety's development at TNAU, with the parental line AC (SP.l) collected from Gnanamedu village, Cuddalore district. The input's release year of 2015 is not confirmed by these sources -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Yield: Bulb yield of about 18.9 t/ha in about 90 days, roughly 18.8% above CO 4 (CO 4 is the comparison variety in this source) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/T.%20Saraswathi,%20et%20al.pdf ; also 18.91 t/ha, 18.78% above COA, in https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Seed production and reproduction: Free-flowering and seed-setting type, producing true seed of roughly 250-300 kg/ha; seed-to-bulb about 90 days, bulb-to-seed 95-100 days -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/T.%20Saraswathi,%20et%20al.pdf

TOPIC: Bulb traits and quality: Pink to light-pink bulbs, about 60-90 g per clump; TSS about 13.2 degrees Brix; storage life reported over 150 days -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/6-4-2017/T.%20Saraswathi,%20et%20al.pdf

TOPIC: Storage and shelf life: A 2015 Journal of Plant Sciences trial found the lowest post-harvest weight loss and storage rot among CO (On) 5, CO-6 and Aca-15 tested in Coimbatore -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370968566_Economics_of_Production_and_Marketing_of_Small_Onion_in_Coimbatore_District ; a 2020 TNAU release note says CO 5 has a short shelf life and was superseded by CO 6 for that trait -- https://www.covaipost.com/coimbatore/13-new-crop-varieties-released-as-pongal-gift-to-farmers-by-tnau-coimbatore/

TOPIC: Disease resistance: Moderately susceptible to purple blotch (Alternaria porri) -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Pest resistance: Susceptible to onion thrips (Thrips tabaci) -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en

TOPIC: Drought tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Heat tolerance: No evidence found (agronomic notes on planting dates and temperature responses exist, but no tolerance rating) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf

TOPIC: Salinity tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Flood tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: Submergence tolerance: No evidence found

TOPIC: QTL/molecular markers: No evidence found

TOPIC: Recommended planting window: Best suited to January planting for economic yield in fertile loamy irrigated soils; a Coimbatore-area study also found December planting gave the highest bulb yield -- https://worldveg.tind.io/record/35310?ln=en ; https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf

TOPIC: Recommended states/regions: Tamil Nadu (named as a preferred variety in TNAU crop notes; crop-growing districts include Perambalur, Trichy, Dindigul, Namakkal, Coimbatore, Erode, Tirunelveli) -- http://www.agritech.tnau.ac.in/horticulture/horti_vegetables_small%20onion.html

TOPIC: Seed availability (NSC/State Seed Corporations): No evidence found

TOPIC: Seed availability (KVKs and farmer level): KVK Namakkal ran a staggered seed nursery of CO (On) 5 for 20 farmers to supply seed for the next crop and reduce delayed-sowing losses, and a KVK Namakkal demonstration showed improved small onion production using CO 5 seed -- https://www.ijcmas.com/7-3-2018/C.%20Sharmila%20Bharathi%20and%20B.%20Mohan.pdf ; https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/success_stories/pdf/horti/2014/h_ss12_2014.pdf

TOPIC: Farmer adoption: A study of adoption among farmers in Perambalur district, Tamil Nadu -- https://ageconsearch.umn.edu/record/367061/

disease_resistance.summary: Purple blotch: low disease index relative to the checks GWO-1 and PWF-131 (relative field observation). No formal disease resistance rating was found, so this is not a confirmed resistance classification. Source: release page for Gujarat Anand White Onion 2.

pest_resistance.summary: Thrips: fewer thrips than the checks GWO-1 and PWF-131 (relative field observation). No formal pest resistance rating was found. Source: release page for Gujarat Anand White Onion 2.

agronomic_details.yield: Average bulb yield of 595 q/ha as reported on the release page (name used: Gujarat Anand White Onion 2). The CSC record lists the average_yield unit as Kg/Ha, so the unit should be reconciled before use.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources
agronomic_details.adaptation: Middle Gujarat, Rabi season, irrigated conditions (release page). The digest treats this as a production condition, not a stress-tolerance finding.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: More long leaves than both checks. Lower percentage of bolting and jointed bulbs than both checks. White skin, globe shape and large bulb size. Higher TSS, pyruvic acid, reducing and non-reducing sugars, and total carbohydrates than the checks (release page, name used: Gujarat Anand White Onion 2).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Release-page comparison with checks: bulb yield 25% higher than GWO-1 and 45% higher than PWF-131 (average 595 q/ha). Thrips and purple blotch were lower than the checks. Bolting and jointed-bulb percentages were lower than the checks. Quality traits (TSS, pyruvic acid, sugars, total carbohydrates) were higher than the checks. (2) Agronomy trial using the name GAWO 2: three consecutive seasons at the College of Horticulture Farm, Anand Agricultural University, testing organic and consortium nutrient treatments (CC + NPK consortium referenced), transplanting in December and harvest in April. This was not a varietal comparison and no yield results were given in the digest. The year of the extended summary could not be verified from the retrieved text.
