disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial leaf blight (BLB): moderate tolerance claimed by the developer, and listed as resistant or moderately resistant in an IRRI-hosted hybrid rice table. Blast: moderate tolerance claimed by the developer only. Also listed as resistant or moderately resistant in the same IRRI-hosted table: RTV and BS (abbreviations as listed in the digest; full names not stated in the digest). The developer describes the hybrid as having moderate blast tolerance. The IRRI table is the only independent source; the developer claims are not independently verified.

pest_resistance.summary: Whitebacked planthopper (WBPH): resistant or moderately resistant, per the IRRI-hosted hybrid rice table. No evaluation of other insect or pest species found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Developer's specified yield potential: 7.5-8.0 t/ha. Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives a yield figure of 5.98, with unit and basis not stated. Long-term multi-environment tests (2005-2019) report JKRH 3333 yielding about 10% more than inbred checks. The drip-irrigation study reports it as statistically superior in grain yield among genotypes tested (values not given in the digest).
agronomic_details.stability: Long-term multi-environment tests (2005-2019) report yield about 10% above inbred checks across environments. The developer describes wider adaptability. No environment-specific stability statistics found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Developer describes wider adaptability and suitability for direct seeding and machine sowing. A breeding review lists it among hybrids suited to aerobic conditions. Recommended states per the CSC-aligned Krishak Jagat entry: West Bengal, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh. Conflict: a second Krishak Jagat entry gives a 2017 record under Madhya Pradesh; this should be checked against the CSC minutes. The IRRI-hosted proceedings list Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. The company states notification for cultivation across India, which is broader than the CSC state list.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 135-140 days (developer specification; Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives the same duration)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Plant height 105-110 cm; 12-14 productive tillers per plant; panicle about 30 cm, compact; non-lodging, strong sturdy stem with heavy tillering; medium slender grain; good cooking quality; high hulling and milling recovery (developer's claims). Parentage: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) AICRIP Initial Hybrid Rice Trial, medium slender, Kharif 2021, 32 locations: JKRH-3333 served as National Check Hybrid-1 (NCH-1); location-wise yields and checks are tabulated in the report, but the values are not in the digest. (2) 56th Annual Rice Research Group Meeting 2021 draft proceedings: JKRH-3333 (NCH-1) listed among checks in the trials; no yield values in the digest. (3) Long-term multi-environment tests, 2005-2019: JKRH 3333 among hybrids yielding about 10% more than inbred checks. (4) Drip-irrigated rice root study: JKRH 3333 listed with strong root length and volume and statistically superior grain yield among genotypes tested. Trial site details and quantitative values are not in the digest for (2) and (4).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JKRH 3333 (CSC minutes name) / JKRH-3333 (Seednet name), rice hybrid (paddy)

Name note: The evidence below refers to "JKRH 3333" or "JKRH-3333" on JK Agri Genetics pages and in ICAR/AICRIP documents. Both names are used in the sources, so I treated them as the same variety. The search budget was 4 queries, and none targeted seednet.gov.in directly, so the Seednet portal entry is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate tolerance to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) and blast is claimed for JKRH 3333 by the developer. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333-moderate-tolerance-to-blb-blast/
- The developer describes wider adaptability and moderate blast tolerance, with a strong sturdy stem and heavy tillering. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- A paper on drip-irrigated rice lists JKRH 3333 as a genotype with strong root length and volume, and as statistically superior in grain yield among the genotypes tested. -- https://f1000research.com/articles/6-125/v2
- A hybrid rice table lists JKRH3333 as resistant or moderately resistant to BLB, RTV, BS and WBPH. The table is in the IRRI-hosted 6th International Hybrid Rice Symposium proceedings. -- http://books.irri.org/9789712203039_content.pdf
- A breeding review lists JKRH 3333 among hybrids suited to aerobic conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351749037_Rice_breeding_in_India_eight_decades_of_journey_towards_enhancing_the_genetic_gain_for_yield_nutritional_quality_and_commodity_value
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for JKRH 3333 specifically. The only abiotic items were the aerobic-suitability listing and the drip-irrigation root study above.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderate tolerance to BLB and blast is the developer's claim (see stress section). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333-moderate-tolerance-to-blb-blast/
- Resistant or moderately resistant to BLB, RTV, BS (bacterial sheath/sheath blight-type entry as listed) and WBPH. Source table is cited under stress tolerance. -- http://books.irri.org/9789712203039_content.pdf
- Insect or other pest evaluation beyond WBPH: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Crop duration 135-140 days, medium slender grain, yield potential 7.5-8.0 t/ha, plant height 105-110 cm, 12-14 productive tillers per plant, 30 cm compact panicle, non-lodging stem (developer's specification). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333-moderate-tolerance-to-blb-blast/
- Suitable for direct seeding and machine sowing, with good cooking quality and high hulling and milling recovery (developer's claims). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- Krishak Jagat hybrid list gives the IET number 20759, release 2013 and 2016, duration 135-140 days, and a yield figure of 5.98 (unit and basis not stated). -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- AICRIP Initial Hybrid Rice Trial (medium slender), Kharif 2021, 32 locations: JKRH-3333 served as National Check Hybrid-1 (NCH-1). Location-wise yields and checks are tabulated. -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf
- 56th Annual Rice Research Group Meeting 2021 draft proceedings list JKRH-3333 (NCH-1) among checks in the trials. -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- Long-term multi-environment tests (2005-2019) report JKRH 3333 as one of the hybrids yielding about 10% more than inbred checks. -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/csc2.20747

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: No evidence found. The sources give the IET identifier 20759 but no parent lines.
- QTL or marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: JK Agri Genetics Limited (JKAGL), Hyderabad, which states it was notified by the Government of India. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- The company says it has in-house crop breeding and biotechnology R&D units recognised by DSIR and several multi-location trial centres. The research page does not name the lead breeder. -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The company achievements page names no individual for this hybrid. -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/achievements/
- Collaborations listed for rice (BSSKV Dapoli, IIRR, IARI, Intelli Biotechnology): these are company-level and are not attributed to this variety by name. -- https://jkagri.com/research-and-development/
- CVRC or CVRC-type notification: the company timeline states the hybrid was notified by the Government of India for cultivation across India, without a date or notification number. -- https://jkagri.com/timeline/2009/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level address, JK Agri Genetics Limited: 1-10-177, 4th floor, Varun Towers, Begumpet, Hyderabad – 500016. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/
- Breeder name, role, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute email or phone: No evidence found on the pages retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (2022). Grain yield performance of hybrid rice in relation to inbred cultivars in long-term multi-environment tests in India. Crop Science -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/csc2.20747 (DOI 10.1002/csc2.20747)
- Authors not shown in retrieved snippet (year not stated in snippet, the F1000 page is about 3403 days old). Variation in rice root traits assessed by phenotyping under drip irrigation. F1000Research, article 6-125 v2 -- https://f1000research.com/articles/6-125/v2
- AICRIP Hybrid Rice Progress Report (2021), Initial Hybrid Rice Trial, Medium Slender, Kharif 2021. Hybrid Rice Progress Report, AICRIP -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/HybridRiceProgressReport-2021.pdf
- Authors not shown (2021). Draft Proceedings of the 56th Annual Rice Research Group Meeting. ICAR-IIRR -- https://icar-iirr.org/56%20ARGM%20Draft%20Proceedings%202021-%202.08.2021.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- JK Agri Genetics product listing for JKRH 3333 under Field Crops and Paddy. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/ and https://jkagri.com/product-category/field-crops/paddy/page/2/
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales: No evidence found.
- Excluded: a news item about a seed dispute refers to "JKRH-333" (missing a digit), so it is not this variety. -- https://scanx.trade/stock-market-news/companies/jk-agri-genetics-seeks-arbitration-67-74-lakh-dues/53082566

RECOMMENDED STATES
- West Bengal, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat and Andhra Pradesh, as listed in the hybrid release list for 2016 and the 2013 and 2016 entries. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- A second entry in the same list gives a 2017 record for JKRH 3333 under Madhya Pradesh. This conflicts with the 2016 entry and should be checked against the CSC minutes. -- https://www.krishakjagat.org/crop-cultivation/list-of-hybrid-paddy-released-notified-in-india-from-1994-to-2021/
- The IRRI-hosted proceedings list JKRH 3333 among recommended hybrids for Bihar, Chhattisgarh and Gujarat. -- http://books.irri.org/9789712203039_content.pdf
- The company says the hybrid was notified for cultivation across India, which is broader than the CSC state list. -- https://jkagri.com/product/jkrh-3333/

drought.details: JR-81 is described as drought tolerant and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and recurring drought. While generally drought tolerant, it may require protective life-saving irrigation under severe stress conditions. It shows tolerance to terminal drought stress and has been part of screening and identification programs for drought tolerance.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to terminal heat stress and has been subject to correlation studies related to grain yield and heat tolerance. It is also listed in contexts related to heat stress tolerance in rice.

salinity.details: While 'salt tolerant lines' are mentioned in one document where JR-81 is also referenced, there is no direct evidence stating JR-81 itself is salt tolerant.

flood.details: Submergence tolerance is distinct from general flood tolerance. Although mentioned in reports discussing flash floods and non-lodging/submergence tolerant varieties in general, specific flood tolerance for JR-81 is not detailed.

disease_resistance.summary: JR-81 is reported to be tolerant to sheath blight and sheath rot.

pest_resistance.summary: JR-81 shows resistance to White-backed planthopper (WBPH) and Brown planthopper (BPH).

agronomic_details.yield: Yield varies by condition: 40 Q/ha for general/rainfed conditions. For irrigated conditions, it yields 55.0-60.0 Q/ha. A derivative (JR 81-01) recorded a yield of 6580 kg/ha (65.8 Q/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Recommended for both rainfed and irrigated conditions, suggesting good adaptability across different water management regimes.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, irrigated conditions, recurring drought conditions, and as aerobic rice.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Short duration, ranging from 110-125 days, with specific mentions of 110 days, 119.06 days, and a range of 120-125 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf (82 cm) with long slender (LS) grains.

drought.details: JR-81 is described as drought tolerant and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and recurring drought. While generally drought tolerant, it may require protective life-saving irrigation under severe stress conditions. It shows tolerance to terminal drought stress and has been part of screening and identification programs for drought tolerance.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to terminal heat stress and has been subject to correlation studies related to grain yield and heat tolerance. It is also listed in contexts related to heat stress tolerance in rice.

salinity.details: While 'salt tolerant lines' are mentioned in one document where JR-81 is also referenced, there is no direct evidence stating JR-81 itself is salt tolerant.

flood.details: Submergence tolerance is distinct from general flood tolerance. Although mentioned in reports discussing flash floods and non-lodging/submergence tolerant varieties in general, specific flood tolerance for JR-81 is not detailed.

submergence.details: JR-81 is listed in contexts discussing submergence stress tolerance and has been evaluated in trials for this trait. It is mentioned as suitable for semi-deep water conditions with implied one-week submergence tolerance. A derivative, JR 81-01, was explicitly tested for submergence tolerance and anaerobic germination.

disease_resistance.summary: JR-81 is reported to be tolerant to sheath blight and sheath rot.

pest_resistance.summary: JR-81 shows resistance to White-backed planthopper (WBPH) and Brown planthopper (BPH).

agronomic_performance.adaptation: Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, irrigated conditions, recurring drought conditions, and as aerobic rice.

drought.details: JRH-19 is a drought-tolerant and low-water-required paddy variety, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and considered resistant to drought/moisture/water stress. It is listed among climate-resilient varieties and varieties important for drought tolerance studies.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to terminal heat stress and listed in contexts discussing heat stress tolerance and climate-resilient varieties.

salinity.details: JRH-19 is described as salt tolerant and highly resistant in contexts related to salinity, and recommended for coastal saline regions. It has been investigated for its performance under salinity conditions.

flood.details: JRH-19 is listed among varieties associated with flood tolerance, and in advisories that also mention flood tolerant varieties.

disease_resistance.summary: JRH-19 is reported to be resistant to major diseases and is described as highly resistant to 'black' (disease type not further specified).

pest_resistance.summary: JRH-19 is tolerant to insect pests and resistant to major pests.

agronomic_details.yield: JRH-19 is a high-yielding hybrid. Reported yields vary; earlier annual reports indicate an average yield of 5.00 t/ha, while more recent test entry data shows yields of 3.40 t/ha (against a national check of 3.20 t/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly stated, but its high tolerance to multiple abiotic stresses (drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence, cold) suggests good stability across various challenging environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: JRH-19 is a non-Basmati hybrid suitable for both irrigated ecosystems and direct sown rainfed conditions, including semi-deep water environments with up to one week of submergence tolerance. It is specifically adapted to Madhya Pradesh.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: JRH-19 is a short duration, semi-dwarf variety, with a plant height of 82 cm. It produces long slender (LS) grains.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has undergone extensive evaluation, including front-line demonstrations under irrigated ecosystems and consistent assessment in Annual Rice Research Group Meetings (ARGM) of ICAR-IIRR and AICRIP.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JR 21 (JR 81-01), rice

Name note: The CSC release name is JR 21 and the variety code is JR 81-01. The Seednet name JR 10 was not in my queries, so no evidence below is tied to it specifically. Searches 1 to 4 used "JR 21" and its variants. Only one result (global-agriculture) describes the variety itself. The rest of the findings below are gaps, not confirmed facts.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for JR 21.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searches returned no blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight or insect resistance data for JR 21.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No variety-specific evidence found for maturity, yield or trial performance. The only trial result returned is a 2022-23 Kharif sponsored trial at JNKVV, Jabalpur, testing a foliar biostimulant (AGMA) on paddy growth and yield. It does not concern JR 21 and should not be used as variety evidence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380720265_Effect_of_biostimulants_on_growth_and_yield_of_rice

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is recorded as "Not specified" and no marker or QTL study was returned.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution per input record: Jawahar Lal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. Lead breeder names and station were not found. Release reporting describes JR 21 as an open-pollinated rice variety released by the Government of India after consultation with the Central Seed Committee -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-jr-21-jr-81-01/

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No JNKVV official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL was returned by the searches. A JNKVV institute contact page still needs to be located (for example via jnkvv.org, which I did not verify).

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on JR 21 was returned. The P. Ananda Kumar Wikipedia result is unrelated to this variety and is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. Searches returned no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings. Seednet listing under JR 10 was not checked.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Madhya Pradesh (release notification as reported) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/rice-variety-jr-21-jr-81-01/. The same report is dated 25 September 2023, while the input record gives 2 May 2023 as the release date. The two dates were not reconciled. The official CSC/seednet notification was not retrieved.

Recommended next steps: search "JR 10 paddy seednet" for the portal listing; search "JR 81-01 rice JNKVV" and "JNKVV rice varieties Jabalpur" for breeder and trial records; and check the ICAR/AICRP rice annual reports for JNKVV entries. I could not complete these within the four-search limit.

drought.details: JR 10 is a drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. It has been screened for drought stress tolerance in trials. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance was isolated from JR 10.

heat.details: The variety is tolerant to terminal heat stress and has been included in screenings for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: JR 10 is mentioned in the context of salinity tolerant rabi crops for reclamation.

flood.details: While mentioned in discussions related to flood-prone rice cultivation, specific flood tolerance for JR 10 is not explicitly stated.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant against bacterial leaf blight, grain discoloration, and sheath-rot.

pest_resistance.summary: Resistant against stem-borer and leaf folder. Tolerant against brown plant-hopper and sheath mite.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Kalachampa (rice/paddy)

Name note: variety_name "Kalachampa" and seednet_variety_name "KALACHAMPA" refer to the same variety. No Seednet portal page surfaced in the searches, so every finding below is from non-Seednet sources and applies to both names. A Drishti article calls it "Keonjhar Kalachampa", so the name may carry a district qualifier in some sources.

Search limit: the four permitted web_search calls were used, and a fifth call was refused. Breeder, contact, trial, and publication coverage is therefore thin. Gaps are marked "No evidence found" where the searches returned nothing usable.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Drishti IAS, "Indigenous Paddy Variety: Keonjhar Kalachampa", https://www.drishtiias.com/daily-updates/daily-news-analysis/indigenous-paddy-variety-keonjhar-kalachampa (describes it as a local paddy variety that has shown resilience to major diseases, pests, and the effects of climate change; no drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data found)

DISEASE AND PEST -- Drishti IAS, same URL (general resilience to major diseases and pests stated; no specific resistance genes or scores found)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- WASSAN, "KALACHAMPA: The story of a registered variety derived from..." case study, December 2022, https://www.wassan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Kalachampa-WGoSS-Case-Study-December-2022.pdf (reports a breeder-seed production plot at the Pipili farm during Kharif 2016, with a visit by the Principal Secretary; yield and maturity figures not captured)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The only parentage information is the WASSAN title "derived from", which suggests selection from a local landrace. The parentage field in the record is "Not specified".

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- WASSAN case study, https://www.wassan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Kalachampa-WGoSS-Case-Study-December-2022.pdf (the variety is described as a registered variety derived from local material in Odisha, a recognised centre of rice diversity; a named lead breeder was not confirmed). Institution of record per CSC: Director of Agriculture, Government of Odisha. Release year per record: 2015 (2015-06-25).

CONTACT DETAILS -- No official breeder or institute contact found. The only address seen is a private seed dealer listing, not an official contact: IndiaMART listing "Natural Yellow Kalachampa", https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kalachampa-21136282062.html (seller address given as House No-17, Uparasahi, Sahoo PS, Kendubilwo, Pratapur, Khordha, Bhubaneswar, 752102, Odisha). Treat it as a dealer contact, not an institutional one. Director of Agriculture, Odisha, office contact details: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found in peer-reviewed journals, AICRP/ICAR reports, or KrishiKosh. The WASSAN case study (https://www.wassan.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/Kalachampa-WGoSS-Case-Study-December-2022.pdf) is a grey-literature NGO document, not a peer-reviewed source.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- IndiaMART listing, https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/kalachampa-21136282062.html (a 20 kg bag of "Natural Yellow Kalachampa" is listed at about ₹700 in Bhubaneswar; a second dealer, Suryadev Seeds, is also listed). No NSC, OSSC, KVK, or SAU seed sale evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Odisha per the CSC record (recommended_states_raw). No independent confirmation found in the searches; the Drishti and WASSAN sources place the variety in Odisha.

drought.details: Identified as short duration drought tolerant, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and drought-prone areas of Subarnapur. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) was isolated from this drought tolerant rice cultivar, and molecular breeding efforts aim to develop varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: Exhibits high temperature stress tolerance. Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in this variety, contributing to the development of abiotic tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: Listed as salinity tolerant.

flood.details: While submergence tolerance is noted, general flood tolerance is not explicitly detailed.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to neck blast, rice tungro disease, bacterial leaf blight (BLB), and false smut (through pyramiding efforts). It is also mentioned in the context of multiple disease resistant lines.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to brown plant hopper (BPH) and resistant to stemborer, leaf folder, and gall midge. It is generally mentioned in the context of insect pest resistance in rice ecosystems, with yellow stem borer being a major pest.

agronomic_details.yield: 65 q/ha
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly stated, but recommended across multiple states and for both rainfed and irrigated conditions suggests adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, as well as irrigated, mid-duration cultivation. It is also noted as a short duration variety. Cultivated in drought-prone areas such as Subarnapur.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-Basmati, long slender grain type. Exhibits high germination (77.33%) and maximum seedling survival (81.09%).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Kalinga Dhan 1201 was subject to on-farm trials conducted by Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) Deogarh, where Kalinga Dhan 1204 reportedly performed better.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular markers are utilized for validation of high temperature stress tolerance. Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) is applied in breeding for drought, heat, and submergence stress tolerance. Molecular breeding has been employed for developing rice varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Specific QTL names or positions are not detailed, but MAS is a key breeding strategy for stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1201, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not explicitly mentioned.
commercial_info.availability_status: Released in 2021 and listed on ICAR's rice database, indicating general availability for cultivation.
commercial_info.kvk: It has been included in on-farm trials by KVK Deogarh, suggesting availability for research and extension purposes.

agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Kalinga Dhan- 1301 is a non-Basmati rice variety noted for being protein-rich. It is also known by its breeding designations IET 26024 and OR 2573-15.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: The variety has undergone extensive evaluation through field trials, including those conducted as part of the Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM). Specific screenings were performed for submergence tolerance (at 4 to 6 centers) and high temperature tolerance. On-farm trials have also been reported.

heat.details: No heat tolerance evidence for Karjat-184 was found in the results.

salinity.details: Karjat-184 was included with Karjat 4 and Ratnagiri 6 in a study of genotypes grown under salt treatment, and the Kunkerkar profile mentions salt-tolerant rice improvement and Karjat-184. The snippets do not give a clear tolerance score, so the level is tentative. The DBSKKV varieties page lists saline-soil tolerance for a variety near the Karjat-184 entry, and it is unclear whether this applies to Karjat-184. Karjat-184 is also a parent of salt-related crosses such as IR64 x Karjat 184 (ISCAR).

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for Karjat-184 was found.

disease_resistance.summary: A molecular screening figure (marker RM-122 linked to bacterial blight and blast) reports blast resistance alleles in Karjat-184. This is a marker-based indication, not field-confirmed resistance. The CSC disease reaction is Not Specified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karjat-10 (variety_name) / KARJAT-1 (seednet_variety_name), rice (Paddy)

Name note: The search found no Seednet record for Karjat-10. The only "KARJAT-1" evidence refers to a different, older variety (Karjat-1, notified 15/05/1990, S.O. 386(E)). Under this heading, the Seednet name is not supported for Karjat-10 by any evidence found. Results for "Karjat-10" are the only ones tied to the target variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Karjat-10. One 2025 trial paper reports Karjat-10 among direct-seeded genotypes, but it discusses heat and drought avoidance only in general terms for early-flowering genotypes, not for Karjat-10 -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue10S/PartC/S-9-10-15-893.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Karjat-10 is described as non-shattering and non-lodging, with dwarf stature (Mahabeej seed catalogue). No disease or pest resistance rating was found for Karjat-10 -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=15
No evidence found for blast, bacterial blight, brown plant hopper or gall midge resistance in Karjat-10. The resistance data found belongs to other Karjat lines (Karjat-184, Karjat-8) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/334681259_Karjat-184_an_early_rice_variety_for_Konkan_region_of_Maharashtra_state

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Karjat-10 is a long slender grain type with average grain yield of 5.0 to 5.2 t/ha, per the Additional Director of RARS Karjat -- https://thebetterindia.com/131542/rice-research-institute-karjat-maharashtra/
Maturity is given as 120 to 145 days -- https://thebetterindia.com/131542/rice-research-institute-karjat-maharashtra/ ; the Mahabeej catalogue gives 140 to 145 days -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=15
Recommended seed rate is 60 kg/ha, with 140 to 145 days duration and fertilizer responsiveness (Mahabeej) -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=15
A 2025 Karjat (Kharif) trial found Karjat-10 had 100 days to 50% flowering, the highest plant height among the tested lines in one comparison, the longest panicle (26.25 cm), and the highest grain yield per plant (36.10 g) -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue10S/PartC/S-9-10-15-893.pdf
Standard agronomic package for RARS Karjat rice: 150:100:150 kg N:P2O5:K2O per ha in kharif -- https://old.dbskkv.org/Research/Research_Stations_&_Organogram.html (general station guidance; Karjat-10 not named)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found for QTL, marker or molecular studies on Karjat-10.
Parentage check: the supplied parentage (Holamaldiga/Z x IR-36) is not confirmed by any source found. The only pedigree found for a Karjat culture is for KJT-2-2-44-10 (Kasruri/IR 50, pedigree selection at RARS Karjat), which is not named as Karjat-10 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296389929_Super_fine_rice_variety_Karjat_8_for_low_land_areas_of_Maharashtra_State

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Karjat, under Dr. Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth (DBSKKV), Dapoli, since 1972 -- https://www.isasat.org/Vol-ii,issue-i/AARJ_2_1_z_ad1_Karjat%20centennary.pdf
Named RARS Karjat rice staff in 2025: MP Gawai, Jr. Rice Breeder (Karjat-10 trial paper) -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue10S/PartC/S-9-9-45-876.pdf ; Dr. BD Waghmode, Rice Specialist, RARS Karjat -- https://www.biochemjournal.com/archives/2025/vol9issue10S/PartC/S-9-9-45-876.pdf
Earlier staff: Dr. LS Chavan, Additional Director, RARS Karjat -- https://thebetterindia.com/131542/rice-research-institute-karjat-maharashtra/ ; Dr. AK Shinde (lead author, RARS Karjat) -- https://www.isasat.org/vol-ii-issue-ii-july-2018/3_AARJ_II_2_Shinde%20et%20al_128-140.pdf
Who released Karjat-10 and when: not found. The Mahabeej catalogue lists its release year as "N.N" (not noted) -- https://www.mahabeej.co.in/cereals?id=15 . The 2024-08-02 CSC release date is not confirmed by any source found, and Karjat-10 was already in trials and seed catalogues in 2019 and 2025.

drought.details: Chandragiri (referred to as Khandagiri in search results due to matching parentage and institutional association) is identified as a drought-tolerant variety. It is described as dwarf statured, early duration (90-95 days), and highly tolerant to anaerobic germination and vegetative stage drought stress. Lower tiller production during water stress may be a determinant of its drought tolerance. It is frequently used as a local check or control variety in trials evaluating other short-duration drought-tolerant rice varieties in drought-prone areas.

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance found.

salinity.details: Khandagiri is listed among varieties tested for salt tolerance or used in breeding programs for salt-tolerant cultivars. It is included in lists with known salt-tolerant varieties like Lunishree and VTL11. Rhizospheric regions near Khandagiri, India, have yielded bacteria proved to promote salt tolerance in rice seedlings. It has also been part of anther culture research aimed at developing salt-tolerant rice.

flood.details: Khandagiri has been described as tolerant to stagnant flooding and is associated with discussions on flood-tolerant rice.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Leaf folder. No other specific disease resistance information found.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Leaf folder. No other specific pest resistance information found.

agronomic_details.yield: As a local check variety, its yield is generally lower than newer high-yielding varieties like Sahbhagi Dhan. Sahbhagi Dhan recorded 35.5-36.5 q/ha, which was 28.6% higher than Khandagiri. Reported yield for Khandagiri ranges from 3000-3200 kg/ha (30-32 q/ha). Farmers have replaced lower-yielding rice varieties like Khandagiri with higher-yielding alternatives in some demonstrations.
agronomic_details.stability: Yield enhancement over Khandagiri was observed even in normal rainfall years (up to 19%) and during stress years when compared to newer varieties.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well-adapted to rainfed irrigated uplands and drought-prone upland/shallow lowland environments.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dwarf statured, with lower tiller production during water stress. Grain to straw ratio found to be lower than Sahabhagidhan.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Extensive on-farm assessments and cluster demonstrations have been conducted in various districts of Odisha (e.g., Malkangiri, Subarnapur, Gajapati, Kalahandi, Koraput), often using Khandagiri as a control or local check variety to evaluate newer drought-tolerant lines.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (SNP/SSR) or QTL positions are identified. However, it has been included in genetic diversity analyses.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: It is associated with research concerning the Sub1 locus, a major QTL for submergence tolerance, though it is not explicitly stated that Chandragiri (Khandagiri) carries the Sub1 gene.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Studies have explored its phenological, physiological, and yield markers for drought tolerance, including lower tiller production under water stress. Anther culture response in crosses involving Khandagiri has been studied.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not specified by name.
commercial_info.availability_status: Readily available in recommended states, particularly Odisha, for drought-prone areas, often from 'reliable sources' or as part of government-backed contingency plans.

drought.details: Chandragiri (referred to as Khandagiri in search results due to matching parentage and institutional association) is identified as a drought-tolerant variety. It is described as dwarf statured, early duration (90-95 days), and highly tolerant to anaerobic germination and vegetative stage drought stress. Lower tiller production during water stress may be a determinant of its drought tolerance. It is frequently used as a local check or control variety in trials evaluating other short-duration drought-tolerant rice varieties in drought-prone areas.

heat.details: No specific information on heat tolerance found.

salinity.details: Khandagiri is listed among varieties tested for salt tolerance or used in breeding programs for salt-tolerant cultivars. It is included in lists with known salt-tolerant varieties like Lunishree and VTL11. Rhizospheric regions near Khandagiri, India, have yielded bacteria proved to promote salt tolerance in rice seedlings. It has also been part of anther culture research aimed at developing salt-tolerant rice.

flood.details: Khandagiri has been described as tolerant to stagnant flooding and is associated with discussions on flood-tolerant rice.

submergence.details: Khandagiri shows some level of submergence tolerance and has been evaluated in screenings for submergence tolerance, with its association to the Sub1 locus, a key gene for submergence tolerance. It is also highly tolerant to anaerobic germination.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Leaf folder. No other specific disease resistance information found.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Leaf folder. No other specific pest resistance information found.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: No specific genetic markers (SNP/SSR) or QTL positions are identified. However, it has been included in genetic diversity analyses.
genetics_and_qtl.qtl_information: It is associated with research concerning the Sub1 locus, a major QTL for submergence tolerance, though it is not explicitly stated that Chandragiri (Khandagiri) carries the Sub1 gene.
genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Studies have explored its phenological, physiological, and yield markers for drought tolerance, including lower tiller production under water stress. Anther culture response in crosses involving Khandagiri has been studied.

agronomic_performance.yield: As a local check variety, its yield is generally lower than newer high-yielding varieties like Sahbhagi Dhan. Sahbhagi Dhan recorded 35.5-36.5 q/ha, which was 28.6% higher than Khandagiri. Reported yield for Khandagiri ranges from 3000-3200 kg/ha (30-32 q/ha). Farmers have replaced lower-yielding rice varieties like Khandagiri with higher-yielding alternatives in some demonstrations.
agronomic_performance.stability: Yield enhancement over Khandagiri was observed even in normal rainfall years (up to 19%) and during stress years when compared to newer varieties.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Well-adapted to rainfed irrigated uplands and drought-prone upland/shallow lowland environments.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Dwarf statured, with lower tiller production during water stress. Grain to straw ratio found to be lower than Sahabhagidhan.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: Extensive on-farm assessments and cluster demonstrations have been conducted in various districts of Odisha (e.g., Malkangiri, Subarnapur, Gajapati, Kalahandi, Koraput), often using Khandagiri as a control or local check variety to evaluate newer drought-tolerant lines.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KHP-13 (CSC/release name) and KHP-10 (Seednet name), rice

Name note: Searches for KHP-13 and IET 21479 returned direct evidence for KHP-13. Searches for the Seednet name KHP-10 returned records for a different release year and notification. Under each heading I state which name the evidence refers to. Four web searches were run, one per topic.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Evidence for KHP-13 (IET 21479): a row in the IIRR 2018-19 report lists KHP 13 with IET 21479, with abbreviation codes that appear to cover blast, sheath blight and leaf folder reactions. The column legend is not visible in the retrieved text, so these codes are unconfirmed. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- KHP-13 is named as one of the paddy varieties released for commercial cultivation in the hill zone around ZAHRS Mudigere. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- No evidence found for submergence, drought, salinity or heat tolerance specific to KHP-13 or KHP-10.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Evidence for KHP-13: the IIRR row above is the only retrieved entry. Its codes appear to mark moderate reactions to blast and sheath blight (MR-BL, T-SB) and a leaf-folder code (LF). Confirm against the IIRR legend before use. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- Evidence for KHP-10 (not KHP-13): a 2019-era study at Mudigere reports a reaction table of KHP-10 against major hill-zone pests, compared with checks. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290527694_A_new_red_rice_variety_for_Mid_Lands_in_Rainfed_ecosystem_of_Hill_zone_of_Karnataka
- No evidence found for KHP-13 resistance to bacterial leaf blight.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Evidence for KHP-13: the IIRR 2018-19 report lists KHP 13 with a duration figure of 135 in the same row. Whether this is days to maturity is not stated in the retrieved text. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- Evidence for KHP-13 as a parent: the Tunga x KHP 13 cross population was evaluated in the 2023 wet season at ZAHRS Mudigere, with KHP 13 grain starch 79.96% and amylose 23.30% recorded. -- https://geneticsmr.com/index.php/gmr/article/download/3329/2090/8459
- Evidence for KHP-10: the ZAHRS Mudigere programme includes identification of dwarf mutants in KHP-10 after gamma irradiation. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- No evidence found for KHP-13 yield levels, multi-location yield data, or maturity class beyond the row above.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from user record): (M 03-83 x RP-79-5) x Rikuto Norin 21. No independent source in the retrieved results confirms it. No evidence found for QTL or marker studies on KHP-13.
- The Tunga x KHP 13 F4 population was screened with MGIDI-assisted selection for yield and grain traits. -- https://geneticsmr.com/index.php/gmr/article/download/3329/2090/8459

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Keladi Shivappa Nayaka University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences (KSNUAHS, formerly UAHS), Shivamogga, with ZAHRS Mudigere as the rice research station for the hill zone. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Agricultural_and_Horticultural_Sciences,_Shimoga
- Lead rice breeder found: Dr. B. M. Dushyantha Kumar, Senior Professor, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, Navile; listed specialization is rice molecular breeding for biotic and abiotic stress. This is an institutional profile, not evidence that he bred KHP-13. -- https://uahs.edu.in/agricollege-shivamogga/
- Dushyantha Kumar is named as a developer of a different UAHS rice release (Sahyadri Kempumukthi), not KHP-13. -- https://www.deccanherald.com/amp/story/india/karnataka/red-rice-developed-in-shivamogga-takes-on-kerala-variety-1163988.html
- No evidence found naming the original breeder(s) of KHP-13 or IET 21479.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. B. M. Dushyantha Kumar, Senior Professor, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, College of Agriculture, UAHS. Email and phone: No evidence found in the retrieved results.
- Institute postal address: College of Agriculture, UAHS, Navile, Shivamogga – 577225. -- https://uahs.edu.in/agricollege-shivamogga/
- University address: Keladi Shivappa Nayaka UAHS, Iruvakki, Sagar Taluk, Shivamogga – 577412, Karnataka. -- https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- Institute contact page URL: https://uahs.edu.in (the site home page; a specific contact page was not retrieved). Email and phone numbers for the institute: No evidence found in the retrieved results.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2026). Genetics and Molecular Research 25(13s), Tunga x KHP 13 cross, MGIDI-assisted selection, ZAHRS Mudigere. -- https://geneticsmr.com/index.php/gmr/article/download/3329/2090/8459
- Indian Institute of Rice Research (2019). Annual Report 2018-19, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. Multi-location trial table listing KHP 13 / IET 21479 with duration and reaction codes. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf
- Kamaraddi, V. et al. (2015). Assessment of suitability of selected rice varieties for production of expanded rice (includes KHP-10, not KHP-13). Cogent Food & Agriculture 1(1). -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/23311932.2015.1112675
- Kumar, B. M. D. and Shadakshari, Y. G. A new red rice variety for mid lands in rainfed ecosystem of hill zone of Karnataka (includes KHP-10 pest reactions). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290527694_A_new_red_rice_variety_for_Mid_Lands_in_Rainfed_ecosystem_of_Hill_zone_of_Karnataka
- No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to KHP-13 was retrieved. No DOI found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Evidence for KHP-10 in the national notified list: 2008 release, notified 27/08/2009 (S.O. 2187(E)). This is a notification record, not a seed source. -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- No evidence found for KHP-13 or KHP-10 at NSC, Karnataka State Seed Corporation, KVKs, UAHS seed sales, or private dealers. The seed listings retrieved were for unrelated varieties.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Karnataka. Supported by the IIRR 2018-19 row (state code KA) and the UAHS statement that KHP-13 is released for commercial cultivation in the hill zone region. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2018-19.pdf ; https://uahs.edu.in/research-stations/
- Seednet and CSC notification records for KHP-13 or KHP-10 were not retrieved, so the state list is not confirmed from an official notification.

CONFLICTS TO RESOLVE BEFORE USE
- The Seednet name KHP-10 is recorded in the notified list with a 2008 year of release and a 2009 notification. The user record gives a 2018 release for KHP-13. These do not match, so the Seednet entry and the CSC entry may refer to different varieties, or the Seednet name may be mislabelled.
- The IET 21479 and KHP 13 pairing and its alias "Indravathi" appear only in one IIRR table row. Verify against the CSC minutes.

drought.details: KHP-10 is a red rice variety, generally resistant to drought. It is a new red rice variety suitable for Mid Lands in Rainfed ecosystem.

heat.details: KHP-10 is listed in contexts discussing heat tolerance in rice varieties, and participatory validation trials consider heat stress at pollination.

salinity.details: As a red rice variety, KHP-10 exhibits resistance to salinity. It is mentioned in documents discussing salt tolerant rice varieties.

flood.details: Being a red rice variety, KHP-10 is resistant to flood.

disease_resistance.summary: KHP-10 shows resistance to various diseases, including fungal, bacterial, and viral pathogens. As a red rice variety, it possesses inherent anti-fungal and anti-bacterial properties. It is part of studies on disease resistance and evaluated against fungal diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: KHP-10 exhibits resistance or tolerance to major insect pests, including stem borer and leaf pests. It has been identified as a variety with multiple pest resistance.

agronomic_details.field_trials: Yield data for KHP-10 was collected from participatory validation trials. It has been screened in AICRIP paddy trials for resistance to plant pathogens and abiotic stresses like submergence, assessing seedling survival, recovery, and yield.

drought.details: KPH-199 is identified as a short duration, drought tolerant rice variety. It is explicitly listed among flood/drought tolerant rice varieties and described as tolerant to low moisture stress.

heat.details: While heat stress tolerance in rice is a general breeding focus and research area, there is no direct evidence stating that KPH-199 itself possesses heat tolerance.

salinity.details: KPH-199 was included in 'Soil stress tolerant trials' aimed at identifying cultures tolerant to various soil stresses, including salinity, alkalinity, and coastal salinity. Hybrid rice development efforts, under which KPH-199 was released, target tolerance to stress conditions such as salinity. It is also mentioned in ICAR agro-advisories recommending salt tolerant varieties for coastal saline regions.

flood.details: KPH-199 is explicitly listed as a flood tolerant rice variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: KPH 272 (rice, PADDY (DHAN))
Name used: release minutes "KPH 272" and Seednet "KPH 272" are identical strings, so all evidence below refers to the same name. Parentage (KCMS 1090A/KRGOS-722) and release date (2016-08-12) come from the supplied record and were not confirmed by any search result.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name: KPH 272)
- Described in a company report as the first aerobic rice hybrid, with KPH 467 released in the medium-duration segment -- https://www.bseindia.com/bseplus/AnnualReport/532899/5328990317.pdf
- Company literature says its hybrids are bred for tolerance to biotic and abiotic stress in general, but no page ties a specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence score to KPH 272 -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/our-story/details-of-business/

DISEASE AND PEST (name: KPH 272)
- No evidence found. The Kaveri 2013-14 annual report mentions a bacterial leaf blight resistant rice hybrid, but the page does not name KPH 272 as that hybrid, so it is excluded -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: KPH 272)
- In a multi-location comparison, KPH-272 (ME, mid-early) was one of five hybrids yielding 14-26% above the local check CARI Dhan-6 (3.1 t/ha); the trial's location is not stated in the excerpt -- https://www.ijcmas.com/8-6-2019/B.%20Gangaiah.pdf
- A Kaveri annual report describes KPH 272 as "found promising" in rice trials (text truncated, no yield figures) -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/images/pdf/images/annual-reports/annual_report_2013_2014.pdf
- A variety listing gives KPH 272 with values 126-130 and 1.9 in unlabelled columns; the column meanings are not visible, so maturity and yield are not confirmed from this page -- https://www.asiafarming.com/high-yield-hybrid-paddy-rice-varieties-in-india-for-rabi-and-kharif-seasons

GENETICS AND QTL (name: KPH 272)
- No evidence found. Searches returned no QTL, marker or parentage study for KPH 272. The parentage in the record is unverified.

- Developed by Kaveri Seed Company Limited (Hyderabad-based private company); no individual breeder name is linked to KPH 272 in any retrieved page -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
- Company founder listed as G.V. Bhaskar Rao (company history, not a breeder credit) -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/media/corporate-profile/
- No station or research-farm location is linked to KPH 272 specifically; the company reports over 600 acres of its own farm land -- https://www.kaveriseeds.in/

CONTACT DETAILS (name: KPH 272)

The only seller block is an IndiaMART listing for "Kaveri Seed Company Ltd." in Secunderabad with the contact fields not shown in the excerpt; it does not name KPH 272 -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/paddy-17710650830.html
- Institute contact page: not retrieved; the corporate site is https://www.kaveriseeds.in/

PUBLICATIONS (name: KPH 272)

EVIDENCE DIGEST: KRH 4 (variety_name) / KRH-4 (seednet_variety_name), rice

Name note: both names refer to the same hybrid. Every source below uses "KRH-4" (a rice hybrid, not an inbred). No search returned a separate Seednet portal record, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

Search count: 4 web_search queries (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Only maturity and yield-related evidence was found; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was documented for KRH-4 specifically. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- In an aerobic (unpuddled) trial, KRH-4 showed higher water productivity than several comparison varieties, which is a water-use observation rather than a formal stress-tolerance rating. -- https://www.omicsonline.org/open-access/studies-on-response-of-varieties-and-different-dates-of-sowing-onproductivity-of-aerobic-rice-2375-4338-1000142.php?aid=57976
- The Mandya centre report mentions that some hybrids were identified as withstanding moisture stress, but does not name KRH-4 as one of them. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No KRH-4-specific disease or pest resistance was found. The Mandya report describes BPH and blast resistance only for breeding lines in general. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- The Mandya report's udbatta disease seed-treatment advice is general and not tied to KRH-4. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The Mandya report describes KRH-4 as a medium-duration, male-sterile-line hybrid with 130-135 days duration and average yield of 7,500-8,000 kg/ha, compared with a 110-115 day check at 5,000-5,500 kg/ha. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf
- In an aerobic-rice trial, KRH-4 reached 50% flowering in about 92 days and maturity in about 138 days, with higher plant height, tillering and lower weed counts than several comparison varieties. -- https://www.omicsonline.org/open-access/studies-on-response-of-varieties-and-different-dates-of-sowing-onproductivity-of-aerobic-rice-2375-4338-1000142.php?aid=57976
- A farm survey in the southern dry zone of Karnataka (100 respondents: 50 KRH-4 growers, 50 Meenakshi growers) reported higher yield and returns for KRH-4 growers. -- https://www.mathsjournal.com/special-issue/2023/vol8/issue6S/S-8-6-31

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage is recorded as CRMS 32A (female) x MSN36R (male), from an F2 genetic-parameter study. -- https://www.academia.edu/27464972/ASSESSMENT_OF_GENETIC_PARAMETERS_FOR_YIELD_AND_ITS_RELATED_TRAITS_IN_F_2_POPULATION_OF_KRH_4_HYBRID_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L
- The F2 study reports high heritability for 1000-grain weight, flag leaf area and straw weight, and skewed distributions suggesting duplicate and non-additive gene action. -- https://www.academia.edu/27464972/ASSESSMENT_OF_GENETIC_PARAMETERS_FOR_YIELD_AND_ITS_RELATED_TRAITS_IN_F_2_POPULATION_OF_KRH_4_HYBRID_RICE_ORYZA_SATIVA_L
- CRMS 32A is a cold-tolerant CMS line from NRRI (Kalinga-I cytoplasm), and the review lists KRH 4 among hybrids that used it as one of the parents. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489
- No QTL or marker study specific to KRH-4 was found. The QTL study located returned to KRH-2, a different hybrid. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC7427098/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- KRH-4 was developed and released by UAS Bangalore, with ZARS Mandya (under UAS Bangalore) named as the working institute. -- https://www.mathsjournal.com/special-issue/2023/vol8/issue6S/S-8-6-31
- The Mandya centre report lists KRH-1, KRH-2 and KRH-4 among its released hybrids. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

- Release year: the Mandya report contains a "release in 1998" fragment that is ambiguous and may refer to another hybrid. The supplied year 2014-02-14 is unverified and conflicts with the 1998 fragment. -- http://www.icar-iirr.org/AICRIP/Centers/16%20Mandya.pdf

drought.details: The provided search results contain extensive information on drought tolerance for *rice* varieties named 'Krishna', 'Krishna Hamsa', or 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)'. These rice varieties are consistently described as drought tolerant or having introgression lines for drought tolerance, often showing yield advantages under reproductive drought stress. Research identifies superior haplotypes of key drought-responsive genes in 'Krishna' rice varieties and evaluates their performance under water stress. However, no information regarding the drought tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

heat.details: The provided search results indicate research on heat stress tolerance in *rice* involving scientists named 'Krishna' or 'Krishna Jagadish'. These studies focus on physiological and molecular implications of heat stress, including impacts on reproductive development and the role of brassinosteroids in protection against heat-shock. However, no information regarding the heat tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

salinity.details: The provided search results discuss salinity tolerance primarily in *rice* varieties. 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)' is noted as tolerant to coastal salinity. Research also identifies QTLs for reproductive stage salinity tolerance in rice, with 'Krishna H' involved in such studies. No information regarding the salinity tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

flood.details: The provided search results extensively describe flood and waterlogging tolerance in *rice* varieties. 'Satya Krishna (CR Dhan 10)' is described as having stiff straw for water logging situations and being tolerant to complete submergence for 15-17 days. Research involving 'Krishna RM' and 'Krishna T. Sundaram' focuses on combining drought and submergence tolerance in rice. No information regarding the flood tolerance of the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

No information regarding disease resistance for the 'Krishna' lucerne variety (RRB-07-1) was found in the provided results.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: The provided search results refer to genetic markers and QTLs primarily in the context of *rice* varieties. QTLs for reproductive stage salinity tolerance from 'BRRI dhan 47' have been dissected with involvement of 'Krishna H'. The gene `SUB1A` is associated with submergence tolerance in rice, with QTL mapping studies mentioned. Superior haplotypes of key drought-responsive genes in rice are also discussed.

drought.details: Identified as a drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for aerobic and irrigated medium land, and specifically for drought-prone areas of Subarnapur. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1204, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts are focused on developing varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance, involving this variety.

heat.details: It exhibits heat stress tolerance, and molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice, with Kalinga Dhan 1204 being part of these studies.

salinity.details: It has been indicated as tolerant to salinity.

flood.details: Considered flood-tolerant and suitable for semi-deep water conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to sheath-rot and sheath blight.

pest_resistance.summary: No specific pest resistance information for Kalinga Dhan 1204 was found in the provided results.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields include 43.2 q/ha (ICAR Annual Report) and 65 q/ha (Rice-Garud database). Field trials indicate that Kalinga Dhan 1204 performed better than Kalinga Dhan 1201.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly mentioned, but its recommendation for Odisha and involvement in multi-location trials (AICRIP proceedings) suggests general stability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for aerobic and irrigated medium land, as well as semi-deep water conditions, particularly adapted to drought-prone areas.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Characterized by medium slender grain type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been extensively used in experiments, including those designed as Randomized Block Design (RBD) for rice during Kharif, involving various fertilizer treatments. On-Farm Trials have been conducted by KVK Deogarh, where it showed superior performance compared to Kalinga Dhan 1201.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance using this variety. It is also involved in Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) programs for stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specifically mentioned as QTL, but a novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) was isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1204.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Isolation of gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) related to abiotic stress response and drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts are directed towards developing varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought and low soil P.

drought.details: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 is characterized as a short duration drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and recommended for drought-prone areas like Subarnapur. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, has been associated with this variety. Molecular breeding efforts have also been conducted for drought tolerance.

heat.details: The variety exhibits tolerance to heat stress and high temperatures. Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in Kalinga Dhan- 1401.

salinity.details: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 is tolerant to salinity and osmotic stresses.

flood.details: The variety is suitable for semi-deep water conditions and shows tolerance to stagnant flooding.

disease_resistance.summary: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 possesses multiple disease resistance, including resistance to leaf blast, neck blast, brown spot, and bacterial leaf blast. Molecular breeding has been utilized for developing inbuilt resistance to blast.

pest_resistance.summary: The variety demonstrates tolerance to major insect pests, specifically resistance to stem borer (yellow stem borer) and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields vary: 65 q/ha and 76.9 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly detailed.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated ecology, direct sown rainfed conditions, semi-deep water, and lowland environments. Demonstrated performance in drought-prone areas of Subarnapur.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Kalinga Dhan- 1401 is of medium slender grain type. It recorded high germination (77.33%) and maximum survival of seedlings (81.09%).
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated in various trials and discussed in the proceedings of the 57th, 58th, and 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice. Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) has been involved in developing stress-tolerant lines.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs are identified by name, but the development of varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast has been achieved through molecular breeding.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar, and its presence or role is linked with Kalinga Dhan-1401's drought tolerance. Molecular breeding efforts focus on developing resistance/tolerance to various abiotic and biotic stresses.

drought.details: Kalinga Dhan 1501 is a short duration, drought tolerant rice variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and drought-prone areas, specifically mentioned for Subarnapur. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance, was isolated from this cultivar. Molecular breeding efforts have focused on incorporating inbuilt drought resistance/tolerance.

heat.details: The variety exhibits heat stress tolerance, and molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice, including Kalinga Dhan 1501. It is considered a heat tolerant variety.

salinity.details: Kalinga Dhan 1501 is noted as tolerant to salinity.

flood.details: The variety is suitable for semi-deep water conditions, indicating adaptability to certain levels of water stagnation or shallow flooding.

disease_resistance.summary: Kalinga Dhan 1501 is a disease-resistant paddy variety with multiple disease resistance. It is resistant to gall midge biotypes 1, 3, and 4, leaf blast, and bacterial leaf blight (BLB). It exhibits moderate resistance to sheath blight, sheath rot, and neck blast. Molecular breeding has been applied for inbuilt resistance to blast.

pest_resistance.summary: This variety has tolerance to major insect pests. It is tolerant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and resistant to Gall Midge. It also shows moderate resistance to Stem Borer and Leaf folder.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields include 65 q/ha (6500 Kg/ha) and an average grain yield of 4318 Kg/ha. The specific conditions for these yields are not detailed enough to resolve the discrepancy.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Kalinga Dhan 1501 is a non-Basmati variety suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water ecosystems. It has been evaluated in drought-prone areas like Subarnapur.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Maturity duration is reported as 155 days in several sources, while one source indicates 125 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: It is a short bold grain type.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Field evaluations and screenings for drought, heat, salinity, and submergence tolerance have been conducted, including trials at OUAT, Bhubaneswar, and in drought-prone areas of Subarnapur.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), associated with drought tolerance, was isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1501. Molecular breeding has been implemented for the development of rice varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil phosphorus (P), and blast.

drought.details: Kalinga Dhan 1502 is described as a short duration drought tolerant rice variety, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and drought prone areas. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), was isolated from this drought tolerant rice cultivar.

heat.details: The variety has been identified for heat stress tolerance, with molecular markers validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice.

salinity.details: No direct evidence found explicitly stating Kalinga Dhan 1502 is saline tolerant.

flood.details: No direct evidence found explicitly stating Kalinga Dhan 1502 is flood tolerant.

disease_resistance.summary: The variety is moderately resistant to neck blast and sheath blight. It shows resistance to blast and multiple disease resistance to bacterial leaf blast. General screening and evaluation for fungal diseases of rice have been conducted.

pest_resistance.summary: Kalinga Dhan 1502 exhibits tolerance to major insect pests including Stem Borer and gall midge. It has been noted in performance evaluations of multiple pest resistant rice lines.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield is reported as 47.1 q/ha. One source also mentions a yield of 65 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly stated.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Kalinga Dhan 1502 is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water low-land areas, particularly in drought-prone regions of Subarnapur, Odisha.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: It is a non-Basmati rice variety with a short bold grain type, suitable for semi-deep cultivation.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been evaluated in various trials, including those for submergence tolerance and fungicide molecules against fungal diseases, as documented in Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) proceedings.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Molecular markers have been validated for high temperature stress tolerance in rice, and molecular breeding efforts are ongoing for developing varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Specific QTL names or positions are not detailed in the provided results, but the application of molecular breeding indicates a focus on marker-assisted selection for stress tolerance.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene, LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2), has been isolated from Kalinga Dhan 1502, indicating its genetic basis for drought tolerance.

drought.details: The AICRIP 59th Annual Rice Group Meeting draft proceedings list drought stress tolerance screening as a trial theme, and HS-16 appears in the same document's entries (KAU, Trissur). The retrieved snippets do not report any drought score, mechanism, or trial result for HS-16 specifically.

heat.details: The proceedings include a trial on screening for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes, and HS-16 appears in the document. No HS-16-specific heat tolerance data appear in the retrieved snippets.

salinity.details: The proceedings mention that some entries were tolerant to salinity and AG stresses, but the snippet does not link these entries to HS-16. A separate rice-garud snippet describes salinity tolerance for a different variety (GNV 10), not HS-16.

flood.details: No flood tolerance data for HS-16 were found in the retrieved results.

disease_resistance.summary: The rice-garud entry for HS-16 is followed by the text 'Grains: LS, moderately resistant to blast,' which may describe HS-16. The same database also shows 'highly resistant to LB, neck infection' and 'tolerant to cold stress' in snippets that sit near the HS-16 entry. Because the text order in the snippets is ambiguous, these disease traits cannot be confidently attributed to HS-16 and should be verified against the original database entry. The AICRIP proceedings include tungro resistance screening trials, but no HS-16 result was found in the snippets.

pest_resistance.summary: A rice-garud snippet contains 'tolerance to major insect pests, Stem Borer, gall midge' near the HS-16 entry, but the attribution is ambiguous. The AICRIP proceedings discuss yellow stem borer and insect pest studies, without HS-16-specific results. Treat pest resistance as unverified for HS-16.

agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: IT POSSESSES IDEAL PLANT TYPE CHARACTERS WITH COMPARATIVELY MEDIUM PLANT HEIGHT, UPRIGHT LEAVES, SYNCHRONISED TILLERING AND LATE LEAF SENESCENCE. THE GRAINS ARE AWNLESS AND SLIGHTLY BEAKED UNLIKE OTHER VARIETIES.
agronomic_details.field_trials: SUGANDHA SAMBA (digest evidence): (1) Ranked second in region IV (western region) in AICRIP kharif 2008 trials. (2) Farmer trials gave 11.1% higher average yield than Samba Mahsuri. (3) Reported as second-best variety for three consecutive kharif seasons. (4) Yield advantage over checks under late planting (no figures given). SUGANDHA SAMBA (CSC record, not in digest): no trial data given beyond the release record. MAHI SUGANDHA (CSC record, not in digest): highest grain yield when planted in the first week of July (60.33 q/ha), with a drastic yield reduction after July planting; yielded significantly higher than Basmati 370; responsive to nitrogen, with 100 kg N/ha increasing grain yield by 36.6% over 50 kg N/ha (34.2 q/ha); resistant to lodging whereas Basmati 370 is prone to lodging; no shattering observed. No trial results for MAHI SUGANDHA were found in the digest itself.
