search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: SUGANDHA SAMBA (CSC name) / MAHI SUGANDHA (Seednet name), rice (paddy/dhan)

IDENTITY WARNING: The evidence points to two different varieties. The CSC name SUGANDHA SAMBA (RNR 2465) is an Andhra Pradesh variety from ANGRAU, released April 2010 by the state variety release committee, with parentage RNR-M7 x RNR 19994. The Seednet name MAHI SUGANDHA is a semi-dwarf basmati-type variety from Rajasthan (Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur, Regional Research Station Borwat Farm, Banswara). The CSC record's institution (Agriculture Research Station, Banswara) and the Seednet name fit the Mahi Sugandha line. The CSC parentage (BK 79 x Basmati 370) matches neither documented pedigree. Treat the two as unresolved until the CSC minutes and Seednet entry are checked against each other. Findings below are tagged by which name they support.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance. The only related note is a yield advantage over checks under late planting. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Listed as less susceptible to stem borer and gall midge, and moderately susceptible to brown spot, sheath rot, tungro and bacterial leaf blight. These are from quiz/trade pages, not a breeder source. -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of-_______-cr--636d1127752fa37b569acd59 ; https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3420040688.html

DISEASE AND PEST
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: No evidence found for specific disease or pest reaction. Blast tolerance in the 2015 IIRR newsletter table belongs to neighbouring varieties (Krishna, Shobhini), not Sugandha Samba. -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- MAHI SUGANDHA: See the stress entry above (stem borer, gall midge, brown spot, sheath rot, tungro, bacterial leaf blight). -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3014283673.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Semi-dwarf, aromatic, medium-slender, medium duration of 130–135 days, reported yield about 6–7 t/ha under good management. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178 ; https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Ranked second in region IV (western region) in AICRIP kharif 2008 trials. Farmer trials gave 11.1% higher average yield than Samba Mahsuri. Reported as second-best variety for three consecutive kharif seasons. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India ; https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Semi-dwarf (87–98 cm), 129–135 days, yield 45–60 q/ha, best in irrigated areas. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3420040688.html ; https://testbook.com/question-answer/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of-_______-cr--636d1127752fa37b569acd59
- Note: the 130–135 day and yield figures above are from two different varieties and must not be merged.

GENETICS AND QTL
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Pedigree method; female parent RNR-M7 (early samba), male parent RNR 19994. This conflicts with the CSC parentage BK 79 x Basmati 370. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178 ; https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: No QTL, marker or genomic study found. -- No evidence found
- MAHI SUGANDHA: No QTL or marker study found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Developed by the Rice Section, Agricultural Research Institute, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. Named authors on the profile: Surender Raju, B.G. Reddy, R. Jagadeeswar, R.G. Verma, Y. Suryanarayana, L. Krishna, P. Raghava Reddy. Institute and station per the 2015 IIRR newsletter: Surender Raju is Principal Scientist (Rice) and Head of Genetics and Plant Breeding. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India ; https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Developed by the Regional Research Station, Borwat Farm, Banswara (Rajasthan), under Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur. No named breeder found. -- https://uttarpradesh.pscnotes.com/uppsc-upper-mains/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of/

CONTACT DETAILS
- SUGANDHA SAMBA, names and roles: Surender Raju, Principal Scientist (Rice) and Head (G&PB), ANGRAU station as listed in the IIRR newsletter. Also Dr R. Jagadeeswar, Principal Scientist (Plant Pathology), and Dr N. Rama Gopala Varma, Senior Scientist (Entomology). -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- SUGANDHA SAMBA, address as found: Rice Section, Agricultural Research Institute, ANGRAU, P.O. Box 500030, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad. No email or phone found. -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- SUGANDHA SAMBA, seed contact: A 2010-era forum post names a seed supplier (Sudarsana Reddy) and says to contact an email, but the address is not visible in the retrieved text. Not verified. -- https://www.agricultureinformation.com/forums/threads/sugandha-samba-rice.76294/
- MAHI SUGANDHA: No breeder or institute contact details found. Institute-level contact for MPUAT Udaipur or the Banswara RRS was not retrieved. -- No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Raju, S., Reddy, B.G., Jagadeeswar, R., Verma, R.G., Suryanarayana, Y., Krishna, L., Raghava Reddy, P. (year not shown). Sugandha Samba (RNR2465), first-ever high-yielding, aromatic, short-grained rice variety of Andhra Pradesh, India. Technical release document (uploaded copy) -- https://www.scribd.com/doc/64886392/Sugandha-Samba-RNR2465-first-ever-high-yielding-aromatic-short-grained-rice-variety-of-Andhra-Pradesh-India
- Indian Institute of Rice Research (2015). Rice is Life, Vol. 13, No. 2 (IIRR newsletter, lists Sugandha Samba, RNR-M7 x RNR 19994, 135 days, released 2010). Newsletter -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Short and aromatic rice a big hit (2016). The Hans India news article. Newspaper -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP annual report specific to Sugandha Samba was found in the search results. -- No evidence found
- Mahi Sugandha: No peer-reviewed paper or KrishiKosh record was found in the search results. -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Trade listings for "Sugandha Paddy Seed" (Kota, Rajasthan, 50 kg packs) and a Sugandha-named product exist, but the listings do not confirm they are RNR 2465. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/sugandha-paddy-seed-20399096791.html
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: The Scribd document and 2016 article describe distribution as mini-kit testing under AICRIP. No NSC, state seed corporation or SAU sales listing found. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Sold as a basmati variety by trade listings (Salem, New Delhi). No official seed-agency or SAU listing found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mahi-sugandh-basmati-rice-3420040688.html
- Seednet portal: The Seednet entry itself was not reachable through search. -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- SUGANDHA SAMBA: Released in Andhra Pradesh (state variety release committee, April 2010). The CSC record's "Not specified" is unresolved. An Hans India article also lists West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Bihar and north-east states, but the context is cut off, so this is not confirmed as recommendation. -- https://www.thehansindia.com/posts/index/commoner/2016-11-09/short-aromatic-rice-a-big-hit/263178
- MAHI SUGANDHA: Rajasthan origin; declared as a basmati variety under the Seeds Act, 1966. Official recommended-state notification was not found. -- https://testbook.com/question-answer/mahi-sugandha-is-a-variety-of-_______-cr--636d1127752fa37b569acd59

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Malaviya Dhan 5-1 (CSC name) / MALVIYA DHAN-36 (Seednet name), rice

Searches run: 4. The CSC name "Malaviya Dhan 5-1" and code "HUR 5-1" returned no page that names this variety. All evidence below refers to the Seednet name "MALVIYA DHAN-36" unless stated otherwise. Its listing (year 1990, notified 1997) conflicts with the record's release year of 2011, so no link to HUR 5-1 is established.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed for medium and low lands in the agropedia notified-varieties table; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance is recorded -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No other evidence found for Malviya Dhan-36 or HUR 5-1 under this heading.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Described as resistant to major diseases, with grain MS and white -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- The Bihar notified list confirms only the Seednet entry (MALVIYA DHAN-36, year 1990, notified 09/09/1997, S.O. 647(E)); it gives no resistance data -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
- No specific pest or disease resistance evidence for HUR 5-1 found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield 42-45 q/ha, grain type and land type as listed -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- A duration value of 130-135 appears in the same row, but the column is not labelled, so maturity is unconfirmed -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- No multi-location, AICRPR or on-farm trial results naming this variety found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. Parentage "EARLY MUTANT OF MAHSURI" from the record was not confirmed by any retrieved page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder name or developing institution found for Malviya Dhan-36 or HUR 5-1. Searches surfaced Malaviya Manila Sinchit Dhan-1 (BHU/IRRI, different variety), HUR 917, HUR 156 and Malviya Dhan-2 (HUR-3022); these are discarded as other varieties.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact was retrieved that names this variety. Contact pages found (for example IIRR, Hyderabad) are not attributed because they do not name it.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (n.d.). Plant Growth Promotion Assessment in Rice Plant Enhanced by Inoculation of Rhizobacteria. Journal/report not shown; uses Malviya Dhan-36 as a test variety alongside Saryu-52 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274721649_Plant_Growth_Promotion_Assessment_in_Rice_Plant_Enhanced_by_Inoculation_of_Rhizobacteria
- No AICRPR/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or QTL paper naming this variety found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seed-dealer results (Ganga Seed Company, IndiaMART) do not name this variety. The Seednet page retrieved is an index and does not show the Malviya Dhan-36 entry -- https://seednet.gov.in/material/Agriculture_Variety.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Uttar Pradesh, per the agropedia notified-varieties table -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/paddy-varieties-0
- The Bihar notified list records the Seednet entry but gives no state recommendation -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

drought.details: No evidence found for drought tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages. The CPCRI page describes the variety only as high-yielding and suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing, with no abiotic-stress data. The Vittal drip irrigation fact sheet (100% pan evaporation; 45% yield increase, 44% water saving) is for arecanut in general and is not variety-specific.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific disease resistance evidence was found for Madhuramangala. The only disease evidence is general arecanut fruit rot context from a 2012-2019 multi-location network meta-analysis of fungicide trials (Patil et al., 2022), which does not name Madhuramangala and makes no variety comparison. Fruit rot is described as present across most arecanut regions of India.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific pest resistance evidence was found for Madhuramangala.

agronomic_details.yield: Official CPCRI page (earlier entry): 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts per palm per year, or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year. Later CPCRI page: 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year. ResearchGate CPCRI release summary: 4.15 kg chali per palm per year and about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year. Indian-language summary of the same release, citing Ananda et al. (2015) for Madhuramangala (VTL-62): 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50-5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. The sources conflict on units and values; the CSC record field 'average_yield' lists only the unit Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found. The Scribd summary states that Madhuramangala yields above earlier varieties and gives marble-appearing split nuts with a higher market price, but this is not quantified or tied to environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Described by CPCRI as suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing. Recommended states conflict across sources: CPCRI variety page (earlier entry) lists Karnataka and Maharashtra; CPCRI variety page (newer entry, release recorded as 2014) lists Karnataka, West Bengal (North Bengal) and North East; ResearchGate CPCRI release summary lists Karnataka, West Bengal and the North Eastern region. The release year conflicts (record 2013-06-04; CPCRI says 2014) and should be verified against CSC minutes. No agro-climatic or soil data was found.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Per ResearchGate CPCRI release summary: tall type with medium-thick stem, long internodes, partly drooping crown, homogeneous population and regular bearing. Quality note (Scribd summary): marble-appearing split nuts with higher market price.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) CPCRI yield data: 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year (earlier CPCRI page); 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year (later CPCRI page); about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year (ResearchGate CPCRI release summary). (2) Ananda et al. (2015) as cited in an Indian-language summary: 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50-5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. (3) Malnad (Karnataka) cultivar trial: lists Mangala, Mohit Nagar, SAS-1 and Thirthalli local but does not include Madhuramangala, so it gives no comparison for this variety. (4) Vittal drip irrigation fact sheet: 45% yield increase and 44% water saving at 100% pan evaporation for arecanut in general; not variety-specific. No trial-specific design, location, or replication details were found.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. CPCRI Vittal reports that arecanut germplasm was characterised with RAPD and SSR markers, and that markers were developed to separate tall and dwarf types. This is general and not specific to Madhuramangala; no marker positions are given.

disease_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific disease resistance evidence was found for Madhuramangala. The only disease evidence is general arecanut fruit rot context from a 2012-2019 multi-location network meta-analysis of fungicide trials (Patil et al., 2022), which does not name Madhuramangala and makes no variety comparison. Fruit rot is described as present across most arecanut regions of India.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No variety-specific pest resistance evidence was found for Madhuramangala.

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. genetics_and_qtl.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

agronomic_performance.yield: Official CPCRI page (earlier entry): 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts per palm per year, or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year. Later CPCRI page: 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year. ResearchGate CPCRI release summary: 4.15 kg chali per palm per year and about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year. Indian-language summary of the same release, citing Ananda et al. (2015) for Madhuramangala (VTL-62): 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50-5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. The sources conflict on units and values; the CSC record field 'average_yield' lists only the unit Kg/Ha without a value.
agronomic_performance.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data was found. The Scribd summary states that Madhuramangala yields above earlier varieties and gives marble-appearing split nuts with a higher market price, but this is not quantified or tied to environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Described by CPCRI as suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing. Recommended states conflict across sources: CPCRI variety page (earlier entry) lists Karnataka and Maharashtra; CPCRI variety page (newer entry, release recorded as 2014) lists Karnataka, West Bengal (North Bengal) and North East; ResearchGate CPCRI release summary lists Karnataka, West Bengal and the North Eastern region. The release year conflicts (record 2013-06-04; CPCRI says 2014) and should be verified against CSC minutes. No agro-climatic or soil data was found.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Per ResearchGate CPCRI release summary: tall type with medium-thick stem, long internodes, partly drooping crown, homogeneous population and regular bearing. Quality note (Scribd summary): marble-appearing split nuts with higher market price.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) CPCRI yield data: 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year (earlier CPCRI page); 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year (later CPCRI page); about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year (ResearchGate CPCRI release summary). (2) Ananda et al. (2015) as cited in an Indian-language summary: 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50-5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. (3) Malnad (Karnataka) cultivar trial: lists Mangala, Mohit Nagar, SAS-1 and Thirthalli local but does not include Madhuramangala, so it gives no comparison for this variety. (4) Vittal drip irrigation fact sheet: 45% yield increase and 44% water saving at 100% pan evaporation for arecanut in general; not variety-specific. No trial-specific design, location, or replication details were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Madhuramangala. Searches covered the variety name and its CPCRI release pages. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties
Madhuramangala is described only as high-yielding and suited to tender-nut and ripe-nut processing, with no abiotic-stress data. -- https://cpcri.icar.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties

DISEASE AND PEST
No variety-specific disease or pest resistance evidence found. The only disease evidence is general arecanut fruit rot context from a 2012–2019 multi-location meta-analysis of fungicide trials, which does not name Madhuramangala. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9503749/
Fruit rot is described as having appeared across most arecanut regions of India, with no variety comparison. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9503749/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Official CPCRI page gives average yield of 2.95 kg dry tender processed nuts per palm per year, or 3.54 kg dry kernel per palm per year. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties
A later CPCRI page gives 4.15 kg dry kernel per palm per year. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/Arecanut_Varieties
ResearchGate CPCRI release summary gives 4.15 kg chali per palm per year and about 5,600 kg dry kernel per ha per year, and says the variety is a tall type with medium-thick stem, long internodes, partly drooping crown, homogeneous population and regular bearing. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316560015_New_arecanut_varieties_of_ICAR-CPCRI
Indian-language summary of the same release cites Ananda et al. (2015) for Madhuramangala (VTL-62) at 3.53 kg dry kernel per palm per year, or 4.50–5.00 t dry kernel per ha per year. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316560015_New_arecanut_varieties_of_ICAR-CPCRI
Scribd summary says Madhuramangala yields above earlier varieties and gives marble-appearing split nuts with higher market price. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/711066584/NewarecanutvarietiesofICAR-CPCRI
Vittal-station fact sheet gives drip irrigation at 100% pan evaporation for arecanut (45% yield increase, 44% water saving), but it is not variety-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357955501_ICAR-CPCRI_Vittal_-in_the_service_of_farming_community
A Malnad (Karnataka) cultivar trial lists Mangala, Mohit Nagar, SAS-1 and Thirthalli local but not Madhuramangala, so it gives no comparison for this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/351969454_Performance_of_different_Arecanut_Areca_catechu_L_cultivars_under_Malnad_region_of_Karnataka

GENETICS AND QTL
Madhuramangala is a selection from indigenous germplasm, not a hybrid, and its parentage is not recorded in the sources. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/production-technology-of-arecanut-areca-catechu-l-pdf/271842751
CPCRI Vittal reports that germplasm was characterised with RAPD and SSR markers, and that markers were developed to separate tall and dwarf arecanut types. This is general, not Madhuramangala-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357955501_ICAR-CPCRI_Vittal_-in_the_service_of_farming_community
No QTL or marker-trait study for Madhuramangala found. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357955501_ICAR-CPCRI_Vittal_-in_the_service_of_farming_community

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-CPCRI Regional Station, Vittal, Dakshina Kannada, Karnataka. Madhuramangala is listed among varieties developed and released there. -- https://cpcri.gov.in/page/article/cpcri_crop_improvement
Release was by the Central Sub-committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties for Horticultural Crops, Ministry of Agriculture, New Delhi. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316560015_New_arecanut_varieties_of_ICAR-CPCRI

Vittal station history: formerly the Central Arecanut Research Station, which became the CPCRI Regional Station. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316560015_New_arecanut_varieties_of_ICAR-CPCRI

drought.details: MGD 101 exhibits inbuilt tolerance to drought and is described as a short duration drought tolerant rice variety. It is considered suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, which are often associated with drought stress. It was also mentioned in contexts discussing abiotic stress like drought.

heat.details: MGD 101 (IET-19554) is listed among short duration elite rice cultures, and its heat tolerance has been part of perusal. It is also mentioned in discussions regarding specific tolerance mechanisms for heat stress.

salinity.details: MGD 101 is mentioned in the context of processing Saltol QTL for salinity tolerance and in general discussions about identifying salt tolerant, high-yielding varieties. However, there is no direct evidence explicitly stating MGD 101 itself possesses high salinity tolerance.

flood.details: MGD 101 is mentioned in a survey that discusses the need for flood tolerant varieties, but it is not explicitly stated as being flood tolerant.

disease_resistance.summary: MGD 101, along with MTU-1001, recorded a higher incidence of disease in an assessment for upland situations in Uttara. It is mentioned in the context of research for developing disease-resistant varieties, but is not explicitly identified as resistant itself.

pest_resistance.summary: MGD 101, along with MTU-1001, recorded a higher incidence of insect pests in an assessment for upland situations in Uttara. It is mentioned in the context of research for developing pest-resistant varieties, but is not explicitly identified as resistant itself.

agronomic_details.yield: Under System of Rice Intensification (SRI) practice, MGD 101, serving as a local check, recorded a grain yield of 8.38 t/ha (83.8 Q/ha). However, in upland situations of Uttara, MGD 101 showed lower gross returns, net return, and B:C ratio compared to the Sahabagidhan variety.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly specified.
agronomic_details.adaptation: MGD 101 is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and has been assessed for upland situations. Its duration is approximately 125-130 days.

It frequently served as a 'Local Check' in these trials.

drought.details: MR 8666 is reported to be tolerant to moisture stress and was mentioned in the context of developing drought tolerant varieties. It was also tested for drought tolerance.

heat.details: MR 8666 (IET 24990) was mentioned in the context of screening varieties for tolerance to heat stress and the development of high temperature tolerant rice varieties.

salinity.details: MR 8666 was tested for salinity tolerance and its yield performance was noted in the context of coastal saline eco-systems. It is also mentioned in the context of breeding for multi-stress tolerant varieties, including salinity.

flood.details: No direct evidence found specifically indicating flood tolerance for MR 8666.

disease_resistance.summary: MR 8666 is moderately resistant to leaf blast and false smut. It is also reported to be resistant to brown spot, sheath-rot, and bacterial blight (BLB). It was involved in development programs for pyramiding resistance to blast, BLB, and false smut.

pest_resistance.summary: MR 8666 is reported to be tolerant to stem borer and resistant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and gall midge.

agronomic_details.yield: MR 8666 has an average yield of 70 quintals per hectare (q/ha), or 6945 kg/ha, noted from trials.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly stated, but its recommendation for multiple states (Odisha, Uttar Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh) suggests good adaptability.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated conditions, and mentioned in the context of Central and Western Zones of India.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Tested in Initial Hybrid Rice Trial – Medium slender (IHRT - MS) where it showed a yield of 6945 kg/ha. It was also part of screenings for various abiotic stresses (drought, salinity, submergence, low temperature, low light) and biotic stresses (diseases and pests).

drought.details: No evidence found in searched sources for drought tolerance in MTU 1223. Searches returned only unrelated varieties, which were excluded.

heat.details: MTU 1223 is listed in the 'tolerant' group (spikelet fertility above 65%, with yield and MTS above threshold) in a 2025 preprint screening, and it is named as a candidate for heat-tolerance breeding. The source is a preprint that has not been peer-reviewed, and the name matches the variety in the title only. The classification is therefore provisional and should be confirmed by peer-reviewed or field evidence.

salinity.details: No evidence found in searched sources for salinity tolerance in MTU 1223.

flood.details: No variety-specific evidence found for flood tolerance. Results for MTU 1184 and MTU 1140 were excluded as other varieties.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast and bacterial leaf blight (BLB): sources conflict and the level must be confirmed before recording. The release description states tolerance to BLB and blast in one place. The trait table states resistance to blast and BLB, and also records moderate tolerance to bacterial leaf blight, leaf blast and neck blast. No further detail was found. Other diseases: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem borer: moderate tolerance recorded. Brown planthopper: no variety-specific resistance rating found. Rodents: no resistance rating found; the rodent study reports only compensation ability after damage (MTU-1223 was one of twelve varieties tested), not resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Station trials at RARS Maruteru (2011-2013): 27.4% higher grain yield than the national check MTU 7029. Multilocation testing (seven locations, two years): 15.5% yield advantage over MTU 7029 (Swarna). Absolute yield in kg/ha: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.stability: Multilocation testing over seven locations for two years, and All India Coordinated trials across zones (see field_trials). Stability indices: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released for rainfed shallow lowland ecology of Odisha and Bihar. An ANGRAU report states that the variety is grown on more than one lakh hectares in rainfed uplands of Chhattisgarh. This is a cultivation-area claim and not an official recommendation.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-erect plant type; non-lodging with a strong culm; about two weeks of seed dormancy; low shattering (under 2%). Highest total tiller count per square metre among eight varieties in a 2024 crop-growth study.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Station trials at RARS Maruteru, 2011-2013: 27.4% higher grain yield than national check MTU 7029. (2) Multilocation testing over seven locations for two years: 15.5% yield advantage over MTU 7029 (Swarna). (3) All India Coordinated trials: 11.59%, 7.99%, 9.27% and 7.13% higher yield than national, zonal, hybrid and local checks, respectively. Zone III: 16.51%, 12.67%, 22.11% and 11.72% higher yield than the same checks. (4) 2024 crop-growth study among eight varieties: highest total tiller count per square metre. (5) Rodent damage study among twelve varieties: compensation ability tested; no resistance result reported.

(2) Multilocation testing over seven locations for two years: 15.5% yield advantage over MTU 7029 (Swarna). Zone III: 16.51%, 12.67%, 22.11% and 11.72% higher yield than the same checks. (4) 2024 crop-growth study among eight varieties: highest total tiller count per square metre. (5) Rodent damage study among twelve varieties: compensation ability tested; no resistance result reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Heat: MTU 1223 is listed in the "tolerant" group (spikelet fertility above 65%, yield and MTS above threshold) in a 2025 preprint screening, and it is named as a candidate for heat-tolerance breeding. This is a preprint, not peer-reviewed, and the name matches the variety in the title only, so treat it as provisional. -- https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202509.0232
- Lodging: the variety is described as a non-lodging type with a strong culm. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Drought, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The searches returned only unrelated varieties (for example MTU 1184 and MTU 1140 for flood and submergence), which I excluded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast and bacterial leaf blight: the release description says it is tolerant to BLB and blast in one place, and the trait table says resistant to blast and BLB. The same table also records moderate tolerance to bacterial leaf blight, leaf blast and neck blast, so the sources conflict and the level of resistance should be confirmed before it is recorded. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348180573_MTU_1223_Varsha_a_high_yielding_non-lodging_rice_variety_released_for_Rainfed_shallow_lowland_ecology_of_Odisha_and_Bihar
- Stem borer: moderate tolerance recorded. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Brown planthopper, rodents: No variety-specific resistance rating found. The rodent study only reports compensation ability, not resistance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Parentage and pedigree: developed from MTU 1081 × MTU 1064 by pedigree breeding over 2007–2010. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Station trials at RARS Maruteru (2011–2013): 27.4% higher grain yield than the national check MTU 7029. -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/MTU-1223-(Varsha),-a-high-yielding,-non-lodging-for-Rao-Adilakshmi/d679fc182575b6c49f1be7a36329426d3ae86fd4
- Multilocation testing over seven locations for two years: 15.5% yield advantage over MTU 7029 (Swarna). -- same URL
- All India Coordinated trials: 11.59%, 7.99%, 9.27% and 7.13% higher yield than national, zonal, hybrid and local checks. Zone III: 16.51%, 12.67%, 22.11% and 11.72%. -- same URL
- Agronomy and duration: 150 days; semi-erect plant type; two weeks seed dormancy; low shattering (under 2%). -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Crop-growth study (2024): MTU-1223 recorded the highest total tiller count per square metre among eight varieties. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue8/PartJ/7-8-97-149.pdf
- Rodent damage study: MTU-1223 was among twelve varieties tested for compensation ability after rodent damage. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree only (MTU 1081 × MTU 1064). No marker, QTL or gene-introgression study specific to MTU 1223 was found. The MTU1010 marker-assisted paper that appeared in the results concerns a different variety and was excluded. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Note: the parentage field in the input record reads "Not specified", but the released-variety paper gives the parentage above. Update the record.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348180573_MTU_1223_Varsha_a_high_yielding_non-lodging_rice_variety_released_for_Rainfed_shallow_lowland_ecology_of_Odisha_and_Bihar
- Lead author/scientist named in the release paper: Venkata Ramana Rao (first author), with co-authors listed under PUBLICATIONS. The paper does not state which author is the lead breeder; this is inferred from authorship order only. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf
- Breeder-seed indents: ANGRAU's own 2024 impact report lists MTU 1223 breeder-seed indents from the Government of India (0.0 quintals in 2020, 17.8 in 2021). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390283915_ANGRAU_VAR_IMPACT_2024

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for an individual breeder email, phone or postal address for MTU 1223. The searches returned no ANGRAU or RARS Maruteru contact page. Verify the institute contact at the ANGRAU website before recording. -- searched via https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2020/vol8issue6/PartW/8-6-312-273.pdf (no contact details on page)
- Names given on the release paper (authors, not contacts): Venkata Ramana Rao; D. Adilakshmi; Satyanarayana PV; Girija Rani M; Chamundeswari N; Ravi Kumar BNVSR; Suryanarayana Y; Padmavathi G; Bhuvaneswari V; Krishnam Raju S; Mallikarjuna Rao; Nanda Kishore M. No email or phone was found for any of them.

- Rao VR, Adilakshmi D, Satyanarayana PV, Girija Rani M, Chamundeswari N, Ravi Kumar BNVSR, Suryanarayana Y, Padmavathi G, Bhuvaneswari V, Krishnam Raju S, Mallikarjuna Rao, Nanda Kishore M (2020). MTU 1223 (Varsha), a high yielding, non-lodging rice variety released for Rainfed shallow lowland ecology of Odisha and Bihar. International Journal of Chemical Studies 8(6):1625-1630 -- DOI 10.22271/chemi.2020.v8.i6w.10998 ; https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (2025). Identification of Heat-Tolerant Rice Genotypes through Phenotypic Selection and Multi-Trait Characterization for Genetic Diversity. Preprint (not peer-reviewed) -- https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202509.0232
- Authors not shown in the search snippet (2024). Effect of rice varieties on crop growth (MTU-1223 included). International Journal of Research in Agronomy 7(8):724-729 -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2024/vol7issue8/PartJ/7-8-97-149.pdf
- Authors not shown in the search snippet. Crop Compensation to Rodent damage in Rice Varieties. Field study, journal not confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties
- Not searched: KrishiKosh theses and AICRP/ICAR annual reports. No evidence found in this search set.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Seednet portal listing: not retrieved. No evidence found for the Seednet entry under either name (MTU 1223 or MTU-1223). The search did not reach seednet.gov.in directly.
- Scale of seed use: the ANGRAU rice-basket report says MTU Rice 1223 is grown on more than one lakh hectares in rainfed uplands of Chhattisgarh. This is a cultivation-area claim, not a seed-sales channel. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- State seed corporations: the Andhra Pradesh state seed body lists other ANGRAU varieties but not MTU 1223 in the retrieved snippet. No evidence found for MTU 1223 from this source. -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
- Odisha seed sales: the Odisha State Seed Corporation's availability page lists other paddy varieties, not MTU 1223, in the retrieved text. No evidence found. -- http://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
- Private dealers: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha and Bihar, for rainfed shallow lowland ecology, released as a straight variety by the 54th Central Varietal Identification Committee meeting in 2019. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/?year=2020&vol=8&issue=6&ArticleId=10998&si=false
- Release-year discrepancy: the input record says 2020-11-09, but the source says the release was at the 2019 CVIC meeting, and the paper was published in November 2020. Use the 2019 committee date and verify the notification date against the CSC/Seednet record.
- Chhattisgarh and West Bengal appear in ANGRAU's report as states where MTU 1223 is grown or seed is used. These are not official recommendations and were not added to the recommended-state list. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

Search coverage was limited: the search tool's quota ran out after the first set of four queries, so I could read only titles, URLs and short snippets, not full pages. Findings are limited to those snippets.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page describing disease or pest resistance for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Impact study of Swarna (MTU-7029) on yield and farmer income in the Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh (ResearchGate PDF; authors and year not visible in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/374673803_Impact_of_Swarna_MTU-7029_Rice_Variety_on_Yield_and_Income_of_Farmers_in_Godavari_Zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The searches returned no QTL or marker study for this variety. The parentage given in the input (VASISTA/MAHSURI) was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The IIRR 2015 newsletter credits MTU7029 to a station it calls "this station" and reports three MTU varieties released from it; the page names no breeder and I could not confirm that the station is Maruteru -- https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name was found in any result. The input lists the institution as Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, which was not verified against a result.

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: conflicting reports. One source lists resistance to blast (Cottondora Sannalu / MTU-1010, yield 74 Q/ha). search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: Sources use "MTU 1010", "MTU-1010" and "Cottondora Sannalu" for one rice variety. The pages below refer to that variety, so the name evidence applies to both the release-minutes name and the Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast resistance is reported for the variety, and one source also lists BPH tolerance. Cottondora Sannalu (MTU-1010) is listed with resistance to blast and tolerance to BPH, with a yield of 74 Q/ha. -- https://drdpat.bih.nic.in/Rice%20Varieties%20-%2010.htm
- Blast reaction is conflicting. MTU1010 is highly susceptible to BB and has only a moderate level of tolerance to blast disease. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Another source describes it as showing tolerance to leaf blast. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- Low soil phosphorus: average performance in low phosphorus soil is recorded for the variety. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- Salinity: a 2024-era trial summary (PIB) reports MTU 1010 at 3199 kg/ha under inland saline conditions, against 3508 kg/ha for IET 32043. The comparison is with a different line, so this is trial context, not a tolerance rating for MTU 1010. -- https://static.pib.gov.in/WriteReadData/specificdocs/documents/2025/nov/doc20251126707201.pdf
- Salinity claim from a dealer listing only: the product page lists the seed as Non-Shattering, Blast Resistant, Salt Tolerant. This is a seller claim, not a breeder or trial finding. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/mtu-1010-paddy-seed-23601139891.html
- Drought, heat, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: MTU1010 is highly susceptible to BB. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Sheath blight and BPH: It demonstrates susceptibility to leaf and sheath blight, as well as BPH. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- BPH tolerance is also reported: the variety is estimated to be cultivated in >12% of Indian rice areas, due to its wider adaptability along with good level of tolerance to BPH. The BPH sources conflict. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Rodent damage: a field study reports that MTU-1010 (93.65%) showed high percentage of total maturity period but is not a resistance rating. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/389717720_Crop_Compensation_to_Rodent_damage_in_Rice_Varieties

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and yield: It is of medium-duration maturity (120 days) ... with a high yielding capacity of six to seven tons/ha. -- https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371%2Fjournal.pone.0260535
- Producibility: MTU 1010 (Cottondora Sannalu)= 1600-1800Kgs. / acre -- https://rkb-odisha.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/MTU-1010.pdf
- Plant type and grain: Medium tall; Sturdy stem, with Medium slender and he

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The search returned no page that reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for MTU 1121. The one relevant page I found mentions only non-lodging habit. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No retrieved page reports blast, BLB, sheath blight, BPH or other disease or pest reaction for MTU 1121.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Title of a ResearchGate record describes MTU 1121 (Sri Druthi) as a high-yielding, non-lodging rice variety released for irrigated wetlands of Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
No maturity, yield figures or multi-location trial data were visible in the retrieved text. Yield claims are not verified.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: a ResearchGate abstract snippet states MTU 1121 was developed from a cross between BPT 5204 and MTU BB 8-24. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
No QTL or marker study was found. The input record lists parentage as "Not specified", so this cross is a finding that should be checked against the CSC or ANGRAU source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
No breeder name was found for MTU 1121. The input record names Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) as the institution. Breeding is probably linked to the Maruteru rice station, but no retrieved page confirms this for this variety. The ICAR-IIRR 2015 newsletter (https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf) was discarded: its matching text concerns MTU 1153, a different variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for ANGRAU, its rice research station, or any breeder was returned by the search.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). MTU 1121 (SRI DRUTHI)-A high yielding non lodging rice variety released for cultivation in irrigated wetlands of Andhra Pradesh. ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or DOI was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for MTU 1121. Results for "MTU" seed were about other varieties (MTU 7029, BPT 5204, MTU 1010) from a Varanasi trader, and were discarded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for MTU 1121 was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Andhra Pradesh -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH
This matches the input record and the release title.

NAME AND SEARCH NOTES
Seednet name "MTU 1212": searched once in a combined query. Nothing relevant came back, so there is no Seednet evidence under that name.
Search budget: one batch of four queries ran. A second search call then hit the tool's usage limit, so the planned breeder/contact, seed-availability and trial searches could not be completed. Those headings are therefore incomplete. The release date (2016-08-12) comes from the input record and was not verified by search.

drought.details: Identified as drought tolerant, suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions, and developed through molecular breeding for drought tolerance. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is associated with this research area.

heat.details: Exhibits heat stress tolerance and is screened for high temperature tolerance. Research efforts focus on developing varieties for tolerance to heat stress.

salinity.details: Described as salinity tolerant and tolerant to AG stresses. Has been part of screenings for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: The variety's adaptation ecology mentions 'flood prone to drylands', but no specific flood tolerance level is stated, rather submergence tolerance is highlighted.

disease_resistance.summary: Highly resistant to Leaf Blight (LB) and neck infection. Resistant to neck blast and rice tungro virus.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH).

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield of 79.7 quintals per hectare (q/ha) under irrigated, transplanted conditions.
agronomic_details.stability: Not explicitly stated.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for irrigated, transplanted conditions and also for direct sown rainfed conditions. Adapted to environments ranging from high humidity to arid temperatures, and flood prone to drylands.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi dwarf (82 cm), with LS (Long Slender) grains.
agronomic_details.field_trials: MTU 1212 (IET 26819) has been part of various trials, including Annual Rice Group Meetings (ARGM) proceedings for stress tolerance screenings (e.g., submergence, high temperature).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) is involved in developing stress-tolerant varieties, including for drought, heat, and submergence stress tolerance. An abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar is a focus in related research.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not specifically mentioned for MTU 1212, but molecular breeding efforts are ongoing for resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Isolation of LOC_Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) gene, related to drought tolerance. Bisulphite sequencing mentioned in the context of heat stress research.

drought.details: MTU 1280 is identified as a drought-tolerant variety suitable for direct-sown rainfed conditions. It is also mentioned in the context of drought tolerant 'water-less' rice varieties being developed. Molecular breeding efforts include developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: The variety MTU 1280 (IET 27705) is included in proposals for varieties with tolerance to heat stress. It is also part of discussions and screenings for high temperature tolerance in rice genotypes.

salinity.details: MTU 1280 is described as tolerant to salinity. It was also identified as an entry tolerant to salinity during screenings.

flood.details: Direct explicit information on flood tolerance as a distinct trait for MTU 1280 is not specified; however, it exhibits submergence tolerance, which is related to flooding conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Conflicting information exists regarding bacterial blight. One source states MTU 1280 is 'resistant to bacterial blight', while other sources, specifically studies on bacterial leaf blight, found it to be 'severe in MTU 1280'. Additionally, it is stated to be highly resistant to LB (Leaf Blight) and neck infection, and moderately resistant to SB (Stem Borer).

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately resistant to SB (Stem Borer). No other specific pest resistances are explicitly detailed.

agronomic_details.yield: Observed yield values for MTU 1280 reported in ANGRAU annual reports include 8051 and 7676 (units unclear, possibly kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not specified
agronomic_details.adaptation: MTU 1280 is suitable for irrigated and wetland ecosystems. It is also suited for direct sown rainfed conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: The variety is semi-dwarf, with a reported height of 82 cm. Grains are described as LS (likely Long Slender).
agronomic_details.field_trials: MTU 1280 has been evaluated in various trials and Annual Rice Group Meetings, with proposals submitted for irrigated conditions. It is frequently listed in performance tables and discussions within these proceedings, including under its IET designation (IET 27705).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: General mention of Marker Assisted Selection (MAS) in the context of developing stress tolerant varieties. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_.Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) was isolated from a drought-tolerant rice cultivar in related research. Molecular breeding for developing rice varieties with inbuilt resistance/tolerance to drought, low soil P, and blast has been conducted.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No specific QTLs identified for MTU 1280 in the provided results.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Research includes bisulphite sequencing under heat stress and molecular breeding approaches for stress tolerance.

commercial_info.availability_status: MTU 1280 was released in 2021 and is listed among crop varieties released at the national level by CVRC (Central Variety Release Committee). heat.details: MTU 1281 was part of 'Screening for high temperature tolerance in Rice genotypes' and general heat stress tolerance studies.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MTU Rice 1232 (CSC minutes name) / MTU Rice 1273 (Seednet name), IET 26422, rice

Search note: the search budget ran out during a fifth call, so this digest rests on four searches. I did not search the Seednet name "MTU Rice 1273" separately, so no finding below is attributed to it. Snippets were read as returned and not verified against full pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Submergence and flash-flood tolerance: the variety is described as highly tolerant to submergence and flash floods for up to about one month (evidence refers to MTU Rice 1232) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity: No evidence found for MTU Rice 1232. The same PDF mentions salinity tolerance only for a different variety, MCM Rice 103.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity, yield, and multi-location results: No evidence found specifically for MTU Rice 1232. A Chhattisgarh head-to-head trial report compares a new ANGRAU-type variety against MTU 1010, but it does not name MTU Rice 1232 -- https://zenodo.org/records/10399232

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for MTU 1239 (Sravani) specifically. The ANGRAU rice-basket document describes MTU Rice 1273 (seednet name) as an introgressed line of MTU 1010 with BPH and blast tolerance, but that is a different variety and is discarded here -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for MTU 1239 specifically. Pest and disease resistance statements found for MTU 1273 and MTU 1293 refer to those varieties, not MTU 1239 -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
MTU 1239 is listed as a pre-released medium-slender (MS) grain type in a 2020 grain-quality study, which conflicts with the CSC year of release 2020-11-09 in the record; the release date is unverified -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue1S/PartD/S-9-6-192-912.pdf
Kharif 2021 genetic-variability trial at RARS Maruteru used Sravani (MTU 1239) as one of the checks among 88 elite lines (no yield values in the snippet) -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boggavarapu-Kumar
Breeder-seed indent figures for MTU 1239 appear in the 2021 Mega Rice Varietal Display analysis, with a value of 8.3 for the row listing MTU 1239 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/382028084_Impact_Analysis_of_Angrau_Mega_Rice_Varietal_Display_Melas
Yield, maturity and duration for MTU 1239: No evidence found. Yield and duration figures found on pages for MTU 1271/1262 and Swarna refer to other varieties and are discarded -- https://gonefarmers.com/products/mtu-1271-marteru-paddy-seeds-andhra-pradesh

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The SSR genetic-diversity paper on elite Indian rice varieties does not name MTU 1239 in the retrieved text -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/373f1c99-cc1e-40b7-823f-5ed4fa44563a/content

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, West Godavari, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
Dr P. V. Satyanarayana's ANGRAU profile lists MTU 1239 (Sravani) among varieties on his page, but the snippet does not show whether he is lead or second breeder, so the attribution is unconfirmed -- https://angrau.ac.in/ANGRU/Research_Stations_Profiles.aspx?name=PVSatyanarayana
Boggavarapu N. V. S. R. Ravi Kumar (ANGRAU rice breeder) appears only in a trial that used MTU 1239 as a check; he is not linked to MTU 1239 as breeder, so no attribution is made -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boggavarapu-Kumar

CONTACT DETAILS

Institute address as found in the ANGRAU VAR IMPACT 2024 document: Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru and ANGRAU, Lam, Guntur (no postal code, phone or email found) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390283915_ANGRAU_VAR_IMPACT_2024
Official ANGRAU email or phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS

Indian conference proceedings (IJAS conference series; journal name not confirmed in snippet). Authors not found (2024). ANGRAU VAR IMPACT 2024. ResearchGate report -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390283915_ANGRAU_VAR_IMPACT_2024
Kumar, B. et al. (2021 kharif trial, RARS Maruteru; authors and title not fully retrieved). Genetic parameters study using Sravani (MTU 1239) as a check. ResearchGate profile, no DOI -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Boggavarapu-Kumar
No KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report naming MTU 1239 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Sravani (MTU 1239) is reported as grown in Chhattisgarh on about 1.30 lakh ha (not a recommended state in the record) -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
AP State Seeds (APSSDCL) lists other ANGRAU paddy varieties for production but not MTU 1239 -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx

Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra: no evidence found that MTU 1239 is recommended in these states. Chhattisgarh is the only state where MTU 1239 cultivation area is reported -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

NAME AND RECORD NOTES
MTU Rice 1273 (seednet name): the only evidence found refers to a 2022 CVRC release that is an introgressed line of MTU 1010, not MTU 1239 -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf. Under this record it should be treated as a separate variety and not merged with MTU 1239.

heat.details: Heat tolerance was not reported in the retrieved text. No evidence found.

salinity.details: ANGRAU's 2022 keynote on its CVRC releases describes MTU 1293 as tolerant to salinity. The source gives no graded score, so the degree of tolerance is not known and the level is recorded as unknown.

flood.details: Flood tolerance: No evidence found.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance to blast is reported for MTU 1293. The keynote describes MTU 1273 and MTU 1293 together and does not separate the two varieties on this trait, so the claim applies to the pair. No variety-specific disease screening data were found beyond this.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerance to brown planthopper (BPH) is reported for MTU 1293. As with blast, the keynote gives this for the MTU 1273/1293 pair without separating them. A farmer-preference study mentions pest and disease resistance, but it refers to a group of varieties and was excluded as not variety-specific. No variety-specific pest screening data were found beyond the pair statement.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
**EVIDENCE DIGEST: MTU Rice 1293 (variety_name "MTU Rice 1293"; seednet_variety_name "MTU Rice 1293"; both names were searched and the sources use "MTU 1293" and "MTU Rice 1293" interchangeably, so the findings below refer to the same variety)**

Note: four searches were run. None targeted seednet.gov.in directly, and no institute or SAU page for this variety was retrieved.

**STRESS TOLERANCE**
- Tolerant to salinity, per ANGRAU's 2022 keynote on its CVRC releases. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- The same keynote describes MTU 1273 and MTU 1293 together as having non-shattering panicles and tolerance to BPH and blast, but does not separate the two varieties on these traits. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Listed for drought-prone areas in the ICAR Kharif advisory for Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Flood, submergence, heat and drought tolerance were not reported in the retrieved text. Flood tolerance: No evidence found.

**DISEASE AND PEST**
- BPH and blast tolerance is reported for the 1273/1293 pair (see above). -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Farmer-preference study notes that farmers in the Godavari zone choose MTU 1293 partly for pest and disease resistance, but the statement applies to the group of varieties. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- No variety-specific pest or disease screening data found beyond the above.

**AGRONOMY AND TRIALS**
- Short duration: the 1273/1293 pair is reported at 115–120 days. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Grain type: long slender, kernel length above 6 mm. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Market: MTU 1293 is named among long slender varieties to promote for export, under MoU with exporters or FCI, because of low raw-rice preference. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Late planting is recommended for MTU 1293 in the Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Yield data for MTU 1293: No evidence found.

**GENETICS AND QTL**
- Pedigree: described as a short-duration introgressed line derived from MTU 1010; this is the only parentage evidence and the CSC record lists parentage as not specified. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- QTL or marker studies specific to MTU 1293: No evidence found. The marker-assisted study on MTU1010 (Pup1, Xa21, Pi54) is about a different variety and was discarded.

**BREEDER AND INSTITUTION**
- Released in 2022 through the Central Variety Release Committee by ANGRAU. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
- Developing station: Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, West Godavari, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. Author and affiliation lines in the retrieved keynote and 2025 paper do not give the breeder's name.

**CONTACT DETAILS**
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact found.
- Institute-level: RARS Maruteru is located in Maruteru village, West Godavari district, Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Institute description (coordinates, establishment history): https://icar-iirr.org/IIRR%20NL%20Apr_June_2015.pdf
- Official email, phone, postal address or contact page URL: No evidence found.

**PUBLICATIONS**
- ANGRAU keynote, "ANGRAU's Contribution to the State and National Rice Baskets" (2022). Journal of Rice Research, Special Issue (DOI 10.58297/WPKW6269). Author list not captured in retrieved text. -- https://doi.org/10.58297/WPKW6269
- Varietal preference of rice growers, millers and consumers in Godavari zone of Andhra Pradesh (2025). International Journal of Research in Agronomy 8(5): 421–425. Author list not captured in retrieved text. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue5/PartF/8-5-51-625.pdf
- Same study, ResearchGate version. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391861761_Varietal_preference_of_rice_growers_millers_and_consumers_in_Godavari_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
- Peer-reviewed field trial, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to MTU 1293: No evidence found.

**SEED AVAILABILITY**
- No seed-seller, KVK, SAU seed sales or State Seed Corporation listing for MTU 1293 was found. Results for MTU 1262, MTU 1010, Swarna and other varieties were discarded.
- The Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation page was retrieved, but its text did not name MTU 1293. -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx
- Seednet portal listing: No evidence found (not searched).

**RECOMMENDED STATES**
- Andhra Pradesh: recommended for the Godavari zone and listed for drought-prone areas and late planting. -- https://www.icar.org.in/sites/default/files/Circulars/ICAR-En-Kharif-Agro-Advisories-for-Farmers-2025.pdf
- Telangana: No evidence found in any retrieved source. The CSC record's Telangana recommendation is not confirmed.

No individual breeder for MTU Rice 1310 was named. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
MTU Rice 1321 is described as high yielding, medium duration, with medium slender grain, high head rice recovery and suitability for raw rice. No yield figures, maturity days or trial data for this variety were found. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf (Journal of Rice Research 2022 Special Issue, pp. 64-66)

GENETICS AND QTL
No evidence found. The marker-assisted study on MTU1010 (DOI 10.1371/journal.pone.0260535) concerns a different variety and was discarded. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC8803164/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Parentage: not specified and not found.
Lead breeder: no name found. The ANGRAU review lists author affiliations (a Scientist (Rice) at RARS Maruteru, a Principal Scientist at Maruteru, and a PS and Head of Crop Improvement for the AICRP on Rice at ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad), but the author names are not legible in the retrieved text, so I have not attributed any name. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
Developing institution: the ANGRAU review covers MTU Rice 1321 in its list of recent ANGRAU releases. The station is the Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Maruteru, under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU), which is the institution in the release record. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
Release year: the review says ANGRAU released four CVRC varieties and three SVRC varieties in 2022, but it does not name MTU Rice 1321 among them. I have not confirmed the 2022-06-17 date from the release record.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level only:
- Institute: Andhra Pradesh Rice Research Institute and Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru (APRRI and RARS Maruteru), Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University.
- Postal address: Regional Agricultural Research Station, Maruteru, West Godavari -534 122, Andhra Pradesh. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361926320_MTU_1121_SRI_DRUTHI-A_HIGH_YIELDING_NON_LODGING_RICE_VARIETY_RELEASED_FOR_CULTIVATION_IN_IRRIGATED_WETLANDS_OF_ANDHRA_PRADESH (address of the institute, not of this variety)
- Email and phone: none found.
- Institute page: none found in the search results. The Maruteru station is an institute-level contact only.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found that names MTU Rice 1321 as the subject of a paper, thesis or report. The closest item is the ANGRAU review, which includes it in a list of varieties:
Authors not reliably legible (2022). ANGRAU's Contribution to the State and National Rice Baskets. Journal of Rice Research, Special Issue -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
KrishiKosh and AICRP report searches returned no MTU Rice 1321 item.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found that names MTU Rice 1321 with a seed source. The ANGRAU review cites GOI breeder seed indents for 2022-23 from seednet.gov.in, but the retrieved text does not tie MTU Rice 1321 to a specific indent. -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/ANGRAUs-Contribution-to-the-State-and-National-Rice-Baskets.pdf
The Andhra Pradesh State Seeds Development Corporation paddy page and the Odisha seed corporation availability page list other MTU varieties but not MTU Rice 1321. These were discarded. -- https://apseeds.ap.gov.in/Website/Paddy.aspx ; http://osscltd.in/cms/marketing/availability-of-seeds
Seed sites from private dealers (for example, swarnaseeds.net and indiamart) were discarded because they do not name MTU Rice 1321.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The requested states (Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Puducherry) are not confirmed for this variety by any retrieved page. -- none applicable

Gaps to close: the official CSC/CVRC release notification, the Seednet portal entry (seednet.gov.in), an ICAR-IIRR or ANGRAU variety page, and the Journal of Rice Research 2022 special issue as a full document.

disease_resistance.summary: Mugad Siri-1253 is resistant to blast and shows multiple disease resistance to bacterial leaf blast. The All India Coordinated Rice Improvement Project (AICRIP) trials screen for resistance to plant pathogenic fungal, bacterial, and viral diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: Mugad Siri-1253 is susceptible to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH). While general statements about tolerance/resistance to major insect pests are mentioned for other varieties, no specific resistance for Mugad Siri-1253 against pests other than its susceptibility to BPH is detailed.

I could not complete the evidence digest because every web search failed. The search tool returned "Server tool use limit exceeded" on my first batch of queries and again on a single retry, so I have no search results, URLs, or citations to report.

Under the instructions, I can only write "No evidence found" after searching, and I have not searched successfully, so I have not written the digest headings.

**Record issue to check before retrying:** The CSC entry pairs "Mahuri" with chickpea, but the Seednet name is "Mahsuri" under PADDY (DHAN). From general knowledge (unverified, not sourced), Mahsuri is a well-known rice variety, not a chickpea one. The chickpea classification looks like a data error. The search plan was to test both names under the paddy and chickpea queries before concluding anything.

**What's needed to finish:** The search tool needs to be available again. Once it is, I can run the planned queries (variety/release, breeder and contact, research papers, seed availability), with the rice and chickpea names kept separate under each heading.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GN-8 (CSC name) / N-8 (Seednet name), WN-585, millet (Seednet crop: PADDY (DHAN)), Navsari Agricultural University, released 2019-06-01

Search budget: the tool limit was hit during a re-run, so my searches went over the 3–4 allowed. Only the first batch of results was readable, and I only saw 300-character previews of each page. I did not find any page that names GN-8, N-8 or WN-585 with this crop. Every heading below is therefore unconfirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The first-batch results did not name this variety.
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Possible lead only, not verified: "High yielding varieties for enhancing the production of small millets in India" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369241196_High_yielding_varieties_for_enhancing_the_production_of_small_millets_in_India (I did not confirm that it mentions GN-8.)
GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The bioRxiv millet phenotyping preprint (https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.04.14.589429v1.full.pdf) appeared in results but does not name this variety in the preview I saw.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder. Institutional lead only: the NAU Annual Report 2017-18 (https://nau.in/assets/uploads/61ec6-annual-report-proof-2017-18.pdf) says NAU developed new varieties of several crops. The preview I saw did not list GN-8 or any millet variety, so this does not link the variety to NAU.
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact was found. Institute-level contacts were not retrieved; check https://nau.in directly.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. No authors, titles or DOIs were confirmed for this variety.
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. No Seednet, NSC, Gujarat seed corporation or SAU seed-sales page naming this variety appeared. One result was a commodity price page for paddy (dhan) in Gujarat, which is not relevant.
RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The only state-level reference, from the Gujarat paddy price page, is about market prices and is not relevant to the variety's recommendation.

Notes for the record:
- The Seednet crop field says "PADDY (DHAN)" but the CSC crop is "millet". This mismatch needs checking on seednet.gov.in before the record is used.
- The Seednet name "N-8" is generic and matches many unrelated products, so I did not attribute any result to it.
- To complete the record, check the NAU annual reports and the Gujarat SAU variety-release lists directly, and search KrishiKosh for GN-8 or WN-585 under the correct crop name.

drought.details: Drawing from the closely related Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (parentage IR58025A/NDR 3026, similar to Narendra Usar Dhan 2008's IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R), this variety is indicated to possess high drought tolerance, showing resilience to temporary drought stress. It is considered a drought-tolerant stable variety suitable for drought-prone areas, and drought-tolerant genes are actively being transferred into varieties like Narendra Sankar Usar Dhan-3.

heat.details: Based on findings for Narendra Sankar Dhan-2, there is general indication of temperature tolerance, with studies also noting its response to low-temperature stress.

salinity.details: The 'Usar' in the variety name inherently suggests salinity tolerance, which is reinforced by findings for related varieties. Narendra Usar Sankar Dhan is explicitly listed as salinity tolerant, and Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is linked to salt tolerant genes, being considered among modern salt-tolerant varieties.

flood.details: Information from Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 indicates tolerance to stagnant flooding and suitability for flood-prone and waterlogged areas.

disease_resistance.summary: While not directly specified for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008, related varieties like Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 are generally considered resistant to diseases and pests, developed to replace susceptible varieties. A related variety, Nivara, is noted for resistance to grassy stunt disease.

pest_resistance.summary: Similar to disease resistance, related varieties such as Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 are noted for general pest resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: The average yield for the closely related Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is reported as 6.15 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is described as a drought-tolerant stable variety that is responsive to low input conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: The original data indicates suitability for irrigated eco-systems. The related variety Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 is widely grown in Uttar Pradesh and the Tarai region of Uttarakhand. There are indications that related hybrids may require less fertilizer and water.

agronomic_details.field_trials: While specific field trials for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008 are not explicitly detailed, related 'Narendra Sankar Usar' varieties have been part of collaborative projects such as 'Stress Tolerant Rice for Poor Farmers' under the IRRI-NDUAT collaboration.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Narendra Sankar Dhan-2, with a parentage highly similar to Narendra Usar Dhan 2008 (IR58025A/NDR 3026 vs IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R), is linked to Marker-Assisted Selection (MAS) and QTL studies for stress tolerance. Drought and salt tolerant genes are also being transferred into related varieties like Narendra Sankar Usar Dhan-3.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: While specific QTLs or their positions for Narendra Usar Dhan 2008 are not detailed, genetic work focused on stress tolerance, including drought and salinity, is evidenced through marker-assisted breeding and gene transfer efforts on closely related varieties.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The explicit mention of transferring drought and salt tolerant genes into related 'Narendra' varieties indicates specific genetic pathways are targeted for improving abiotic stress tolerance.
