search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Evidence for Sabour Narendra Dhan is limited to ecology: the IRRI-NARES list places it in rainfed shallow lowland conditions, but gives no drought, submergence, heat, salinity or flood test data for it -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf (also https://cgspace.cgiar.org/server/api/core/bitstreams/eeb4bc62-10b4-4743-8ebf-f2e268afbdc2/content)
Sabour Sampanna Dhan (BAU Sabour, a different variety, code BRR0059-563-B-2-1-1) is recorded as drought and submergence tolerant. This does not apply to Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366642727_RICE_VARIETY_SABOUR_SAMPANNA_DHAN_SUBMERGENCE_AND_DROUGHT_TOLERANT_VARIETY
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (the Seednet name, a 1998 hybrid) is noted as non-lodging and tolerant to shattering, with no stress-tolerance data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Sabour Narendra Dhan. The only disease note in the sources concerns Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 hybrid seed purity, not resistance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test
Sabour Vibhuti Dhan (BAU, a different variety) is reported to carry three bacterial blight resistance genes; this does not transfer to Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://agriinsite.com/bau-sabours-new-rice-varieties-withstand-floods-and-disease-in-bihar/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
IRRI-NARES list entry for Sabour Narendra Dhan: rainfed shallow lowland, long slender grain, about 4500 kg/ha, 110-115 days (units and column alignment read from a flattened table, so verify) -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (hybrid, IR 58025A x NDR 3026-3-1R, 1998): mid-early at 125-130 days, semi-tall at 114 cm, 1998 yield 62 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test
No multi-location trial results were found for Sabour Narendra Dhan.

GENETICS AND QTL
No QTL or marker study on Sabour Narendra Dhan was found. The parent IR 58025B (maintainer line) was improved for wide-compatibility gene S5n by marker-assisted backcrossing -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6062963/
The parentage given in the request (IR 58025 A/NDR 3026-3-1R) matches the 1998 hybrid Narendra Sankar Dhan-2, not a verified parentage for Sabour Narendra Dhan -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/73489 and https://www.fao.org/4/x7164t/x7164t08.htm
Code BRR2184 was not found in any source searched.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Sabour Narendra Dhan is listed under BAU Sabour as the developing institute in the IRRI-NARES release list; no lead breeder name was found -- https://books.irri.org/list-of-31-new-irri-nares-varieties-for-india.pdf
BAU Sabour institute leaders named in a 2024-era news report: Vice-Chancellor Dr D.R. Singh, Director of Research Dr A.K. Singh, and Director (Seeds & Farms) Dr Feza Ahmed. These are administrators, not confirmed breeders of this variety -- https://agriinsite.com/bau-sabours-new-rice-varieties-withstand-floods-and-disease-in-bihar/
Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 (1998 hybrid) was developed by Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology, Faizabad, UP -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321148285_Genetic_purity_assessment_of_indica_rice_hybrids_through_DNA_fingerprinting_and_grow_out_test
Release date discrepancy: the Seednet/CSC name Narendra Sankar Dhan-2 was notified in 1999 (S.O. 425(E), 08/06/1999), not 2024 as in the request -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Narendra Sarso (variety_name) / NARENDRA USAR-3 (seednet_variety_name), mustard / PADDY (DHAN), code Sag-1

Scope note: I ran four searches. No result describes a mustard variety called Narendra Sarso, a variety code Sag-1 from ANDUaT, or the Seednet entry. The only evidence touching the Seednet name concerns a paddy (rice) variety, so the two names appear to refer to different crops. Findings below are marked by which name they relate to.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso (mustard) or for NARENDRA USAR-3 (paddy). Searches returned no stress-tolerance data for either. -- none found
- Seednet name only: Narendra Usar Dhan-3 appears in NDUAT's list of rice varieties, which suggests the "USAR" name belongs to a rice variety. Its stress profile was not found. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for either name. -- none found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso or NARENDRA USAR-3 (maturity, yield, sowing or trial data). -- none found
- Related but different variety: NDUAT's mustard list includes Narendra Rai-1, Narendra Sarson-2, Narendra Ageti Rai-4, Narendra Rai-8 (NDYR-8), NDYS-2018. "Narendra Sarson-2" is a near-match in name only and is not evidence for this entry. -- https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf
- Name collision to check: IARI's vegetable mustard cv. Pusa Sag-1 was studied for sowing dates and leaf cutting, so the code "Sag-1" may be confused with Pusa Sag-1. No evidence links it to Narendra Sarso. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320131066_Effect_of_sowing_dates_and_varieties_for_higher_productivity_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The parentage string (LEUNG YAI 148 / IR 9125 / IR 18272) was not located in any result. The IR-numbered lines are IRRI rice lines, which fits the paddy record rather than mustard. -- none found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution: Narendra Deva University of Agriculture and Technology was established on 10th October 1975. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/INTROUCTION.pdf
- Output: more than 155 progressive varieties of field crops, fruits, vegetables and spices are credited to the university. -- https://www.nduat.org/pdf/anduat.pdf
- Breeder name: No evidence found. No result names a lead breeder or scientist for Narendra Sarso or NARENDRA USAR-3.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute headquarters: The Headquarter of the University is at Kumarganj, which is 42 km away from Faizabad district head quarter. -- https://www.nduat.org/Doc/INTROUCTION.pdf
- Postal address as printed in a KVK listing: Krishi Vigyan Kendra, Barasin, Sultanpur- Acharya Narendra Deva University of Agriculture & Technology, Kumarganj, Ayodhya-224 229 (Uttar Pradesh). -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/research-article/improved-seed-production-technology-in-mustard
- Website: Website: www.nduat.org. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acharya_Narendra_Deva_University_of_Agriculture_and_Technology
- Email and phone: No evidence found for the university or any breeder.

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso, Sag-1, or NARENDRA USAR-3 in any journal, AICRP, KrishiKosh, or conference source. I did not search KrishiKosh directly, so this gap is only from the four searches run.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer sources for the named variety. The results were retail listings for generic sarso saag leafy-vegetable seed, which do not identify Narendra Sarso. -- https://nurserylive.com/products/sarso-saag-mustard-leaves-seeds

RECOMMENDED STATES
- No evidence found for Narendra Sarso or NARENDRA USAR-3 recommended in Uttar Pradesh. The UP entry in the record is unverified.

RECORD ISSUES TO RESOLVE BEFORE USE
1. Crop mismatch: the Seednet entry is PADDY (DHAN), while the CSC name is mustard. Confirm the correct crop with the CSC minutes and Seednet.
2. Name mismatch: "Narendra Sarso" was not found in NDUAT's mustard release list, which has Narendra Sarson-2 instead. Check the release notification for the exact name.

basic_info.institution: Gujarat (Navsari Agricultural University, Main Rice Research Centre, Navsari)

drought.details: NAUR-1 is named in a ResearchGate drought-management review listing genotypes, but the snippets do not report any drought tolerance measurement or mechanism for it. The ISWS 2020 abstract mentions NAUR-1 sown at 50 kg/ha in the second week of July in a direct-seeding context, which is not a drought evaluation. No tolerance level can be assigned.

heat.details: No heat tolerance data for NAUR-1 were found. The AAU annual report snippet mentions heat wave conditions alongside NAUR 1, GNR 8 and GNR 3, but the context is a disease or pest reaction (moderately resistant), not heat tolerance.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance is documented for NAUR-1. Agro-advisories recommend NAUR-1 and GNR-2 for the coastal area of Gujarat, but this is a recommendation for the region, not evidence of salt tolerance. The advisory separately tells coastal saline-region farmers to arrange salt-tolerant varieties.

flood.details: NAUR-1 appears in a NAAS agromet bulletin list of recommended paddy varieties for Gujarat, but the bulletin names Swarna Sub-1 and Jalashree for submergence tolerance. NAUR-1 is not reported as flood tolerant.

disease_resistance.summary: The ICAR Annual Report 2011-12 lists NAUR 1 (long slender grain) as moderately resistant to blast (Bl), bacterial leaf blight (BLB) and sheath rot (ShR), and to stem borer (SB), for irrigated areas of Gujarat. The AAU 2023-24 report notes moderate resistance for NAUR 1 together with GNR 8 and GNR 3, but the snippet does not say to which pest or disease.

pest_resistance.summary: The ICAR Annual Report 2011-12 lists moderate resistance to stem borer (SB). The Navsari Agricultural University Main Rice Research Centre document refers to NAUR-1, GNR-2, GNR-3 and GNR-4 as registered varieties and to IET-22629 showing multi-resistant reactions against rice stem borer. The snippet does not clearly attribute this to NAUR-1, so the stem borer evidence rests on the ICAR report.

agronomic_details.yield: The IIRR newsletter lists NAUR 1 (released 2008) at 5.900 t/ha with a long slender (LS) grain type and a duration of 120-125 days. The rice-garud database gives a yield of 50 q/ha for a Gujarat entry in the same listing as NAUR-1, but the snippet does not make clear whether that figure belongs to NAUR-1.
agronomic_details.stability: No multi-environment stability analysis was found. NAUR-1 has been tested repeatedly in AICRIP trials (2016, 2017, 2019) and used as a check in Gujarat.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Irrigated areas of Gujarat. It is also recommended for the coastal area of Gujarat in agro-advisories.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 120-125 days according to the IIRR newsletter (the CSC record is blank)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SLENDER GRAIN WITH LONG PANICLE LENGTH (28 TO 32 CM ) AND L/B RATIO : 3.48, GREEN FOLIAGE WITH STRONG CLUMP AND REMARKABLE SIZE OF FLAG LEAF. Parentage is GR-4 x Pusa 2-48-24 per the CSC record and rice-garud, while the IIRR newsletter gives GR-4 x IET 1705, a discrepancy.
agronomic_details.field_trials: NAUR-1 has been evaluated as a check or entry in AICRIP varietal improvement trials (2016 and 2017 progress reports) and used in direct-seeded rice work reported at the ISWS 2020 conference. Breeding trials at the Main Paddy Research Station, Navsari, used it as a parent (Bhurarata x NAUR-1).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: No QTL, SSR or SNP marker data specific to NAUR-1 were found. The Saltol QTL mention in the AICRIP 2019 report concerns marker-assisted breeding of other lines and is not a trait of NAUR-1.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: None reported for NAUR-1.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: None reported. NAUR-1 has been used as a parent in biofortification breeding, notably in GR-15 (Bhurarata x NAUR-1, 2017), reported with grain zinc of 21.58 mg/kg.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: The ARGM 2022 and 2023 proceedings list NAUR-1 with 0.50 in a breeder seed indent table, together with GNR-2, GNR-3 and others, indicating that breeder seed production is indented. The units are not stated in the snippet, so the quantity should be treated as unconfirmed.
commercial_info.availability_status: limited (indented for breeder seed in 2022-2023 and still recommended in 2021 agro-advisories, but no dealer or sales data were found)
commercial_info.kvk: Not specified in the sources. Seed is likely distributed through Navsari Agricultural University channels, but this is not stated.
commercial_info.private_dealers: No private dealer information found.

agronomic_details.yield: No official multi-location yield data found in searched sources. An unverified YouTube video claims about 35 quintals per acre under NK 5251. This is an anecdotal, non-peer-reviewed claim and is not a trial result.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The Syngenta page claims wide adaptability and good performance under low management, which is a marketing claim and not a stability analysis.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Syngenta NK 5251 page claims wide adaptability. Syngenta NK 5231 page describes suitability for rainfed or irrigated conditions. Agro-climatic fit beyond these statements: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Syngenta lists crop duration of 120-125 days. The Vikaspedia hybrid seed guideline table gives a duration of 128 (column meaning inferred), which conflicts with the Syngenta range.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Syngenta lists kharif season, sowing 15 May to 15 July, seed rate 5-6 kg per acre, spacing 20 cm x 15 cm. The Syngenta NK 5231 page gives the same sowing window, duration, seed rate and spacing and calls the variety mid-early. Morphological characteristics: not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No official multi-location trial results found. AAU Assam Rice Research Institute lists NK 5251 among varieties selected from national programmes but gives no yield data. The YouTube video (anecdotal, about 35 quintals per acre) is not a trial. The Vikaspedia 128-day duration conflicts with the Syngenta 120-125 day range. No other trial results were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 5251 (CSC/release-minute name) / NK-5231 (Seednet portal name), rice

Name note: The search results contain no Seednet portal page, so I could not confirm the Seednet entry directly. Evidence labelled "NK 5231" below comes from Syngenta's separate NK 5231 product pages, not from a Seednet record. Evidence labelled "NK 5251" refers to the CSC/notification name and the NK 5251 hybrid.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance of NK 5251 in the retrieved sources. The Syngenta page only claims wide adaptability and good performance under low management -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251
- The NK 5231 Syngenta page describes it as suitable for rainfed or irrigated conditions, which is a water-regime statement, not a tolerance test -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for blast, bacterial blight, sheath blight, BPH, stem borer or other resistance for NK 5251 or NK-5231.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Syngenta lists NK 5251 as kharif, sown 15 May to 15 July, crop duration 120-125 days, seed rate 5-6 kg/acre, spacing 20 cm x 15 cm -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251
- The Syngenta NK 5231 page gives the same sowing window, duration, seed rate and spacing and calls the variety mid-early -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231
- The Vikaspedia hybrid seed guideline table gives NK-5251 a duration of 128 (days, column meaning inferred), which conflicts with the 120-125 days on Syngenta's page -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- A YouTube video claims about 35 quintals/acre under NK 5251. This is an anecdotal, non-peer-reviewed claim and is not a trial result -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FIY3RvcMAPY
- Official multi-location yield data: No evidence found.
- AAU Assam Rice Research Institute lists NK 5251 among varieties it selected from national programmes, but gives no yield data -- https://www.aau.ac.in/department/department_details/120

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The NK 5251 hybrid's parentage is not stated in any retrieved source (the CSC input also says "Not specified").

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The hybrid is listed as developed by Syngenta India Ltd in the hybrid seed guideline table -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- The IntechOpen hybrid table gives "Developed by: NA" for NK 5251 -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- The DES Study No. 176 lists NK 5251 among private-sector hybrids in the production chain, consistent with a private developer -- https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/2013-14-Spread-of-New-Varieties-of-Hybrid-Rice-and-their-impact-on-the-overall-production-and-productivity.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
- Developing station: No evidence found.
- The sponsoring authority named in the input is blank; the retrieved evidence points to Syngenta India Ltd as the private developer. The input's "Sponsoring authority (not named)" is therefore only partly resolved.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Syngenta India customer care email: customercare.india@syngenta.com -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251-plus
- Syngenta phone numbers, listed on the page as "Crop Protection Toll Free Number": 18002001310 / 020 30699533 / 020 66845533 -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251-plus
- Postal address of Syngenta India or of its seed division: No evidence found.
- Breeder name, role and direct contact: No evidence found.
- Public institute contact (ICAR or SAU): No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- No peer-reviewed paper on NK 5251 was found.
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report entry, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI for NK 5251 was found.
- Report, authors not given in retrieved text: Study No. 176, Spread of New Varieties of Hybrid Rice, Directorate of Rice Research, 2013-14 (DES) -- https://desagri.gov.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/2013-14-Spread-of-New-Varieties-of-Hybrid-Rice-and-their-impact-on-the-overall-production-and-productivity.pdf
- Chapter, authors not given in retrieved text: Current Scenario of Breeding Approaches in Rice (IntechOpen), which lists NK 5251 as a 2012 release. Year and journal fields are as stated on the page -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- Notification record, no author: Bihar DBT list of notified varieties, row "565 · NK 5251 (IET 19738) · 2007 · 10/09/2012 · S.O. 2125(E)". The column meanings are not labelled in the snippet, so the 2007 and 10/09/2012 values may be year of testing and notification date, not release year -- https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Nabarak Beej Bhandar, Narayanpur, Nalbari, Assam, lists "Syngenta NK 5231 Hybrid Rice Seed" in 10 kg packs. Seller contact is on the listing page; the mobile number is hidden -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html
- Desikheti sells an "NK 5251 Paddy Seeds" product page. The retrieved snippet gives no price or stock detail -- https://www.desikheti.com/products/syngenta-nk-5251-paddy-seeds
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK and SAU seed sales: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Syngenta lists Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251
- The IntechOpen table lists Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra and Gujarat -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/77391
- The Vikaspedia table lists Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Bihar among states where NK-5251 is recommended -- https://static.vikaspedia.in/media/files_en/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/hybrid-rice-seed-production.pdf
- The three sources disagree; the input's "Not specified" is replaced by these state lists. A state-level official notification is needed to resolve this.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 5231 (rice)

Search note: I ran four web searches. The Seednet portal and CSC release minutes did not come up in any result, so every finding below is from Syngenta and reseller pages. Variety name: the CSC name is NK 5231 and the Seednet name is NK-5231. No search result showed the Seednet name, so all findings below refer to the NK 5231 name as used by Syngenta.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The Syngenta product page gives only general claims of suitability for rainfed or irrigated conditions and no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The Syngenta pages list no resistance ratings. The only related item is a pocket-insert leaflet PDF, which I could not open. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/nk-5231

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The Syngenta page lists the season as kharif, sowing between 15 May and 15 July, a crop duration of 120 to 125 days, a seed rate of 5 to 6 kg per acre, and spacing of 20 cm between rows and 15 cm between plants. It is described as mid-early duration with bold grain, more grains per panicle, and consistent adaptability. No multi-location trial data was found. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Parentage is not stated in any source, and no marker or QTL study was found. (The search results include a Syngenta NK 5251 page, which is a different variety.) -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5251

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developer: Syngenta India Pvt. Ltd., as given in the CSC record. The Syngenta product pages name no lead breeder, scientist or development station. The breeder-focused search returned only unrelated foreign patent and syndicated pages. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/nk-5231

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found. No email, phone or postal address for Syngenta India or its rice division appeared in the search results. The only location found is a reseller in Narayanpur, Assam (Nabarak Beej Bhandar), which is not an institute contact. Please check the Syngenta India contact page directly. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed papers, AICRP reports, KrishiKosh theses or conference papers on NK 5231 were found. The ICAR 2024-25 annual report that came up in the trial search does not mention this variety in the extracts I could read. -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/2025-10/ICAR%20Eng%20Annual%20Report_2024-25.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- A reseller listing (Nabarak Beej Bhandar, Narayanpur, Assam) offers a 10 kg pack of the variety as in stock, with the listing ID 2855772639455. Availability and pricing were not checked with the seller. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or official seed-sales source was found. -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/syngenta-nk-5231-hybrid-rice-seed-2855772639455.html

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The CSC raw record lists Assam. The Syngenta product page does not name any state. It gives only "major rice-growing areas" and says the variety suits rainfed or irrigated rice. Assam is therefore supported only by the CSC record and the reseller location, not by the company's own recommendation. -- https://www.syngenta.co.in/product/seed/rice/nk-5231

Release year -- The CSC record gives 2 August 2024. I could not find a notification gazette or Seednet entry to confirm it. Parentage is not specified in any source.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The web search tool failed on every attempt with "Server tool use limit exceeded," so I could not run any of the four required searches. The digest below therefore contains only what is in the input record. Nothing has been verified against a source, and I have not filled any heading with invented findings.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: NK 6240 (CSC name) / NK 16520 (Seednet name), maize, NECH-131, Syngenta Seeds

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (search not completed; tool limit error)
DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (search not completed; tool limit error)
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found (search not completed; tool limit error)
GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage from input record only, unverified: female parent IR58025A (A line), maintainer IR58025B (B line). Source: input record, no URL.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution per input record: Syngenta Seeds (private company, not an ICAR institute). No breeder name found (search not completed).
CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found (search not completed). No breeder or institute contact details were available to record.
PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found (search not completed; tool limit error)
SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (search not completed; tool limit error)
RECOMMENDED STATES -- Per input record only, unverified: Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh (raw field "BIHARCHHATTISGARHJHARKANDODISHATELANAGANAUTTAR PRADESH", split by me). Source: input record, no URL.

DATA ISSUES TO RESOLVE
- Year of release is "NaT" (missing); no release or notification date is available.
- The Seednet entry NK 16520 is listed under crop "PADDY (DHAN)", while the variety is maize. Either the Seednet mapping is wrong or it refers to a different product. The two names should not be treated as the same record until checked on seednet.gov.in.
- The "variety_name" and "seednet_variety_name" evidence could not be separated, because no search returned results for either name.

NEXT STEPS
Re-run the four searches once the tool is available: "NK 6240 maize variety", "NK 6240 maize breeder institute", "NK 6240 maize research" and "NK 6240 maize seed availability", plus a Seednet check for NK 16520. Priority sources would be seednet.gov.in, the CSC/ICAR release minutes, KrishiKosh and the AICRP on Maize reports.

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "NLR 3041", so one name was searched. Seednet_crop_name is "PADDY (DHAN)". No Seednet portal page for this variety was returned, so every finding below rests on non-Seednet sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Blast tolerance is claimed in a Nellore district on-farm trial, where NLR-3041 was tested because it was thought to tolerate blast. No blast was seen on either NLR-3041 or BPT 5204 at the panicle-emergence stage, so this is a single-season observation, not a resistance rating -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- The same trial was repeated in a second listing of the KVK page, which gives six locations (Rajuvolupadu, Veerampally, Chennareddypalli) -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/index.php/technologies
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The search returned only unrelated NLR-gene papers and other rice varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Blast (Magnaporthe): tolerance reported in the KVK Nellore trial above -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- Other diseases and insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rainfed lowland thermal-indices study with three sowing dates (June, July, August) and four varieties including NLR-3041: NLR-3041 took the most days to 50% flowering (107.33, against 104.00 for BPT-5204) and had the highest accumulated growing degree days and photothermal units from sowing to harvest (2136.83 °C-day) -- https://sasapjas.org/influence-of-thermal-indices-on-phenology-of-rainfed-lowland-rice/
- On-farm trial (OFT) "Assessment of the performance of Paddy var. NLR-3041 in Nellore district (1st year)", 2018-19, trial no. 1/OFT/C.P/18-19/R/KVK/NLR. Its rationale was that NLR-3041 matches BPT 5204 in cooking quality -- https://www.kvknellore-angrau.org/technologies
- Yield data: No evidence found for NLR-3041 specifically.
- Maturity duration: the thermal-indices paper gives phenology only. Days to maturity: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- A KrishiKosh-hosted thesis (title on the page: "Morphological and molecular divergence for quantitative..."; author not in retrieved text) lists NLR-3041 with parentage BPT5204/NLR145 and institution ARS Nellore -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7451dec-427f-44b7-9ebe-c56b9d0458a5/content
- The same thesis also uses genotype panels that include NLR-3041 in marker profiling. Marker-trait associations for NLR-3041: No evidence found -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/f7451dec-427f-44b7-9ebe-c56b9d0458a5/content
- QTL or marker studies specific to NLR-3041: No evidence found.

- Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found. The ARS Nellore rice papers in the results (C.P.D. Rajan, P. Rajasekhar, U. Vineetha) are about NLR 40054, not NLR-3041, so they are not attributed here -- https://sarr.co.in/wp-content/uploads/Untitled16.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned no NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK sale, SAU sale or dealer listing for NLR-3041. The IFFDC seed list names BPT-5204 but not NLR-3041 -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed

disease_resistance.summary: Blast: resistance is reported. The RARS technical report describes NLR 40024 as blast tolerant and short duration. A Nellore trial report describes it as blast resistant. A blast-resistance marker study lists NLR 40024 among parents selected for blast resistance, yield and quality. No blast score, race spectrum or Pi resistance gene is named for this variety. Leaf blast, neck blast and other diseases: Not found in searched sources. The variety record lists disease reaction as 'Not Specified'.

pest_resistance.summary: No pest resistance is confirmed for NLR 40024. Leaf folder: incidence reported at 18.16% in NLR 40024, above the economic threshold level; this is a susceptibility finding, not resistance. Stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas): a late-sown field test reported 0.11% white ears, scored highly resistant (scale 0), against 19.48% in susceptible check TN1. The digest lists this under NLR 40024 but the source text does not name the entry, so this attribution is not confirmed and is not reported as a resistance finding for this variety. The variety record lists pest reaction as 'Not Specified'.

agronomic_details.yield: Variety record: 6.5 to 7.0 tons/ha. Organic-management trial: mean yield about 6064 kg/ha, reported as the highest of the entries tested (NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha). Record fertilizer response: yields well at 120 kg N/ha, 60 P2O5 and K2O; seed rate 50 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability analysis was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Variety record: early kharif and early rabi seasons in the southern zone of Andhra Pradesh. The Southern Zone 2015 recommendations list Swetha (NLR 40024) for early kharif planting. A Nellore report says it was developed for summer cultivation, which conflicts with the RARS early kharif listing. Digest describes it as suitable for machine harvesting (Nellore trial report, dating unclear).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Variety record: non-lodging, non-shattering, fertilizer responsive. The RARS report describes it as lodging tolerant and short duration. A Nellore report describes it as non-lodging (dating unclear). Morphological characteristics in the record: 'Na.' No further morphological evidence was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Organic-management trial: mean yield about 6064 kg/ha, highest of the entries tested, versus NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha (RARS technical report). (2) Late-sown puddled trial, North Coastal Zone of AP: 6164 kg/ha, reported as the most suitable variety there. The digest does not explicitly name NLR 40024 in this result, so attribution is not confirmed. (3) Late-sown stem borer test: highly resistant score for white ears (0.11%) versus TN1 (19.48%); attribution to NLR 40024 is not explicit in the source text. (4) Southern Zone 2015 recommendations list NLR 40024 (Swetha) for early kharif planting.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources for NLR 40024. Parentage recorded as WGL 14280-1 x NLR 30491 was not found in any search result and remains unverified. The digest reports no SSR, SNP or marker positions for this variety.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Not found in searched sources. No gene or pathway is named for NLR 40024. The Pi resistance gene is not identified.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as blast and lodging tolerant, short duration, suitable for early kharif -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Described as blast resistant and non-lodging, with suitability for machine harvesting (Nellore trial report; the article's dating is unclear) -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434
- Among parents selected for blast resistance, yield and quality in an Indian blast-resistance study -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8 (same study also indexed at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273012781_Identification_and_validation_of_rice_blast_resistance_genes_in_Indian_rice_germplasm)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Stem borer (Scirpophaga incertulas), late-sown field test: 0.11% white ears, scored as highly resistant (scale 0), against 19.48% in susceptible check TN1 -- https://sasapjas.org/study-on-early-duration-rice-varieties-under-late-sown-situation-for-resistance-to-yellow-stem-borer-scirpophaga-incertulas-walker/
- Leaf folder: incidence reported at 18.16% in NLR 40024, above the economic threshold level, so this is not a resistance finding -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Blast: resistance is reported in the sources above; no blast score, race spectrum or resistance gene (Pi) is named for this variety -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Organic-management trial: mean yield about 6064 kg/ha, highest of the entries tested (NLR 34242 at 5735 kg/ha) -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- North Coastal Zone of AP, late-sown puddled conditions: 6164 kg/ha, named as the most suitable variety there -- https://sasapjas.org/study-on-early-duration-rice-varieties-under-late-sown-situation-for-resistance-to-yellow-stem-borer-scirpophaga-incertulas-walker/
- Southern zone 2015 recommendations list Swetha (NLR 40024) for early kharif planting -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf
- Season conflict: a Nellore report says it was developed for summer cultivation, whereas the RARS list says early kharif -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434 ; https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Maturity: described as short duration only; no day count was found for NLR 40024 -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- No evidence found. The blast-resistance marker study lists NLR 40024 as a parent and reports marker-trait co-segregation for other advanced lines, not for this variety -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8
- Parentage WGL 14280-1 x NLR 30491 was not found in any search result. The pedigree in the record is unverified.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Released or listed under Acharya N.G. Ranga Agricultural University (ANGRAU) Nellore-line varieties; ANGRAU's Other-Institute page lists NLR 40024 Swetha -- https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-25/
- The RARS list (rarstpt.org) gives Swetha (NLR40024) with a 2012 year, which conflicts with the 2020-11-09 release date in the record -- https://rarstpt.org/files/rars/ASRN_R_Technologies.pdf
- Breeder names: No evidence found. Principal scientist P. Ramesh Babu is quoted on NLR 34449 only, so he is not attributed to this variety -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434
- Developing station: Nellore ARS/RRS is named in regional reports as the source of NLR-series varieties, and the Hans India report credits "scientists" with developing NLR 40024 (Swetha) -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/paddy-cultivation-area-drops-significantly-in-nellore-dist-785149
- Name check: Seednet name NLR 40024 did not appear in any result; the only alternate name found is "Swetha." No seednet.gov.in page was returned.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder email, phone or postal address for NLR 40024. Institute site appears in results: ANGRAU (https://uasbagriinnovationcenter.in/other-institute-25/ cites angrau.ac.in); no address, email or phone was extracted from the snippets.

PUBLICATIONS
- Gangireddy, A.K., Sreevalli, M.D., Chintala, S. (year not shown in snippet; DOI implies 2025). Integrating phenotypic and molecular profiling for selection of promising advanced breeding lines for blast resistance in rice (Oryza sativa L.). Journal not named in snippet (DOI prefix s11033) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11033-025-10279-8
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Identification and validation of rice blast resistance genes in Indian rice germplasm. ResearchGate indexed PDF -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273012781_Identification_and_validation_of_rice_blast_resistance_genes_in_Indian_rice_germplasm
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Study on early duration rice varieties under late sown situation for resistance to yellow stem borer Scirpophaga incertulas Walker. Journal not named -- https://sasapjas.org/study-on-early-duration-rice-varieties-under-late-sown-situation-for-resistance-to-yellow-stem-borer-scirpophaga-incertulas-walker/
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Management practices for kharif and rabi 2015, Southern Zone production recommendations (report) -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf
- No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP report or ICAR annual report for NLR 40024 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed listings for NLR 40024. The IFFDC availability list and BigHaat paddy catalogue do not include it -- https://iffdc.in/post_detail.php?postname=availability-of-seed ; https://www.bighaat.com/collections/paddy-seeds
- A dated (2018-2019) reader comment says NLR 40024 was not available even with ARS scientists. This is anecdotal -- https://www.hyderabadfirst.in/?p=3434
- The IndiaMART "NLR Paddy Rice" listing is generic and not tied to this variety, so it was discarded -- https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/nlr-paddy-rice-2857826324055.html

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh only, consistent with the record. Evidence: Southern Zone AP early kharif recommendations (https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/reports/Management%20practices%20for%20ZREAC%202015.pdf) and North Coastal Zone of AP suitability (https://sasapjas.org/study-on-early-duration-rice-varieties-under-late-sown-situation-for-resistance-to-yellow-stem-borer-scirpophaga-incertulas-walker/)
- Nellore district farmers use it; Nellore is in the Southern Zone. Notification or CSC/SVRC release minutes were not found, so the release record remains unverified -- https://www.thehansindia.com/andhra-pradesh/paddy-cultivation-area-drops-significantly-in-nellore-dist-785149

heat.details: NMH-1242 was included in a list of 'test genotypes' for 'heat stress'. However, the report explicitly identifies 'Heat tolerant rice genotypes'. No specific heat tolerance level for maize variety NMH-1242 is provided.

salinity.details: No information found regarding salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No information found regarding flood tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: NMH-1242 was listed among 'test genotypes' in reports discussing 'resistance to disease and insect-pests', 'sheath blight pathogen of rice', and 'bacterial blight and brown spot diseases'. However, these contexts primarily describe research on 'rice' varieties. No specific disease resistance for maize variety NMH-1242 is provided, beyond general mentions in DUS testing for biotic resistance.

pest_resistance.summary: NMH-1242 was listed among 'test genotypes' in reports discussing 'resistance to disease and insect-pests' and 'Biological control of insect pests in rice ecosystem'. These references primarily relate to 'rice' pests. A parliamentary discussion mentions NMH-1242 in the context of insecticides' effectiveness against insect pests affecting 'paddy fields', but this does not indicate inherent pest resistance of the maize variety itself. No specific pest resistance for maize variety NMH-1242 is provided, beyond general mentions in DUS testing for biotic resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Quantitative yield data is not provided. However, NMH-1242, as a test genotype, was noted to have 'responded significantly up to the highest' when compared with check cultivars BIO 9637© and PMH 4©.
agronomic_details.stability: NMH-1242 was tested through multi-location trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: It is adapted for the Kharif season, and its performance was evaluated during Kharif 2012. It was also evaluated at UAS, Dharwad.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: NMH-1242 was subjected to field trials, including a performance evaluation of selected medium duration genotypes during Kharif 2012. It was also evaluated as a farmer variety at UAS, Dharwad, and tested through multi-location trials. It was listed among 'Test genotypes' that 'responded significantly up to the highest' in certain trials.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NPH-242 (CSC release name) / NPH-4242 (Seednet name), rice (paddy), Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd.

Search coverage: four web_search queries were run, the maximum allowed. Two used "NPH-242 rice" wording and one used "NPH-4242 paddy" with Assam. None returned a page about this variety. The results that came back were about other products (IR64, a US rice line M-206, the TAK-242 drug trial, and a Nuziveedu hybrid seed catalogue). Those are not evidence for NPH-242, so no finding below is drawn from them.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found (searched for NPH-242 and NPH-4242; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data)

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found (no blast, BLB, sheath blight, BPH or other resistance data located)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found (no maturity duration, yield, or multi-location trial data located)

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found (parentage is "Not specified" in the input record and no pedigree or marker data was located)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found (no lead breeder, developing station, or release notification identified; the institution in the record is Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd., and no page confirming its role in developing this variety was found)

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found (no breeder, institute, or company email, phone, address or contact-page URL was located. Nothing has been inferred or filled in.)

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found (no peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis, or conference paper naming NPH-242 or NPH-4242 was located)

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found (no NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for NPH-242 or NPH-4242 was located. The Nuziveedu Seeds field-crop page that surfaced lists different products, including NP-7020 and the hybrid NPH-207, and is not evidence for this variety.)

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for Assam or any other state. The Assam value comes only from the input record and was not confirmed by any search result.

Suggested next steps, since the search budget is used up: check the Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) for "NPH-4242" under PADDY (DHAN) and the CSC release minutes for the NPH-242 notification; contact Nirmal Seeds Pvt. Ltd. directly for breeder names and parentage; and search KrishiKosh and the Assam Agricultural University or AICRP rice trial reports for the variety name.

drought.details: This variety is described as drought tolerant and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Molecular breeding efforts are noted for developing rice varieties with inbuilt drought tolerance.

heat.details: While temperature stress is mentioned in a general context of research, specific heat tolerance for NPH-XI (IET 27332) is not explicitly stated in the provided results.

salinity.details: The variety is described as salinity tolerant.

flood.details: No explicit mention of flood tolerance. However, it is suitable for semi-deep water conditions and has submergence tolerance.

disease_resistance.summary: This variety is highly resistant to Leaf Blight (LB) and neck infection. It is generally described as disease-resistant and moderately resistant, though specific diseases for the latter are not always detailed.

pest_resistance.summary: NPH-XI (IET 27332) is tolerant to Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) and exhibits tolerance to major insect pests including Stem Borer and Gall Midge.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yields for NPH-XI (IET 27332) are 65 q/ha and 63.5 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Stability across environments is not specified in the provided results.
agronomic_details.adaptation: This variety is suitable for irrigated, transplanted conditions, and also for direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water. It is recommended for cultivation in Jharkhand and West Bengal.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: Reported maturity periods are 130-133 days and 117 days.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: NPH-XI (IET 27332) is a semi-dwarf variety, approximately 82 cm in height. It produces Long Slender (LS) grains and is noted as a protein-rich paddy variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Details on specific field trials beyond general suitability statements are not provided.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not specified for this specific variety in the provided results. A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) was isolated from a drought tolerant rice cultivar in a general context, but not explicitly attributed to NPH-XI (IET 27332). Molecular breeding efforts for drought, low soil P, and blast resistance are mentioned generally for rice varieties.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: A novel abiotic stress responsive gene LOC_. Os06g10210 (OsCHI2) is noted in relation to drought tolerance in rice. EVIDENCE DIGEST: OUAT Kalinga Rice 7 (Barunei), IET 23666, rice

Search status: The search tool hit its usage limit after the first batch of four queries, so I could not run the follow-up checks. Only one result contained the variety name with usable text. The Seednet name ("OUAT Kalinga Rice 7 (Barunei) (IET 23666)") was never returned by any search, so no evidence below is confirmed under that name. Everything below refers to the CSC/OUAT name "OUAT Kalinga Rice 7 (Barunei)." Snippet text was truncated, so the details should be checked against the full PDF.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The search returned no stress-tolerance data for this variety. Not searched in full.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Not searched in full.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The OUAT release list describes it as a medium-duration variety, but the snippet cut off before any maturity, yield, or trial figures. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage from the request is Gouri / IR 65629-22-1. No independent source confirmed it. No QTL or marker evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution: Odisha University of Agriculture and Technology (OUAT), Bhubaneswar. The OUAT release list appears under the Directorate of Research. Lead breeder name: No evidence found. -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone, or address was retrieved. The Directorate of Research, OUAT, Bhubaneswar is the only institutional contact source identified, but no contact details were extracted from it. Source: https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry, or thesis specific to this variety was confirmed. The IIRR Annual Report 2023 mentions "OUAT Kalinga" in its text, but the snippet does not clearly tie it to Barunei, so I have not listed it as a publication. -- https://icar-iirr.org/AnnualReports/IIRR_AR_2023.pdf

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not confirmed. The OUAT release list names the variety, but no seed-sale source was found. Not checked: Seednet, OUAT seed sales, Odisha State Seed Corporation, KVKs, or private dealers.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Odisha (matches the request). Source: https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

RECORD NOTES
- Release year conflict: the request gives 2023-05-02, but the OUAT list is titled "released during 2022-23." Confirm against the CSC minutes before using either date.
- Open items for a follow-up session: the Seednet entry for IET 23666, the CSC minutes, the full OUAT PDF (maturity, yield, and tolerance tables), the IIRR and AICRP rice reports, KrishiKosh theses, and OUAT contact pages.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PAC 801 (rice)

Name note: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "PAC 801" / "PAC-801". Searches 1 to 4 covered both spellings, and the Seednet/PADDY (DHAN) portal did not surface in any result. No result confirms a CSC release notification for this name. The "Uttar Pradesh" recommendation comes only from the input record. Several results are commercial or non-Indian and I have flagged them as such. Four searches were run, the maximum allowed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Advanta's Philippines launch material says PAC 801 is adaptable to both wet and dry seasons. This is a company claim, not trial data. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm
STRESS TOLERANCE -- No independent drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence for PAC 801 was found. No result tests PAC 801 under these stresses. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm

DISEASE AND PEST -- No disease or pest resistance data specific to PAC 801 was found. The Ghana hybrid evaluation lists PAC 801 among the hybrids tested for disease reaction, but the snippet gives no PAC 801 scores. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Advanta's Philippines material gives a potential yield of 11 t/ha and describes grains of about 7.33 mm, slender and long. These are company claims. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Ghana multi-location study lists PAC 801 as a hybrid entry from Advanta Seeds (2015 source) in a yield and disease trial. The snippet does not give PAC 801's yield figures. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A retail-advisory table (Krishi Jagran, May 2020) classes PAC 801 as medium maturity, rainfed, and a better grain yielder. This is not an official ICAR or SAU record. https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No AICRP, ICAR or SAU multi-location trial results for PAC 801 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL -- No parentage, marker or QTL data for PAC 801 was found. Parentage is "Not specified" in the input record and no source supplied it.
GENETICS AND QTL -- Name collision: CR Dhan 801 (IET 25667) is a different NRRI release with a known pedigree (IR81896-B-B-195 / 2*Swarna-Sub1 // IR91659-54-35). It is not PAC 801 and should not be merged with it. https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/1.-leaflet_climatesmart_final.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The institution is Advanta (Advanta Seeds, a private seed company). No named breeder for PAC 801 was found. https://www.advantaseeds.com/crops
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Advanta people named in a Philippines press item (not breeders): Bhupen Dubey, CEO; Seraj Ahmad, Country Business Manager. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The Advanta crops page says it has a wide range of rice maturities and grain types. It does not name PAC 801. https://www.advantaseeds.com/crops

CONTACT DETAILS -- No official email, phone or postal address for Advanta India or any PAC 801 breeder was found in the results. Institute-level contact URL: https://www.advantaseeds.com/crops (no contact details on that page in the snippet).
CONTACT DETAILS -- Names: Bhupen Dubey (CEO, Advanta Seeds); Seraj Ahmad (Country Business Manager, Advanta Seeds). No emails or phones were given for either.

PUBLICATIONS -- No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper on PAC 801 was found.
PUBLICATIONS -- Lists PAC 801 as a tested hybrid, but authors and year are not in the snippet: Evaluation of Yield, Reaction to Diseases, and Grain Physical Attributes of Some Introduced Rice Hybrids in Ghana. Journal not identified in snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/331741636_Evaluation_of_Yield_Reaction_to_Diseases_and_Grain_Physical_Attributes_of_Some_Introduced_Rice_Hybrids_in_Ghana

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU listing for PAC 801 was found. The Seednet entry was not found.
SEED AVAILABILITY -- Advanta is named as the brand on Indian retail pages for other hybrids, such as PAC 8744 and PAC 837. These are different products. The ADV 801 listing (Indiamart) is a separate product name and is not confirmed as PAC 801. https://www.indiamart.com/proddetail/adv-801-hybrid-paddy-25450102430.html
SEED AVAILABILITY -- Advanta's Philippines product, PAC 801 (NSIC Mestizo 60), is a Philippines registration and does not establish Indian availability. https://news.agropages.com/News/NewsDetail---18810.htm

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Uttar Pradesh is taken from the input record only. No CSC minutes, Seednet notification or state gazette confirmed it. Verify before relying on it.

drought.details: PAC 807 is described as a short duration, drought-tolerant hybrid suitable for direct-sown rainfed conditions. It performs well even under water scarcity and has been noted for its drought tolerance as a stress-tolerant rice hybrid (part of the STRASA initiative).

heat.details: Farmers surveyed expressed a demand for more heat-tolerant varieties, and PAC 807 plus was listed in the same surveys. However, there is no direct explicit statement of heat tolerance for PAC 807 itself.

salinity.details: Demand for salt-tolerant rice varieties was noted in surveys where PAC 807 was also listed. PAC 807 plus was mentioned in the context of paddy fields under saline conditions, but no explicit salt tolerance is stated for the variety itself.

flood.details: PAC 807 is recommended in agriculture contingency plans for districts where transient water logging or partial inundation can occur, suggesting it may be suitable for such conditions. However, no explicit flood tolerance is mentioned.

disease_resistance.summary: PAC 807 Plus is described as blast tolerant.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified

agronomic_details.yield: In a rice-chickpea cropping system, PAC 807-chickpea sequence gave a rice crop equivalent yield (RCEY) of 7942 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: The hybrid has 'made its impact with farmers' in various states, suggesting good adoption and performance.
agronomic_details.adaptation: PAC 807 is adapted to direct-sown rainfed conditions and is recommended for hybrid rice cultivation in areas with deep, heavy clay soils, including those prone to transient water logging.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Not specified
agronomic_details.field_trials: PAC 807 has been included in several production-oriented surveys and annual reports from ICAR-IIRR and AICRIP, including surveys in 2019, 2022, and 2023. It is also mentioned in state agriculture contingency plans for Jharkhand (Palamau, Garhwa districts) and in a KVK Gumla trial.

agronomic_details.yield: No numeric yield for PAC 837 Plus was found in the digest. Advanta lists yield data from field locations across India for the 2021/22 and 2022/23 harvests, but no values are given in the digest. For PAC-837 (not confirmed as 'Plus'), the Birsa Agricultural University study reported a 5.2 t/ha grain yield at 35 kg seed/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Advanta notes that results depend on weather and management conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Assam state release (2022-23) per AICRIP report. Assam ASOCA list shows PAC-837 for winter and summer paddy, but this may refer to the non-Plus variety. Marketed as suitable for direct-seeded rice. Aerobic rice trial evidence (non-Plus) from eastern Uttar Pradesh. No agro-climatic zone data found.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 130-135 days (marketed as medium duration in the KrishDoctor listing; not verified by independent trials)
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging, fertilizer responsive, medium maturity (variety record). Marketed with 13-15 productive tillers per plant and suitability for direct-seeded rice. No morphological descriptors found.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Advanta: yield data from field locations across India for 2021/22 and 2022/23 harvests; no numeric results given in the digest. (2) Aerobic rice on-farm trials in Gorakhpur, Deoria and Kushinagar (kharif 2016): PAC 837 (not confirmed as 'Plus') showed better drought tolerance and higher grain yield. (3) Birsa Agricultural University, Ranchi (kharif 2012-2013): PAC-837 (not confirmed as 'Plus') had significantly higher dry matter and a 5.2 t/ha grain yield at 35 kg seed/ha. This study also covered DRRH-3, Arize Tej and Lalat, and is not a PAC 837 Plus-specific trial.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: PAC 837 Plus (rice, hybrid)

Name note: The release-minutes name is "PAC 837 Plus" and the Seednet name is "PAC 837 PLUS". They differ only in capitalisation, so they refer to the same variety. Seednet itself was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-portal evidence was found. Four searches were run: variety/release, breeder, research, and seed availability.

STRESS TOLERANCE:
- Described by a seller as tolerant to blast disease, but this listing is under a VNR Seeds product name ("Mahabali") and conflicts with the Advanta claim, so treat it as unverified -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy
- Aerobic rice on-farm trials in Gorakhpur, Deoria and Kushinagar (2016 kharif) reported PAC 837 (not confirmed as "Plus") with better drought tolerance and higher grain yield -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/talk-on-aerobicrice-technology-onfarm-testing-and-dissemination/63214523
- No evidence found for flood, submergence, heat or salinity tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST:
- Marketed as resistant to bacterial leaf blight (BLB) -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- No peer-reviewed or official resistance-rating evidence found for BLB, blast or insect pests.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS:
- Marketed as medium duration of 130-135 days, 13-15 productive tillers per plant, and suitable for direct-seeded rice -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- Advanta lists yield data from field locations across India for the 2021/22 and 2022/23 harvests, with a caveat that results depend on weather and management -- https://in.advantaseeds.com/products/pac-837-plus
- Birsa Agricultural University (Ranchi), kharif 2012-2013: PAC-837 (not confirmed as "Plus") had significantly higher dry matter and a 5.2 t/ha grain yield at 35 kg seed/ha -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-11-2017/Md.%20Naiyar%20Ali,%20et%20al.pdf
- The same Birsa study covered DRRH-3, PAC-837, Arize Tej and Lalat, so it is not a trial of PAC 837 Plus specifically.

GENETICS AND QTL:
- No evidence found. Parentage given as 837A/837 R was not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION:
- Manufacturer listed as Advanta Seeds (now UPL) -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- AICRIP hybrid rice report 2022-23 records PAC 837 Plus as released in 2022-23 by the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, with a state release for Assam. It lists private-sector breeders as developers, but names no individual breeder -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Draft%20copy%20of%20Hybrid%20Rice%20progress%20report-2022.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS:
- No breeder name, email, phone or postal address found.
- Institute-level contact: Advanta India product page (no contact details on the page) -- https://in.advantaseeds.com/products/pac-837-plus
- Parent company: UPL Limited (formerly Advanta Limited), per the variety record. No UPL contact page was retrieved.

PUBLICATIONS:
- Naiyar Ali, Md. et al. (2017). Effect of seed rate and hybrid rice cultivars on growth and yield at Birsa Agricultural University, Ranchi (kharif 2012-2013). IJCMAS -- https://www.ijcmas.com/6-11-2017/Md.%20Naiyar%20Ali,%20et%20al.pdf (uses PAC-837, not "Plus")
- Hybrid Rice progress report, AICRIP (2022). ICAR AICRIP annual report -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Draft%20copy%20of%20Hybrid%20Rice%20progress%20report-2022.pdf
- Aerobic rice on-farm testing and dissemination talk (2016). Presentation -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/talk-on-aerobicrice-technology-onfarm-testing-and-dissemination/63214523 (uses PAC 837)
- No KrishiKosh theses, DOIs or peer-reviewed papers specific to PAC 837 Plus were found.

SEED AVAILABILITY:
- Sold online as hybrid paddy seed by KrishDoctor -- https://www.krishdoctor.in/product/8VJZbuUtINjWiL0MyQ5a
- Sold online by Agribiz (Advanta brand, 3 kg pack, listed as PAC 837) -- https://agribiz.farm/product/pac-837/
- Sold online by Somani Agro (under the VNR "Mahabali" name) -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy
- Assam's notified-variety list includes PAC-837 under winter and summer paddy, but this may be the non-Plus variety -- https://asoca.assam.gov.in/frontimpotentdata/notified-recommended-varieties-of-different-crops
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sales evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES:
- Assam (state release, 2022-23) -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Draft%20copy%20of%20Hybrid%20Rice%20progress%20report-2022.pdf

drought.details: PAC 837 is identified as a drought-tolerant rice hybrid. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and has been studied for marker-trait association under drought stress. It is listed among rice hybrids tolerant to abiotic stress conditions.

heat.details: PAC 837 is listed among hybrids with adaptations to heat stress tolerance and is considered heat tolerant in nature. Efforts are also noted to incorporate heat tolerance in rice varieties.

salinity.details: PAC 837 is recognized as a rice hybrid tolerant to abiotic stress conditions, including salinity. It is mentioned in contexts where tolerance to stress conditions such as salinity is a desired trait for hybrids. Farmers have expressed a need for salt tolerant varieties, with PAC 837 being cultivated.

flood.details: PAC 837 is listed among varieties capable of adapting to excess water conditions. It is mentioned in the context of flash-flood tolerance and tolerance to water logging, which are important traits for rice cultivation.

disease_resistance.summary: PAC 837 shows moderate resistance (MR) to Rice Tungro Virus (RTV), Bacterial Sheath blight (BS), and Gall Midge (GLH). For PAC 837 Plus, it is tolerant against Blast (Leaf Blast Resistant, LB R-BL) and moderately resistant to Bacterial Sheath Blight (MR-BS). False Smut has become a major problem for PAC 837 in Barpeta district of Assam.

pest_resistance.summary: PAC 837 shows moderate resistance (MR) to Green Leaf Hopper (GLH).

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 6.32 tons/ha. Reported yields also include 5.62 t/ha and 6.30 t/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Its widespread recommendation and inclusion in various national reports and hybrid lists suggest reasonable stability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated areas and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Cultivated during the boro season in Assam. Suitable for medium duration conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging, fertilizer responsive, medium maturity hybrid. It is semi-dwarf, with reported heights ranging from 82 cm to 100 cm. Grains are Long Slender (LS).
agronomic_details.field_trials: PAC 837 has been part of field experiments, national level monitoring team reports (BGREI), production oriented surveys, and research bulletins focusing on hybrid rice seed production technology. It has shown impact with farmers in states like Bihar, Jharkhand, and Gujarat. It has been evaluated in comparison to other hybrids and local checks.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Research has been conducted on PAC 837 to access leaf shape dynamics through marker-trait association under drought stress. This indicates the use of genetic markers in studies involving the variety.

drought.details: PAC 837 is identified as a drought-tolerant rice hybrid. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and has been studied for marker-trait association under drought stress. It is listed among rice hybrids tolerant to abiotic stress conditions.

heat.details: PAC 837 is listed among hybrids with adaptations to heat stress tolerance and is considered heat tolerant in nature. Efforts are also noted to incorporate heat tolerance in rice varieties.

salinity.details: PAC 837 is recognized as a rice hybrid tolerant to abiotic stress conditions, including salinity. It is mentioned in contexts where tolerance to stress conditions such as salinity is a desired trait for hybrids. Farmers have expressed a need for salt tolerant varieties, with PAC 837 being cultivated.

flood.details: PAC 837 is listed among varieties capable of adapting to excess water conditions. It is mentioned in the context of flash-flood tolerance and tolerance to water logging, which are important traits for rice cultivation.

submergence.details: PAC 837 is grouped with hybrids for which submergence tolerance is a desired trait. Farmers have expressed a need for varieties having tolerance to submergence. While not explicitly stated as 'submergence tolerant' for PAC 837 itself, its inclusion in lists of abiotic stress tolerant hybrids and discussions about incorporating submergence tolerance suggests some level of adaptation or ongoing efforts for improvement.

disease_resistance.summary: PAC 837 shows moderate resistance (MR) to Rice Tungro Virus (RTV), Bacterial Sheath blight (BS), and Gall Midge (GLH). For PAC 837 Plus, it is tolerant against Blast (Leaf Blast Resistant, LB R-BL) and moderately resistant to Bacterial Sheath Blight (MR-BS). False Smut has become a major problem for PAC 837 in Barpeta district of Assam.

pest_resistance.summary: PAC 837 shows moderate resistance (MR) to Green Leaf Hopper (GLH).

genetics_and_qtl.genetic_markers: Research has been conducted on PAC 837 to access leaf shape dynamics through marker-trait association under drought stress. This indicates the use of genetic markers in studies involving the variety.

agronomic_performance.yield: Average yield 6.32 tons/ha. Reported yields also include 5.62 t/ha and 6.30 t/ha.
agronomic_performance.stability: Its widespread recommendation and inclusion in various national reports and hybrid lists suggest reasonable stability across different environments.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Adapted to irrigated areas and suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions. Cultivated during the boro season in Assam. Suitable for medium duration conditions.
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: Non-lodging, fertilizer responsive, medium maturity hybrid. It is semi-dwarf, with reported heights ranging from 82 cm to 100 cm. Grains are Long Slender (LS).
agronomic_performance.field_trials: PAC 837 has been part of field experiments, national level monitoring team reports (BGREI), production oriented surveys, and research bulletins focusing on hybrid rice seed production technology. It has shown impact with farmers in states like Bihar, Jharkhand, and Gujarat. It has been evaluated in comparison to other hybrids and local checks.

breeder_and_contacts.breeder: Dr. Sanjay Kumar Chetia, Chief Scientist at Assam Agricultural University (AAU), has conducted studies involving PAC 837, including marker-trait association under drought stress and identification for boro season.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PAC 8744 RICE: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Names: the CSC record name is "PAC 8744" and the Seednet name is also "PAC 8744". No Seednet page was retrieved. Retail pages use "PAC 8744+", "PAC 8744 Plus" and "UPL Advanta 8744+" for what appears to be the same product, and I have treated them as this variety only where the page itself names PAC 8744. Four searches were run (the maximum). All of them returned retailer or trader pages. None returned Seednet, ICAR/CSC, institute, KrishiKosh, AICRP or journal material for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The retailer pages describe it only as suited to irrigated conditions. PAC 8744 Plus is a premium hybrid rice engineered for maximum productivity in irrigated environments. -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial leaf blight (BLB) tolerance is claimed by the seller and not supported by trial data. This medium-duration variety is specifically bred for high Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) resistance, ensuring crop stability. -- https://www.somaniagro.com/collections/paddy
- A second retailer lists tolerance to BLB and no other disease resistance. Tolerance to BLB -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice
- A 2020 advisory lists the PAC 8744+ name as fortified for BLB. PAC 8744+ · Medium maturity irrigated, fortified for BLB, high yielding -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/paddy-cultivation-advisory-amid-covid-19/
- Blast, insect and other pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration and growth habit, per retailer: Kharif Duration: 130 – 135 days, medium maturity, irrigated, with long slender grain and long panicles -- https://mydukaan.io/bumi7/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice
- Yield claim, marketer only: 20% more than OP varieties of the same duration -- https://www.bighaat.com/products/pac-8744-advanta-hybrid-paddy-rice (no trial, station or season data behind it)
- Duration also listed on a second retailer page: Short Description : ONE OF THE BEST HYBRID SEED OF PADDY Duration : 130-135 DAYS. -- https://agribiz.farm/product/pac-8744/
- Multi-location or AICRP trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: No evidence found. The CSC record gives it as not specified, and no page names a parent line.
- QTL, marker or genomic study: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Named breeder or scientist, and developing station: No evidence found.
- Company as shown on retail pages: UPL Advanta 8744+ Seed (3 per packet) -- https://www.flipkart.com/upl-advanta-8744-seed/p/itmcda922e04c552 (the CSC record names Advanta Limited; the retail listing brands it under UPL Advanta.)

CONTACT DETAILS

- Third-party seller, Dharti Agro Chemicals Pvt. Ltd., Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh: Trader - Wholesaler / Distributor of Pac 8744 Hybrid Paddy Seed ... offered by Dharti Agro Chemicals Pvt. Ltd., Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. -- https://www.indiamart.com/ankur-seed-ltd/other-products.html (trader listing; no email or street address was shown; not the developer.)

PUBLICATIONS
- No evidence found. The search returned only unrelated rice papers (Pusa Basmati 1121, IR64, IR8 and genome studies). These were discarded under the relevance rule and are not attributed to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY

drought.details: Paiyur 1, described in the search results as a rice variety, is highly tolerant to drought. It is suitable for direct sown rainfed conditions and is of short duration. Studies indicate it clustered along with the resistant check Pokkali, providing evidence of its drought tolerance.

heat.details: Paiyur 1 clustered with the resistant check Pokkali, suggesting some level of heat stress tolerance.

salinity.details: Paiyur 1 is described as highly tolerant to salinity stress and is recognized as a salt-tolerant rice culture. It has been identified as suitable for saline lands and for raising seedlings in sodic soil with sodic water irrigation. It demonstrated the highest single plant yield under saline conditions among tested genotypes (27.59 g). Its salinity tolerance was achieved through marker-aided selection.

flood.details: Paiyur 1 is listed as a recommended non-lodging and submergence-tolerant paddy variety, implying tolerance to flood conditions.

disease_resistance.summary: Paiyur 1 is tolerant to Rice Tungro Virus (RTV) and is generally categorized as a disease-resistant variety.

pest_resistance.summary: Not specified in the provided search results.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield of Paiyur 1 is reported as 57 Q/ha (5630 Kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Its recommendation for various stress conditions (drought, salinity, submergence) and different cultivation seasons implies a degree of adaptability across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Paiyur 1 is adapted to direct sown rainfed conditions and semi-deep water environments. It is suitable for cultivation in saline and sodic soils. It is recommended for the Navarai season (December-January) and can be sown in June-July or September 15-20. It is specifically identified within the ACZ-IV North Western zone of Tamil Nadu.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Paiyur 1 is characterized by Medium Slender (MS) grains. It is a non-lodging and photosensitive variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Paiyur 1 has been part of test verification centers for rice crops and included in Production Oriented Surveys (POS) in various years (e.g., 2022, 2023).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Paiyur 1's tolerance to drought and salinity stress was developed or improved through marker-aided selection. Specific genetic markers (QTL/SNP/SSR) are not detailed.

genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The variety is a derivative of the cross IR-1721-14 x IR-1330-3. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Palghar-2 (rice). Four searches were run. None returned a source describing the Palghar-2 variety itself, so most headings say "No evidence found."

Name note: The CSC release name is Palghar-2 and the Seednet name is PALGHAR-1. The searches used both names, and none of the results matched either one. The only hits were general Palghar district rice pages. Those pages do not refer to either variety name.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice variety" and "PALGHAR-1 paddy seed availability".

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice variety".

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice variety" and "Palghar-2 rice research paper".

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. Searched "Palghar-2 rice research paper". Parentage IR-22/PALGHAR-141-1 (from the variety record, not verified by search).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for the breeder or the developing station. Only a general reference to Dr. Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth, Dapoli (M.S.) appeared, in a ResearchGate paper on rice input availability in Palghar district -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333652002_Input_availability_sources_for_rice_growers_of_Palghar_district (this confirms the university exists but not that it developed Palghar-2).

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found for any breeder, email, phone, or address. Institution named in the record: Dr. Balasaheb Sawant Konkan Krishi Vidyapeeth, Dapoli. Its official site was not retrieved, so no contact details were verified.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for Palghar-2 or PALGHAR-1. The only item retrieved is not about the variety: Authors not captured (2019 indexing). Input availability sources for rice growers of Palghar district. ResearchGate preprint -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/333652002_Input_availability_sources_for_rice_growers_of_Palghar_district

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for Palghar-2 or PALGHAR-1 from NSC, state seed corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales, or dealers. Searched "PALGHAR-1 paddy seed availability".

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The variety record lists "Not specified." Searches did not confirm a state recommendation.

Gaps and next steps (not run, since the 4-search limit was reached):
- Check seednet.gov.in directly for variety code A0102536 under PALGHAR-1.
- Check the CSC/ICAR release notification for Palghar-2 (2013) for state and parentage details.
- Search KrishiKosh and the Dapoli university site for Palghar-2 trial reports and the breeding station.
