search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I could only complete one of the three required searches. The tool returned "Server tool use limit exceeded" partway through the batch, and later calls failed on the same limit. The digest below is therefore incomplete, and most headings are unresolved rather than negative.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: PAN 2423 (variety_name) / PAN-2423 (seednet_variety_name), rice (Seednet crop: PADDY (DHAN)). Search 1 returned evidence under "PAN 2423"; Seednet (PAN-2423) was not searched successfully.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Not established. No search result addressed drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety. Searches not completed because the tool limit was reached.

DISEASE AND PEST: Not established. No search result addressed disease or pest resistance. Searches not completed because the tool limit was reached.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Partial, unverified marketing claim only. A Hindi-language YouTube video titled "PAN 2423 - The best hybrid seeds rice in India" describes it as a 115-120 day hybrid rice that is said to give higher yield in less time -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bhwvr71-pn4 (commercial promotional content; no trial data; the duration figure is unverified).

GENETICS AND QTL: Not established. No search result addressed parentage or marker studies. The parentage in the record (025A x AN138; AN 138 from IR 75207H; female parent from Annada and Jaloi Minikit) is unverified by any search result. Searches not completed because the tool limit was reached.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Not established. The only company-linked result is a PAN Seeds product category page, which is a commercial source and does not name a breeder or research institute -- https://panseeds.in/product-category/hybrid-rice/ (the visible snippet does not clearly name PAN 2423; it lists "Suitable for Rabi (Boro), non lodging and non shattering, good cooking quality" among hybrid rice features, which I could not tie to this variety).

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found for a breeder, institute or ICAR/SAU contact. The only company presence is the PAN Seeds product page above (https://panseeds.in/product-category/hybrid-rice/); its contact details were not visible in the retrieved snippet. The company's email, phone and address were not verified.

PUBLICATIONS: Not searched successfully (search 3 not run because the tool limit was reached). No publications have been identified.

SEED AVAILABILITY: Partial, commercial only. The PAN Seeds hybrid rice product category page lists hybrid rice seed for sale -- https://panseeds.in/product-category/hybrid-rice/ (variety-level listing for PAN 2423 not confirmed). The YouTube results also promote PAN 2423 seed sales -- https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qcrul-ZCpz0. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or Seednet listing was found; the Seednet search (search 4) was not completed.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Not verified. The record lists Assam, but no search result confirmed a state recommendation or notification.

Gaps to resolve in a follow-up session: the CSC release notification and Seednet entry for PAN-2423; breeder and institute contacts; any AICRP, KrishiKosh or journal trial data; and seed-dealer listings in Assam.

drought.details: PB-1 is recognized as a drought-tolerant rice variety, with studies showing its ability to surpass certain stress conditions. It has been evaluated for multi-stress tolerance including drought. Some trials recorded significant superiority (308.5% and 61.3%) over recurrent parents for drought stress traits.

heat.details: PB-1 has demonstrated heat stress tolerance and is among varieties demanded by farmers for climate variability. It has been included in heat stress tolerance trials.

salinity.details: PB-1 has been evaluated in multi-location testing under inland saline and sodic soils, indicating its salt-tolerant nature. It is listed as a salt tolerant rice variety and has been used in crosses to develop salt tolerant lines (e.g., CSR CPB 69 from CSR 89 IR 15/PB 1).

flood.details: PB-1 is noted for its tolerance to water-submergence and stagnant flooding conditions. It has also shown tolerance to anaerobic germination, which is relevant for flood-prone areas or specific planting methods like direct wet seeding.

disease_resistance.summary: PB-1 is a bacterial blight resistant variety. It shows moderate resistance (MR) to Blast, Stem Rot, and Sheath Rot.

pest_resistance.summary: PB-1 was part of Y-tube olfactometer assays, but the specific nature of its pest reaction (resistance or susceptibility) is not detailed in the provided content.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported yield values in various trials include 175.86 and other figures like 102.00, 135.67, 111.95, though units (e.g., kg/ha or t/ha) are not consistently specified. It is a high-yielding genotype, particularly when tolerant to salinity, alkalinity, and waterlogging stresses.
agronomic_details.stability: Evaluated in multi-location testing under inland saline and sodic conditions, suggesting good stability across different environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted to various stress conditions including drought, heat, salinity, and waterlogging. Suitable for cultivation in areas with moderately saline and sodic soils, and is noted for its ability to smother weeds to a great extent.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Produces extra-long slender translucent grains with 58.2% head rice recovery. Has robust shoot and root development under various stress conditions.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Numerous trials including Advance Variety Trials (AVT-BT), multi-location testing, production oriented surveys, and demonstrations have been conducted. For instance, 57 demonstrations on paddy PB 1 were conducted in 2018-19. It has been used in the evaluation of responses to contrasting sensitive and tolerant rice genotypes.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: SSR markers have been identified in studies involving PB-1.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Major QTLs for abiotic stress tolerance have been identified in varieties including PB-1. Specifically, QTLs for reproductive stage salinity tolerance have been dissected from crosses involving PB-1. It has been used in crosses involving N22 for drought stress traits (PB 1*3/N22).
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: Overexpression of OsTIP1;2 in PB-1 rice conferred tolerance to As[III]. It has been transformed with a zinc transporter gene. OsM4 and OsMB11 are substantially expressed in drought and salinity stress, related to genomic regions identified from crosses involving PB-1.

drought.details: The NRRI bulletin snippet mentions drought tolerance near the Phalguni entry, but the text is fragmented and the row attribution is unclear. The digest does not record this as confirmed, so no drought level is assigned. Mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

heat.details: No evidence found for this variety in the retrieved pages.

salinity.details: No evidence found for this variety in the retrieved pages.

flood.details: The NRRI popular-varieties page states that Phalguni (CR Dhan 801) tolerates water stagnation up to 50 cm and suits delayed transplanting. The digest does not assign a tolerance grade to this flood-type trait, so the level is recorded as unknown. Mechanisms: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Leaf blast: resistant (R-BL) per CRRI/NRRI released-variety entry; also reported as resistant in the ricesci.org summary citing CRRI Annual Report 2009-2010. Sheath rot: moderately resistant (released-variety entry and ricesci.org). Sheath blight: moderately resistant (released-variety entry and ricesci.org). Brown spot: moderately resistant (ricesci.org). Rice stripe virus: moderately resistant (ricesci.org). Tungro: moderate resistance (popular-varieties page). Field tolerance to major diseases and pests is stated on the popular-varieties page without a named disease list. The digest advises checking the NRRI bulletin before using any single reaction as a standard, because the summaries come from different sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Gall midge: resistant (released-variety entry and ricesci.org; popular-varieties page gives moderate resistance). Stem borer: resistant or moderately resistant (released-variety entry); yellow stem borer moderately resistant (ricesci.org); moderate resistance (popular-varieties page). Leaf folder: resistant or moderately resistant (released-variety entry). Planthoppers: resistant or moderately resistant (released-variety entry); brown planthopper (BPH) moderate resistance (popular-varieties page). Whorl maggot: resistant or moderately resistant (released-variety entry). The digest advises checking the NRRI bulletin before using any single reaction as a standard.

agronomic_details.yield: Release list (kharif): 4.0-4.5 t/ha, higher under other conditions. Popular-varieties page: 5.0-6.0 t/ha average productivity. Odisha rice varieties table: 6300 kg/ha potential yield. The release-list and popular-varieties ranges differ and both are reported. Input value supplied: 55.60 Kg/Ha (not confirmed by any digest source; the digest does not report a matching figure).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to irrigated areas of Odisha (popular-varieties page). Suits delayed transplanting and water stagnation up to 50 cm (popular-varieties page). Volume expansion ratio is higher than other NRRI varieties, which is a cooking quality trait and not a stress trait.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 133 DAYS (input value). The digest reports 115-120 days (popular-varieties page) and 117 days (release list); these conflict with the input value.

agronomic_details.field_trials: 2023 kharif, Kalahandi, NICRA project: CR Dhan 801 (Phalguni) on farmer fields gave higher yields than controls, with a net gain of about 4.5 q/ha (ResearchGate preprint on a KVK Kalahandi/OUAT case study). No other trial results found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Submergence/stagnation: NRRI's popular-varieties page says Phalguni (CR Dhan 801) tolerates water stagnation up to 50 cm and suits delayed transplanting -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Submergence (listed as a trait in a table, which conflicts with the NRRI release entry): an Odisha rice varieties table lists CR Dhan 801 (Phalguni) as submergence-tolerant and non-lodging -- https://rkb-odisha.in/rice-in-odisha/rice-varieties-of-odisha/
Drought: the NRRI bulletin snippet mentions drought tolerance near the Phalguni entry, but the text is fragmented and the row attribution is unclear, so I am not recording it as confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338966196_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
Volume expansion (cooking quality, not stress): Phalguni is named among NRRI varieties with higher volume expansion ratio -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/Rice-Varieties-of-NRRI.pdf
Salinity, heat, flood: No evidence found for this variety in the retrieved pages.

DISEASE AND PEST
Released-variety entry (CRRI/NRRI list): resistant to leaf blast (R-BL), moderately resistant to sheath rot and sheath blight, resistant to gall midge, and listed as resistant or moderately resistant to several pests (stem borer, leaf folder, planthoppers, whorl maggot, gall midge) -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Disease/pest reaction summary (ricesci.org, citing CRRI Annual Report 2009-2010): resistant to leaf blast and gall midge; moderately resistant to sheath rot, rice stripe virus, yellow stem borer, brown spot and sheath blight -- http://www.ricesci.org/EN/10.1016/j.rsci.2016.02.001
Field tolerance: the popular-varieties page says it has field tolerance to major diseases and pests, and moderate resistance to leaf blast, tungro, BPH, gall midge and stem borer -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Note: the pest and disease entries name several virus and insect reactions that come from different summaries, so check the NRRI bulletin before using any one reaction as a standard.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Duration and type: 115-120 days, semidwarf, doubled-haploid, for irrigated areas of Odisha -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Duration and height from the release list: 117 days, long slender grain, about 105 cm, kharif yield 4.0-4.5 t/ha and higher under other conditions -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Yield: the popular-varieties page gives 5.0-6.0 t/ha average productivity; an Odisha rice varieties table gives 6300 kg/ha potential yield -- https://rkb-odisha.in/rice-in-odisha/rice-varieties-of-odisha/
Field performance (2023 kharif, Kalahandi, NICRA project): CR Dhan 801 (Phalguni) on farmer fields gave higher yields than controls, with a net gain of about 4.5 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/379581355_Performance_of_Climate_Smart_Rice_var_CR_DHAN_801_A_Case_Study_from_Western_Undulating_Zone_of_Odisha_India
Yield discrepancy: the release-list yield range and the popular-varieties range differ, so cite both.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage conflict: the NRRI variety table records Phalguni as a doubled-haploid derivative of KRH2, not the IR-8 x Siam-29 parentage supplied in the task. The provided parentage was not confirmed by any retrieved source -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/338966196_Rice_Varieties_of_NRRI
Doubled-haploid origin: confirmed by the popular-varieties page and the NRRI table -- https://icar-crri.in/popular-nrri-varieties/
Marker or QTL studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: ICAR-National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack, Odisha; the release list is headed "Rice varieties developed by ICAR-NRRI, Cuttack" -- https://icar-crri.in/released-varieties/
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found in any retrieved page.
Station: NRRI, Cuttack (headquarters). No sub-station named.
Name note: "Orissa" in the input is the former state name for the release state; the release entry itself gives Orissa.
Name note: Phalguni is also listed as CR Dhan 801; NRRI sources treat this as the same variety.
Name note: a different "Phalguna" (IET-2911) in a Karnataka notified list and a 1979 "PHALGUNA" entry in a Bihar list are different varieties and are discarded -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/list-of-notified-paddy-varieties-for-karnataka/ and https://dbtagriculture.bihar.gov.in/licence/Document/Variety.pdf
Seednet name PHALGUNA: No Seednet page was retrieved, so the Seednet record could not be checked.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level address (no breeder contact found): ICAR-National Rice Research Institute, Cuttack, Odisha-753006, India -- https://icar-nrri.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/08/NRRI_Research-Bulletin-No-54.pdf

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics PAU, Ludhiana
seednet_fields.Parentage:
The designation of this line is PAU 6260-3-1-6.
It has been developed from the cross PR 121/ HKR47
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: RYT 3797 is a semi-dwarf, of mid early maturity and will fit well in ricewheat cropping system prevalent in the state. In research trials, RYT 3797 gave an average yield of 7225 kg/ha of paddy.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics:
RYT 3797 is a semi dwarf genotype which matures in about 105 days after
transplanting. It possesses long slender clear translucent grains with average L/B ratio of 3.62
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases:
This genotype is resistant to all the ten pathotypes of bacterial blight
pathogen prevalent in the state. 
susceptible to sheath blight disease against which genetic resistance is not
available.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Like other varieties this is susceptible to major insect pests like stem borer, leaf folder and white backed plant hopper prevalent in the state.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha):
90 kg neem coated urea (NCU)/acre at 0, 21 and 42
days after transplanting in three equal splits.

drought.details: No evidence found in the digest on drought tolerance mechanisms or performance.

heat.details: No evidence found in the digest on heat tolerance mechanisms or performance.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the digest on salinity tolerance mechanisms or performance.

flood.details: No evidence found in the digest on flood tolerance mechanisms or performance. Lodging tolerance is reported (PAU 2022 release statement and Kharif Package of Practices) but is not a flood or submergence measure.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight: described as resistant. The Kharif Package of Practices states that PR 130 resists all ten bacterial blight pathotypes prevalent in Punjab. No evidence found on blast, sheath blight or other diseases.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence found for resistance to brown planthopper (BPH), stem borer or any other pest.

agronomic_details.yield: Average paddy yield 30.0 quintals per acre (PAU release).
agronomic_details.stability: No evidence found across environments (no multi-location trial data).

EVIDENCE DIGEST: PR 130 (rice)

Name note: The CSC release name is "PR 130" and the Seednet name is "PR-113". All evidence below refers to PR 130 (Punjab Agricultural University). None of the four searches returned a Seednet page for PR-113. The Punjab Package of Practices lists PR 113 as a separate, older variety released in 1998, so the Seednet record does not appear to be the same variety and should be checked against the portal.

Search budget: I used all four permitted web_search queries in one batch. The research and contact searches returned little that was specific to PR 130, so several headings below are gaps.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Lodging tolerant, per PAU's 2022 release statement and the Kharif Package of Practices. Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506 ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- Described as bacterial blight resistant; the Package of Practices says it resists all ten bacterial blight pathotypes prevalent in Punjab. No evidence on blast, sheath blight, BPH or stem borer. -- https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Maturity about 105 days after transplanting. Average plant height about 108 cm. Average paddy yield 30.0 quintals per acre (PAU release). Recommended nursery sowing is May 20-31 per the release, and May 25-31 per the Kharif Package of Practices. Grain is long, slender, translucent, with high total and head rice recovery. Multi-location trial data: No evidence found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506 ; https://pau.edu/content/ccil/pf/pp_kharif.pdf ; https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/updates-detaills/new-varieties-of-paddy-released-by-pau/1127

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage: PR 121 × HKR 47, per PAU's release statement. This corrects the "Not specified" entry in the input record. QTL or marker studies: No evidence found. -- https://pau.edu/index.php?DO=viewEventDetail&_act=manageEvent&intID=6506

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Developing institution: Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana (Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics per the input record). Named PAU scientists in the search results: Dr Gurjit Singh Mangat, Additional Director of Research (Crop Improvement), who is quoted on the release; and Dr Buta Singh Dhillon, Senior Rice Breeder, named in a later PAU advisory. CONTACT DETAILS -- Dr Gurjit Singh Mangat, Additional Director of Research (Crop Improvement), PAU -- email, phone and address: not found in search results. drought_tolerance.technical_details: No source reports a drought tolerance rating for PR-114. The PAU package of practices mentions water stress from rainfall failure or canal closure only as a management risk. A genomic-breeding review lists drought QTL (qDTY2.2 + qDTY4.1) for IR64 Drt1 (DRR Dhan 42), not for PR-114. Wild-relative introgression work mentions PR 114 only as a genetic background.

heat_tolerance.technical_details: The Heliyon review's heat-tolerance snippet appears next to a list of varieties (ADT 45, Gayatri, MTU 1010, PR 114), but the snippet does not show that PR 114 itself was tested or found heat tolerant. This is not valid evidence of tolerance.

salinity_tolerance.technical_details: The Heliyon review lists PR 114 with ADT 45, Gayatri, MTU 1010, Pusa 44 and Sarjoo 52 in the context of qSALTOL + qSSISFH8.1 marker-assisted work (ref 92, apparently Singh et al. 2016). This suggests PR 114 was a recipient or background variety for Saltol introgression. It does not show that PR-114 itself is salt tolerant. The NRRI book says the goal is to transfer Sub1 + drought QTL + Saltol into popular varieties. The introgression status or outcome for PR 114 cannot be confirmed from the snippets.

flood_tolerance.technical_details: No flood or waterlogging tolerance data for PR-114 were found. It was released for irrigated medium ecosystems.

submergence_tolerance.technical_details: No evidence that PR-114 carries Sub1 or is submergence tolerant. Mentions of submergence in the ARGM proceedings concern screening trials in general. PR-114 appears in those documents only in seed indent/production tables.

disease_resistance.technical_details: A ResearchGate figure on marker-assisted backcross breeding states PR 114 is resistant to BLB with an average yield of 6.7 t/ha. The NIPHM IPM package lists PR 114 among BLB-resistant varieties (with PR 111, PR 113, PR 115, PR 116, PR 118). The specific Xa genes are not stated in the snippets. Resistance to other diseases is not documented.

key_stress_attributes: BLB resistance (NIPHM IPM package; ResearchGate figure on marker-assisted backcross breeding)
Used as a background variety in Saltol/marker-assisted and wild-relative introgression work. This is not evidence of tolerance in PR-114 itself.

genetic_and_molecular_profile.genetic_markers: No markers are documented for PR-114 itself. The Heliyon review links PR 114 to qSALTOL + qSSISFH8.1 as a recipient or background variety. The wild-relative paper (Plant Breeding, doi:10.1111/pbr.12875) reports that PR 114 crossed with O. nivara accessions (CR100142A, IRGC100593) showed complete fertility restoration.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.qtl_information: Saltol-related QTL (qSALTOL, qSSISFH8.1) are associated with PR 114 in the introgression context. No confirmed introgression outcome or effect size is available.
genetic_and_molecular_profile.breeding_techniques: PR-114 was developed by conventional breeding at PAU. It has since been used as a recipient parent in marker-assisted backcross and wild-relative introgression work.

agronomic_performance.yield_stability: Widely grown in Punjab, which suggests good performance there. No multi-environment stability analysis is available.

agronomic_performance.farmer_adoption: The sarr.co.in review identifies PR-114 as a leading variety in Punjab seed indents. It is present in multiple ARGM breeder seed indent tables (e.g. 13.94 q in 2023-24 and 0.48-19.10 q in other years). No direct farmer feedback is available.

gujarat_scoring_assessment.scoring_rationale: PR-114 has citations: a Heliyon review, a Plant Breeding paper, ICAR proceedings and PAU documents. However, the stress evidence is weak. BLB resistance is documented, but that is a biotic trait and its sources are secondary. Salinity, drought and heat are not shown for PR-114 itself, since the review snippets only list it as a background variety. There is no evidence of suitability for Gujarat. Yield data exist (about 6-6.7 t/ha in Punjab), but their provenance is mixed. The score is therefore at the 50-60 level (some trait, weak citation support), and 50 is chosen because no abiotic stress trait is confirmed and the citations are mostly indirect.

dashboard_data.key_attributes: Semi-dwarf PAU variety for irrigated medium lands; BLB resistant; yield about 6-6.7 t/ha in Punjab; popular in Punjab seed indents; used as a background in Saltol and wild-relative introgression studies.

full_analysis_result.comprehensive_summary: PR-114 is a semi-dwarf, BLB-resistant, high-yielding PAU rice variety (about 6-6.7 t/ha) released around 2000 for irrigated conditions in Punjab. No abiotic stress tolerance (drought, heat, salinity, submergence) is confirmed for the variety itself, since it appears in the literature mainly as a background for Saltol and wild-relative introgression work. Evidence quality is low to moderate and suitability for Gujarat is undocumented.
full_analysis_result.phase1_summary: Semi-dwarf PAU variety with narrow, dark green erect leaves and a height of about 102 cm. Yield is about 6-6.7 t/ha under irrigated Punjab conditions. Maturity duration and parentage are not specified.
full_analysis_result.phase2_summary: BLB resistance is the only documented stress trait. No evidence confirms drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance in PR-114 itself. Its mentions in genomic reviews concern use as a breeding background.

disease_resistance.summary: Bacterial blight (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae): the source reports PR 123 as resistant to all 10 presently prevalent pathotypes of the BB pathogen in Punjab (ResearchGate figure). A PAU-linked summary at apnikheti.com describes it as only moderately resistant to bacterial blight, which conflicts with the first source; the conflict is unresolved. The research paper's disease reaction table (artificial inoculation at PAU) is referenced, but its values were not legible in the extracted text. Sheath blight: susceptible, with no genetic resistance available (ResearchGate figure). The AICRIP Ludhiana document lists PR 123 among bacterial blight variety entries, but gene assignments were not legible.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pests: No evidence found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Across 117 trials, mean 7333 kg/ha, about 8.75% above the check PR 111 (6743 kg/ha). Farm yield about 29 quintal/acre (apnikheti.com). A press account reports average paddy yield about 2.0 quintal/acre above PR 111, with some farmers reporting 90-100 maunds/acre.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources beyond the multi-trial mean reported across 117 trials.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Fits the rice-wheat system in Punjab (ResearchGate figure). The digest notes a 2014 state approval reported in the research paper, which conflicts with the 2015-10-12 release date in the record.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: About 143 days after seeding (ResearchGate figure). The original record listed 'Not Available'.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Semi-dwarf; dark green erect leaves; average plant height about 105 cm; about 338 panicles per square metre; about 136 spikelets per panicle; 88.0% fertility. Grain: extra-long slender, translucent; length/breadth ratio 3.98; head rice recovery 54.68%.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Across 117 trials, 7333 kg/ha, about 8.75% above the check PR 111 (6743 kg/ha). (2) Tested in the AICRIP IVT-IME trial in Kharif 2013 as IET 23774 (no yield result given in the digest). (3) Farm yield about 29 quintal/acre (apnikheti.com). (4) Press account: about 2.0 quintal/acre above PR 111 on average, with some farmers reporting 90-100 maunds/acre.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PR 123 (rice, Punjab Agricultural University, PAU code PAU 3842): evidence digest

Name note: "PR 123" (CSC minutes name) is used in all searches except the seed-availability query, which also used "PR-123" (Seednet name). No Seednet page was found under either spelling, so every finding below refers to the name "PR 123" unless stated otherwise. The 2015-10-12 release date in the record conflicts with the 2014 state approval reported in the research paper; both are noted under RECOMMENDED STATES.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Resistant to all 10 presently prevalent pathotypes of bacterial blight in Punjab -- PR 123 is resistant to all the presently prevalent 10 pathotypes of BB pathogen (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae) in the state of Punjab. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Conflicting bacterial blight description: a PAU-linked summary calls it only moderately resistant to bacterial blight -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/rice
- Sheath blight: susceptible, with no genetic resistance available -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found. The search returned no PR 123-specific tolerance data for these stresses.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Bacterial blight: see STRESS TOLERANCE above. The research paper's disease reaction table (artificial inoculation at PAU) is referenced but its values were not legible in the extracted text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277005303_PR_123_A_New_High_Yielding_Variety_of_Superfine_Rice_Oryza_sativa_L
- Insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Semi-dwarf, dark green erect leaves, average plant height about 105 cm -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Maturity about 143 days after seeding; fits the rice-wheat system in Punjab -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Yield components: about 338 panicles per square metre, about 136 spikelets per panicle, 88.0% fertility -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Across 117 trials, 7333 kg/ha, about 8.75% above the check PR 111 (6743 kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Farm yield about 29 quintal/acre -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/cereals/rice
- Average paddy yield about 2.0 quintal/acre above PR 111, with some farmers reporting 90-100 maunds/acre; this is a press account -- https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/archive/features/rice-variety-pr-111-replaces-pr-123-84192
- Grain quality: extra-long slender, translucent grain, length/breadth ratio 3.98, head rice recovery 54.68% -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- Tested in the AICRIP IVT-IME trial in Kharif 2013 as IET 23774 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303

GENETICS AND QTL
- Designation PAU 3842-59-7-1-1, from the cross PR 116///PR 108/IRRI 76//PR 106-P2, by pedigree selection. This gives the parentage that the record lists as "Not specified" -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/PR-123-a-new-variety-of-superfine-rice_fig1_277005303
- QTL and marker studies: No evidence found. A PAU-AICRIP Ludhiana table lists PR 123 among bacterial blight variety entries, but gene assignments were not legible -- http://aicrip-intranet.in/Documents/AicripSite/Centers/31%20Ludhiana.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to most patho types of Xanthomonas oryza (Bacterial Blight). Also reported as highly resistant to Leaf Blight (LB), neck infection (Neck Blast), and 'Sh.' (possibly Sheath Blight). Screening for resistance to Rice Tungro Disease was conducted in trials, though PR-124's specific resistance level to Tungro is not detailed.

pest_resistance.summary: PR-124 is reported to be susceptible to Stem Borer (SB), Leaf Folder (LF), and White-backed Planthopper (WBPH). Discussions in meetings included general assessment of insect pests like yellow stem borer.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Adapted for irrigated conditions in Haryana and Punjab. It is classified as a Non-Basmati variety and is suitable for semi-deep water conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: PR-124 is a semi-dwarf variety, with a height of 82 cm. It produces long slender (LS) grains and is described as a protein-rich paddy variety.
agronomic_details.field_trials: The variety has been part of various trials, including Farmer Field Trials, collaborative trials with Agronomy on returns in transplanted rice, and yield loss assessment due to major rice pests. Numerical data (e.g., 3.42, 9.60, 6.18) are listed for PR-124 in trial summaries within the 59th Annual Rice Group Meetings proceedings, though the specific metrics for these numbers are not defined.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Pratibha (rice) -- variety_name "Pratibha" / seednet_variety_name "PRATIBHA" (OR 2172-7, IET 21582; SOWBHAGYA/ARC 6650; OUAT; released 2018-08-10)

Search budget: 4 web_search queries were run (one batch of four, covering variety/release, breeder/institution, research/trials, and seed availability). No query returned a page that names the rice variety Pratibha. Under each heading below, "No evidence found" means none of the four searches surfaced a relevant record. It does not mean the variety lacks such data. Seednet was not reached directly, so neither name was confirmed on that portal.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. Searches returned only other OUAT rice releases (Kalinga Rice 1/Kolab, Kalinga Dhan 1205) with no Pratibha entry -- https://ouat.ac.in/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-sub-station-jeypore-koraput/technologies-generated-jaypore/ ; https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found for Pratibha. The OUAT 2022-23 release list covers other rice varieties' resistance profiles only -- https://ouat.ac.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/Varieties-released-during-2022-23.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for Pratibha (maturity, yield, plant height, or trial data not retrieved) -- https://ouat.ac.in/regional-reaearch-and-technology-transfer-sub-station-jeypore-koraput/technologies-generated-jaypore/

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found -- no Pratibha pedigree or marker study surfaced beyond the parentage supplied in the brief.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Institution is OUAT, Bhubaneswar (per the supplied record). No lead breeder name was found. A general source notes that Odisha's rice seed breeders are based at OUAT or at national institutes -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10460-024-10666-0

CONTACT DETAILS: No breeder or named contact found. Institute-level domain only: OUAT website https://ouat.ac.in (Directorate of Research, Bhubaneswar, appears on the 2022-23 release PDF above). No email, phone, or postal address for the institute or Directorate was retrieved in these searches.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found for Pratibha. Only general rice-in-Odisha references surfaced, which do not cover this variety -- http://books.irri.org/TechnicalBulletin16_content.pdf (S.R. Das, IRRI Technical Bulletin 16, 2012, on Odisha rice and OUAT/CRRI releases; not specific to Pratibha).

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found for Pratibha. The Odisha seed-distribution report notes seed supply gaps for some varieties but names no Pratibha seed source -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES: Supplied record says Odisha. No independent notification or state recommendation text for Pratibha was found in the searches.

Suggested next steps (outside this search budget): check the CSC/ICAR release notification for the 2018 Odisha entry, the seednet.gov.in variety page under PRATIBHA, the OUAT Directorate of Research variety list for 2018, and KrishiKosh for OUAT theses or papers.
